* **Intersect** - Remove everything outside of the Shape to leave only the overlapping areas.
* **Exclude** - Show only the areas that do not overlap (the opposite of Intersect).

info

Booleans are additive so each operation will act on the result of the operations above it.

Example

1. Draw 2 Rectangles with the Rectangle tool so that they overlap each other.
2. In the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/), click the + icon next to the **Deformers** attribute on **Rectangle1**.
3. Select **Boolean** from the list.
4. Double click the **Boolean** to load it into the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).
5. Connect rectangle2.id→boolean.clippingShapes.
6. Set the visibility on **Rectangle2** to **off** in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/) (click the 'eye' icon).
7. Set the **Mode** to **Subtract**.

chunks.title: Chop Path
chunks.heading: Chop Path > Chop Path > UI
chunks.text:
**Count** - Set how may slices to chop the Shape into.

**Angle** - Set the angle of the slices.

**Offset** - Add a position offset to the slices along the **Angle**. Connect a Behaviour (e.g. Random) to affect each slice independently.

**Spread** - Add a position offset to the slices perpendicular to the **Angle**. Connect a Behaviour (e.g. Random) to affect each slice independently.

**Flatten Shape** - When checked, when a sub-mesh like a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) or [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) is being 'chopped', the child-meshes are flattened into a single mesh.

Flattened Shapes

Note that with **Flatten Shape** checked:

chunks.title: Chop Path
chunks.heading: Chop Path > Chop Path > UI
chunks.text:
* The Shape is handled 'as one' meaning the slices are based on the overall bounding box of the Layer rather then each of the individual child-meshes. This can affect the position of the resulting slices.
* Any input materials are removed. A [Sub-Mesh Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) can be then added to the Shape and used to apply individual materials to each slice. For example, add a **Sub-Mesh** as a **Deformer** to a **Duplicator** after the **Chop Path**, and then add a [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/) to the Sub-Mesh's **Fill Color** to assign a color to each slice.

chunks.title: Clean Up
chunks.heading: Clean Up > Clean Up > UI
chunks.text:
**Use Distance** - Check to use the **Distance** attribute.

**Distance** - If points fall within this value they will be removed.

**Use Angle** - Check to use the **Angle** attribute.

**Angle** - If points are positioned at an angle less than this value they will be removed.

chunks.title: Color Blend
chunks.heading: Color Blend > Color Blend > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Gradient Mode** - Select an interpolation for the **Gradient**. See [Gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/).

**Gradient** - Set the colors to blend between. See [Gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/).

**Use Alpha** - When unchecked, ignore the alpha set on all color stops.

Example

1. Create an Ellipse.
2. Create a **Color Blend**.
3. Connect colorBlend.id→ellipse.color.
4. Add a [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/) to the **Color Blend**.
5. Move the **Falloff** away/towards the Ellipse.

chunks.title: Color Material Override
chunks.heading: Color Material Override > Color Material Override > Intro
chunks.text:
**Material Overrides** allow the materials inside complex/deep mesh structures like SVGs or Text to be edited. This can be achieved via the [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) Behaviour's Fill or Stroke tabs.

By adding an **Color Material Override** to a Sub-Mesh, it's possible to blend between the original Color and the values set by the Override. A [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/) can then be added to the **Sub-Mesh** to control the effect.

chunks.title: Color Material Override
chunks.heading: Color Material Override > Color Material Override > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Color** - Set a color using hex or rgb values (note - only rgb values can be animated).

Example

1. Import an SVG into the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).
2. Drag it in to the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) and choose **Asset Layer** from the options to create an [SVG Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/svg-shape/).
3. Connect a [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) to the **Deformer** attribute of the **SVG Shape**.
4. On the **Sub-Mesh**, switch to the **Fill** tab in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).
5. Use the `+` button to add an **Color Material Override** to the **Fill Overrides** attribute.
6. Set a **Color**.
7. On the **Color Material Override**, open the **Falloff** tab and right click to add a [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/).
8. Move the **Falloff** over the **SVG Shape**.

As the Falloff moves over the SVG, the colors of the Shapes will become the color set on step 6.

Overriding the colors in an SVG to green via a Falloff

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Behaviours)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Behaviours) > Common Attributes (Behaviours) > UI
chunks.text:
* Behaviour* Falloffs

**Strength** - Determine the strength of the Behaviour.

info

Many, but not all Behaviours include the Graph Widget below.

**Graph** - Click the icon to pop up a Graph Widget. This can be used to shape the effect of a Behaviour. See [Graph Attribute](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/graph-attribute/).

A list for adding and setting [Falloffs](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/).

To add a Falloff either right click on the **Falloffs** row and select \*\*Add Falloffs > Falloff \*\*or [connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) an existing one.

**Visibility icon** (eye) - Enable/ disable the Falloff.

**Layer Mode** - Set the layer mode of each Falloff. Each Falloff affects the result of the layers below:

* **Normal (Add)** - Output values.
* **Min.** - All values will be reduced the lowest value.
* **Max.** - All values will be increased to the highest value.
* **Minus** - Subtract the values.
* **Multiply** - Multiply the values, decreasing values.
* **Screen** - Multiply the inverse of values, increasing values.
* **Overlay** - High values will be increased and the low values will be decreased.

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Behaviours)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Behaviours) > Common Attributes (Behaviours) > UI
chunks.text:
The list can be reordered by simply dragging and dropping.

info

Each layer adds to the result of the layers below it so layer order is very important. For example, with 3 Falloffs:

* The first (bottom) Falloff has to be set to **Normal (Add)** otherwise there are no values for it to add/subtract from.
* The second Falloff will act on the bottom Falloff. e.g. if set to **Minus** it will subtract the values set by the bottom Falloff.
* The third Falloff will act on the result of the Falloffs below it.

In the example below we have 3 Falloffs connected to a [Color Blend](/docs/nodes/behaviours/color-blend/).

The **Color Blend** translates values of 0 as pink (the color on the left hand side of its gradient) and values of 1 as green (the color on the right hand side of its gradient).

* **Falloff 1** is a **Circle** and its **Layer Mode** is set to **Normal (Add)**.
* **Falloff 2** is a smaller **Circle** but its **Layer Mode** is set to **Minus**.
* **Falloff 3** is a **Rectangle** and its **Layer Mode** is set to **Multiply**.

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Behaviours)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Behaviours) > Common Attributes (Behaviours) > UI
chunks.text:
* **Falloff 1** simply passes values of 1 to 0 (from its centre out towards its edge) which the Color Blend converts from green (1) to pink (0).
* **Falloff 2** subtracts its values from Falloff 1's. In the centre, both Falloffs have a value of 1 and so because 1−1=01 - 1 = 01−1=0 the Color Blend gives us pink.
* **Falloff 3** uses its values to multiply the result of Falloff 2. Inside the rectangle the Falloff is passing values of 1 and outside 0 (we've used the Graph to create a hard falloff). Anything×0=0Anything \times 0 = 0Anything×0=0 so everything outside the rectangle is pink. Any values within the rectangle are multiplied by 1 so remain unchanged.

chunks.title: Contours to Sub-Meshes
chunks.heading: Contours to Sub-Meshes > Contours to Sub-Meshes > Intro
chunks.text:
Convert [Path Contours](/docs/nodes/shapes/#meshes) within Shapes into sub-meshes so that individual Contours can be manipulated.

This Layer converts the underlying mesh structure of a Shape which will have no visible effect on a Shape until other Behaviours that support sub-meshes are added after it.

chunks.title: Contours to Sub-Meshes
chunks.heading: Contours to Sub-Meshes > Contours to Sub-Meshes > UI
chunks.text:
**Keep Holes** - When checked, Contours within Contours are treated as holes and 'grouped'. Note that a Contour must be entirely within another Contour to be predictably treated as a hole.

Example

1. Using the [Pen](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pen-tool/) tool, draw several closed Contours. Do not deselect the Shape as you draw to ensure all Contours are drawn within the same Shape.
2. Click the Editable Shape's **Deformers** attribute `+` button and choose **Contours to Sub-Meshes**.
3. Click the Editable Shape's **Deformers** attribute `+` button and choose **Sub-Mesh**.
4. Navigate to the Sub-Mesh's **Fill** tab and check **Replace Fill**.
5. Right click the Sub-Mesh's **Color** attribute > Add Array > Color Array.
6. Click the Color Array's `+ Add` button twice to add two more indices to the array and set some colours.

Each Contour drawn on step one will be applied a color from the Color Array.

chunks.title: Curves to Lines
chunks.heading: Curves to Lines > Curves to Lines > UI
chunks.text:
**Lines per Curve** - Set how many subdivisions will be used between the bézier points.

Example

1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. Using the `+` next to the **Deformers** attribute, add a **Curves to Lines** Behaviour.
3. Set **Lines per Curve** to 1.

chunks.title: Distance
chunks.heading: Distance > Distance > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Target** - Connect a shape to measure from.

**Offset** - Add/subtract a value to the output.

Example

1. Create two [Basic Shapes](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/)
2. Create a **Distance**.
3. Connect basicShape1→distance.target.
4. Connect distance.id→basicShape2.rotation.
5. Move Basic Shape 1

As Basic Shape 1 and Basic Shape 2 move, Basic Shape 2's rotation changes.

info

[Measure](/docs/nodes/utilities/measure/) can also be used to calculate the distance between two Shapes/transforms but it is not possible to use Measure's output to drive either of the Input Shape's transforms as that would create a cycle. Distance allows this as per the example above.

chunks.title: Extend Open Paths
chunks.heading: Extend Open Paths > Extend Open Paths > UI
chunks.text:
**Mode** - Determine the units for the extended lengths:

* **Pixels** - Extend the length of the Path by a specific number of pixels.
* **Percentage of Length** - Extend the length of the Path based on a percentage of its original length.

**Extend Start** - Specify the length in px/% to extend the start of the Path by.

**Extend End** - Specify the length in px/% to extend the end of the Path by.

**Angle Mode** - Determine the direction of the extended ends

* **Path Tangent** - Paths are extended along the tangent of the start/end points.
* **Path Curvature** - Paths are extended by tracing a circle that represents the curvature at the end of the Path.
* **Arc** - - Paths are extended by generating an arc.
* **Custom...** - Paths are extended along a custom angle.

**Arc Radius** - When **Angle Mode** is set to **Arc**, set the radius of the circle the arc is drawn along.

**Arc Sweep Angle** - When **Angle Mode** is set to **Arc**, set the amount of 'the circle' to draw

**Arc Direction** - Determine which side of the path’s tangent the arc centre is placed on:

chunks.title: Extend Open Paths
chunks.heading: Extend Open Paths > Extend Open Paths > UI
chunks.text:
* **Normal** - The arcs are placed along the path's normals.
* **Inverted** - The arcs are placed on the other side of the path's normals.

**Opposite Direction for End** - The end arc is the opposite of what 'Arc Direction' says.

**Start Angle** - When **Angle Mode** is set to **Custom**, set a angle to extend the start of the Path along.

**End Angle** - When **Angle Mode** is set to **Custom**, set a angle to extend the end of the Path along.

Example

1. Draw an open Path with the [Pen](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pen-tool/) or [Pencil](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pencil-tool/) tool.
2. Double click the Shape's Layer to load its UI into the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).
3. Click the `+` button next to the Shape's **Deformers** attribute.
4. Choose **Extend Open Paths** from the list.
5. Increase the **Extend Open Paths**'s **Start** and **End** values.

chunks.title: Fill Rule
chunks.heading: Fill Rule > Fill Rule > Intro
chunks.text: The Fill Rule Behaviour can be used to define how holes and self-intersections affect a Shape's fill.

chunks.title: Fill Rule
chunks.heading: Fill Rule > Fill Rule > UI
chunks.text:
**Mode:**

* **Even Odd** - Any Contour that intersects with another Contour will create a hole.
* **Winding** - In order to create a hole, an intersecting Contour must be drawn in the opposite direction to another.

chunks.title: Flare
chunks.heading: Flare > Flare > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Direction** - Set the axis for the Shape to deform along:

* **Vertical** - Deform along the Y axis.
* **Horizontal** - Deform along the X axis.

**Amount** - Increase/Decrease the strength of the effect. Note - divisions along the edge are required.

**Start Stretch** - Scale the points at the top of the Shape perpendicular to the axis.

**End Stretch** - Scale the points at the bottom of the Shape perpendicular to the axis.

**Graph** - Use the Graph to adjust the curve of the effect. See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/).

chunks.title: Flatten Shape Layers
chunks.heading: Flatten Shape Layers > Flatten Shape Layers > Intro
chunks.text: Flatten Shape Layers can be used as a deformer on Shapes containing sub-meshes to flatten their internal hierarchy into one single Path or Layer.

chunks.title: Flatten Shape Layers
chunks.heading: Flatten Shape Layers > Flatten Shape Layers > UI
chunks.text:
**Mode**:

* **Single Path** - Flattens all geometry into one path. Note - this mode will remove any materials.
* **Single Layer** (keeps materials) - Flattens the sub-mesh hierarchy into a single layer.

**Maintain Transforms** - In certain scenarios, transform information may be lost when applying a Flatten Shape Layers – check this attribute to maintain them. An example of this is applying a Flatten Shape Layers to a Pre-Comp containing a Duplicator which is not positioned at 0,0.

info

Order of operations is really important when using Flatten Shape Layers.

Example

1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. Click the `+` on the **Text Shape**'s Deformers attribute and select [Path Offset](/docs/nodes/behaviours/path-offset/) to create and connect one.
3. Set an **Offset** value on the **Path Offset**.
4. On the **Text Shape**, load its **Stroke** tab and check **Stroke**.

The result should look something like:

5. Click the `+` on the **Text Shape**'s Deformers attribute and select **Flatten Shape Layers** to create and connect one.

The result should look something like:

chunks.title: Four Point Warp
chunks.heading: Four Point Warp > Four Point Warp > Intro
chunks.text:
Deform Shapes using a four corner warp with bézier handles.

Loading Cavalry Player…

Increase/decrease 'Warp'.

chunks.title: Four Point Warp
chunks.heading: Four Point Warp > Four Point Warp > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Centre** - The centre position of the warp.

**Size** - The dimensions of the warp.

**Triangulate** - When checked, a connected Shape will also be triangulated to enable texture deformation.

**Quality** - Determine the tesselation density. A higher setting will create a smoother deformation.

**Corner Transforms** - Each corner includes the following:

* **Corner** - The position of the corner.
* **In Handle** - The offset position of the in handle relative to the corner.
* **Out Handle** - The offset position of the out handle relative to the corner.

Example

1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. Click the  button on the Deformers attribute and choose **Four Corner Warp**.
3. With the **Four Corner Warp** selected and the [Select](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) tool active, move the corner points and/or their handles.

chunks.title: Frame
chunks.heading: Frame > Frame > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Value** - Set a multiplier for time.

**Interpolation Mode** - Determine how the value is output:

* **Frame** - Output the current frame∗Valueframe \* Valueframe∗Value.
* **Seconds** - Increase the value every second (depends on the **Frame Rate** of the Composition).

**Cycle Length** - When **Interpolation Mode** is set to **Seconds**, set how many seconds it takes to add the 'value'.

**Graph** - When **Interpolation Mode** is set to **Seconds**, adjust the interpolation of the value over a second. See [Graph Attribute](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/graph-attribute/).

**Offset** - Offset the time in frames.

**Start Frame** - Set a frame for time to begin on.

**Time** - An auto connection to the [Composition](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/) time.

Example

chunks.title: Frame
chunks.heading: Frame > Frame > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a [Basic Line](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-line/).
2. Set its **Pivot.X** to **100**.
3. Right click on the Basic Line's **Rotation** attribute and choose **Add Behaviour > Frame**.
4. Set the Frame Behaviour's:
   * **Interpolation Mode** to **Seconds**.
   * Open the **Graph** and set the left point's **Position** to **0.95**.
   * Set the **Value** to **-6** (a clock's second hand rotates 6° every second).
5. Press Play.

This will create the second hand of a ticking clock.

chunks.title: Get Vector
chunks.heading: Get Vector > Get Vector > Intro
chunks.text: **Get Vector** can be used in combination with points on a Duplicator to return the direction between a point and a target.

chunks.title: Get Vector
chunks.heading: Get Vector > Get Vector > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Target** - Connect a Shape to get a vector from.

**Normalize** - The returned value is normalized to a value of between 0 and 1.

Example

1. Create a [Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/).
2. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) it to a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).
3. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) a [Value2](/docs/nodes/behaviours/value2/) to **Shape Position** on the **Duplicator**.
4. Add a [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/) to the **Value2** Behaviour.
5. Create a [Get Vector](/docs/nodes/behaviours/get-vector/) Behaviour.
6. Uncheck **Normalize**.
7. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) getVector.id→value2.value.
8. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) falloff.id→getVector.target.

chunks.title: HSV Material Override
chunks.heading: HSV Material Override > HSV Material Override > Intro
chunks.text:
**Material Overrides** allow you to edit materials inside complex/deep mesh structures like SVGs or Text. This can be achieved via the [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) Behaviour's Fill or Stroke tabs.

By adding an **HSV Material Override** to a Sub-Mesh, it's possible to blend between the original Hue, Saturation and Color and the values set by the Override. A [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/) can then be added to the **Sub-Mesh** to control the effect.

chunks.title: HSV Material Override
chunks.heading: HSV Material Override > HSV Material Override > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Hue** - Set a value for the hue.

**Saturation** - Set a value for the saturation.

**Value** - Set the value.

Example

1. Import an SVG into the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).
2. Drag it in to the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) and choose **Asset Layer** from the options to create an [SVG Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/svg-shape/).
3. Connect a [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) to the **Deformer** attribute of the **SVG Shape**.
4. On the **Sub-Mesh**, switch to the **Fill** tab in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).
5. Use the `+` button to add an **HSV Material Override** to the **Fill Overrides** attribute.
6. Adjust the Hue, Saturation and Value values.
7. On the **HSV Material Override**, open the **Falloff** tab and right click to add a [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/).
8. Move the **Falloff** over the **SVG Shape**.

As the Falloff moves over parts of the SVG, they will change color.

chunks.title: Is Within
chunks.heading: Is Within > Is Within > Intro
chunks.text: Switch properties based on whether a Shape's position falls within another. **Is Within** will output a value of `0` when a Shape is `outside` the **Within Shape** and `1` when it is `inside`.

chunks.title: Is Within
chunks.heading: Is Within > Is Within > UI
chunks.text:
**Within Shape** - Connect a shape to be used as the boundary for other shapes to fall within.

Lines

Lines containing **2 points** can be used as the **Within Shape**. The **left** side of the line is considered the **inside** — imagine walking along the line in its path direction and looking left. Path direction can be viewed in the Viewport by selecting a Shape with the [Edit Shape](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/edit-shape-tool/) tool.

If using a [Basic Line](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-line/) then remember to reduce **Divisions** to **0**.

**Invert** - Switch the result so that `0` is output when a Shape is inside the **Within Shape** and `1` when it's outside.

Example

1. Create 2 [Polygons](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/).
2. Name them **Poly** and **Zone**.
3. Create an **Is Within** Behaviour.
4. Connect zone.id→isWithin.withinShape.
5. Create a [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/).
6. Add a second index to the array and set a color.
7. Connect isWithin.id→colorArray.index.
8. Connect colorArray.id→poly.fillColor.

As **Poly** is moved, when its pivot is within the **Zone** Shape, its color will change to the second index of the Color Array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Deformer
chunks.heading: JavaScript Deformer > JavaScript Deformer > Intro
chunks.text:
The **JavaScript Deformer** can be used to manipulate the points of a Shape in interesting and novel ways.

For more information on how JavaScript can be used across all JavaScript Layers see [JavaScript Layers](/docs/nodes/general/javascript-layers/).

[See JavaScript Layers→](/docs/nodes/general/javascript-layers/)

This deformer is similar to the [JavaScript Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/javascript-shape/) and [JavaScript Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/javascript-utility/), only it has some additional syntax available to it so that it has access to a Shape's geometry. This has access to all of the [Context Module](/docs/tech-info/scripting/context-module/) which means data can be saved and loaded for use between frames.

See the [Deformer Module](/docs/tech-info/scripting/deformer-module/) for Member Functions exclusive to this Layer.

chunks.title: JavaScript Deformer
chunks.heading: JavaScript Deformer > JavaScript Deformer > UI

chunks.title: Knot
chunks.heading: Knot > Knot > Intro
chunks.text:
Add gaps to open or closed Paths where a Contour self-intersects.

Gaps are created where a single contour self-intersects

chunks.title: Knot
chunks.heading: Knot > Knot > UI
chunks.text:
**Mode** - Set where gaps are created along the Path.

* **Over First** - Gaps are created at intersections in a repeating order of over, under, over, under...
* **Under First** - Gaps are created at intersections in a repeating order of under, over, under, over...
* **Gaps on Both** - Gaps are created at intersections on both sections of the Path.
* **Geometric** - A gap's over/under order is determined by local geometry making them stable during simulations.

**Gap Width** - Set the size of the gaps in pixels.

Example

1. Using the [Pen](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pen-tool/) or [Pencil](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pencil-tool/) tool, draw a Path that crosses itself.
2. Click the `+` button on the Path's **Deformers** attribute and choose **Knot**.

Gaps will be created where the Path intersects with itself.

Limitations

In certain scenarios, the Contour's geometry and the order of intersections can mean it's not possible to create the correct gaps for some types of knot.

Note that an intersection that occurs where a loop is created by reversing bézier handles is not included.

chunks.title: Lattice Deformer
chunks.heading: Lattice Deformer > Lattice Deformer > Intro
chunks.text:
Deform Shapes using a flexible grid of control points.

Loading Cavalry Player…

Drag the 'Deform' slider to move the Lattice points.

chunks.title: Lattice Deformer
chunks.heading: Lattice Deformer > Lattice Deformer > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Grid Count** - Set the number of control points for the Lattice's grid.

**Triangulate** - When checked, a connected Shape will also be triangulated to enable texture deformation.

**Deformers** - Connect a Behaviour to perform 'per-point' manipulation of the lattice points.

**Controllers** - Connect a [Lattice Controller](/docs/nodes/utilities/lattice-controller/) which can be used to manipulate the position, rotation and scale of multiple Lattice points.

chunks.title: Lattice Deformer
chunks.heading: Lattice Deformer > Lattice Deformer > UI > Buttons
chunks.text:
* **Reset Lattice** - Return any Lattice points to their original grid positions.
* **Keyframe Selection** - Add keyframes to the selected Lattice points.
* **Add Controller to Selection** - Add a [Lattice Controller](/docs/nodes/utilities/lattice-controller/) which can be used to translate the current selection of Lattice points.

chunks.title: Lattice Deformer
chunks.heading: Lattice Deformer > Lattice Deformer > Layer tool
chunks.text:
With the Lattice Layer selected and the [Select](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) tool active, a Layer tool will appear in the Viewport.

To select Lattice points either:

* Click to select.
* `Cmd/Ctrl` + click individual points to add to the selection.
* Marquee select multiple points.
* Hold `Option/Alt` and draw around points to select them.

When multiple points are selected, a manipulator will appear that can be used to move them.

chunks.title: Lattice Deformer
chunks.heading: Lattice Deformer > Lattice Deformer > Layer tool > Viewport Snapping
chunks.text: The Lattice's Layer tool respects [Viewport Snapping](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#snapping). Where multiple points are selected and when using the manipulator, the last point selected will be used for the snapping. Alternatively, click a specific point within the selection and drag it to use that point for the snapping.

chunks.title: Look At
chunks.heading: Look At > Look At > Intro
chunks.text:
Rotate shapes towards a target.

Loading Cavalry Player…

Use the Position controls to move the Null.

chunks.title: Look At
chunks.heading: Look At > Look At > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Target** - Connect a transform (Shape) to aim at.

**Offset** - Add/subtract a value to the output(s).

Example

1. Create a [Polygon](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/).
2. Set its **Sides** to **3**.
3. Create a [Null](/docs/nodes/utilities/null/) (Shortcut: `Shift` + `Cmd/Ctrl` + `=`).
4. Create a **Look At**.
5. Connect null.id→lookAt.target.
6. Connect lookAt.id→polygon.rotation.
7. Move the **Null**.

chunks.title: Manipulator
chunks.heading: Manipulator > Manipulator > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Position** - Set the position [x,y]. 0,0 is in the centre of the Composition.

**Rotation** - Set the rotation (in degrees).

**Scale** - Set the scale values [x,y].

**Pivot** - Set the pivot point [x,y]. This is useful when animating rotation and scale.

chunks.title: Material Sampler
chunks.heading: Material Sampler > Material Sampler > Intro
chunks.text:
The **Material Sampler** samples an **Input Shape** and then outputs values of between 0-1 depending on the value (lightness/darkness) of the shape (e.g. black = 0, white = 1). Alternatively it will output the color if connected to an attribute that supports it (e.g. **Fill Color**).

It can be used in combination with [Shaders](/docs/nodes/effects/) to control attributes for other shapes and is particular useful when used alongside a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).

Performance

The Material Sampler has some known performance issues, particularly when sampling many points (e.g. a Duplicator). Consider using the [Image Sampler](/docs/nodes/utilities/image-sampler/) when working with higher point counts.

chunks.title: Material Sampler
chunks.heading: Material Sampler > Material Sampler > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Value** - A multiplier.

**Input Path** - Connect a Shape with a Material to sample from.

**Graph** - Use the graph to remap the output values.

**Offset** - Add/subtract a value to the output(s).

Example

1. Import an image to the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).
2. Drag the image into the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) (this will create a [Footage Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/footage-shape/)).
3. Create a **Material Sampler**.
4. Connect footageShape.id→materialSampler.inputShape.
5. Create a [Rectangle](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/rectangle/).
6. With the **Rectangle** selected, click the Duplicator [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/) item.
7. Connect materialSampler.id→duplicator.shapeScale.

The shapes will be scaled dependent on the image.

caution

The **Material Sampler** does not currently support **SkSL Shaders** this includes the [Noise Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/noise-shader/).

caution

chunks.title: Material Sampler
chunks.heading: Material Sampler > Material Sampler > UI
chunks.text: The Material Sampler does not currently support frame changes when used within a **Pre-Comp**. Please try and use a [Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/group/) instead of a [Composition](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/) if possible as a workaround.

chunks.title: Mesh Solver
chunks.heading: Mesh Solver > Mesh Solver > Intro
chunks.text: Connect deformers to create drawing machines or iterative effects like differential growth.

chunks.title: Mesh Solver
chunks.heading: Mesh Solver > Mesh Solver > UI
chunks.text:
**Time** - A default connection to the [Composition's](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/) **Time** attribute.

**Start Frame** - The frame at which the solver initialises or resets.

**Pre-Roll Iterations** - Number of deformer iterations applied to the input geometry for all frames at or before the **Start Frame**.

**Level Mode** - These presets set the Level value:

* **Custom...** - Manually set a **Custom Level**.
* **Text (Lines)** - Sets a Level value of 1.
* **Text (Words)** - Sets a Level value of 2.
* **Text (Characters)** - Sets a Level value of 3.

**Custom Level** - Manually set the Level value.

**Deformers** - A list of connected Deformers. Use the + button to create and connect a Behaviour or drag and drop an existing one to connect it.

**Keep Previous Meshes** - Number of previous frame results to keep as sub-meshes. Creates motion blur-like trails. Only works in Internal Feedback mode.

chunks.title: Modulate
chunks.heading: Modulate > Modulate > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Mode**:

* **Remainder** - Create a sequence based on a **Divisor** value.
* **Pass/Fail** - Create a sequence based on whether the remainder is 0 (pass) or not (fail).
* **Custom Pattern** - Create a custom sequence.

**Divisor** - Setting a value of **n** will create a sequence of numbers from **0:n-1**. e.g. a value of **3** will create a sequence of **0,1,2,0,1,2,0**... (see below).

**Index Offset** - Offset the order of the pattern. e.g. if the pattern is **0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2**... an **Index Offset** of **1** will result in **1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 0**...

**Offset** - Offset the start value. e.g. if the pattern is **0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2**... an **Offset** of **2** will result in **2, 3, 4, 2, 3, 4**...

**Pass Value** - When the remainder **is** 0, output this value.

**Fail Value** - When the remainder **is not** 0, output this value.

**Custom Pattern** - Enter a pattern of values separated by commas.

Example (Remainder)

chunks.title: Modulate
chunks.heading: Modulate > Modulate > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create 3 [Basic Shapes](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/) (circle, rectangle, polygon).
2. With all 3 Shapes selected, click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
3. Set **Count** to **x = 5**, **y = 5** on the Duplicator.
4. Create a **Modulate**.
5. Set **Divisor** to **3**.
6. Connect modulate.id→duplicator.shapeId.

With a **Divisor** of 3 **Modulate** is outputting values of *0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 0*... so the **Duplicator** outputs *circle, rectangle, polygon, circle, rectangle, polygon, circle*... (depending on the order they were added).

Example (Pass/Fail)

chunks.title: Modulate
chunks.heading: Modulate > Modulate > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a [Basic Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/).
2. With the Shape selected, click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
3. Set the **Distribution** to **Linear** on the Duplicator.
4. Set **Count** to **9** and **Size** to **900.**
5. Create a [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/).
6. Add a second index and set a different color.
7. Connect colorArray.id→basicShape.FillColor.
8. Create a **Modulate** Behaviour.
9. Set **Mode** to **Pass/Fail**.
10. Set **Divisor** to **3**.
11. Connect modulate.id→colorArray.index.

The resulting sequence is **0,1,1,0,1,1,0**... (see below for the math). If the **Pass Value = 0** and **Fail Value = 1** then that translates to **pass, fail, fail, pass, fail, fail, pass**... If the colors on the Color Array are red and green the resulting sequence of colors will then be **red, green, green, red, green, green, red, green**...

info

The **Remainder** and **Pass/ Fail** modes use **Modular Math**.

Here we're dividing a *number* using a **Divisor** of **3**. Observe what happens to the **remainder** value as the *number* increments by one.

chunks.title: Modulate
chunks.heading: Modulate > Modulate > UI
chunks.text:
* 0÷3=00 \div 3 = 00÷3=0 remainder **0**
* 1÷3=01 \div 3 = 01÷3=0 remainder **1**
* 2÷3=02 \div 3 = 02÷3=0 remainder **2**
* 3÷3=13 \div 3 = 13÷3=1 remainder **0**
* 4÷3=14 \div 3 = 14÷3=1 remainder **1**
* 5÷3=15 \div 3 = 15÷3=1 remainder **2**
* 6÷3=26 \div 3 = 26÷3=2 remainder **0**
* **...**

The remainders start at **0** and increase by **1** each time until the number reaches one less than the **Divisor**. After that, the sequence repeats. So to create the sequence **0,1,2,3,0,1,2,3,**... a **Divisor** of **4** is required.

chunks.title: Morph
chunks.heading: Morph > Morph > Intro
chunks.text: Morph between Shapes with different point counts. Morph differs to a [Blend Shape](/docs/nodes/behaviours/blend-shape/) in that is doesn't require the shapes to have matching point counts. For example, morphing between a [Rectangle](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/rectangle/) (4 points) and a [Polygon](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/polygon/) (5 points) is possible.

chunks.title: Morph
chunks.heading: Morph > Morph > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Mode**:

* **Simple Morph** - Sample additional points in order to match the point counts. Note - Falloff's are not supported in this mode.
* **Wave Morph** - Converts both paths via a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to perform the morph before converting the resulting path back. This can be useful for morphing complex shapes like text characters for example.

**Morph Divisions** - Determine the subdivision level used when sampling the shapes.

**Sampling Offset** - This will offset the pointId. This can be useful to fix instances where two shapes might 'fold' inside out due to points trying to move to the opposite sides.

Example

1. Create an [Ellipse](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/ellipse/) and a [Polygon](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/polygon/).
2. Add a **Morph Behaviour**.
3. Connect polygon.id→morph.morphTarget.
4. Connect morph.id→ellipse.deformers.
5. Scrub **Strength** on the Morph.

chunks.title: Motion Stretch
chunks.heading: Motion Stretch > Motion Stretch
chunks.text:
Experimental Feature

chunks.title: Motion Stretch
chunks.heading: Motion Stretch > Motion Stretch > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Speed Threshold** - Set a threshold for the effect to take place within.

**Deformers** -

chunks.title: Noise
chunks.heading: Noise > Noise > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Strength Fade to Zero** - When checked, **Strength** (including [Falloffs](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/)) will interpolate between **0** and the **result**. When unchecked it will interpolate between the **Minimum** and **Maximum** values.

**Use Normals** - When checked, deformation will be based on the normals of the Shape. When unchecked, points are scaled from the middle of the shape. This attribute is only relevant when the Noise Behaviour is used as a **Deformer**.

**Noise Type** - Set the type of noise to generate:

chunks.title: Noise
chunks.heading: Noise > Noise > UI > Common Noise Attributes
chunks.text:
* **Minimum** - Set a minimum value to output.
* **Maximum** - Set a maximum value to output.
* **Offset** - Add/subtract a value to the output(s).
* **Frequency** -
* **Separate Channels** - Output a different value to the x, y channels.
* **Seed** - Set the random seed.
* **Use Layer as Seed** - When checked, the **Seed** will differ for each Layer the Noise Behaviour is connected to. See also [Layer Seed](/docs/nodes/utilities/layer-seed/).
* **Stagger** - Offset each noise sample in time. When used with a Duplicator (or any sub-mesh), a different **Time** value will be passed to each Id.
* **Looping** - Check to enable looping noise. Note that this will affect the **Time Scale** of the Noise.
* **Loop Length** - Set the number of frames over which a loop will occur.
* **Time** - This attribute is automatically connected to the comp's frame number. Disconnect it if static Noise is required.
* **Time Scale** - Increase/ decrease the speed of the noise.
* **Noise Position** - Set the position of the noise.
* **Noise Rotation** - Set the rotation of the noise.
* **Noise Scale** - Set the scale of the noise.
* **Use Position Context** - When checked, the effect of the Noise will dif

chunks.heading: Noise > Noise > UI > Common Noise Attributes
chunks.text:
fer depending on the position of any other Layers that it is connected to. Unchecking this attribute will result in all Layers being passed the same values regardless of their position.
* **Use Index Context** - When checked, the Noise Behaviour will pull [Context](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/context/). This can be used to control how each Id is affected when used in combination with a sub-mesh (Duplicator, Text, SVG etc). Unchecking this attribute will result in all Layers being passed the same values regardless of their Id.
