chunks.title: Number Range to Color
chunks.heading: Number Range to Color > Number Range to Color > UI
chunks.text:
**Source Minimum** - The smallest value within the range.

**Source Maximum** - The largest value within the range.

**Value** - Connect a range of values (e.g. from a [Spreadsheet](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/) Utility).

**Gradient** - The **Source Minimum** value is remapped to the color value set on the far left of the gradient, the **Source Maximum** value is remapped to the color value set on the far right of the gradient.

**Clamp** - When checked, the output will never go above or below the **Maximum** or **Minimum** values.

info

This layer is also used as a base for options on the [Spreadsheet](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/) Utility. The **Value** attribute will not appear within the **Spreadsheet's** [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) UI as that is being driven by the data on the Layer itself.

Example

chunks.title: Number Range to Color
chunks.heading: Number Range to Color > Number Range to Color > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create 2 [Shapes](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/) (shape1 and shape2).
2. Create a **Number Range to Color**.
3. Set:
4. **Source Minimum** = `-100`
5. **Source Maximum** = `100`
6. Connect shape1.position.y→numberRangeToColor.value.
7. Connect numberRangetoColor.id→shape2.fillColor.
8. Move **Shape1** up and down in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

As **Shape1** reaches a position of **100** in the **Y** axis, **Shape2**'s\*\* Fill Color\*\* will be set to white (the far right of the gradient). As it moves down to a position of **-100** in **Y**, **Shape2**'s **Fill Color** will move towards black (the far left of the gradient). If **Clamp** is checked then as **Shape1** moves above **100, Shape2** will remain white.

Inverting Values

Regardless of the values entered in **Minimum** and **Maximum**, the smallest value will always be used as the **Minimum** and the largest value as the **Maximum**. For example, where the value entered into the **Minimum** attribute is actually larger than the **Maximum** attribute, those values will be inverted as part of the Layer's calculation.

chunks.title: Number Range
chunks.heading: Number Range > Number Range > Intro
chunks.text: The **Number Range** can be used to remap values within a range. For example, if a set of input values are in a range of `0-100` the **Number Range** can be used to increase those values to output a range of `0-400`.

chunks.title: Number Range
chunks.heading: Number Range > Number Range > UI
chunks.text:
**Source Minimum** - The smallest value within the range of the input.

**Source Maximum** - The largest value within the range of the input.

**Value** - Connect a range of values (e.g. from a Spreadsheet)

**Minimum** - The value to remap **Source Minimum** to.

**Maximum** - The value to remap **Source Maximum** to.

**Graph** - See [Graph Attribute](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/graph-attribute/)

**Clamp** - When checked, the output will be clamped at the **Maximum** or **Minimum** values when the input is above or below them. When unchecked, the output values are looped.

**Offset** - Add/subtract a value to/from the output.

Spreadsheet

This Layer is also used as a base for options on the [Spreadsheet](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/) Utility. The **Value** attribute will not appear within the **Spreadsheet** [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) UI as that is being driven by the data connected to the Spreadsheet.

Example

chunks.title: Number Range
chunks.heading: Number Range > Number Range > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create 2 [Shapes](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/) (Shape1 and Shape2).
2. Create a **Number Range**.
3. Set:
   * **Source Minimum** = `-100`
   * **Source Maximum** = `100`
   * **Minimum** = `-400`
   * **Maximum** = `400`
4. Connect shape1.position.y→numberRange.value.
5. Connect numberRange.id→shape2.position.y.
6. Move **Shape1** up and down in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

As **Shape1** reaches a position of **100** in the **Y** axis, **Shape2** will move to a position of **400**. If **Clamp** is checked then as **Shape1** moves above **100** **Shape2** will remain at **400**.

Inverting Values

Regardless of the values entered in **Minimum** and **Maximum**, the smallest value will always be used as the **Minimum** and the largest value as the **Maximum**. For example, where the value entered into the **Minimum** attribute is actually larger than the **Maximum** attribute, those values will be inverted as part of the Layer's calculation. This is also true of **Source Minimum** and **Source Maximum**.

chunks.title: Oscillator
chunks.heading: Oscillator > Oscillator > Intro
chunks.text:
Deform and affect Shapes using trigonometric wave patterns.

Web Player 👀

The interactive widget below demonstrates the **Cavalry Web Player** (work in progress). This is an embedded native Cavalry Scene (`.cv` file) playing back in a browser using attributes promoted to the [Control Centre](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/control-centre/) to generate the UI.

Loading Cavalry Player…

chunks.title: Oscillator
chunks.heading: Oscillator > Oscillator > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

* Behaviour* Deformer

**Strength Fade to Zero** - When checked, **Strength** (including [Falloffs](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/)) will interpolate between **0** and the **result**. When unchecked it will interpolate between the **Minimum** and **Maximum** values.

**Type** - Select a type for the wave:

* **Sine** - Create a sine wave.
* **Cosine** - Create a cosine wave.
* **Tangent** - Create a tangent wave.

**Wave Style** - Select a shape for the wave:

* **Normal** - A smooth, curved wave.
* **Square** - A square wave.
* **Triangle** - A triangular wave.
* **Sawtooth** - A sawtooth wave.
* **Custom...** - Use the **Graph** to create a custom wave.

**Graph** - When **Wave Style** is set to **Custom...** use the graph to draw a custom wave. See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/).

**Minimum** - Set the minimum height of the wave.

**Maximum** - Set the maximum height of the wave.

**Value Offset** - Offset the min/max values.

**Stagger** - When used with a Duplicator this will stagger the movement in time across duplicates.

chunks.title: Oscillator
chunks.heading: Oscillator > Oscillator > UI
chunks.text:
**Separate Channels** - Generate different values for x and y.

**Time Mode** - Determine how the Frequency attribute relates to time (a period is the distance between two peaks of the wave):

* **Seconds** - The **Frequency** value represents periods per second. If **Frequency** is set to `1` and **Time Scale** is set to `1`, a sine wave will move up and down once every second.
* **Minutes (BPM)** - The **Frequency** value represents periods per minute. If **Frequency** is set to `60` and **Time Scale** is set to `1`, a sine wave will move up and down once every second.

**Frequency** - Set the frequency of the waves (a higher number will create more frequent waves).

**Time** - An auto connection to the [Composition](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/)'s time.

**Time Offset** - Offset the animation/time (in seconds).

**Time Scale** - A multiplier for time.

**Use Normals** - When checked deformation will be based on the normals of the Shape. When unchecked points are scaled from the middle of the Shape.

**Number of Waves** - Set the number of complete waves to create along/around the Path.

Looping

chunks.title: Oscillator
chunks.heading: Oscillator > Oscillator > UI
chunks.text:
An Oscillator can be set to loop every `x` seconds using the **Time Mode**, **Frequency** and **Time Scale** attributes. Where a loop is required over a specific period of frames a [Math Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/math/) can be used to create a relationship between FPS and time. For example:

1. Create a Shape.
2. Right click on the **Position** attribute > `Add Behaviour > Oscillator > Y`.
3. Set the Oscillator's **Minimum** to `-100` and the **Maximum** to `100`.
4. Create a [Math Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/math/).
5. Open the [Composition Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/) and connect the **Frame Rate** to the Math's **First** attribute.
6. Enter a value to represent the number of a frames a loop should take into the Math's **Second** attribute.
7. Set the Math's **Operation** to **Divide**.
8. Connect math.id→oscillator.frequency.

If the Comp's **Frame Rate** changes, the Oscillator will continue to loop on the frame number entered into the Math's **Second** attribute.

chunks.title: Oscillator
chunks.heading: Oscillator > Oscillator > UI
chunks.text:
Alternatively the Math could be replaced with an [Attribute Expression](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-interaction/#attribute-expressions) by connecting the Composition's **Frame Rate** to the Oscillator's **Frequency** and then adding an Attribute Expression of `/32` where 32 is the frame number for the Oscillator to loop on.

Circular motion

When using two Oscillators (Sine or Cosine) to create a circular motion, a **Time Offset** of `0.25` should be added to one of the Oscillators.

info

When connecting an Oscillator to e.g. *position.x* on a Shape, use **Time Scale** to speed up the oscillation.

Legacy Oscillator

Legacy Oscillator

The **Oscillator** was updated in **Cavalry 2.4**. Legacy scenes (scenes created before Cavalry 2.4) will continue to use the old Oscillator but can be manually updated to use the current Oscillator. To do this:

1. **Save** a new version of the Scene.
2. Create a new **Oscillator**.
3. Match the new Oscillator's **settings** to the legacy Oscillator's.
4. Replace any existing **connections** from/to the legacy Oscillator with the equivalent from/to the new Oscillator.

chunks.title: Oscillator
chunks.heading: Oscillator > Oscillator > UI
chunks.text:
Settings will need to be tweaked in order to closely match the original Scene. In particular:

* **Time Scale** - It's likely this will need reducing from the original value to match the speed of the legacy Oscillator.
* **Frequency** - This is now dependent on the new **Time Mode** so will need adjusting accordingly.
* **Frequency** - If the Oscillator was being used as a **Deformer**, note that the new **Number of Waves** attribute under the **Deformer** tab should now be used to control the number of waves that the deformation produces. For example, if the legacy Oscillator was being used as a **Deformer** with a **Frequency** of `10`, a similar equivalent will be an Oscillator with a **Frequency** of `1` and a **Number of Waves** of `10`.

chunks.title: Path Average
chunks.heading: Path Average > Path Average > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Iterations** - Set the number of times the smoothing process is applied.

**Cutoff Frequency** - Control the amount of smoothing where lower values will create a smoother result.

chunks.title: Path Offset
chunks.heading: Path Offset > Path Offset > UI
chunks.text:
**Closed Paths Mode** - Determine which direction(s) the path is offset in:

* **Single Sided** - A positive **Offset** value will offset the path outwards.
* **Double Sided** - Offset the path both inwards and outwards.

**Open Paths Cap Style** - Set the appearance of caps (each end of the stroke) on open paths:

* **Flat** - A flat end that terminates at the end point.
* **Round** - A hemispherical end with the end point at its centre.
* **Projecting** - A flat end that projects half the Stroke's **Width** beyond the end point.
* **Joined** - Extend the caps so they connect each end of the path.

**Offset** - Set a value to offset a path by.

**Rounded** - Add rounding to any external corner points.

Example

chunks.title: Path Offset
chunks.heading: Path Offset > Path Offset > UI
chunks.text:
1. Draw a closed Shape with the [Pen](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pen-tool/) tool.
2. In the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/), Click the **Deformers** attribute `+` icon and choose **Path Offset**.
3. Right click on the Path Offset's **Offset** attribute and choose `Add Behaviour > Stagger`.
4. Set the Stagger's **Maximum** to `100`.
5. With the Shape selected, click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
6. Set the Duplicator's **Distribution** to [Point](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/point-distribution/).

Each duplicated path increases in size. Try increasing the Duplicator's **Count** and/or adjusting the Stagger's [Graph](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/graph-attribute/).

info

Path Offset does not support a mixture of closed and open Contours within the same [Path](/docs/nodes/shapes/). Paths are offset as a whole producing more predictable results for Text. It is however, possible to connect the same Path Offset to more than one Shape.

chunks.title: Path Relax
chunks.heading: Path Relax > Path Relax > Intro
chunks.text:
Move path points away from each other.

Loading Cavalry Player…

Increase 'Relaxation Strength' to relax the path's points.

chunks.title: Path Relax
chunks.heading: Path Relax > Path Relax > UI
chunks.text:
**Iterations** - How many times to apply the relaxation process. Higher values will result in stronger separation.

**Radius** - The distance points must be within each other to be pushed apart.

**Relaxation Strength** - A multiplier for the distance points push away from their neighbours.

chunks.title: Pathfinder
chunks.heading: Pathfinder > Pathfinder > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

* Behaviour* Deformer* Value

**Travel** - Move the Shape along a percentage of the **Input Shape**’s length.

**Loop** - When checked, a Shape will return to the beginning of the Path and continue animating. When unchecked a shape will continue in the direction of the first/ last point.

**Reverse Input Path** - Reverse the direction of the Input Path.

**Input Shape** - Connect a Shape to position/deform the Shape along.

**Taper Graph** - Create a taper along the length of the **Input Shape**.

**Path Offset** - Move the Shape away from the **Input Shape**.

**Flip** - Flip the Shape along its x axis. This is particularly useful for Text.

**Rotation Offset** - Add an offset to the **Rotation**.

**Rotation** (read only) - Outputs the rotation along the normal of the **Input Shape**. Connect this to the **Rotation** attribute of another Shape.

Example (Deformer)

chunks.title: Pathfinder
chunks.heading: Pathfinder > Pathfinder > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a [Rectangle](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/rectangle/).
2. Set the **Edge Divisions** for the Rectangle's **Width** (W) to `20`.
3. Click the `+` icon next to **Deformers** on the Rectangle and add a **Pathfinder**.
4. Draw a path with the [Pen tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pen-tool/).
5. Connect path.id→pathfinder.inputShape.

Example (animate along a path)

1. Create an [Ellipse](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/).
2. Draw a path with the [Pen tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pen-tool/).
3. Create a **Pathfinder**.
4. Connect path.id→pathfinder.inputShape.
5. Connect pathfinder.id→ellipse.position.

info

Use the [Align](/docs/nodes/behaviours/align/) behaviour to pin Shapes to their top/ bottom/ left/ right edges before adding a Pathfinder to deform shapes on the inside or outside of the **Input Path**.

chunks.title: Pinch
chunks.heading: Pinch > Pinch > Intro
chunks.text: Pinch and pull Shapes within a [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/) by moving a [Null](/docs/nodes/utilities/null/).

chunks.title: Pinch
chunks.heading: Pinch > Pinch > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Active** - Enable/ disable the Deformer. This is useful when initially placing the Falloffs for **Bind Area** and **Pinch Point**.

**Bind Area** - The area where the **Pinch** is active. By default, a [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/) called **Pinch Binder** is added and connected to this attribute when creating a **Pinch Deformer**. Any shape points falling within this Falloff will be affected with any outside being ignored.

**Pinch Point** - By default, a [Null](/docs/nodes/utilities/null/) called **Pinch Mover** is created and connected to this attribute when creating a Pinch Deformer. This Null can then be repositioned to 'pinch' the Shape it is deforming.

Example

1. Create an [Ellipse](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/)
2. Set **Radius** to W = 300, H = 300.
3. Uncheck **Bézier**.
4. Using the `+` icon on the **Deformer** attribute, select **Pinch** from the list.
5. Move the **Pinch Binder** [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/) so its centre is over the edge of the Ellipse.
6. Move the **Pinch Mover** [Null](/docs/nodes/utilities/null/).

chunks.title: Pinch
chunks.heading: Pinch > Pinch > UI
chunks.text: The part of the Ellipse within the Falloff is deformed. Try increasing the size of the **Pinch Binder** Falloff or adjusting its **Falloff Graph**.

chunks.title: Position Blend
chunks.heading: Position Blend > Position Blend > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**First (origin)** - Enter the position [x,y] for the Shape's origin.

**Second** - Enter the position [x,y] for the Shape's destination (e.g. the position it will move to when a Falloff is over its origin.

Example

1. Create a [Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/).
2. Create a **Position Blend**.
3. Connect positionBlend.id→shape.position.
4. Set **Second** to 50, 50.
5. Right click on the \*\*Falloff \*\*attribute and select **Add Falloff**.
6. Move the Falloff.

The shape will move towards the position set in **Second** when the **Falloff** passes over the position set in **First**.

chunks.title: Push Along Vector
chunks.heading: Push Along Vector > Push Along Vector > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Use Normals** - When checked, deformation will be based on the normals of the Shape. When unchecked points are deformed from the middle of the shape.

**Direction** - Manually set the vector to deform along.

**Reverse Direction** - Invert the **Direction**.

Example

1. Create an [Ellipse](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/ellipse/).
2. Set its **Radius** to `200,200`.
3. Uncheck **Bézier**.
4. Click the `+` button on the Ellipse's **Deformers** attribute and choose **Push Along Vector**.
5. On the Push Along Vector:
   1. Set **Strength** to `1000%`.
   2. Check **Use Normals**.
6. Open the Push Along Vector's **Falloff** tab and then right click in the Falloffs input > Add Falloff > Falloff.
7. Move the [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/) around the edges of the Ellipse.

chunks.title: Random
chunks.heading: Random > Random > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Strength Fade to Zero** - When checked, **Strength** (including [Falloffs](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/)) will interpolate between **0** and the **result**. When unchecked it will interpolate between the **Minimum** and **Maximum** values.

**Use Normals** - When checked deformation will be based on the normals of the Shape. When unchecked points are scaled from the middle of the shape. Only relevant when used as a Deformer.

**Minimum** - Set the minimum number to be generated.

**Maximum** - Set the maximum number to be generated.

**Seed** - Set the random seed.

**Use Layer as Seed** - When checked, the **Seed** will differ for each Layer the Random Behaviour is connected to. See also [Layer Seed](/docs/nodes/utilities/layer-seed/).

**Offset** - Add/subtract a value to the output.

**Separate Channels** - Generate different random values for x and y.

**Use Bias Graph** - When checked, the **Bias Graph** can be used to set the probability of a random number.

**Bias Graph** - See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/).

chunks.title: Resample Path
chunks.heading: Resample Path > Resample Path > UI
chunks.text:
**Merge Overlaps** - When checked, any overlapping Contours will be either removed or joined depending on the **Mode**.

**Mode** - Select the type of resampling:

* **Union** - Join the Contours together where they overlap.
* **Simplify** - Remove any parts of the Contours that overlap with each other.

**Simplify** - Reduce the number of points on the Path.

**Simplify Threshold** - Set a distance within which a point will be removed. A larger value will result in a simpler Path.

**Resample as Béziers** - Convert the simplified points to bézier points.

**Corner Angle** - Any corner points which join at an angle above this value will be unaffected by the resampling and remain as corner points.

chunks.title: Reverse Path
chunks.heading: Reverse Path > Reverse Path > Intro
chunks.text: Reverse the direction of Contours within a Path (a Path can contain multiple Contours).

chunks.title: Reverse Path
chunks.heading: Reverse Path > Reverse Path > UI
chunks.text:
**Mode** - Choose which Contours to reverse:

* **Reverse All** - Reverse all the Contours in a Path.
* **Reverse Clockwise** - Reverse only the clockwise Contours in a Path. The result is that all contours will have their direction set to Counter-Clockwise.
* **Reverse Counter-Clockwise** - Reverse only the counter-clockwise Contours in a Path. The result is that all contours will have their direction set to Clockwise.

chunks.title: Round
chunks.heading: Round > Round > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Value** - Connect a value to round.

**Rounding** - Set the nearest integer to round to. e.g. setting to 10 will round the **Value** to the nearest 10.

**Type** - Set the type of rounding.

* **Round** - Round up or down to the nearest value.
* **Round Up** - Only round up.
* **Round Down** - Only round down.

**Deformer Mode** - When Round is used as deformer, select which axis it affects:

* **X** - Affect the X axis.
* **Y** - Affect the Y axis.
* **Both** - Affect both the X and Y axes.

chunks.title: Rubber Hose Limb
chunks.heading: Rubber Hose Limb > Rubber Hose Limb > UI
chunks.text:
**Start Controller** - A Shape ([Null](/docs/nodes/utilities/null/) by default) which can be used to control the top of the Shape.

**End Controller** - A Shape ([Null](/docs/nodes/utilities/null/) by default) which can be used to control the bottom of the Shape

**Joint Position** - Determine the percentage along the Shape for the position of the joint.

**Length** - The length of the limb.

**Taper Graph** - Create a taper along the length of a Shape (geometry only). See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/).

**Flip** - Flip the joint to bend the other way.

**Stretch** - When the distance between the controllers is bigger than the original Shape, stretch the Shape to fit the distance.

**Curvature** - Set the bézier handle length for the joint. 0% is a linear joint, 100% sets the handle length to maximum.

**Rotation** - When using the commands to create a Rubber Hose rotation is automatically connected to **End Rotation** [Nulls](/docs/nodes/utilities/null/).

**Offset** -

Divisions

Any Shape/Line will need divisions for the deformation to work.

Example

chunks.title: Rubber Hose Limb
chunks.heading: Rubber Hose Limb > Rubber Hose Limb > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a [Basic Line](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-line/)
2. Set **Divisions** to **50**
3. With the Line selected choose ***Animation > Attach Rubber Hose Limb*** from the menu.

chunks.title: Skew
chunks.heading: Skew > Skew > UI
chunks.text:
**Strength** - Determine the strength of the Behaviour

**Skew** - Set the amount of skew [x, y]

**Pivot X** - The skew pivot point, from left to right.

**Pivot Y** - The skew pivot point from bottom to top.

chunks.title: Sound
chunks.heading: Sound > Sound > Intro
chunks.text:
Playback audio and drive deformation or values.

Get started with audio import and the Sound Behaviour.

chunks.title: Sound
chunks.heading: Sound > Sound > Intro > Working with Audio
chunks.text:
Dragging an audio file directly from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) into the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) or [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) will create a **Sound Behaviour** and connect the audio file.

In order to hear audio in playback, **Audio Playback** must be enabled in the settings at the bottom of the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#audio-playback).

Editing audio in Pre-Comps

Setting the in/out points of a **Pre-Comp** containing a **Sound Behaviour** will not affect the audio output – audio must be clipped within its parent Composition.

chunks.title: Sound
chunks.heading: Sound > Sound > UI
chunks.text:
* Behaviour* Falloffs* Advanced

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**File** - Drag in an audio file from the [Asset Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).

**Frequency Scale** - Choose a model to sample the audio file's frequencies with:

* **Logarithmic** - Mirror the structure of musical octaves, where each octave represents a doubling of frequency similar to the way musical scales are organised.
* **Mel** - Mirror the non-linear way humans perceive pitch differences making it useful for speech.
* **Bark** - Mirror how humans perceive sound, incorporating the concept of auditory masking and bandwidths.
* **Linear** - The frequency bins are divided linearly (no remapping).

**Frequency Range Hz** - Customise the range of frequencies to sample the file within.

**Equaliser** - Preview the sound file and isolate Frequency Bands. Use the cursor to remove/add bands to be omitted/included. The buttons to the right can be used to activate or deactivate all bands.

**Frequency Bands** - Set the number of bands to sample.

chunks.title: Sound
chunks.heading: Sound > Sound > UI
chunks.text:
**Volume Clipping** - Values that fall below this threshold will be ignored (represented by a red line in the equalizer).

**Band Weighting Graph** - Use a graph to control the contribution of individual bands to the output value where the position `P` (0..1) of the curve represents the **Frequency Range Hz** (L..H). A value `V` of 0 removes that frequency's contribution, a value of 1 will double its contribution. The default value of 0.5 will leave the values unchanged.

**A-Weighting** - When checked, [A-weighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-weighting) is applied to account for the relative loudness perceived by the human ear.

**Value Offset** - Add/remove a value to the input.

**Frame Offset** - Offset audio playback in the timeline.

**Sub Steps** - Can be used to 'smooth' the sound signal. With a value of 0 Cavalry samples the audio file at each frame number. By adding sub steps Cavalry will sample more often. e.g. a value of 1 will sample at frames 0.5, 1 and 1.5 and create an average of those values.

chunks.title: Sound
chunks.heading: Sound > Sound > UI
chunks.text:
**Smoothing Frames** - Smooth the sound signal by increasing the number of frames used to create a sample. For example, a value of `2` will sample the current frame and the one before and average out those values.

Performance

When using **Sub Steps** and **Smoothing Frames** expect a performance hit of (smoothingFrames+1)∗subSteps(smoothingFrames+1)\*subSteps(smoothingFrames+1)∗subSteps

e.g. **Smoothing Frames = 2** and **Sub Steps = 4** will create a **(2 + 1) \* 4 = 12x** time penalty on the Layer.

**Maximum dB** (Output) - The maximum dB value found within the asset connected to the **File** attribute.

**File Length** (Output) - The duration of the asset connected to the **File** attribute (in frames).

**Active Bands** (Output) - The number of active frequency bands selected in the **Equaliser**.

**Volume Adjustment** - Increase/decrease the volume of the audio track.

**Pan** - Bias audio towards the left (negative) or right (positive) stereo channels.

info

Note that it's not possible to make connections to the **Volume Adjustment** or **Pan** attributes. Any adjustments required here should be driven with keyframes.

chunks.title: Sound
chunks.heading: Sound > Sound > UI
chunks.text:
See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/).

**Use Index Context** - When checked, [Context](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/context/) can be passed to other Layers. For example, this could be used to map each frequency band to each of the individual Shapes within a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).

**Play Audio** - When checked, the audio will be audible. This is the equivalent of toggling the speaker icon in the Scene Tree to on.

Example

1. Import an audio asset.
2. Drag the asset into the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) or [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) to create a Sound Behaviour.
3. Create a Shape.
4. Connect sound.id→shape.position.y.
5. Increase the Sound Behaviour's **Strength** (depending on the audio asset).
6. Play

The audio will drive the vertical movement of the Shape.

info

The **Sound Behaviour** outputs in **dB** (decibels) which can differ depending on the audio asset.

Combining audio tracks

Use the [Behaviour Mixer](/docs/nodes/behaviours/behaviour-mixer/) to combine the outputs of several Sound Behaviours.

info

chunks.title: Sound
chunks.heading: Sound > Sound > UI
chunks.text:
Dragging an audio file directly from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) into the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) or [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) will create a **Sound Behaviour** and connect the audio file.

caution

When using **Sub Steps** and **Smoothing Frames** expect a performance hit of (smoothingFrames+1)∗subSteps(smoothingFrames+1)\*subSteps(smoothingFrames+1)∗subSteps

e.g. **Smoothing Frames = 2** and **Sub Steps = 4** will create a **(2 + 1) \* 4 = 12x** time penalty on the node.

chunks.title: Spring
chunks.heading: Spring > Spring
chunks.text:
Experimental Feature

This is an experimental feature. To enable, check **Enable Experimental Features** in [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/). Experimental features are only available as part of a **Professional** licence.

chunks.title: Spring
chunks.heading: Spring > Spring > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Damping** -

**Mass** -

**Speed Limit** -

chunks.title: Squash and Stretch
chunks.heading: Squash and Stretch > Squash and Stretch > Intro
chunks.text: Squash and stretch Shapes with options to add bulge and preserve a Shape's area.

chunks.title: Squash and Stretch
chunks.heading: Squash and Stretch > Squash and Stretch > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Amount** - Determine how exaggerated the deformation is. Use a positive value to stretch or a negative value to squash.

**Pin** - Pin the effect to the bounding box of the Shape:

* **Centre** - Pin to the centre of the Shape.
* **Top** - Pin to the top of the Shape.
* **Bottom** - Pin to the bottom of the Shape.

**Bulge** - Set a value for the amount of bulge.

**Automatic Bulge Adjustments** - When checked, the **Bulge** will automatically fade on/off as the Shape squashes.

**Graph** - Adjust the shape of the **Bulge**.

**Area Preservation** - When checked, the **Bulge** will be scaled in order to preserve the original Shape's area. This is useful for maintaining a more realistic result.

**Subdivide Geometry** - When checked, the **Bulge** will be automatically subdivided into shorter edges for a smoother deformation.

**High Quality** - When **Subdivide Geometry** in checked, increase the point sampling for a higher quality output.

**Use Levels** - When checked, the child-meshes can be affected independently.

**Level Mode** - Choose which level(s) of a Mesh to affect.

chunks.title: Squash and Stretch
chunks.heading: Squash and Stretch > Squash and Stretch > UI
chunks.text:
* **Custom...** - Manually set a **Custom Level**.
* **Text (Lines)** - Used with a Text Shape, this will affect each **line**.
* **Text (Words)** - Used with a Text Shape, this will affect each **word**.
* **Text (Characters)** - Used with a Text Shape, this will affect each **character**.

**Custom Level** - Set the level within the Mesh's hierarchy to affect.

chunks.title: Stagger
chunks.heading: Stagger > Stagger > Intro
chunks.text:
Generate sequential values between a minimum and maximum.

A **Stagger** is useful when used with a sub-mesh such as a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) or [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).

Example

1. Create a Shape.
2. With the **Shape** selected, click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
3. Create a **Stagger**.
4. Set the Stagger's **Maximum** to **200**.
5. Connect stagger.id→duplicator.shapePosition.y.

In the image below, a **Stagger** is connected to a Duplicator's **Shape Position Y** attribute. The first `Id` is assigned the Stagger's **Minimum** value (-100) and the last `Id` is assigned the Stagger's **Maximum** value (100), with all the other`Ids` being assigned the values in-between. This results in the diagonal line.

A Stagger connected to a Duplicator's Shape Position.

Here's how that looks in a table representing a Duplicator with a **Count** of 5 (Ids 0-4) and a Stagger with a **Minimum** value of -100 and a **Maximum** value of 100:

chunks.title: Stagger
chunks.heading: Stagger > Stagger > Intro

chunks.title: Stagger
chunks.heading: Stagger > Stagger > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Minimum** - Set a minimum or 'start' value.

**Maximum** - Set a maximum or 'end' value.

**Offset** - Add/subtract a value to the **Minimum** and **Maximum** values.

**Graph** - See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/).

chunks.title: Stagger
chunks.heading: Stagger > Stagger > UI > Understanding the Stagger Graph
chunks.text:
The Stagger Graph's axes are not fixed values, they represent:

* **X axis** - the first and last `Id` within a sub-mesh. This can depend on the **Count** for a Duplicator or the number of characters in a **string** (for Text).
* **Y axis** - the Stagger's **Minimum** and **Maximum** values.

The axes of the Stagger's Graph.

By default, the graph is a straight line meaning that values are output in a linear way. If the **Minimum = 0** and the **Maximum = 200** then at a point half way along the X axis the graph will output a value of 100.

The middle Id is assigned a value half way between the Minimum and Maximum.

The Graph's curve can be adjusted to affect the values outputted by the Stagger.

The result of adjusting the Graph's curve.

chunks.title: Stagger
chunks.heading: Stagger > Stagger > UI > Using Stagger with Time
chunks.text:
A Shape's animation offset in time using a Stagger.

A Stagger can also be used to offset animation. The principles are exactly the same but it's often necessary to 'flip' the Stagger's default Graph where the expectation is for the first Id to be the first to animate.

Where a Stagger is used with a Duplicator's **Shape Time Offset** the values for each `Id` are calculated as follows:

`Stagger Value + Current Frame = Shape Time Offset`

In the table below, see how that translates when there are 3 `Ids` (0-2) in a Duplicator and a Stagger with a **Minimum** value of `-11` and a **Maximum** value of `0`.

tip

It's often useful to set the Stagger's **Minimum** attribute to a **negative** value with a **Maximum** value of 0 so that any offset animation doesn't start before frame 0.

chunks.title: Stagger
chunks.heading: Stagger > Stagger > UI > Using Stagger with Time

chunks.title: Stagger
chunks.heading: Stagger > Stagger > UI > Using Stagger with Time
chunks.text:
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Id Stagger + Frame = Time Offset|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 2 -11 0 -11|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 -5 0 -5|  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 0 0 0 0 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

Inverting Values

Regardless of the values entered in **Minimum** and **Maximum**, the smallest value will always be used as the **Minimum** and the largest value as the **Maximum**. For example, where the value entered into the **Minimum** attribute is actually larger than the **Maximum** attribute, those values will be inverted as part of the Layer's calculation.

chunks.title: Stitches
chunks.heading: Stitches > Stitches > Intro
chunks.text:
Fill closed Paths with a stitch effect.

A Text Shape filled with stitches plus a Bevel Deformer.

chunks.title: Stitches
chunks.heading: Stitches > Stitches > UI
chunks.text:
**Distance** - The distance between each stitch in pixels. Connect a Behaviour to this attribute to create a variation or patterns of gaps. Note that [Stagger](/docs/nodes/behaviours/stagger/) is not supported – use the **Spread** attribute instead.

**Spread** - A tinned ‘stagger’ style effect which incrementally increases the gaps between stitches.

**Disconnection Multiplier** - How far away the next connection point can be before a new Contour is started. Setting this to a very low value can be used as a way to create hatching.

**Rotation** - Set a rotation for the stitches in degrees.

**Keep Original Path** - When checked, the original Path is drawn.

Example

1. Create a [Rectangle](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/rectangle/).
2. Disable **Fill**.
3. Enable **Stroke**.
4. Click the `+` button on the Path's **Deformers** attribute and choose **Stitches**.
5. Set **Disconnection Multiplier** to `0`.
6. Set **Rotation** to `45`.

chunks.title: Sub-Mesh
chunks.heading: Sub-Mesh > Sub-Mesh > Intro
chunks.text:
Meshes in Cavalry can contain a hierarchy of other Shapes within them. These meshes are referred to as ‘child-meshes’. This hierarchy is a tree structure much like the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/), only it exists within a [Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/)'s Mesh.

For example, a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) consists of **Lines**, **Words** and **Characters**, a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) creates a Mesh built of many **Input Shapes** and [SVG](/docs/nodes/shapes/svg-shape/)s can have any number of layers within layers. The **Sub-Mesh** Behaviour provides a way to access and affect these individual child-meshes by specifying the level(s) within a hierarchy.

Create a mesh hierarchy

It's also possible to create mesh hierarchies that can be affected by a **Sub-Mesh** manually. For example:

Two Ellipses within a [Pre-Comp](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/):

* Pre-Comp
  + Ellipse1
  + Ellipse2

Two Ellipses within a [Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/group/) which is then the **Input Shape** to a [Custom Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/custom-shape/):

* Custom Shape
  + Ellipse1
  + Ellipse2

chunks.title: Sub-Mesh
chunks.heading: Sub-Mesh > Sub-Mesh > UI
chunks.text:
* Shape* Advanced

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Position** - Set the X and Y position. 0,0 is in the centre of the Composition.

**Rotation** - Set the rotation (in degrees).

**Scale** - Set the X and Y scale values.

**Opacity** - Set the opacity.

**Visibility** - Affect the visibility on a per child-mesh basis.

**Time Offset** - Offset the animation curves on a per child-mesh basis.

**Recalculate Pivot** - When checked, place the pivot for each child-mesh based on the **Pivot Position**.

**Pivot Position** - When **Recalculate Pivot** is checked, position the pivots by aligning them to each child-mesh's bounding box.

**Deformers** - A list of connected Deformers.

**Filters** - A list of connected [Filters](/docs/nodes/effects/).

**Level Mode** - Choose which level(s) of a Mesh's hierarchy to affect.

chunks.title: Sub-Mesh
chunks.heading: Sub-Mesh > Sub-Mesh > UI
chunks.text:
* **Custom...** - Manually set a **Custom Level Range**.
* **Text (Lines)** - Used with a Text Shape, this will affect each **line**.
* **Text (Words)** - Used with a Text Shape, this will affect each **word**.
* **Text (Characters)** - Used with a Text Shape, this will affect each **character**.
* **All** - Affects all sub-meshes, regardless of level.

info

The **Level Mode** provides several settings designed to make working with Text easier. For example, the **Text (Words)** mode sets internal **Custom Level Range** values of `2, 2`. While these settings will affect any words in a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/), the same settings can also be valid for an [SVG Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/svg-shape/).

**Custom Level Range** - Set the level within the Mesh's hierarchy to affect. This can also be used to set a range of levels. For example, setting a range of `1, 2` might be used to override the color of an SVG for all the shapes on levels 1 and 2 but not on level 3.

info

As the **Level** value increases, the Sub-Mesh travels deeper into the Shape's hierarchy.

**Flatten Mesh at Level** - All child-meshes below this level will be merged and brought up to this one.

chunks.title: Sub-Mesh
chunks.heading: Sub-Mesh > Sub-Mesh > UI
chunks.text:
**Index Mode** - Determine how the indices are assigned to the child-meshes:

* **Unique** - Assign a unique index for each child-mesh. For example, when adding a **Sub-Mesh** to a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) and then adding a [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/) to the **Sub-Mesh**, the colors will loop over each character.
* **Child Index** - Assign a unique index for each child-mesh within its parent. For example, a 'word' is the parent of a 'character' – when adding a **Sub-Mesh** to a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) and then adding a [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/) to the **Sub-Mesh**, the colors will loop over each character but the indices will start from `0` on the first character of each word. This can be used to create repeating effects. The table below provides an example of how the indices are assigned for each option when used with a Text Shape and the string `HELLO WORLD`:

chunks.title: Sub-Mesh
chunks.heading: Sub-Mesh > Sub-Mesh > UI

chunks.title: Sub-Mesh
chunks.heading: Sub-Mesh > Sub-Mesh > UI > Fill and Stroke
chunks.text:
**Sub-Mesh** also has Fill and Stroke tabs. They are identical to those found on [Shapes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) apart from two exceptions.

**Replace Fill/Stroke** - When checked the Sub-Mesh will overwrite any materials on the shapes it is connected to with the Color and/or Shaders set in this tab.

**Replacement Mode** - By default, all materials will be replaced but, by using this option, certain conditions can be targeted:

* **Replace All** - Sub-Mesh will replace the Fill/Stroke of all sub-meshes.
* **Replace Missing** - Sub-Mesh will only replace the Fill/Stroke of any sub-meshes that **do not** have **Fill/Stroke** enabled.
* **Replace Existing** - Sub-Mesh will only replace the Fill/Stroke of any sub-meshes that **do** have **Fill/Stroke** enabled.

**Fill/Stroke Overrides** - See [Color Material Override](/docs/nodes/behaviours/color-material-override/) and [Alpha Material Override](/docs/nodes/behaviours/alpha-material-override/).

**Use Index Context** - When checked, the Sub-Mesh will pull [Context](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/context/). This can be used to control how Ids are assigned and so affect each child-mesh individually.

info

chunks.title: Sub-Mesh
chunks.heading: Sub-Mesh > Sub-Mesh > UI > Fill and Stroke
chunks.text:
Levels for [Text](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) are as follows:

1. Line.
2. Word.
3. Character.

Example usage

1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. Create a **Sub-Mesh** Behaviour.
3. Connect subMesh.id→textShape.deformers
4. Set **Position Y** on the **Sub-Mesh** to **30**.
5. Right click on the **Falloff** attribute and select 'Add Falloff'.

When the **Falloff** is animated over the text, each letter will move up 30px.

chunks.title: Subdivide
chunks.heading: Subdivide > Subdivide > UI
chunks.text:
**Smooth Angle** - Filter the points whose edges join at an angle **greater than** this value.

**Subdivisions** - Set the number of subdivisions to add.

**Threshold** - Set the distance between two subdivision points after which any further subdivision is prevented.

**Curve to End Points** - When checked, this can improve the resulting curve at the ends of open Paths.

chunks.title: Swap Color Override
chunks.heading: Swap Color Override > Swap Color Override > Intro
chunks.text:
Material Overrides allow you to edit materials inside complex/deep mesh structures like SVGs or Text. This can be achieved via the [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) Behaviour's Fill or Stroke tabs.

The **Swap Color Override** enables you to take one specific color within a [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) (e.g. an SVG, Text Shape or Duplicator) and swap it for another one.

chunks.title: Swap Color Override
chunks.heading: Swap Color Override > Swap Color Override > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes +](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/)

**Old Color** - Set the color to swap from.

**New Color** - Set the color to swap from the **Old Color** to.

Example

1. Import an SVG into the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).
2. Drag it in to the Viewport to create an [SVG Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/svg-shape/).
3. Connect a [Sub Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) to the Deformer attribute of the **SVG Shape**.
4. On the **Sub Mesh**, switch to the **Fill** tab in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).
5. Use the `+` button to add a **Swap Color** to the **Fill Overrides** attribute.
6. Set a value for **Old Color** that matches one in the SVG.
7. Set a value for **New Color** to swap Old Color to.

Swapping the color in an SVG from pink to green via a Falloff.

chunks.title: Travel Deformer
chunks.heading: Travel Deformer > Travel Deformer > Intro
chunks.text:
Reposition the start points for all Contours within a Path. Some features like Stroke or Pathfinder already have a Travel attribute but the Travel Deformer provides a way to manipulate contours for other custom uses such as:

* Travel a Shape that's constrained to the point of another Shape along that Shape.
* Travel tapered/dashed strokes along/around a path (when Trim ≠ 0 or 100%).

chunks.title: Travel Deformer
chunks.heading: Travel Deformer > Travel Deformer > UI
chunks.text:
**Travel** - Set the position of the Contour's first point as a percentage along the Contour's length.

info

Note that for open Contours, **Travel** will remove any part of the path before the start point.

chunks.title: Value Blend
chunks.heading: Value Blend > Value Blend > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**First** - This value will be output when **Strength** = 0.

**Second** - This value will be output when **Strength** = 100.

chunks.title: Value Solver
chunks.heading: Value Solver > Value Solver > Intro
chunks.text:
Store the values from previous frames in order to accumulate and/or fade them over time.

Using a Solver to set the number of sides on a polygon.

chunks.title: Value Solver
chunks.heading: Value Solver > Value Solver > UI
chunks.text:
* Solver* Advanced

**Mode** - Set the Solver's mode:

* **Accumulate** - Add the **Value** on each frame.
* **Highest** - If the value on the current frame is higher than the **Value** then it is kept.
* **Lowest** - If the value on the current frame is lower than the **Value** then it is kept.
* **Velocity** - Multiply the velocity of a Shape by the **Value**. See example below.

**Value** - Set the value to be added to the solver on each frame.

**Fade Mode** - Determine whether values should remain persistent or fade back to the initial value.

* **Off** - Don't fade values.
* **Multiply by Value** - On each frame, multiply values based on the **Fade Value**.

**Fade Value** - The speed at which the value will return to its initial values once the Solver is 'off' (e.g. outside a [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/)). The lower the value, the quicker the fade.

**Offset** - Add/subtract a value to the output.

**Start Frame** - Set the first frame to start the solver on. By default, this is connected to the [Composition's](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/) **Frame Range** (Start) attribute — remove this connection to set a custom value.

chunks.title: Value Solver
chunks.heading: Value Solver > Value Solver > UI
chunks.text:
**Time** - A default connection to the [Composition's](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/) **Time** attribute.

**Use Cache** - When checked, the simulation can be saved to a `.sdcache` file. This can be useful for faster playback with heavier simulations or for retiming via the **Cache Offset**. It is also required for Motion Blur.

**Cache File Path** - Set the location the cache file is saved. This is determined when first caching a solver or use the folder icon to open a Finder/ Explorer window and navigate to an existing `.sdcache` file.

**Cache Offset** - Set a time offset for the cache.

Example

chunks.title: Value Solver
chunks.heading: Value Solver > Value Solver > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a **Value Solver**.
2. Set its **Offset** to **2** and set **Fade Mode** to **Multiply by Value**.
3. Right click on the **Value Solver's** **Value** attribute in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) and add a [Value Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/value/).
4. Set the **Value** on the **Value Behaviour** to **0.5**.
5. Add a [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/) to the **Value Behaviour**.
6. Make a [Polygon](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/).
7. Connect valueSolver.id→polygon.sides.
8. Select the **Polygon** and click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
9. Move the playhead forward so it's not on frame 0.
10. Move the Falloff around in the Viewport.

As the **Falloff** is moved over the Polygons, their number of sides increase and then return back to 2. As there's no such thing as a 2 sided polygon the shapes disappear. By setting the **Offset** on the **Value Solver** to **3** then the shapes become triangles (3 sided polygons) when outside of the Falloff.

In the example above, the colour is also being affected. To do this simply:

chunks.title: Value Solver
chunks.heading: Value Solver > Value Solver > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create another [Value Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/value/).
2. Connect valueSolver.id→value.value.
3. Connect value.id→polygon.materialColor.r.
4. Ramp up the **Strength** attribute on the **Value**.

In this example the **Value** is simply being used as a multiplier to set values that have a visible effect on a range of 0-255 (the red channel).

Example - Velocity

1. Create an [Ellipse](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/ellipse/).
2. In the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/), right click on the **Position** attribute and choose `Add Behaviour > Noise`.
3. Set the [Noise](/docs/nodes/behaviours/noise/)'s **Minimum** and **Maximum** to **-100**, **100**.
4. Create a **Value Solver**.
5. Set the Value Solver's **Mode** to **Velocity**.
6. Set the Value Solver's **Value** to **0.1**.
7. Set the Value Solver's **Offset** to **1**.
8. Connect valueSolver.id→ellipse.scale.x.
9. Connect ellipse.scale.x→ellipse.scale.y.
10. Play.

As the Ellipse increases in velocity, its Scale also increases.

chunks.title: Value
chunks.heading: Value > Value > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Value** - Set a value.

**Offset** - Add/subtract a value from the **Value**.

**Time Offset** - Set a value to offset any animation curves by. For example, if the **Position.X** of one Shape is connected to the Value's **Value**, the Time Offset can be used to delay the animation of another Shape when the Value's Id (output) is connected to the other Shape's **Position.X**. Negative values are backward in time.

chunks.title: Value2 Blend
chunks.heading: Value2 Blend > Value2 Blend > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**First** - This `X,Y` value will be output when **Strength** = 0.

**Second** -This `X,Y` value will be output when **Strength** = 100.

chunks.title: Value2 Solver
chunks.heading: Value2 Solver > Value2 Solver > Intro
chunks.text: Store the two dimensional values from previous frames in order to accumulate and/or fade them over time.

chunks.title: Value2
chunks.heading: Value2 > Value2 > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Value** - Set two dimensional values.

**Offset** - Add/subtract a value from the **Value**.

**Time Offset** - Set a value to offset any animation curves by. For example, if the **Position** of one **2D** Shape is connected to the Value2's **Value**, the Time Offset can be used to delay the animation of another Shape when the Value2's Id (output) is connected to the other Shape's **Position**. Negative values are backward in time.

info

The Id (output) connection on a Value2 is a vector and so can be used to make connections to the same data types. e.g. 2D position.

chunks.title: Value3 Blend
chunks.heading: Value3 Blend > Value3 Blend > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**First** - This `X,Y,Z` value will be output when **Strength** = 0.

**Second** -This `X,Y,Z` value will be output when **Strength** = 100.

chunks.title: Value3
chunks.heading: Value3 > Value3 > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Value** - Set three dimensional values.

**Offset** - Add/subtract a value from the **Value**.

**Time Offset** - Set a value to offset any animation curves by. For example, if the **Position** of one **2.5D** Shape is connected to the Value3's **Value**, the Time Offset can be used to delay the animation of another Shape when the Value3's Id (output) is connected to the other Shape's **Position**. Negative values are backward in time.

info

The Id (output) connection on a Value3 is a vector and so can be used to make connections to the same data types. e.g. 2.5D position.

chunks.title: Visibility Sequence
chunks.heading: Visibility Sequence > Visibility Sequence > Intro
chunks.text:
The **Visibility Sequence** Behaviour can be used to affect the visibility of [sub-meshes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) like a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) or [Text](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/). The visibility for each sub-mesh can be determined by setting a range. Any sub-meshes that fall outside the range will have their visibility set to off.

For example, when using a **Visibility Sequence** connected to a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) with a **Count** of 10, a **Start** value of **10%** would set the visibility of the first sub-mesh in the Duplicator to off (10% of 10 is 1 and so the first sub-mesh falls outside the range).

chunks.title: Visibility Sequence
chunks.heading: Visibility Sequence > Visibility Sequence > UI
chunks.text:
**Start** - Set a percentage to mark the start of the range.

**End** - Set a percentage to mark the end of the range.

**Travel** - Incrementally offset the range by one sub-mesh at a time.

**Always On** - Enter a comma separated list of Ids to always remain visible. Colons can also be used to set ranges - `1,3,5:8`

**Always Off** - Enter a comma separated list of Ids to always remain invisible. Colons can also be used to set ranges - `1,3,5:8`

**Invert** - Invert the resulting range so anything outside of the range is set to on.

Example

1. Hold `Option/Alt` and click the **Ellipse tool** to create an **Ellipse**.
2. With the **Ellipse** selected, click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
3. Set **Distribution** to **Linear**.
4. Set **Count** to **10**.
5. Set **Size** to **1000**.
6. Right click on the **Shape Visibility** attribute.
7. Choose **Add Behaviour > Visibility Sequence**.
8. Load the **Visibility Sequence** into the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).
9. Set **Start** to 50%.

The first 5 sub-meshes of the Duplicator will be hidden.

chunks.title: Voxelize
chunks.heading: Voxelize > Voxelize > Intro
chunks.text: Convert Shapes into voxels with control over their size and scale to create gaps.

chunks.title: Voxelize
chunks.heading: Voxelize > Voxelize > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Size** - Set the size of the voxel grid.

**Voxel Scale** - A multiplier for **Size**. Reducing this attribute will create gaps between voxels.

info

To place Shapes on voxels or move through a voxel grid then use the **Voxelize Distribution** on the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).

chunks.title: Wave
chunks.heading: Wave > Wave > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Mode** - Set the shape of the distortion:

* **Sine** - A smooth, undulating wave shape.
* **Square** - A hard edged, square shape.
* **Sawtooth** - A sharp shape similar to the teeth on a saw blade.
* **Triangle** - A triangular zigzag shape.

**Number of Waves** - Set the number of complete waves to create along/around the Path.

**Adaptive Wave Counts** - When checked, the number of waves adapts to each Contour's length to create a more even deformation.

**Amplitude** - Set the height of the waves.

**Travel** - Move the waves along/around the Path.

**Sample Points** - Increase/decrease the number of points used to create the effect. The higher the value the smoother the result.

**Output Béziers** - When checked, smooth curves are output even with a low **Sample Points** value.

chunks.title: Effects
chunks.heading: Effects > Effects
chunks.text:
Effects include [Filters](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/) and [Shaders](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/) which can be added to Shapes in order to adjust their appearance.

**Shaders** can be added to the materials (Fill and/or Stroke) of a Shape in order to generate gradients or patterns. They can be layered or stacked on top of one another and combined to create more complex effects.

**Filters** alter the existing materials of a Shape by changing the properties or positions of pixels.

Shaders and Filters can also be used in combination with each other.

Order of Operations

When combining Filters and Shaders, note that Shaders are added to a Shape's materials before a Filter is applied.

chunks.title: Filters
chunks.heading: Filters > Filters
chunks.text:
**Filters** alter the existing materials of a Shape by changing the properties or positions of pixels.

Filters can be connected to multiple Shapes. For example, a single [Drop Shadow Filter](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/drop-shadow-filter/) can be connected to multiple Shapes so that they all inherit the same appearance.

Example

1. Create an [Ellipse](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/ellipse/).
2. Open the Ellipse's **Fill** tab in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).
3. Right click in the **Shaders** input and choose `Add Shader > Gradient Shader`.
4. Open the Ellipse's **Shape** tab.
5. Click the `+` icon next to the **Filters** Attribute and choose [Halftone](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/halftone-filter/).

Vector vs Raster

Note that adding **Filters** to Shapes results in a rasterised 'image' in the Viewport. The underlying vector Shape is unaffected but the resulting render will be anti-aliased. This should only really be noticeable when zooming into the Viewport.

chunks.title: Background Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Background Blur Filter > Background Blur Filter > Intro
chunks.text: A **Background Blur Filter** blurs the areas of a Shape that sit within another Shape. It can be used to soften or take focus away from background elements – a common effect used in UI design for interactive menus.

chunks.title: Background Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Background Blur Filter > Background Blur Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Blur Amount** - Set the amount of blur (px) to apply to the Shape.

**Blur Shape** - Connect a Shape to define the areas the blur is applied to.

Example

1. Create 2 Shapes (Shape1 and Shape2).
2. Move them apart slightly so one overlaps the other.
3. Load **Shape1** into the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/), click the `+` button on the **Filters** attribute and select **Background Blur**.
4. Connect **Shape2** as the **Blur Shape** to the Background Blur.
5. Set Shape2's **Opacity** to **10%**.

---

chunks.title: Bilateral Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Bilateral Blur Filter > Bilateral Blur Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Add an edge-preserving blur that smooths areas of similar color while maintaining sharp edges.

This can be used for several tasks including noise reduction, skin smoothing and pre-processing for edge detection.

Photo by Milin John on Unsplash

chunks.title: Bilateral Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Bilateral Blur Filter > Bilateral Blur Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Amount** - Set the amount of blur in pixels to apply to the Shape.

**Edge Threshold** - Set edge detection sensitivity. A lower value will preserve more edges.

**Color Tolerance** - Combine similar colors within a tolerance. A higher value will result in a wider range of colours being combined.

---

chunks.title: Black and White Filter
chunks.heading: Black and White Filter > Black and White Filter > UI
chunks.text:
Move the six colour sliders right or left to brighten or darken the respective tones of the Shape. For example, moving the **Reds** slider to 0 will move any of the red tones in the image towards black.

**Reds** - Brighten or darken the red tones.

**Yellows** - Brighten or darken the yellow tones.

**Greens** - Brighten or darken the green tones.

**Cyans** - Brighten or darken the cyan tones.

**Blues** - Brighten or darken the blue tones.

**Magentas** - Brighten or darken the magenta tones.

chunks.title: Box Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Box Blur Filter > Box Blur Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Add a fast box blur to Shapes and Shaders. This is a good blur for Scenes where playback speed is a priority.

Photo by charlesdeluvio on Unsplash

chunks.title: Box Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Box Blur Filter > Box Blur Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Amount** - Set the amount of blur in pixels to apply to the Shape.

---

See other blur Filters:

[Background Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/background-blur-filter/)
[Bilateral Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/bilateral-blur-filter/)

[Directional Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/directional-blur-filter/)
