[Luminance Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/luminance-blur-filter/)
[Zoom Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/zoom-blur-filter/)

chunks.title: Brightness and Contrast Filter
chunks.heading: Brightness and Contrast Filter > Brightness and Contrast Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Brightness** - A larger value increases the highlights while a smaller value will increase the shadows.

**Contrast** - Expand/shrink the overall tonal range.

chunks.title: Bulge Filter
chunks.heading: Bulge Filter > Bulge Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Distort a Shape by wrapping it onto a spherical surface, creating a bulge or pinch effect.

Photo by Sergey Shmidt on Unsplash

chunks.title: Bulge Filter
chunks.heading: Bulge Filter > Bulge Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Sampling Quality** - Controls how the image is sampled/interpolated. The options can be thought of as low to high quality from top to bottom and can be useful when working with fine details like text.

* **Nearest Neighbour** – Uses the closest pixel without blending.
* **Bilinear** – Blends between nearby pixels for smoother results. Good for general image scaling but can introduce a softness/blur.
* **Catmull–Rom** – A high-quality resampling method that produces sharper results and preserves fine detail.
* **Mitchell** – Balanced high-quality filtering.

**Passthrough Background** - When checked, the background outside the bulge's sphere will be rendered when **Blend Mode** is set to **Replace**.

**Amount** - Determine the strength of the spherical distortion where positive values create a bulge effect and negative values create a pinch effect.

**Centre** - Set the centre point of the spherical effect in pixels where 0,0 is the centre of the image.

**Radius** - Set the radius of the spherical effect as a percentage of the Shape's size.

chunks.title: Bulge Filter
chunks.heading: Bulge Filter > Bulge Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Refraction** - When unchecked, the effect becomes a simple height-map distortion without optical effects.

**Refractive Index** - Set the material's refractive index to control how much light bends. Common values include 1.33 (water), 1.5 (glass) and 2.5 (diamond).

**Chromatic Aberration** - When **Refraction** is checked, set the amount of color separation in pixels at the sphere's edges to simulate light dispersion through glass.

chunks.title: Chroma Key Filter
chunks.heading: Chroma Key Filter > Chroma Key Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Remove green/blue screen from video/images with advanced matte controls.

Photo by Ben Collins on Unsplash

chunks.title: Chroma Key Filter
chunks.heading: Chroma Key Filter > Chroma Key Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**View** - Select what to render in the Viewport:

* **Final Result** - The composited result with transparency.
* **Source** - Original unprocessed image.
* **Alpha** - The transparency channel in grayscale.
* **Status** - A diagnostic view where red = transparent, green = opaque and yellow = edges.

**Screen Color** - The color to become transparent (usually green or blue background). Use the Color Picker to select a colour from the image. Solid black will result in no key.

**Screen Gain** - Control how aggressively colors are keyed. Higher values remove more background.

**Screen Balance** - Adjust the color saturation measurement. 0.0 = use the maximum of other channels, 0.5 = use the average (green screens), 1.0 = use the minimum (blue screens).

---

**Shadow Tolerance** - Determine how much darker variations of the screen color can be to be included in the matte. This is useful for removing shadows cast on the background.

**Shadow Softness** - Control the transition between areas in and out of shadow. A higher value will create a smoother transition.

---

chunks.title: Chroma Key Filter
chunks.heading: Chroma Key Filter > Chroma Key Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Alpha Bias** - Adjust bias to reduce foreground/subject transparency. Use the Color Picker to select a colour from the image.

**Use Alpha Bias for Despill** - When checked, the 'Alpha Bias' color is used to affect despill calculations.

**Despill Bias** - Remove color spill from the edges of the matte. Picking hair or skin tones will often produce the best results.

**Despill Strength** - Control the overall strength of the despill. Use lower values for subtle despill or higher values for aggressive removal.

---

**Pre-Blur** - Blur the input image before keying to reduce any noise/grain. This does not affect the output.

**Detail Recovery** - Recover fine details like hair strands that may have been incorrectly keyed out. Uses edge detection and color analysis to identify areas that should remain opaque where 0 = no recovery and 1 = maximum recovery.

**Edge Softness** - Control the softness of the matte's edges where 0 = hard edges and 1 = very soft edges to help create a smoother transition between opaque and transparent pixels.

---

**Clip Black** - Set the transparency cutoff. Matte values below this value become fully transparent. Use carefully to avoid hard edges.

chunks.title: Chroma Key Filter
chunks.heading: Chroma Key Filter > Chroma Key Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Clip White** - Set the opacity cutoff. Matte values above this value become fully opaque. Use carefully to avoid hard edges.

**Clip Rollback** - Soften the effect of clipping by restoring some edge detail. Higher values restore more of the original matte.

**Screen Dilate** - Grow or shrink the matte's edges. Use sparingly as too much erosion can produce poor mattes.

**Screen Softness** - Blur the matte's edges for smoother compositing. This only affects edges and not solid areas. Small values are recommended.

---

**Despot Black** - Remove isolated transparent spots in opaque areas to clean up any small holes that may appear within the foreground/subject.

**Despot White** - Remove isolated opaque spots in transparent areas to clean up any small holes that may appear within the background.

---

**Screen Replace** - Determine the method for how colors in the foreground/subject are replaced when using 'Despill' for advanced color correction.

**Replace Color** - Set the color used to replace any color spill in foreground/subject. Set to dominant foreground/subject colors like skin or fabric for best results.

---

chunks.title: Chroma Key Filter
chunks.heading: Chroma Key Filter > Chroma Key Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Shadow Gain** - Adjust the matte's contrast in dark areas. Higher values make shadows more opaque.

**Midtones Gain** - Adjust the matte's contrast in mid-range areas. Higher values improve edge definition.

**Highlights Gain** - Adjust the matte's contrast in bright areas. Higher values make highlights more opaque.

chunks.title: Chromatic Aberration Filter
chunks.heading: Chromatic Aberration Filter > Chromatic Aberration Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Chromatic aberration is a real world phenomenon in which light rays passing through a lens focus at different points depending on their wavelength. The result is a separation of colours at the edges of an image.

Photo by Honza Reznik on Unsplash

chunks.title: Chromatic Aberration Filter
chunks.heading: Chromatic Aberration Filter > Chromatic Aberration Filter > UI
chunks.text:
* Settings* Colors

**Strength** - Increase/ decrease the strength of the effect.

**Lens Type** - Select the lens:

* **Concave** - Use a concave lens.
* **Fisheye/ Barrel Distortion** - Use a fisheye lens.

**Padding** - Increase/ decrease the bounds of the original image.

**Alignment X** - Set the x position for the centre of the lens.

**Alignment Y** - Set the y position for the centre of the lens.

**Scale** - Increase/ decrease the scale of the effect.

**Repetitions** - Set the number of times the effect of the Filter is processed.

**Repetition Distance** - Set the distance between the first and last of the repetitions.

**Rotation** - Rotate each repetition.

**Distortion Radius** - Set a radius to determine where the simulated lens distortion occurs.

**Red Channel** - Set the color used in the red channel.

**Green Channel** - Set the color used in the green channel.

**Blue Channel** - Set the color used in the blue channel.

**Red Channel Offset** - Set the strength of the distortion for the red channel.

**Green Channel Offset** - Set the strength of the distortion for the green channel.

chunks.title: Chromatic Aberration Filter
chunks.heading: Chromatic Aberration Filter > Chromatic Aberration Filter > UI
chunks.text: **Blue Channel Offset** - Set the strength of the distortion for the blue channel.

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Filters)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Filters) > Common Attributes (Filters) > UI
chunks.text:
* Filter* Mattes

**Blend Mode** - Set the [blend mode](/docs/nodes/general/blend-modes/) for the Filter. Note that, where multiple Filters are connected to a Shape, this blend mode affects how Filters blend with each other and not how Shapes blend with other Shapes in the Viewport — use the **Blend Mode** under a Shape's **Shape** tab to affect that.

**Opacity** - Reduce/increase the effect of the Filter.

**Sample/Greyscale/Sort Mode** - Determine how the Shader is sampled:

* **Luma (Gamma Corrected)** - Sample the gamma corrected average brightness values.
* **Average** - Sample the average brightness values. This is a fast calculation.
* **Saturation** - Sample the saturation values.
* **Value** - Use the brightest of the R, G or B values and apply its value to the lower two. For example, if the red channel has a value of 0.8 and that value is higher than the blue and green channels, then set the blue and green to 0.8 too.
* **Red Channel** - Sample the values held in the red channel.
* **Blue Channel** - Sample the values held in the blue channel.
* **Green Channel** - Sample the values held in the green channel.

**Mattes** - A list of Shapes used as mattes for the Filter.

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Filters)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Filters) > Common Attributes (Filters) > UI
chunks.text:
Settings for each matte can be accessed via the  icon on the matte's row.

* **Matte Shape** - The input connection from the Shape.
* **Enabled** - Enable/disable the matte.
* **Mode** - Determine how the Shape's luminance or alpha is used:
  + **Luminance** - Use the luminance of the Shape where white pixels will remove the filter entirely and black pixels will have no effect.
  + **Luminance Inverted** - The inverse of the above.
  + **Alpha** - Use the opacity of the Shape where opaque pixels will remove the filter entirely and transparent pixels will have no effect.
  + **Alpha Inverted** - The inverse of the above.
* **Blend Mode** - Choose a [Blend Mode](/docs/nodes/general/blend-modes/) for the matte.
* **Opacity** - Reducing this value will reduce the effect of the matte.
* **Feather** - Soften the edges of a matte.

**Tile Mode** - Determine what happens at the borders of the matte:

* **Clamp** - Use the first and last values of the image.
* **Repeat** - Repeat/loop the image.
* **Decal** - Cut out the image.

**Apply Mode** - Determine how the matte affects the Filter's result:

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Filters)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Filters) > Common Attributes (Filters) > UI
chunks.text:
* **Filter Input** - Only the pixels inside the matte(s) are filtered. In the case of a Blur, this will create a softer edge. This can be more performant than 'Filter Input' as only the pixels inside the matte(s) are filtered.
* **Clip Output** - All pixels are filtered and then the result is clipped by the matte(s). This results in a sharp edge at the borders of the matte (unless a **Feather** is added).

chunks.title: Directional Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Directional Blur Filter > Directional Blur Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Blur a Shape along an axis to create a streaking effect or simulate motion blur.

Photo by Xingye Jiang on Unsplash

chunks.title: Directional Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Directional Blur Filter > Directional Blur Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Angle** - Set the direction of the blur in degrees.

**Blur Amount** - Set the distance/strength of the directional blur effect. Higher values create more pronounced blur streaks.

---

See other blur Filters:

[Background Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/background-blur-filter/)
[Bilateral Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/bilateral-blur-filter/)
[Fast Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/fast-blur-filter/)
[Box Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/box-blur-filter/)
[Gaussian Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/gaussian-blur-filter/)
[Luminance Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/luminance-blur-filter/)
[Zoom Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/zoom-blur-filter/)

chunks.title: Distort Edges Filter
chunks.heading: Distort Edges Filter > Distort Edges Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

* Filter* Shader

**Border** - Distortion width in pixels.

**Amplitude** - The maximum a pixel can be displaced.

**Edge Sharpness** - Control how the distortion blends into the Shape.

**Direction** -

* **Both** - Push pixels inside and outside a Shape.
* **Outward** - Only push pixels towards the outside a Shape.
* **Inward** - Only push pixels towards the inside a Shape.

**Show Preview** - Preview the Input Shader in the Viewport along the Shape's border.

**Preview Opacity** - Set the opacity of the preview.

**Input Shader** - Select a Shader to use for the distortion.

chunks.title: Distortion Filter
chunks.heading: Distortion Filter > Distortion Filter > UI
chunks.text:
* Settings* Shader

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Amplitude** - Determine the strength of the distortion.

**Sample Mode** - Determine how the **Input Shader** is sampled. See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/).

**Invert** - Reverse the values of the **Input Shader** — values of `0-1` are inverted to `1-0`.

**Direction Mode** - Set the type of distortion:

* **Lens** - Push the pixel coordinates towards or away from the centre. Values above 0.5 will move away from the centre, values below 0.5 will move towards the centre.
* **Directional** - Push the pixel coordinates along a direction specified by the **Direction Angle**. Values above 0.5 will move along the Direction Angle, values below 0.5 will move in the opposite direction. e.g. the `Direction Angle - 180`.
* **Warp** - Push the the pixel coordinates in an direction where a pixel's value is remapped to a direction. Values of 0-1 are remapped to angles of 0˚-360˚.

**Curve Interpolation** - Determine how values from the Distortion Shader are remapped (only active when **Direction Mode** is set to **Lens**):

chunks.title: Distortion Filter
chunks.heading: Distortion Filter > Distortion Filter > UI
chunks.text:
* **Sine Wave** - Use sine wave (s-curve) remapping. This will create a smoother distortion.
* **Linear** - Use linear remapping.

**Distortion Offset** - Increase/ decrease the distortion. Note - not applicable when the **Direction Mode** is set to **Warp**.

**Automatic Padding** - Automatically adjust the bounding box of the Shape based on the result of the distortion. Note - only applicable when the **Direction Mode** is set to **Directional** or **Warp**.

**Padding** - Manually adjust the bounding box of the Shape to show/ clip the result of the distortion.

**Direction Angle** - Set the angle for the **Directional** Direction Mode.

**Use Single Direction** - Push pixels in one direction when the **Direction Mode** is set to **Directional**. All values above 0 will be moved along the **Direction Angle**.

**Show Preview** - Show a preview of the **Input Shader** in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

**Preview Opacity** - Increase/ decrease the opacity of the **Input Shader** preview.

**Input Shader** - Select a Shader to drive the distortion.

chunks.title: Dithering Filter
chunks.heading: Dithering Filter > Dithering Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Dithering is an image processing operation used to create the illusion of color depth in images with a limited color palette. Colors not available in the palette are approximated by a diffusion of colored pixels from within the available palette.

Photo by Joe Ng on Unsplash

chunks.title: Dithering Filter
chunks.heading: Dithering Filter > Dithering Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Mode** - Select a dithering mode:

* **Blend** - Generate half of the pattern using the color's bit depth.
* **Classic** - Uses a dithering algorithm where colors are either 1 or 0.
* **Grayscale** - The brightness of the image/Shape is used.

**Greyscale Mode** - Determine how the image/Shape is sampled. See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/).

**Bit Depth** - Determine the resulting bit depth.

**Size** - The size of the resulting dithered 'pixels'.

**Pattern** - Set the type of dithering pattern to apply:

* **Bayer** - Produces a very distinctive cross-hatch pattern.
* **Bricks** - Produces a brick like pattern.
* **Stripes** - Produces a striped pattern.
* **Bubbles** - Produces a bubble pattern.
* **Virus** - Produces an abstract pattern.
* **Blue Noise** - Produces a pattern based on blue noise.
* **White Noise** - Produces a pattern based on noise.
* **Custom** - Use a **Shader** to create a custom pattern.

**Shader** - Add/connect a custom Shader.

**Contrast** - Increase/decrease contrast to affect how gradually the pattern changes.

**Bias** - Adjust the dithering to affect darker or brighter areas of the Shape.

chunks.title: Drop Shadow
chunks.heading: Drop Shadow > Drop Shadow > UI
chunks.text:
**Blur Amount** - Set the amount of blur for the shadow [x,y].

**Offset** - Set a position offset for the shadow [x,y].

**Rotation** - Rotate the drop shadow around the centre of the Shape.

**Color** - Set the drop shadow's color using hex or rgb values (note - only rgb values can be animated).

chunks.title: Edge Detection Filter
chunks.heading: Edge Detection Filter > Edge Detection Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Convert the boundaries of colors within images to lines.

Photo by Dong Cheng on Unsplash

chunks.title: Edge Detection Filter
chunks.heading: Edge Detection Filter > Edge Detection Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Line Color** - Set the color for the resulting lines.

**Sample Spacing** - Set the width used to detect the edges.

**Background Color** - Set the color for the resulting background.

**Detection Algorithm** - Select the edge detection method:

* **Sobel** - Samples the image for edges and creates lines based on the intensity of each edge. Sobel is a more approximate algorithm so is faster to compute.
* **Canny** - Iterates on the Sobel algorithm and can be used to create a cleaner, more uniform result.

**Greyscale Mode** - Determine how the image is sampled. See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/).

**Threshold** - Remove the weaker edges found by the Filter.

**De-noise Level** - Blur the image to smooth out detail.

**Step Lines** - When checked, the smooth/soft default result for edges in removed.

chunks.title: Erosion Filter
chunks.heading: Erosion Filter > Erosion Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Amount** - Set the erosion amount in pixels.

**Direction Mode** - Determine the direction of the erosion:

* **Uniform** - Erode in all directions
* **Directional** - Erode along a specific **Angle**.

**Angle** - Set the angle for **Directional** erosion.

**Direction Strength** - Determine the bias toward the specified **Angle**.

chunks.title: Fast Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Fast Blur Filter > Fast Blur Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Add blur to Shapes and Shaders. This is a good blur for Scenes where playback speed is a priority. Where a higher quality blur is required, see the [Gaussian Blur](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/gaussian-blur-filter/).

Photo by DARKROOMLABS on Unsplash

chunks.title: Fast Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Fast Blur Filter > Fast Blur Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Amount** - Set the amount of blur (px) to apply to the Shape.

---

See other blur Filters:

[Background Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/background-blur-filter/)
[Bilateral Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/bilateral-blur-filter/)
[Box Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/box-blur-filter/)
[Directional Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/directional-blur-filter/)
[Gaussian Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/gaussian-blur-filter/)
[Luminance Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/luminance-blur-filter/)
[Zoom Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/zoom-blur-filter/)

chunks.title: Fill Color Filter
chunks.heading: Fill Color Filter > Fill Color Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Blend Mode** - See [Blend Modes](/docs/nodes/general/blend-modes/).

**Color** - Set the color using Hex, RGB or HSV values.

**Premultiply** - When checked, the calculation for transparent pixels is premultiplied.

info

Animating color is only directly possible for RGB values. If HSV is required then connect an [HSV Color Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/hsv-color/) to the **Color**.

chunks.title: Gamma Correction Filter
chunks.heading: Gamma Correction Filter > Gamma Correction Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Premultiply** - When checked, the calculation for transparent pixels is premultiplied.

**Gamma Value** - The gamma curve is calculated as output=inputgammaValueoutput = input^{gammaValue}output=inputgammaValue. The default **Gamma Value** of 2.2 delivers a balanced or ‘neutral’ tone between highlights and shadows.

chunks.title: Gaussian Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Gaussian Blur Filter > Gaussian Blur Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Add high-quality Gaussian blur to Shapes and Shaders. This is very similar to the [Blur Filter](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/fast-blur-filter/) but produces higher quality results.

Photo by untldshots on Unsplash

chunks.title: Gaussian Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Gaussian Blur Filter > Gaussian Blur Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Amount** - Set the amount of blur in pixels to apply to the Shape.

---

See other blur Filters:

[Background Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/background-blur-filter/)
[Bilateral Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/bilateral-blur-filter/)
[Fast Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/fast-blur-filter/)
[Box Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/box-blur-filter/)
[Directional Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/directional-blur-filter/)
[Luminance Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/luminance-blur-filter/)
[Zoom Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/zoom-blur-filter/)

chunks.title: Glow Filter
chunks.heading: Glow Filter > Glow Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Add a glow effect to a Shape with optional granular controls for individual RGB channels.

Photo by Juan Felipe on Unsplash

chunks.title: Glow Filter
chunks.heading: Glow Filter > Glow Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Blend Mode** - Determine how the Filter blends with the Shape. See [Blend Modes](/docs/nodes/general/blend-modes/).

**Mode** - Determine how the color channels are affected:

* **Simple Controls** - Settings affect all the color channels together.
* **Individual Channel Controls** - Affect each color channel individually.

**Glow Radius** - Set how far the glow extends from the Shape.

**Intensity** - Increase/decrease the intensity of the glow.

**Red Glow Radius** - Set how far the glow in the red channel extends from the Shape.

**Green Glow Radius** - Set how far the glow in the green channel extends from the Shape.

**Blue Glow Radius** - Set how far the glow in the blue channel extends from the Shape.

**Intensity RGB** - Increase/decrease the intensity of the glow for the red/green/blue channels.

**Glow Tint** - Set a color to multiply the input glow values with.

**Source Gamma** - Set a threshold to adjust the luminance values of the Glow's input using an inverse gamma adjustment. Decrease this value to restrict the Glow to the brighter values of the source image. The **Draw Mode** set to **Glow Input** can be used to preview the resulting input.

chunks.title: Glow Filter
chunks.heading: Glow Filter > Glow Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Source White Point** - Adjust the Glow input’s white point. A value of `0.5` will result in all luminance values greater than `0.5` being set to white.

**Draw Mode** - Set the draw mode:

* **Result** - Output the resulting glow.
* **Glow Input** - Display a preview of any **Gamma** and **White Point** adjustments to the source image.

chunks.title: Gradient Map Filter
chunks.heading: Gradient Map Filter > Gradient Map Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Generate a gradient based on the brightness of an input.

The Shape's tonal range (from dark to light) is mapped to the gradient's colors (from left to right).

Photo by Brandon Romanchuk on Unsplash

chunks.title: Gradient Map Filter
chunks.heading: Gradient Map Filter > Gradient Map Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Reverse** - Reverse the direction of the **Gradient**.

**Premultiply** - When checked, the calculation for transparent pixels is premultiplied.

**Gradient Mode** - Select an interpolation for the **Gradient**. See [Gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/).

**Gradient** - Set the color stops for the [gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/).

chunks.title: Grain Filter
chunks.heading: Grain Filter > Grain Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Add a fine grain to emulate the visual appearance of film stock.

Photo by Alex Shuper on Unsplash

chunks.title: Grain Filter
chunks.heading: Grain Filter > Grain Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Grain Type** - Determine if the grain is colorised or black and white:

* **Color** - Set individual grain values for each color channel.
* **Monochrome** - Create uniform grain across all color channels.

**Grain Amount** - When **Grain Type** is set to **Monochrome**, determine how much grain to apply to the image. Higher values create a more visible noise texture.

**Size** - When **Grain Type** is set to **Monochrome**, determine the size of the grain. Larger values will create coarser noise.

**Red Amount** - When **Grain Type** is set to **Color**, set the amount of grain in the red channel. Use for color-specific noise control.

**Green Amount** - When **Grain Type** is set to **Color**, set the amount of grain in the green channel. Use for color-specific noise control.

**Blue Amount** - When **Grain Type** is set to **Color**, set the amount of grain in the blue channel. Use for color-specific noise control.

**Red Size** - When **Grain Type** is set to **Color**, set the size of grain in the red channel. Use for per-channel grain size variation.

chunks.title: Grain Filter
chunks.heading: Grain Filter > Grain Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Green Size** - When **Grain Type** is set to **Color**, set the size of grain in the green channel. Use for per-channel grain size variation.

**Blue Size** - When **Grain Type** is set to **Color**, set the size of grain in the blue channel. Use for per-channel grain size variation.

---

**Log Grain** - Control the color space in which the grain is generated. 'Log' space will create more film-like grain characteristics.

**Texture** - Determine how much of the original image influences grain placement. Higher values make the grain follow the image structure.

---

**Sharpen** - Sharpen the image before the noise is added. Higher values create more defined edges and details.

**Sharpen Edges Only** - When checked, sharpening is only applied to image regions with a sharp contrast between light and dark areas.

---

**Highlight** - Set how much grain appears in image highlights. Lower values reduce grain in bright areas.

**Midtone** - Set how much grain appears in image midtones. Controls grain in the middle luminance range.

**Shadow** - Set how much grain appears in image shadows. Higher values add more grain to dark areas.

---

chunks.title: Grain Filter
chunks.heading: Grain Filter > Grain Filter > UI
chunks.text: **Time** - By default, this is connected to the Composition's Time. Remove this connection to prevent the grain from evolving during playback.

chunks.title: Halftone Filter
chunks.heading: Halftone Filter > Halftone Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Halftone is a reprographic technique that simulates continuous-tone imagery through the use of dots, varying in size to generate a gradient-like effect.

Photo by Chandri Anggara on Unsplash

chunks.title: Halftone Filter
chunks.heading: Halftone Filter > Halftone Filter > UI
chunks.text:
* Settings* Colors

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Pattern** - Set a style for the Halftone:

* **Classic** - Simple dots.
* **Ink** - Dots that 'bleed' into each other.
* **Strokes** - Lines that increase/decrease in width.
* **Quads** - Square/diamond shapes.

**Size** - Increase/ decrease the size of the pattern.

**Offset** - Add/subtract a value to the Filter's position.

**Rotation** - Rotate the effect.

**Sample Mode** - Determine how color values are sampled.

* **Luma (Gamma Corrected)** - Output the weighted sum of the gamma-corrected RGB values.
* **Brightness** - Output the mean of the RGB values.

**Red Multiplier** - Increase/ decrease the values in the red channel of the pattern (when **Use CMYK** is unchecked).

**Green Multiplier** - Increase/ decrease the values in the green channel of the pattern (when **Use CMYK** is unchecked).

**Blue Multiplier** - Increase/ decrease the values in the blue channel of the pattern (when **Use CMYK** is unchecked).

**Contrast** - Increase/decrease contrast to affect how gradually the size of the pattern changes across the Shape.

chunks.title: Halftone Filter
chunks.heading: Halftone Filter > Halftone Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Threshold** - Increase/decrease the threshold used to determine the size of the pattern. A value of 1 (default) will mean a dot will fill a white area with a full circle and black area with the background.

**Softness** - Set how soft the edge is for the pattern.

**Use CMYK** - When checked, Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and Black dots are used to represent the colours in the image. This is a representation of CMYK colors rather than any true color space conversion.

CMYK

**CMYK** or Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and Key (Black) are colours used in print where the white of the paper is used for brighter. This results in smaller dots being used to represent lighter parts of the image which is the inverse to the way the halftone is calculated in RGB mode (when **Use CMYK** is unchecked).

**Black Gamma** -

**Foreground Color** - Select a color for the circles when in RGB mode (when **Use CMYK** is unchecked).

**Background Color** - Select a color for the background.

**Cyan** - Set a color to be used for the cyan channel.

**Cyan Transform** - Offset the position and rotation of the cyan pattern.

**Magenta** - Set a color to be used for the magenta channel.

chunks.title: Halftone Filter
chunks.heading: Halftone Filter > Halftone Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Magenta Transform** - Offset the position and rotation of the magenta pattern.

**Yellow** - Set a color to be used for the yellow channel.

**Yellow Transform** - Offset the position and rotation of the yellow pattern.

**Black** - Set a color to be used for the black (key) channel.

**Black Transform** - Offset the position and rotation of the black (key) pattern.

Legacy Scenes

Scenes using the **Halftone Filter** created in a version before **Cavalry 1.5** will open using the legacy version of this Filter. It's recommended to replace the Filter with the new one if possible. Be aware that they are not 100% like-for-like so may not be a perfect match.

chunks.title: HSV Adjustment Filter
chunks.heading: HSV Adjustment Filter > HSV Adjustment Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Adjust the Hue, Saturation and Value of a Shape.

Photo by Kirill Petropavlov on Unsplash

chunks.title: HSV Adjustment Filter
chunks.heading: HSV Adjustment Filter > HSV Adjustment Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Hue** - Shift the hues of the Shape around the colour wheel.

**Saturation** - Increase/decrease the saturation of the Shape.

**Legacy Saturation** - When checked, the Shape's saturation is multiplied by the **Saturation** attribute to give a more intense result.

**Value** - Set the lightness of the Shape.

**HSL** - When checked, Hue, Saturation and Value is converted to Hue, Saturation and Lightness. The **Value** attribute above is used to set the Lightness value instead.

chunks.title: Inner Shadow Filter
chunks.heading: Inner Shadow Filter > Inner Shadow Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Blur Amount** - Set the amount of blur for the shadow.

**Offset** - Offset the position of the shadow.

**Spread** - Expand or contract the shadow. Note that this uses a morphological technique which provides real-time performance but may result in slight inaccuracies for certain Shapes, particularly when a low **Blur Amount** is used.

**Color** - Set the color for the shadow.

chunks.title: Invert Filter
chunks.heading: Invert Filter > Invert Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Channel** - Select a channel to invert.

* **RGB** - Invert all channels.
* **Red** - Invert the red channel.
* **Green** - Invert the green channel.
* **Blue** - Invert the blue channel.
* **Alpha** - Invert the alpha channel.

**Skip Transparent** - When checked and **Channel** is set to **Alpha**, transparent pixels outside of the shape (excluding around the edges of the image) are not affected.

**Preserve Edges** - Clean up the alpha contained within anti-aliased edges.

chunks.title: Levels Filter
chunks.heading: Levels Filter > Levels Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Remap the black and white levels of a Layer to correct its tonal range and color balance.

Photo by Nahil Naseer on Unsplash

chunks.title: Levels Filter
chunks.heading: Levels Filter > Levels Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Histogram** - Displays an analysis of the Layer. The **Channel** can be used to filter which channels are displayed.

Multiple Layers

Like any other [Filter](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/), the **Levels Filter** can be connected to more than one Layer. In this situation, the histogram will display the levels for the 'highest Layer in the stack'. For example, with two Shapes in a Composition connected to the same **Levels Filter**, the histogram will display the levels for the Shape **above** the other in the layer stack.

Toggle the visibility of the Layers on top to display the histogram for Layers below.

**Channel** - Select a channel to affect:

* **RGB** - Affect all channels.
* **Red** - Only affect the red channel.
* **Green** - Only affect the green channel.
* **Blue** - Only affect the blue channel.
* **Alpha** - Only affect the alpha channel.

**In Black** - Any input values below this value are considered to be black and remapped to the **Out Black** level.

**In White** - Any input values above this value are considered to be white and remapped to the **Out White** level.

**Out Black** - Set the output black level.

**Out White** - Set the output white level.

chunks.title: Levels Filter
chunks.heading: Levels Filter > Levels Filter > UI
chunks.text: **Gamma** - Set the gamma correction applied to the input values where values greater/less than `1` will darken/lighten a Layer.

chunks.title: Light Sweep Filter
chunks.heading: Light Sweep Filter > Light Sweep Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Simulate a light source moving over a Layer.

Photo by Tomáš Pokorný on Unsplash

chunks.title: Light Sweep Filter
chunks.heading: Light Sweep Filter > Light Sweep Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Sweep Intensity** - Set the light's brightness.

**Direction** - Set the angle the sweep moves across a Layer in degrees.

**Shape** - Select a shape for the sweep.

**Centre** - Set the light sweep's centre point.

**Cone Width** - Set the width of the light beam.

**Centre Percentage** - Set a percentage of the cone's width that remains fully lit.

**Use Falloff** - When the Shape is set to Line, limit the light sweep's distance from the Centre along its Y axis.

**Falloff Distance** - Set the distance over which the light falls off after passing the Centre.

**Edge Intensity** - Set the intensity of an additional glow at the edges of the light sweep.

**Edge Thickness** - When **Edge Intensity** is greater than 0, set the thickness of the light sweep's edges.

**Light Color** - Set the color of the light.

chunks.title: Linear Wipe
chunks.heading: Linear Wipe > Linear Wipe > UI
chunks.text:
**Completion** - Set a percentage for how complete the wipe is.

**Rotation** - Set the angle of the wipe.

**Screen Space** - When checked the wipe is based on the composition rather than local to the Shape.

chunks.title: Luminance Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Luminance Blur Filter > Luminance Blur Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Blur one Layer based on the luminance values of another. For example, a [Gradient Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/gradient-shader/) from one Shape can be used to drive the blur amount of another.

Photo by Andrea Cau on Unsplash

chunks.title: Luminance Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Luminance Blur Filter > Luminance Blur Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Input Shape** - Connect a Shape to sample the luminance from.

**Maximum Blur** - Set the amount of blur where luminance is 1 (white).

**Minimum Blur** - Set the amount of blur where luminance is 0 (black).

**Invert Luminance** - Invert the luminance of the **Input Shape**.

**View Mode** - Select the view rendered to the Viewport:

* **Final Result** - Show the resulting blur.
* **Luminance** - Preview the luminance values.

Example

1. Create a Rectangle (Rectangle 1).
2. Set its **Size** to `300,200`.
3. In the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/), click the `+` button on Rectangle 1's **Filters** attribute and choose **Luminance Blur**.
4. Create a second Rectangle (Rectangle 2).
5. Set its **Size** to `500,500`.
6. Load **Rectangle 2**'s **Fill** tab, click Shader and choose [Gradient Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/gradient-shader/) from the list.
7. Hide **Rectangle 2**.
8. Connect rectangle2.id→luminanceBlur.inputShape.
9. Increase the **Luminance Blur**'s **Maximum Blur**.

chunks.title: Luminance Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Luminance Blur Filter > Luminance Blur Filter > UI
chunks.text:
Try rotating **Rectangle 2** or select the [Gradient Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/gradient-shader/) and then use its [layer tool](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/gradient-shader/#layer-tools) to adjust the gradient in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

---

See other blur Filters:

[Background Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/background-blur-filter/)
[Bilateral Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/bilateral-blur-filter/)
[Fast Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/fast-blur-filter/)
[Box Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/box-blur-filter/)
[Directional Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/directional-blur-filter/)
[Gaussian Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/gaussian-blur-filter/)
[Zoom Blur Filter→](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/zoom-blur-filter/)

chunks.title: Mirror Filter
chunks.heading: Mirror Filter > Mirror Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Reverse a Shape along a centre line to create a reflection.

Photo by Terrillo Walls on Unsplash

chunks.title: Mirror Filter
chunks.heading: Mirror Filter > Mirror Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Tiling** - Determine what happens at the borders of the image.

* **Decal** - Do not wrap the image.
* **Repeat** - Repeat the image.

**Offset** - Set the position of the mirror's centre line.

**Rotation** - Set the angle of the mirror’s orientation.

**Padding** - Increase/decrease the boundary of the result.

info

Mirror uses the **Persist Opacity** Blend Mode as its default. This removes the original Shape on the reflected side of the mirror's centre line.

chunks.title: Mirror Filter
chunks.heading: Mirror Filter > Mirror Filter > UI > Layer Tool
chunks.text:
Certain attributes can be manipulated in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) with the [Select tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/). When the **Mirror Filter** is selected in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/), a purple UI will appear in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

* To **Offset** the Mirror's centre line, click + drag the white dot in the centre of the purple line.
* To set the **Rotation** of the Mirror's centre line, click + drag the white dot offset from the centre of the purple line.

info

If the same **Mirror Filter** is connected to multiple Shapes/ outputs, then the first connection is used to position the purple UI in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/). This can be identified by clicking the purple output connection icon for the **Mirror Filter** in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) or [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) and picking the bottom layer in the list that appears.

info

chunks.title: Mirror Filter
chunks.heading: Mirror Filter > Mirror Filter > UI > Layer Tool
chunks.text: Note that Viewport tools will not appear if a Mirror Filter is added to a Sub-Mesh Behaviour.

chunks.title: Pixel Sorting Filter
chunks.heading: Pixel Sorting Filter > Pixel Sorting Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Reorder a Layer's pixels by sorting them according to various attributes such as brightness.

Photo by Masahiro Miyagi on Unsplash

caution

This effect is computationally heavy and so may slow down a Composition, particularly on older hardware.

chunks.title: Pixel Sorting Filter
chunks.heading: Pixel Sorting Filter > Pixel Sorting Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Direction** - Set the sorting direction to vertical or horizontal.

**Detail** - Increase/decrease the detail sampled from the image. A higher value will generate a 'noisier' result.

**Threshold** - Set the threshold within which pixels are sampled.

**Reverse Sort** - Invert the order pixels are sorted to.

**Masks** - Add Shapes to isolate the effect.

Masks

Note that any Shapes added as Masks will be automatically switched into **Wireframe** mode. This can be restored by right clicking on a Shape in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) and unchecking the **Wireframe** option or the attribute is also accessible via the **Advanced** tab in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).

chunks.title: Pixelate Filter
chunks.heading: Pixelate Filter > Pixelate Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Redraw a Layer using squares/ triangles of uniform color.

Photo by Eugene Golovesov on Unsplash

chunks.title: Pixelate Filter
chunks.heading: Pixelate Filter > Pixelate Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Pixel Size** - Set the size of a pixel. Think of a pixel as a square rather than an actual pixel!

**Pixel Shape** - Select the Shape for the resulting pixels:

* **Normal** - Create square pixels.
* **Triangle** - Split each square pixel into two triangles.
* **Squared Triangle** - Split each square pixel into two triangle and arrange them so that 4 triangles create squares on a 45˚ angle.
* **Hexagon Triangle** - Create a hexagonal pattern.

**Invert Leading Diagonal** - Reverse the direction of the triangles when **Pixel Shape** is set to **Triangle**.

**Pixel Scale** - Set the scale of each pixel to create a border between them.

**Border Color** - Set the color of the space that appears between pixels as the **Pixel Scale** is reduced.

chunks.title: Polar Coordinates Filter
chunks.heading: Polar Coordinates Filter > Polar Coordinates Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Remap Cartesian coordinates (x,y) to polar coordinates (r,θ\thetaθ) to wrap an image around a central point.

Loading Cavalry Player…

Move Align X all the way to the right and then increase/decrease the Width.

chunks.title: Polar Coordinates Filter
chunks.heading: Polar Coordinates Filter > Polar Coordinates Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Sampling Quality** - Controls how the image is sampled/interpolated. The options can be thought of as low to high quality from top to bottom and can be useful when working with fine details like text.

* **Nearest Neighbour** – Uses the closest pixel without blending.
* **Bilinear** – Blends between nearby pixels for smoother results. Good for general image scaling but can introduce a softness/blur.
* **Catmull–Rom** – A high-quality resampling method that produces sharper results and preserves fine detail.
* **Mitchell** – Balanced high-quality filtering.

**Centre** - Offset the polar origin from the Layer's centre.

**Radius** - Set the outer radius as a percentage of the Layer's shortest dimension.

**Inner Radius** - Push the Layer's bottom edge away from the Centre as a percentage of the **Radius**.

**Rotation** - Rotate the polar coordinates.

**Angular Range** - Set an angle to create a wedge of the circle.

**Inside Out** - Flip the mapping so the bottom of the source becomes the outer edge and the top maps to the pole.

**Edge Feather** - Feather the inner and outer circular edges.

chunks.title: Posterize Filter
chunks.heading: Posterize Filter > Posterize Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Create a low color depth look by reducing the color variation of Shapes to solid tones or colours.

Photo by Klara Kulikova on Unsplash

chunks.title: Posterize Filter
chunks.heading: Posterize Filter > Posterize Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Levels** - Determine the complexity of the resulting image. A lower value will reduce the number of colored areas creating a simpler result whereas a larger value will increase the detail.

chunks.title: Radial Wipe Filter
chunks.heading: Radial Wipe Filter > Radial Wipe Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Completion** - Set a percentage for how complete the wipe is.

**Mode** -

* **Counter-Clockwise** - Wipe in a counter-clockwise direction.
* **Clockwise** - Wipe in a clockwise direction.
* **Both** - Wipe in both directions.

**Feather** - The amount of feather

**Start Angle** - The angle the wipe starts at.

**Screen Space** - When checked the wipe is based on the composition rather than local to the Shape.

chunks.title: RGB Split Filter
chunks.heading: RGB Split Filter > RGB Split Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Split and offset the red, green and blue channels of a Shape.

Photo by Tom Podmore on Unsplash

chunks.title: RGB Split Filter
chunks.heading: RGB Split Filter > RGB Split Filter > UI
chunks.text:
* Settings* Colors

**Base Layer** - Show/ hide the original layer.

**Blend Mode** - Select a [Blend Mode](/docs/nodes/general/blend-modes/).

**Strength** - Increase/ decrease the offset of each color channel.

**Automatic Padding** - Automatically increase the padding based on the filters settings. This will prevent any cropping that may otherwise occur.

**Padding** - Increase/ decrease the padding for the Shape. This can be used to crop the edges of the Shape.

**Repetitions** - Set the number of times the effect of the Filter is processed.

**Repetition Distance** - Set the distance between the first and last of the repetitions.

**Rotation** - Rotate each repetition.

**Red Channel** - Set the color used in the red channel.

**Green Channel** - Set the color used in the green channel.

**Blue Channel** - Set the color used in the blue channel.

**Red Channel Offset** - Set the position offset for the red channel.

**Blue Channel Offset** - Set the position offset for the blue channel.

**Green Channel Offset** - Set the position offset for the green channel.

chunks.title: Scan Lines Filter
chunks.heading: Scan Lines Filter > Scan Lines Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
The Scan Lines Filter can be used to mimic the effect of a CRT monitor.

Photo by Raphael Lopes on Unsplash

chunks.title: Scan Lines Filter
chunks.heading: Scan Lines Filter > Scan Lines Filter > UI
chunks.text:
* Scan Lines* Shadow Mask

**Use Scan Lines Resolution** - When checked, the image is sampled along the centre of each scan line and the result used to set each scan line's colour across its height.

**Line Count** - Set the total number of scan lines to divide the shape into.

**Line Width** - Set the width of each scan line as a percentage.

**Line Feather** - Feather or blur each scan line by setting a percentage of the gap between scan line.

**Line Opacity** - Set the opacity of the scan line.

**Line Color** - Set the color for the scan lines.

**Line Rotation** - Set a rotation value for the scan lines.

**Interlace Frame Interval** - Set how many frames each interlace step

**Brightness Boost** - Increase the brightness of the resulting image.

A shadow mask is used in CRT televisions to ensure the beams accurately hit the screen to ensure the resulting picture is not blurred.

**Use Shadow Mask** - Enable the shadow mask.

**Use Shadow Opacity** - Increase/ decrease the opacity of the shadow mask.

chunks.title: Scan Lines Filter
chunks.heading: Scan Lines Filter > Scan Lines Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Shadow Mask Scale** - Increase/ decrease the size of the shadow mask. The shadow mask is a 3x3 grid of RGB plus 1 row of black so increasing the scale to 2 will create a 6x6 grid of RGB plus 1 row of black.

**Red Channel** - Set a color to define the 'red' channel.

**Green Channel** - Set a color to define the 'green' channel.

**Blue Channel** - Set a color to define the 'blue' channel.

chunks.title: Scrape Filter
chunks.heading: Scrape Filter > Scrape Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Stretch pixels from a line to create a smeared effect.

Photo by Christine Kozak on Unsplash

chunks.title: Scrape Filter
chunks.heading: Scrape Filter > Scrape Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Padding** - Increase/decrease the bounds of the filter's result.

**Amount** - Decrease/increase the stretch.

**Offset** - Offset the position of the line used to sample the Shape (from the Shape's centre).

**Unlock Offset** - When checked, any Offset along the length of the sampler line (e.g. in Y) will also be offset in the resulting smear. The best way to see the difference between checked an unchecked is to scrub Offset.Y when all other settings are default.

**Rotation** - Rotate the line drawn to sample the Shape.

**Invert** - Flip the effect to the other side of the line.

chunks.title: Scrape Filter
chunks.heading: Scrape Filter > Scrape Filter > Layer tool
chunks.text:
With the [Select tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) enabled and the **Scrape Filter** selected in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) a interactive UI will appear in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

* To affect the **Offset** - Click and drag the white circle in the centre.

info

Note that Viewport tools will not appear if a Scrape Filter is added to a Sub-Mesh Behaviour.

chunks.title: Sharpen Filter

chunks.title: Shift Channels Filter

The Shift Channels Filter replaces red, green, blue, and alpha channels with values from other channels.

Photo by Mathias Appel on Flickr

chunks.title: Shift Channels Filter

chunks.text:

Use the drop downs to select from the options below:

chunks.title: SkSL Filter
chunks.heading: SkSL Filter > SkSL Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Write custom filters in SkSL ("Skia Shading Language").

Example SkSL Filters. Photo by Davies Designs Studio on Unsplash.

SkSL ("Skia Shading Language") is a variant of GLSL which is used as Skia's internal shading language. With some minor modifications, GLSL code from sites like <https://www.shadertoy.com/> can be converted for use in Cavalry.

For more detail on the differences between GLSL and SkSL see the [Skia documentation](https://github.com/google/skia/blob/main/src/sksl/README.md).

Integer Uniforms

The SkSL Filter does not accept integer uniforms, please use floats instead.

chunks.title: SkSL Filter
chunks.heading: SkSL Filter > SkSL Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Blend Mode** - See [Blend Modes](/docs/nodes/general/blend-modes/).

**Filter Code** - Write/paste/edit SkSL code here.

**Padding** - Where a Filter produces pixels that fall outside of the original Shape's boundary this can be used to expand it.

**Inputs** - Click the `+` button to to choose a uniform type and add one. Uniforms can be renamed by right clicking on an attribute and choosing **Rename...**. This name can then be used as a variable in the **Filter Code**.

chunks.title: SkSL Filter
chunks.heading: SkSL Filter > SkSL Filter > UI > Export to Plugin
chunks.text:
Click `Export to Plugin...` to load an export window which can be used to export the Layer as a [Plugin](/docs/tech-info/third-party-plugins/).

**Author** - Set the string to populate the `"author"` key in `definitions.json`. This field will be remembered between sessions.

**Plugin Name** - Set the string to populates the `"niceName"` key in `strings.json`

**Encrypt** - When checked, the exported files will be encrypted.

**Export...** - Click `Export` to choose a location to export the files to. The **Author** and **Plugin Name** fields are required.

Notes

Note that it's likely some adjustments to the exported files will be required. For example, icons, tooltips etc may need to be added.

chunks.title: Slit Scan Filter
chunks.heading: Slit Scan Filter > Slit Scan Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Perspective** - Increase/decrease the distortion of the Shape.

**Offset** - Offset the top half of the effect in the Y axis.

**Time** - By default, this is connected to the Composition's Time.

**Rotation** - Rotate the effect.

**Frame Speed** - Increase/decrease the speed in which the effect animates. Use negative values to reverse the movement.

**Mirror Scan** - When checked, the **Frame Speed** direction for the top half of the effect is reversed meaning both the top and bottom will animate towards or away from the centre.

**Glow Size** - Increase/decrease the intensity of the glow that emanates from the centre of the effect.

**Glow Blend Mode** - Set how the glow blends with the Shape.

**Glow Color** - Set a color for the glow.

chunks.title: Spherise Filter
chunks.heading: Spherise Filter > Spherise Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Map an input Shape onto a sphere that can be rotated.

Photo by NASA

Aspect Ratio

For best results, the Shape being filtered should have dimensions with an aspect ratio of 2:1.

chunks.title: Spherise Filter
chunks.heading: Spherise Filter > Spherise Filter > UI
chunks.text:
* Settings* Lighting

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Sampling Quality** - Controls how the image is sampled/interpolated. The options can be thought of as low to high quality from top to bottom and can be useful when working with fine details like text.

* **Nearest Neighbour** – Uses the closest pixel without blending.
* **Bilinear** – Blends between nearby pixels for smoother results. Good for general image scaling but can introduce a softness/blur.
* **Catmull–Rom** – A high-quality resampling method that produces sharper results and preserves fine detail.
* **Mitchell** – Balanced high-quality filtering.

**Centre** - Set the position of the sphere.

**Radius** - Set the radius of the sphere as a percentage of the Shape's size.

**Visibility** - Determine which sides of the sphere are visible when using images that contain transparency:

* **Both** - Show both the front and the back of the sphere.
* **Front** - Show only the font of the sphere.
* **Back** - Show only the back of the sphere.

**Rotation** - Rotate the sphere around its X, Y or Z axis in degrees.

chunks.title: Spherise Filter
chunks.heading: Spherise Filter > Spherise Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Enable Lighting** - Enable diffuse lighting on the sphere's surface.

**Light Position** - Set the 3D position of the light source.

**Light Intensity** - Set the brightness of the light source.

**Light Color** - Set the color of the light source.

**Ambient Strength** - Set the amount of ambient light (base illumination).

**Ambient Color** - Set the color of the ambient light.

**Specular Strength** - Set the intensity of the specular highlights.

**Specular Color** - Set the color of the specular highlights.

**Shininess** - Set the size and sharpness of the specular highlights. Higher values will create smaller, sharper highlights.

**Use as Bump Map** - When checked, the Shape's material is used as a bump map to add surface detail lighting.

**Bump Map Strength** - Increase/decrease the affect the bump map has on the surface lighting.

**Enable Self Shadowing** - When checked, shadows are added to the back of the sphere.

**Shadow Intensity** - Determine how dark the shadowed areas become.

**Shadow Softness** - Determine the softness of the shadow's transition from dark to light.

**Back Exposure** - Set the brightness of the back/interior surfaces of the sphere.

chunks.title: Stripes Filter
chunks.heading: Stripes Filter > Stripes Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Padding** - Increase/decrease the bounds of the filter's result.

**Sampler Offset** - Offset the position of the line used to sample the Shape (from the Shape's centre).

**Unlock Offset** - When checked, any Offset along the length of the sampler line (e.g. in Y) will also be offset in the resulting stripes. The best way to see the difference between checked an unchecked is to scrub Offset.Y when all other settings are default.

**Sampler Rotation** - Rotate the line drawn to sample the Shape.

**Clipping Range** - Crop the resulting effect. 0% = the top of the Shape, 100% = the bottom of the Shape.

**Rotation** - Rotate the result of the effect.

chunks.title: Stripes Filter
chunks.heading: Stripes Filter > Stripes Filter > Layer tool
chunks.text:
With the [Select tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) enabled and the **Stripes Filter** selected in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) a interactive UI will appear in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

A purple line is drawn in the Viewport to represent the position and angle of the sampler.

* To affect the **Offset** - Click and drag the white circle in the centre.
* To affect the **Offset Rotation** and **Rotation** - Click and drag the white circle offset from the centre.
* To affect just the **Offset Rotation** - Hold `Option/Alt` and click and drag the white circle offset from the centre.

chunks.title: Threshold Filter
chunks.heading: Threshold Filter > Threshold Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
The Threshold Filter converts all pixels lighter than the threshold to white and all pixels darker than the threshold to black. It can be used to create high contrast, black and white results.

Photo by Oğuzhan Edman on Unsplash

chunks.title: Threshold Filter
chunks.heading: Threshold Filter > Threshold Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Threshold** - Set the value that a pixel will be considered lighter or darker than.

chunks.title: TriTone Filter
chunks.heading: TriTone Filter > TriTone Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Map dark, mid-tone and bright values to specified colors.

Photo by Greg Rosenke on Unsplash

chunks.title: TriTone Filter
chunks.heading: TriTone Filter > TriTone Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Highlights** - Set a color for the highlights.

**Mid-Tones** - Set a color for the mid-tones.

**Shadows** - Set a color for the shadows.

chunks.title: Venetian Blinds Filter
chunks.heading: Venetian Blinds Filter > Venetian Blinds Filter > UI
chunks.text:
**Completion** - Set a percentage for how complete the wipe is.

**Width** - Set the width of each 'blind'.

**Feather** - Set a feather (blur).

**Rotation** - Set the angle of the blinds.

**Screen Space** - When checked the wipe is based on the composition rather than local to the Shape.

chunks.title: Vignette Filter
chunks.heading: Vignette Filter > Vignette Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Simulate the light falloff characteristic when viewing images through certain types of lenses.

Photo by Tom Depont on Unsplash

chunks.title: Vignette Filter
chunks.heading: Vignette Filter > Vignette Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Offset** - Offset the position of the Vignette from the centre of the Shape.

**Scale** - Increase/decrease the size of the Vignette.

**Rotation** - Rotate the Vignette around the centre of the Shape.

**Exposure** - Increase/decrease the exposure of the image where the Vignette covers it.

**Feather** - Increase/decrease how soft the edge of the Vignette is.

**Vignette Shape** - Select a Shape for the Vignette:

* **Circle** - A circular shape. Note that the Vignette is stretched to fit the aspect ratio of the Shape.
* **Shape** - A polygon with an arbitrary number of **Sides**.

**Sides** - When the **Vignette Shape** is set to **Shape**, determine how many sides the polygon has.

**Color** - Set the color for the Vignette.

chunks.title: Zoom Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Zoom Blur Filter > Zoom Blur Filter > Intro
chunks.text:
Blur a Shape outwards from a central point with customisable attenuation.

Photo by Hanson Lu on Unsplash

chunks.title: Zoom Blur Filter
chunks.heading: Zoom Blur Filter > Zoom Blur Filter > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/common-attributes-filters/) +

**Origin** - Set the centre point of the blur where 0,0 is the centre of the Shape.

**Amount** - Set the distance/strength of the blur.

**Attenuation Multiplier** - Multiply the blur based on the distance from the 'Origin'. A lower value will create a harder transition.

---

See other blur Filters:

chunks.title: Shaders
chunks.heading: Shaders > Shaders
chunks.text:
**Shaders** can be added to the materials (Fill and/or Stroke) of a Shape in order to generate gradients or patterns. They can be layered or stacked on top of one another and combined to create more complex effects.

Shaders can be connected to multiple Shapes. For example, a single [Gradient Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/gradient-shader/) can be connected to multiple Shapes so that they all inherit the same appearance.

Example

1. Create an [Ellipse](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/ellipse/).
2. Open the Ellipse's **Fill** tab in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).
3. Right click in the **Shaders** input and choose `Add Shader > Gradient Shader`.

This creates a [Gradient Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/gradient-shader/) and connects it to the Ellipse's Fill. Double click the **Gradient Shader** to load its Attribute Editor UI and adjust its properties.

chunks.title: Blend Shader
chunks.heading: Blend Shader > Blend Shader > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/common-attributes-shaders/) +

**Shaders** - A list of connected Shaders. Right click > Add Shader, drag/ drop an existing Shader or make a connection to add Shaders.

Use the cog icon to adjust the settings for each layer:

* **Shader** - The connected Shader.
* **Invert** - Reverse the values of the Shader.
* **Sample Mode** - Determine how the **Input Shader** is sampled:
  + **RGB** - Use the combined RGB values.
  + **Luma (Gamma Corrected)** - Use the gamma corrected brightness values.
  + **Saturation** - Use the saturation values.
  + **Lightness (Value)** - Use the lightness values (average of the RGB channels).
  + **Red Channel** - Sample the values held in the red channel.
  + **Blue Channel** - Sample the values held in the blue channel.
  + **Green Channel** - Sample the values held in the green channel.

chunks.title: Checkerboard Shader
chunks.heading: Checkerboard Shader > Checkerboard Shader > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/common-attributes-shaders/) +

**Size** - Set the size of a single tile.

**Offset** - Offset the checkerboard's position.

**Rotation** - Set an angle for the tiles.

**Filter** - These settings can improve image quality in both the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) and for renders – particularly when resizing images.

* **None (Fastest)** - No resampling will be performed when the images are resized – this is the lowest quality setting.
* **Bilinear** - Basic resampling is performed. This is low quality but it's very fast.
* **Mipmaps** - Mipmaps are pre-calculated, optimised, low resolution versions of the image created via Bilinear interpolation. These are used to get the best quality and performance when scaling images down.
* **Bicubic** - This is the slowest method but it produces the best quality when scaling images up.

Color

Use the [Gradient Map](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/gradient-map-filter/) Filter to re-map the black and white tiles to other colors.

chunks.title: Color Shader
chunks.heading: Color Shader > Color Shader > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/common-attributes-shaders/)

**Color** - Set the color using hex or rgb values (note - only rgb values can be animated).

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Shaders)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Shaders) > Common Attributes (Shaders) > UI
chunks.text:
**Blend Mode** - Set the [blend mode](/docs/nodes/general/blend-modes/) for the Shader. Note that, where multiple Shaders are connected to a Shape, this blend mode affects how Shaders blend with each other in the **Shaders** attribute's stack and not how Shapes blend with other Shapes in the Viewport — use the **Blend Mode** under a Shape's **Shape** tab to affect that.

**Alpha** - Set how opaque/transparent a Shader is.

chunks.title: Gradient Shader
chunks.heading: Gradient Shader > Gradient Shader > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/common-attributes-shaders/) +

**Screen Space** - When checked the gradient is drawn in screen space. The result being that a Shape will move through the gradient. When unchecked the gradient 'sticks' to a Shape.

**Reverse** - Reverse the direction of the Gradient.

**Premultiply** - When checked, the calculation for transparent pixels is premultiplied.

**Tiling** - Determine what happens at the borders of the gradient.

* **Clamp** - Use the first and last values of the gradient.
* **Repeat** - Repeat/ loop the gradient.
* **Mirror** - Mirror/ ping pong the gradient.
* **Decal** - Cut out the gradient.

**Gradient Mode** - Select an interpolation for the **Gradient**. See [Gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/).

**Mode** - Select the type of gradient:

* **Conical** - A two point conical gradient.

chunks.title: Gradient Shader
chunks.heading: Gradient Shader > Gradient Shader > UI
chunks.text:
+ **Gradient** - Set the color stops for the [gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/).
  + **Start Radius** - Set the radius for the color stop at the start of the gradient.
  + **End Radius** - Set the radius for the color stop at the end of the gradient.
  + **Start Centre** - Position the centre of the start of the gradient.
  + **Wrap UVs** - When checked, the last Stop will interpolate with the first Stop (and vice versa) meaning the Gradient will wrap. Note - if both the first and last Stop are positioned at `0` or `1` checking this attribute will have no visible effect.
* **Linear** - A linear gradient.

chunks.title: Gradient Shader
chunks.heading: Gradient Shader > Gradient Shader > UI
chunks.text:
+ **Gradient** - Set the color stops for the [gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/).
  + **Scale** - Scale the gradient.
  + **Rotation** - Rotate the gradient.
  + **Gradient Scales with Rotation** - When checked the gradient will be scaled to fit the shape(s) along the axis of Rotation.
  + **Offset** - Offset the position of the gradient.
  + **Wrap UVs** - When checked, the last Stop will interpolate with the first Stop (and vice versa) meaning the Gradient will wrap. Note - if both the first and last Stop are positioned at `0` or `1` checking this attribute will have no visible effect.
* **Radial** - A gradient created along a radius (centre out).

chunks.title: Gradient Shader
chunks.heading: Gradient Shader > Gradient Shader > UI
chunks.text:
+ **Gradient** - Set the color stops for the [gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/).
  + **Scale** - Scale the gradient.
  + **Radius Mode**:
    - **Fixed Radius** - Set a fixed radius for the gradient.
    - **Bounding Box** - Set the gradient to scale with a Shape.
  + **Size Ratio** - A multiplier for the **Bounding Box**.
  + **Radius** - Set a **Fixed Radius** for the gradient.
  + **Offset** - Offset the position of the gradient [x,y].
  + **Wrap UVs** - When checked, the last Stop will interpolate with the first Stop (and vice versa) meaning the Gradient will wrap. Note - if both the first and last Stop are positioned at `0` or `1` checking this attribute will have no visible effect.
* **Shape** - A polygonal gradient created along a radius (centre out).

chunks.title: Gradient Shader
chunks.heading: Gradient Shader > Gradient Shader > UI
chunks.text:
+ **Gradient** - Set the color stops for the [gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/).
  + **Scale** - Scale the gradient.
  + **Radius Mode**:
    - **Fixed Radius** - Set a fixed radius for the gradient.
    - **Bounding Box** - Set the gradient to scale with a Shape(s).
  + **Size Ratio** - A multiplier for the **Bounding Box**.
  + **Radius** - Set a **Fixed Radius** for the gradient.
  + **Offset** - Offset the position of the gradient [x,y].
  + **Shape Sides** - Set the number of sides for the Gradient's shape.
  + **Wrap UVs** - When checked, the last Stop will interpolate with the first Stop (and vice versa) meaning the Gradient will wrap. Note - if both the first and last Stop are positioned at `0` or `1` checking this attribute will have no visible effect.
* **Sweep** - A gradient that travels around a circle.

chunks.title: Gradient Shader
chunks.heading: Gradient Shader > Gradient Shader > UI
chunks.text:
+ **Gradient** - Set the color stops for the [gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/).
  + **Rotation** - Set a rotation for the gradient.
  + **Start Angle** - Set the angle the gradient starts at.
  + **End Angle** - Set the angle the gradient ends at.
  + **Offset** - Offset the start/ end angles of the gradient.
  + **Wrap UVs** - When checked, the last Stop will interpolate with the first Stop (and vice versa) meaning the Gradient will wrap. Note - if both the first and last Stop are positioned at `0` or `1` checking this attribute will have no visible effect.

chunks.title: Gradient Shader
chunks.heading: Gradient Shader > Gradient Shader > UI > Layer Tools
chunks.text:
Stops can be manipulated in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) with the [Select tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/). When the **Gradient Shader** is selected in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/), the Gradient is represented in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

* **To adjust the Gradient's Size Ratio/ Rotation** (Radial and Shape) - Click + drag the white dots with purple outline at either end of the Gradient. Use `Cmd/Ctrl` + click + drag to only affect **Rotation**.
* **To update a Stop's Position** - Click + drag a Stop along the purple line.
* **To increase/decrease a Stop's Interpolation** - `Shift` + drag left/right.
* **To increase/decrease a Stop's Jitter** - `Cmd/Ctrl` + drag left/right .
* **To duplicate a Stop** - `Option/Alt` + drag.
* **To delete a Stop** - Select a Stop and hit the `Delete` key.
* **To change a Stop's Color** - Double click a Stop and adjust the Stop's color in the Color Editor that pops up or, drag a swatch from the Color Window and drop it on a Stop.

tip

chunks.title: Gradient Shader
chunks.heading: Gradient Shader > Gradient Shader > UI > Layer Tools
chunks.text:
Gradients use a Shape's bounding box to position colors. There are some cases where this might require some management. For example, if using a Sweep Gradient on an Ellipse's Stroke, changing the Stroke's Trim wil change its bounding box which will, in turn, change the Gradient's position.

To work around this - try applying the Gradient to an Ellipse's Fill and then using an Arc Shape as a Clipping Mask. In this set up, the Ellipse's bounding box does not change so the Gradient remains fixed in place.

chunks.title: Image Shader
chunks.heading: Image Shader > Image Shader > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/common-attributes-shaders/) +

**File** - Connect an image asset. This can be directly from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) or via an [Asset Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/asset-array/) or [Asset from Smart Folder](/docs/nodes/utilities/asset-from-smart-folder/). Still images, image sequences and video are supported.

**Filter** - These settings can improve image quality in both the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) and for renders – particularly when resizing images:

* **None (Fastest)** - No resampling will be performed when the images are resized – this is the lowest quality setting.
* **Bilinear** - Basic resampling is performed. This is low quality but it's very fast.
* **Mipmaps** - Mipmaps are pre-calculated, optimised, low resolution versions of the image created via Bilinear interpolation. These are used to get the best quality and performance when scaling images down.
* **Bicubic** - This is the slowest method but it produces the best quality when scaling images up.

**Scale Mode** - Set how the image fits a Shape's bounding box:

chunks.title: Image Shader
chunks.heading: Image Shader > Image Shader > UI
chunks.text:
* **None** - Do not scale.
* **Fit Contain** - Fit the image to the bounding box of the Shape so that the whole image is always visible.
* **Fit Width** - Fit the image's width to the width of the Shape's bounding box.
* **Fit Height** - Fit the image's height to height of the Shape's bounding box.
* **Fit Cover** - Fit the image to the width or height of the Shape's bounding box so that it fills the Shape while maintaining its aspect ratio.

**Tiling** - Determine what happens at the borders of the image:

* **Clamp** - Use the first and last values of the image.
* **Repeat** - Repeat/loop the image.
* **Mirror** - Mirror/ping pong the image.
* **Decal** - Cut out the image.

**Scale** - Increase/decrease the scale of the image.

**Offset** - Offset the position of the image.

**Rotation** - Rotate the image.

**Looping** - When checked an [Image Sequence](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/image-sequences/), video or gif will be set to infinitely loop.

chunks.title: Image Shader
chunks.heading: Image Shader > Image Shader > UI
chunks.text:
**FPS** - Set the frame rate an [Image Sequence](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/image-sequences/) will play back at. By default this control is connected to the Composition's frame rate but this can be manually set by removing the connection.

**Time** - A connection to the Composition's Time which is used to drive the frame number of a video or image sequence.

**Missing Frames** - Determine how frames missing from an image sequence are displayed:

* **Noise** - Display a noise pattern.
* **Nearest Frame** - Display the nearest 'found' frame. For example:

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
