chunks.title: Multi-Point Gradient Shader
chunks.heading: Multi-Point Gradient Shader > Multi-Point Gradient Shader > Intro
chunks.text: Create complex gradients by setting the position, color and influence for multiple points.

chunks.title: Multi-Point Gradient Shader
chunks.heading: Multi-Point Gradient Shader > Multi-Point Gradient Shader > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/common-attributes-shaders/) +

**Premultiply** - When checked, the calculation for transparent pixels is premultiplied.

**Gradient Mode** - Select an interpolation for the **Gradient**. See [Gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/).

**+ Add** (button) - Add a new Point to the gradient.

*Each Point includes the following attributes:*

* **Color** - Set a color for the Point.
* **Position** - Set a position for the Point.
* **Influence** - Determine the strength of the Point.
* **Jitter** - Add noise to the interpolation curve based on its intensity. Jitter will be added between the selected Stop and the next one to its right.

Create Stops from a Palette

The stops of a **Multi-Point Gradient Shader** can be set via the **Set Gradient from Palette** option from the disclosure menu in the [Color Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/). Select a **Multi-Point Gradient Shader** Layer and then run the command. The stops created will be randomly positioned based on the Composition's resolution.

chunks.title: Multi-Point Gradient Shader
chunks.heading: Multi-Point Gradient Shader > Multi-Point Gradient Shader > UI > Layer Tool
chunks.text:
Points can be manipulated in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) with the [Select tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/). When the **Multi-Point Gradient Shader** is selected in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/), small purple dots will appear in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

* **To move a Point** - Click + drag a purple dot.
* **To duplicate a Point** - `Option/Alt` + click + drag a purple dot.
* **To increase/decrease a Point's Influence** - `Shift` + click + drag a purple dot.
* **To delete a Point** - Select a purple dot and hit the delete key.
* **To change a Point's Color** - Double click a purple dot and adjust the Point's color in the Color Editor that pops up or, drag a swatch from the Color Window and drop it on a purple dot.

tip

Press `Escape` to close the **Color Editor** window to maintain selection.

info

chunks.title: Multi-Point Gradient Shader
chunks.heading: Multi-Point Gradient Shader > Multi-Point Gradient Shader > UI > Layer Tool
chunks.text:
If the same **Multi-Point Gradient Shader** is connected to multiple Shapes/ outputs, then the first connection is used to position the purple dots in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/). This can be identified by clicking the purple output connection icon for the **Multi-Point Gradient Shader** in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) or [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) and picking the bottom layer in the list that appears.

caution

The **Layer Tool** is not available if the **Multi-Point Gradient Shader** is connected to a [Blend Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/blend-shader/).

chunks.title: Noise Shader
chunks.heading: Noise Shader > Noise Shader > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/common-attributes-shaders/) +

**Noise Type** - Select the noise type:

* **Perlin Noise**
* **Simplex Noise**
* **Cellular Noise**

**Scale** - Increase/ decrease the scale of the noise [x,y].

**Offset** - Offset the noise position in x the y directions.

**Minimum** - Set a minimum value for the noise (0 = black).

**Maximum** - Set a maximum value for the noise (1 = white).

**Gamma** - Set the gamma correction where values greater/less than `1` will darken/lighten a Layer.

**Time** - This attribute is automatically connected to the comp's frame number. Disconnect it for static Noise.

**Time Scale** - Increase/decrease the speed of the noise.

**Frequency** - Increase/decrease the frequency of the noise.

**Amplitude** - Multiplies the **Minimum** and **Maximum** values.

**Cycles** - Compress the noise into a smoothly repeating pattern. Setting **Octaves** to `1` will often produce more predictable results. **Minimum** and/or **Gamma** can be used to increase contrast.

chunks.title: Noise Shader
chunks.heading: Noise Shader > Noise Shader > UI
chunks.text:
**Octaves** - The number of octaves over which the noise function is calculated. Each octave is at about twice the frequency, i.e., half the size of the previous one, but this can be altered with the **Lacunarity** control.

**Lacunarity** - A higher value will create more or larger 'gaps'.

chunks.title: Shape to Shader
chunks.heading: Shape to Shader > Shape to Shader > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/common-attributes-shaders/) +

**Render Quality** - The Shader renders the Input Shape to an image which is then used as the output. Set the resolution of the image to balance quality with performance:

* **High** - Render 100% of the pixels.
* **Medium** - Render 50% of the pixels.
* **Low** - Render 25% of the pixels.
* **Very Low** - Render 12.5% of the pixels.

**Input Shape** - Connect a Shape to generate the Shader from.

Example

1. Create a [Ellipse](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/ellipse/).
2. Create a [Rectangle](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/rectangle/).
3. Change the Rectangle's Fill Color.
4. Create a **Shape to Shader**.
5. Connect ellipse.id→shapeToShader.inputShape.
6. Connect shapeToShader.id→rectangle.shaders.
7. Hide the **Ellipse**.

chunks.title: SkSL Shader
chunks.heading: SkSL Shader > SkSL Shader > Intro
chunks.text:
SkSL ("Skia Shading Language") is a variant of GLSL which is used as Skia's internal shading language. With some minor modifications, GLSL code from sites like <https://www.shadertoy.com/> can be converted for use in Cavalry.

For more detail on the differences between GLSL and SkSL see the [Skia documentation](https://github.com/google/skia/blob/main/src/sksl/README.md).

Integer Uniforms

The SkSL Shader does not accept integer uniforms, please use floats instead.

chunks.title: SkSL Shader
chunks.heading: SkSL Shader > SkSL Shader > UI
chunks.text:
**Blend Mode** - See [Blend Modes](/docs/nodes/general/blend-modes/).

**Shader Code** - Paste/edit SkSL code here.

**Inputs** - Click the `+` button to to choose a uniform type and add one. Uniforms can be renamed by right clicking on an attribute and choosing **Rename...**. This name can then be used as a variable in the **SkSL Code**.

To sample an input shader use `inputShader.eval(p)` where `inputShader` is the name of the uniform and `p` is the coordinate to be sampled.

chunks.title: SkSL Shader
chunks.heading: SkSL Shader > SkSL Shader > UI > Export to Plugin
chunks.text:
Click `Export to Plugin...` to load an export window which can be used to export the Layer as a [Plugin](/docs/tech-info/third-party-plugins/).

**Author** - Set the string to populate the `"author"` key in `definitions.json`. This field will be remembered between sessions.

**Plugin Name** - Set the string to populates the `"niceName"` key in `strings.json`

**Encrypt** - When checked, the exported files will be encrypted.

**Export...** - Click `Export` to choose a location to export the files to. The **Author** and **Plugin Name** fields are required.

Notes

Note that it's likely some adjustments to the exported files will be required. For example, icons, tooltips etc may need to be added.

chunks.title: SkSL Shader
chunks.heading: SkSL Shader > SkSL Shader > UI > Built in Uniforms
chunks.text:
Built in Uniforms can be added to the **Shader Code**:

* `resolution` - the size of the Shape being rendered which can be used to produce Shaders that scale to their contents. See the example in `Create > Demo Scenes > Custom Shaders and Filters > Truchet Tiles`.

chunks.title: SLA Shader
chunks.heading: SLA Shader > SLA Shader > Intro
chunks.text:
Create novel noise effects.

Credit

The SLA Shader is kindly provided under licence by David Farmer in celebration of the life of [Mark Coleran](https://www.pushing-pixels.org/coleran/).

chunks.title: SLA Shader
chunks.heading: SLA Shader > SLA Shader > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/common-attributes-shaders/) +

**Noise Type** - Select the noise type:

**Octaves** - The number of octaves over which the noise function is calculated. Use a higher value to increase the amount of detail in the noise pattern.

**Scale** - Increase/decrease the scale of the noise.

**Offset** - Offset the noise position in x/y.

**Color A** - Set a color for the noise to interpolate with **Color B**.

**Color B** - Set a color for the noise to interpolate with **Color A**.

**Invert** - Invert RGB colors. Note that this is a post process so is not 'flipping' **Color A** and **Color B** – alpha is not affected.

**Gamma** - Set the gamma correction applied to the input values where values greater/less than `1` will darken/lighten a Layer.

**Displacement** - Increase this value to create more turbulent noise.

**Time** - This attribute is automatically connected to the Composition's frame number. Disconnect it for static Noise.

**Time Scale** - Increase/decrease the speed of the noise.

chunks.title: Voronoi Shader
chunks.heading: Voronoi Shader > Voronoi Shader > Intro
chunks.text:
A Voronoi diagram is a type of tessellation pattern that can be found in nature, such as in cells or a giraffe's coat, and is often used in architecture, art and computer science.

It is generated by scattering a number of points on a plane and subdividing it into cells enclosing a portion of the plane closest to each point.

chunks.title: Voronoi Shader
chunks.heading: Voronoi Shader > Voronoi Shader > UI
chunks.text:
* Settings* Hierarchical Colors

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/common-attributes-shaders/) +

**Offset** - Offset the position of the pattern.

**Scale** - Increase/decrease the size of the pattern.

**Rotation** - Change the angle of the pattern.

**Time** - This attribute is automatically connected to the Composition's frame number which will evolve the pattern in playback. Remove this connection if a static voronoi pattern is required or replace it with a [Frame Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/frame/) to increase/decrease the speed of the voronoi's evolution.

**Loop Length** - Set the duration in frames that it takes for the **Distortion Amount** to loop. A smaller value will increase the speed of the voronoi's evolution (and vice versa).

**Distortion Amount** - The voronoi pattern is initially generated from a uniform grid of points. This attribute can be used to move the points in random directions to create a less uniform pattern.

**Seed** - Change the direction of the **Distortion Amount** to create a different pattern.

**Style** - Define the appearance of the cells:

chunks.title: Voronoi Shader
chunks.heading: Voronoi Shader > Voronoi Shader > UI
chunks.text:
* **Flat** - Fill the cells with the **Cell Color**.
* **Greyscale** - Fill each cell with a random greyscale (black to white) color. Note that the range is clamped so that the darkest cell is never 100% black. Black can then be used for the **Edge Color** so that edges can be isolated when using a [Gradient Map Filter](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/gradient-map-filter/) to recolor the cells. See tip below.
* **Euclidean** - Fill the cells with a radial gradient centred on each grid point.
* **Manhattan** - Fill the cells with a 4 sided shape gradient centred on each grid point.

Gradient Map

To set a different color for each cell, set the **Style** to **Greyscale** and then add a [Gradient Map Filter](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/gradient-map-filter/) to the Shape. This can be used to remap the Voronoi's greyscale (dark to light) values to colors. The darkest cell is prevented from being fully black by design and so, if the **Edge Color** is set to black (#000000), the area from **position** `0 - 0.02` (far left) along the Gradient Map Filter's gradient can be used to isolate and affect the color of the Voronoi's edges.

chunks.title: Voronoi Shader
chunks.heading: Voronoi Shader > Voronoi Shader > UI
chunks.text:
**Equidistant Edges** - When the **Style** is set to **Euclidean**, this will draw the gradient along a line perpendicular to the edges to create a 'pyramid' look.

**Greyscale Seed** - Randomly change the greyscale colors set by the **Greyscale** style.

**Cell Color** - Set a color to fill the cells when the **Style** is set to **Flat**.

**Type** - Select how the pattern is generated:

* **Normal** - Create a pattern which can also generate gaps along the edges between the cells.
* **Hierarchical** - Create a pattern with the option to further sub-divide the cells into smaller cells. When **Style** is set to **Flat**, the color for the cells at each **Level** can be set in the **Hierarchical Colors** tab.

**Edge Width** - When **Style** is set to **Normal**, increase/decrease the width of the gap between edges.

**Edge Feather** - When **Style** is set to **Normal**, increase/decrease the softness of the edges. This attribute has a soft minimum of `0` but it is possible to set a negative value by entering one manually.

**Roundness** - When **Style** is set to **Normal**, increase/decrease the fillet where each edge connects to create a softer, more rounded look.

chunks.title: Voronoi Shader
chunks.heading: Voronoi Shader > Voronoi Shader > UI
chunks.text:
**Edge Color** - When **Style** is set to **Normal**, set the color of the gaps between edges.

**Levels** - When **Style** is set to **Hierarchical**, set the number of times cells can be subdivided. For example, a value of **2** will subdivide some of the cells once and then subdivide some of those cells again. The top/first level is **0**.

**Levels Amount** - When **Style** is set to **Hierarchical**, recursively increase/decrease the chance of the cells being subdivided.

When **Style** is set to **Flat** and **Mode** is set to **Hierarchical**, the color for the cells at each **Level** can be set.

**Level 0 Color** - Set a color for all the cells at level 0.

**Level 1 Color** - Set a color for all the cells at level 1.

**Level 2 Color** - Set a color for all the cells at level 2.

**Level 3 Color** - Set a color for all the cells at level 3.

**Level 4 Color** - Set a color for all the cells at level 4.

chunks.text:
Adjacent Edges

When Shapes are perfectly aligned edge-to-edge, seams can appear between those edges due to anti-aliasing. Try using **Alpha Add** to create a seamless join. Note that this is only supported when the **Background's Alpha = 0**. To remove the Composition's background go `Composition > Toggle Background Alpha`.

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.heading: Introduction > Introduction > Intro
chunks.text: **Distributions** are used by several other layers including the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) and [Connect Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/connect-shape/). They provide a way to distribute points which can then be used to position Shapes.

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.heading: Introduction > Introduction > Types
chunks.text:
[Array](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/array-distribution/) - Distribute points by specifying positions for each index.

[Circle](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/circle-distribution/) - Distribute points in a radial pattern.

[Custom](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/custom-distribution/) - Distribute points using JavaScript.

[Fibonacci](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/fibonacci-distribution/) - Distribute points in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

[Grid](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/grid-distribution/) - Distribute points in a grid.

[Intersections](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/intersections-distribution/) - Distribute points where paths intersect.

[Linear](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/linear-distribution/) - Distribute points in a horizontal or vertical line.

[Mask](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/mask-distribution/) - Distribute points and remove any that fall outside another Shape.

[Math](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/math-distribution/) - Distribute points using mathematical expressions.

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.heading: Introduction > Introduction > Types
chunks.text:
[Particle](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/particle-distribution/) - Distribute points onto a [Particle Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/particle-shape/).

[Path](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/path-distribution/) - Distribute points along a path.

[Point](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/point-distribution/) - Distribute points at 0,0.

[Random](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/random-distribution/) - Distribute points to random positions.

[Rose](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/rose-distribution/) - Distribute points in a rose pattern. [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose\_(mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_(mathematics))

[Shape Edges](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/shape-edges-distribution/) - Distribute points onto another Shape's edges.

[Shape Points](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/shape-points-distribution/) - Distribute points onto another Shape's points/vertices.

[Sort](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/sort-distribution/) - Distribute points by reordering the Ids of another Distribution.

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.heading: Introduction > Introduction > Types
chunks.text:
[Shuffle](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/shuffle-distribution/) - Distribute points by rearranging the Ids of another Distribution.

[Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/sub-mesh-distribution/) - Distribute points onto the positions of child-meshes.

[Transform](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/transform-distribution/) - Distribute points onto the position of a Layer.

[Voxelize](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/voxelize-distribution/) - Distribute points by voxelizing another Shape.

chunks.title: Array Distribution
chunks.heading: Array Distribution > Array Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Add** (button) - Add indices.

**Position** - Set the position of a duplicate [x,y]. Index **(0): Position** sets the position of the first point, **(1): Position** sets the second etc.

chunks.title: Circle Distribution
chunks.heading: Circle Distribution > Circle Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Count** - Set the number of points.

**Radius** - Set the radius of the circle the points are distributed on.

**Start Angle** - Set an angle around the circle to position the first Id (id0).

**Angle** - Set the angle around the circle the points are distributed within.

**Include End** - When checked, a point will be added to the end of the distribution. This is unchecked by default to prevent two points being positioned on top of each other for a 360˚ angle.

**Use Rotation** - When checked, points will be aligned along the normals of the circle.

**Flip** - When checked, the direction of the circle is reversed.

**Travel** - Move the duplicated points along a percentage of the circle’s length.

chunks.title: Custom Distribution
chunks.heading: Custom Distribution > Custom Distribution > Intro
chunks.text: Distribute points using a JavaScript Utility via the [Point Cloud](/docs/tech-info/scripting/cavalry-module/#point-cloud-class) class.

chunks.title: Custom Distribution
chunks.heading: Custom Distribution > Custom Distribution > UI
chunks.text: **Input Distribution** - Connect a [JavaScript Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/javascript-utility/). See `Create > Demo Scenes > JavaScript > SpiroGraph Distribution` for an example.

chunks.title: Fibonacci Distribution
chunks.heading: Fibonacci Distribution > Fibonacci Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Count** - Set the number of duplicated points.

**Radius** - Set the radius.

**Angle** - Set the amount the spiral rotates.

chunks.title: Grid Distribution
chunks.heading: Grid Distribution > Grid Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Count** - Set the number of points [x,y].

**Size** - Set the distance to distribute the points over depending on the **Size Mode**.

**Pattern Offset** - Set a value to offset every other row/column. [x,y].

**Size Mode** - Determine how the **Size** attribute is used:

* **Fit** - Distribute points within the **Size** values.
* **Step** - The **Size** values determine the gaps between each point.

**Direction** - Determine whether points are ordered in rows or columns.

* **Flow Columns** - Points are ordered from left to right then bottom to top.
* **Flow Rows** - Points are ordered from bottom to top then left to right.

info

Points are ordered from bottom left to top right by default. Use negative **Size** values to order shapes from top to bottom or right to left instead.

chunks.title: Intersections Distribution
chunks.heading: Intersections Distribution
chunks.text:
* * Layers* General* Distribution Types* Intersections Distribution

On this page

chunks.title: Linear Distribution
chunks.heading: Linear Distribution > Linear Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Count** - Set the number of points.

**Size** - Set the distance to distribute the points over depending on the **Size Mode**.

**Direction**:

* **Horizontal** - Distribute points horizontally.
* **Vertical** - Distribute points vertically.

**Size Mode**:

* **Fit** - Distribute points within the **Size** values.
* **Step** - The **Size** values determine the gap between each point.

chunks.title: Mask Distribution
chunks.heading: Mask Distribution > Mask Distribution > Intro
chunks.text:
Distribute points and remove any that fall outside another Shape.

Check out Kyle Daily's tutorial.

chunks.title: Mask Distribution
chunks.heading: Mask Distribution > Mask Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Input Distribution** - Select a **Distribution Type**.

**Distribution Masks** - Connect Shapes to mask the points created by the Distribution Type.

chunks.title: Math Distribution
chunks.heading: Math Distribution > Math Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Count** - Set the number of points.

**Expression** - Enter an expression. See [Mathematical Expressions](/docs/tech-info/maths/) for syntax.

chunks.title: Particle Distribution
chunks.heading: Particle Distribution > Particle Distribution > Intro
chunks.text:
Distribute points onto a [Particle Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/particle-shape/).

This is a way to attach geometry to each Particle via the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) or, for example, to use a Particle Shape as the input to a [Connect Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/connect-shape/) (or any other Layer that uses a Distribution).

chunks.title: Particle Distribution
chunks.heading: Particle Distribution > Particle Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Input Shape** - Add the [Particle Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/particle-shape/) to distribute points onto.

Example

1. Create a **Particle Shape**.
2. Create a [Connect Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/connect-shape/).
3. Under the Connect Shape's **Source** tab, set the **Source Distribution** to **Particle**.
4. Connect particleShape.id→connectShape.sourceGenerator.inputShape.
5. Play

Try adding a second Particle Shape to the **Target Distribution** and experimenting with the Connect Shape's settings.

chunks.title: Path Distribution
chunks.heading: Path Distribution > Path Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Count Mode**:

* **Per Shape** - Distribute points along the entire Shape. For example, if a **Duplicator** is used as the **Input Shape**, the value in **Count** would be distributed evenly across the entire Shape.
* **Per Sub-Mesh** - Distribute points along each sub-mesh. For example, if a **Duplicator** is used as the **Input Shape**, the value in **Count** would be distributed evenly across each sub-mesh resulting in a total of`[Count] x [the Count of the Input Shape]` Shapes.
* **Per Contour** - Distribute points across each contour. For example, if a path created with the Pencil containing more than one line (contour) was used as the **Input Shape**, the value in **Count** would be distributed evenly across each of those contours.

**Count** - Set the number of duplicated points per [**Count Mode**].

**Input Shape** - Add the Shape to distribute points along.

**Travel** - Move the points along a percentage of the **Input Shape**’s length.

**Length** - Set the length of the path that will be used (1 = full length).

**Use Rotation** - Align the duplicated Shapes along the normals of the path.

**Flip** - Reverse the direction of the path.

chunks.title: Path Distribution
chunks.heading: Path Distribution > Path Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Exclude End** - When checked, the end of an open path is ignored. This is the equivalent of increasing the Count by 1 but removing the last point.

**Offset** - Offset points around the path.

chunks.title: Point Distribution
chunks.heading: Point Distribution > Point Distribution > Intro
chunks.text: Distribute points at 0,0. This can be useful when assigning **Shape Positions** via external sources like [Spreadsheet](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/) data or a [Value2 Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/value2-array/).

chunks.title: Random Distribution
chunks.heading: Random Distribution > Random Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Shape** - Set the Shape to distribute points within.

**Size** - Set the size for the **Shape**.

**Count** - Set the number of points.

**Seed** - Set the random seed.

**Use Probability** - Position points based on a **Probability** value.

**Probability** - The higher the value the more likely it will return 'true'. For example, [connecting](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) a [Material Sampler](/docs/nodes/behaviours/material-sampler/) or [Image Sampler](/docs/nodes/utilities/image-sampler/) to this attribute with a greyscale image or gradient would mean that the points are more likely to be scattered in the lighter areas.

Points positions are biased towards the higher values in the gradient.

**Threshold** - Set clip values [low, high]. Using the example above, a **Threshold** of `L = 0` and `H = 1` would mean the full range of dark and light values are used. Any **Probability** values outside of this threshold are skipped.

**Relax** - When checked, the points will try to move away from each other.

**Relax Distance** - Set the distance the points are trying to move away from each other.

chunks.title: Random Distribution
chunks.heading: Random Distribution > Random Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Max Iterations** - Set how many times the relax algorithm is run. A higher number is more accurate but slower.

**Keep Shape** - When checked, any points positioned outside of the **Size** parameters will be culled.

chunks.title: Rose Distribution
chunks.heading: Rose Distribution > Rose Distribution > Intro
chunks.text: Distribute points in a [rose pattern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_(mathematics)).

chunks.title: Rose Distribution
chunks.heading: Rose Distribution > Rose Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Count** - Set the number of points.

**Radius** - Set the radius of the rose.

**Seed** - A mathematical rose can be thought of as a drawing machine. The X and Y values represent the radii for each gear of such a machine.

**Length** - A distance along the rose shape (1 is full distance).

chunks.title: Shape Edges Distribution
chunks.heading: Shape Edges Distribution > Shape Edges Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Distribution Shape** - Add the path to distribute points along.

**Use Rotation** - Align the points along the normals of the **Distribution Shape**.

**Fill All** - Distribute a point on every edge of the Distribution Shape.

**Count** - Set the number of points.

**Edge Bias** - Move points along the edge's length.

chunks.title: Shape Points Distribution
chunks.heading: Shape Points Distribution
chunks.text:
* * Layers* General* Distribution Types* Shape Points Distribution

On this page

chunks.title: Shape Points Distribution
chunks.heading: Shape Points Distribution > Shape Points Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Distribution Shape** - Add the path to distribute points along.

**Fill All** - Distribute a point on every vertex of the **Distribution Shape**.

**Count** - Set the number of points.

Example

1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. `Option/Alt` + click on the icon in the **Fill** tab to disable Fill.
3. `Option/Alt` + click on the icon in the **Stroke** tab to enable Stroke.
4. Set:
   1. **String** to `a`.
   2. **Font Size** to `600`.
   3. **Alignment** to **Centre**.
   4. **Vertical Alignment** to **Middle**.
5. Create an Ellipse.
6. Set its **Radius** to `5,5`.
7. With the Ellipse selected, click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) button in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
8. Set the **Distribution** to **Shape Points**.
9. Drag the **Text Shape** from the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) into the **Distribution Shape** control.

chunks.title: Shuffle Distribution
chunks.heading: Shuffle Distribution > Shuffle Distribution > Intro
chunks.text:
Distribute points by rearranging the Ids of a sub-mesh.

Check out Kyle Daily's tutorial.

chunks.title: Shuffle Distribution
chunks.heading: Shuffle Distribution > Shuffle Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Input Distribution** - Connect a sub-mesh to affect the ids of.

**Reverse** - Reverse the ids.

**Shuffle** - Randomise the ids.

**Seed** - Set the random seed.

Before (left) and after (right) shuffling a Distribution.

Shuffling does not affect the draw order of each id. Notice in the image above that `id0` has remained behind and `id8` on top.

chunks.title: Sort Distribution
chunks.heading: Sort Distribution > Sort Distribution > Intro
chunks.text:
Distribute points by reordering the Ids of another Distribution.

Check out Kyle Daily's tutorial.

chunks.title: Sort Distribution
chunks.heading: Sort Distribution > Sort Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Input Distribution** - Set or connect a Distribution to affect the Ids of.

**Mode** - Choose from the following options:

* **Horizontal** - Sort the Ids from left to right. For example, `Id0` will be set to the point furthest to the left.
* **Vertical** - Sort the Ids from bottom to top. For example, the lowest point will be set to `Id0`.
* **Distance from Centroid** - Sort the Ids from the centroid of the Input Distribution. For example, the point nearest the centroid will be set to `Id0`.
* **Target** - Sort the Ids based on the position of another Shape. For example, the point nearest the Target will be set to `Id0`.

**Target** - Connect a shape to be used as a **Target**.

**Reverse** - Invert the result depending on the **Mode**.

chunks.title: Sub-Mesh Distribution
chunks.heading: Sub-Mesh Distribution > Sub-Mesh Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Input Shape** - Connect a sub-mesh (Duplicator/ Type/ SVG) to place Shapes on to.

**Fill All** - Automatically set the **Count** to the number of sub-meshes.

**Count** - Set the number of points.

**Scale To Fit** - When used with the Duplicator, scale the Shapes to the size of the sub-meshes.

**Scale Multiplier** - When used with the Duplicator, scale all duplicated Shapes.

**Keep Aspect Ratio** - When scaling, maintain the aspect ratio of the **Input Shape**.

**Ignore Empty Sub-Meshes** - If parts of the sub-mesh are empty, do not distribute points on to those parts.

chunks.title: Transform Distribution
chunks.heading: Transform Distribution > Transform Distribution > Intro
chunks.text: Distribute points onto the position of a Layer with a transform (Shape/Null/Falloff).

chunks.title: Voxelize Distribution
chunks.heading: Voxelize Distribution > Voxelize Distribution > UI
chunks.text:
**Input Path** - Set the Shape(s) to be voxelized.

**Size** - Set the size of a voxel.

**Screen Space** - When checked the entire screen is voxelized with the Input Path being used as a ‘clipping mask’. The Input Path can then travel through the voxelized space.

chunks.title: JavaScript Layers
chunks.heading: JavaScript Layers > JavaScript Layers > Intro
chunks.text:
JavaScript can be used on various Layers including the [JavaScript Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/javascript-utility/), [JavaScript Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/javascript-shape/), [JavaScript Deformer](/docs/nodes/behaviours/javascript-deformer/), [JavaScript Emitter](/docs/nodes/utilities/javascript-emitter/), [JavaScript Modifier](/docs/nodes/utilities/javascript-modifier/) and [JavaScript Emitter](/docs/nodes/utilities/javascript-emitter/) to set many attribute types in Cavalry.

The primary data types that can be written from an expression are:

chunks.title: JavaScript Layers
chunks.heading: JavaScript Layers > JavaScript Layers > Intro

chunks.title: JavaScript Layers
chunks.heading: JavaScript Layers > JavaScript Layers > Intro
chunks.text: |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Color** `color` An attribute containing `R`, `G`, `B` and `A` values.| **Point Data** `pointData` Points generated by [Distributions](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/). See [Using Point data](#using-point-data).| **Asset** `assetId` Accepts a `.json`, `.txt` or `.csv` Asset. See [Using Assets](#using-assets).| **Layer** `layerId` Accepts any Layer. See [Using Layer data](#using-layer-data). | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

chunks.title: JavaScript Layers
chunks.heading: JavaScript Layers > JavaScript Layers > Intro
chunks.text:
This means that Layers that support JavaScript can be connected to any of the above data types in Cavalry.

Connecting two incompatible data types (e.g the expression returns an `int`, but the JavaScript is connected to a `string`), will trigger an attempt to automatically convert the data type however, matching the outputs correctly is highly recommended to provide better control over factors like floating point precision.

All of the above types are also available as inputs and can be referenced by their attribute name in the script. To add another attribute as a variable hit the `+` button at the bottom of the UI and choose the relevant data type. An input connection can then be made from another attribute with a matching data type. By default, the variable names are the letter `n` followed by a number, e.g `n0`, `n1`. However, these can be renamed by right clicking on the attribute and choosing `Rename`.

Variable Names

Variable names are case sensitive and must **not** contain spaces.

JavaScript imports a [Context Module](/docs/tech-info/scripting/context-module/) which contains several useful members for use with a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).

chunks.title: JavaScript Layers
chunks.heading: JavaScript Layers > JavaScript Layers > Intro

chunks.title: JavaScript Layers
chunks.heading: JavaScript Layers > JavaScript Layers > Intro
chunks.text: When setting variables at the global level, use `var` rather than `let`/`const`. Because JavaScript Layers run every frame, using `let`/`const` globally will fail because when the expression runs for a second time, the variable will already exist and can't be reassigned.

chunks.title: JavaScript Layers
chunks.heading: JavaScript Layers > JavaScript Layers > Using Assets

chunks.title: JavaScript Layers
chunks.heading: JavaScript Layers > JavaScript Layers > Using Assets

chunks.title: JavaScript Layers
chunks.heading: JavaScript Layers > JavaScript Layers > Using Point data
chunks.text:
1. Create a [JavaScript Deformer](/docs/nodes/behaviours/javascript-deformer/).
2. Click the `+` button towards the bottom of its Attribute Editor UI, add choose 'Add Point Data' to add a new Dynamic Attribute.
3. Create a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).
4. Right click on the **Distribution** attribute and choose `Reveal Generator`.
5. Delete the Duplicator (leaving the Grid Distribution).
6. Connect gridDistribution.id→javaScriptDeformer.n1 (this is the new Point Data attribute added in step 2).
7. Replace the code in the JavaScript input with either:
   * `console.log(n1.points[0].position.x);` or;
   * `console.log(n1.points.length);`
8. Create a Shape.
9. Connect javaScriptDeformer.id→shape.deformers. This is required for the JavaScript Deformer to calculate.

Step the playhead to the next frame to print the values to the [JavaScript Console](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/javascript-console/). The first example will output the first pointId's position.x (change the value in [0] to return other pointIds) whereas the second will return the number of points in the Distribution (9 for a default 3x3 grid).

chunks.title: JavaScript Layers
chunks.heading: JavaScript Layers > JavaScript Layers > Using Layer data
chunks.text:
The connected Layer's type determines which objects are available:

* **Drawable** (e.g. Null, Falloff) - a **layer** object will become available with the following 2D World Space Transform variables:
  + **position** (e.g. `n1.layer.position`, `n1.layer.position.x`)
  + **rotation** (e.g. `n1.layer.rotation`, `n1.layer.rotation.z`)
  + **scale** (e.g. `n1.layer.scale`, `n1.layer.scale.x`)
* **Shape** (e.g. Rectangle, Duplicator) - a `mesh` property (e.g `n1.mesh`) becomes available, representing the mesh hierarchy in local space. The `mesh` property is an instance of the [Mesh class](/docs/tech-info/scripting/cavalry-module/#mesh-class) from the [Cavalry Module](/docs/tech-info/scripting/cavalry-module/).

When using a **Layer** dynamic input, use `hasInput` to determine if a Layer is connected or not. For example, this can be used to prevent attempting to read non-existent mesh data.

```
// Assuming 'n1' is a Layer dynamic input.

console.log(n1.hasInput);

// Returns true if a Layer is connected 'n1'.
```

2D vs 2.5D rotation

JavaScript does not distinguish between 2D and 2.5D Layers so use `rotation.z` for 2D Layers.

chunks.title: Motion Blur
chunks.heading: Motion Blur > Motion Blur > Intro
chunks.text:
Motion blur is used to mimic the effect of a physical camera (and the human eye). Rapid movement will appear streaked over a single exposure (or frame) depending on the shutter speed. A slower shutter speed results in a longer exposure resulting in a blurrier image.

In computer animation, a lack of motion blur can result in fast moving objects appearing stepped or staggered. This can be prevented by adding motion blur.

To enable motion blur for a Shape, load its UI into the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) and choose an motion blur type from the **Motion Blur** drop down under the **Shape** tab.

chunks.title: Motion Blur
chunks.heading: Motion Blur > Motion Blur > Motion Blur Types > Full
chunks.text:
**Full** Motion blur is recommended where Shapes are being deformed or animated using [Path Animation](/docs/nodes/shapes/editable-shape/). This includes Deformers that 'transform' Shapes like [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) or [Auto-Animate](/docs/nodes/behaviours/auto-animate/).

To enable **Full** Motion Blur for a [Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/) it must be enabled in two places:

1. Enable **Motion Blur** via the icon at the top of the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/). It can also be enabled via the [Composition Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/) which can be accessed via the cog icon at the top of the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/). Open the window and check the **Motion Blur** attribute.
2. Enable **Motion Blur** on the Shape. This can be done via the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/). Load a Shape's UI and choose **Full** from the **Motion Blur** drop down under the **Shape** tab.

chunks.title: Motion Blur
chunks.heading: Motion Blur > Motion Blur > Motion Blur Types > Full
chunks.text:
Further options are available in the [Composition Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/) window to fine tune how **Motion Blur** behaves.

info

Motion Blur must be turned on in the [Composition Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/) for any Shapes with **Full** Motion Blur enabled to appear blurred. Disabling Motion Blur in the Composition Settings will turn off **Full** Motion Blur for all Shapes.

chunks.title: Motion Blur
chunks.heading: Motion Blur > Motion Blur > Motion Blur Types > Transform Only
chunks.text:
**Transform Only** motion blur is more performant than **Full** motion blur but does not support Deformers or [Path Animation](/docs/nodes/shapes/editable-shape/). It's recommended to use **Transform Only** motion blur where only a Shape's transform (Position/Rotation/Scale/Pivot/Skew) is animated. It can also be used with [Camera](/docs/nodes/utilities/camera/) animation.

To enable **Transform Only** Motion Blur for a [Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/):

* Load a Shape's UI into the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) and choose **Transform Only** from the **Motion Blur** drop down under the **Shape** tab.

Further options are available via the cog icon to fine tune how **Motion Blur** behaves:

chunks.title: Motion Blur
chunks.heading: Motion Blur > Motion Blur > Motion Blur Types > Transform Only
chunks.text:
* **Blend Mode** - Set the [blend mode](/docs/nodes/general/blend-modes/) for how the motion blurred samples combine with the Shape.
* **Strength** - Determines the mix of blurred and un-blurred samples (or output and input).
* **Blur Centre** - Affects whether the blur is backward or forward of the current frame. The default of 0 will centre it on the frame (the motion blur will be even in both directions of travel).
* **Samples** - Determine how many times the motion blur is sampled. A higher number will result in a smoother blur but also comes with a performance penalty.
* **High Quality Samples** - When checked, sub-steps are calculated between frames. This can be useful to create a more precise blur for very fast animation with sudden changes in direction over individual frames.

chunks.title: Vector artwork support
chunks.heading: Vector artwork support > Vector artwork support > Intro
chunks.text: Cavalry supports importing and exporting SVG artwork meaning it's possible to copy/paste SVG code from other vector apps like Adobe Illustrator, Affinity and Figma.

chunks.title: Vector artwork support
chunks.heading: Vector artwork support > Vector artwork support > Import
chunks.text:
As well as importing [SVG](/docs/nodes/shapes/svg-shape/) as an **Asset**, `.svg` files can be imported and converted when dragging or pasting them into the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

Dragging an **SVG** file from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) or file system into the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) or pasting SVG data via the clipboard will invoke a pop-up dialogue with two options:

* **Asset Layer** - Create an **SVG** layer and connect the `.svg` asset to the **File** attribute.
* **Separate Layers** - Separate the `.svg` asset into individual layers, convert each one into an [Editable Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/editable-shape/) and set the **Fill** and **Stroke** to match.

info

Hold `Option/Alt` when dragging an SVG asset from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) or file system into the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) or [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/) to bypass the modal and **Separate Layers**.

chunks.title: Vector artwork support
chunks.heading: Vector artwork support > Vector artwork support > Import > Copy and Paste SVG data
chunks.text:
It's possible to copy/paste SVG code from other vector apps like Adobe Illustrator, Affinity and Figma.

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Application Instructions|  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Adobe Illustrator** **Edit > Copy** (`Cmd/Ctrl` + `C`)| **Figma** Right click on a path and select **Copy/Paste as > Copy as SVG**.| **Affinity** **Edit > Copy** (`Cmd/Ctrl` + `C`). Ensure **Copy Items as SVG** is checked in Settings > General > Miscellaneous | | | | | | | |

chunks.title: Vector artwork support
chunks.heading: Vector artwork support > Vector artwork support > Export
chunks.text:
Cavalry Compositions can be rendered to SVG via the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/) or via the `File > Render Current Frame to SVG...` menu item.

Cavalry Shapes can also be copied to the clipboard. To copy a Shape to the clipboard as SVG, select a Shape in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) and `right click > Copy as SVG`.

Multiple Shapes

To copy multiple Shapes to the clipboard as SVG data, add them to a [Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/group/) and then copy the Group. Note that the Group's **Blending and Opacity Mode** must be set to **Individual Shapes**.

caution

Support for svg can be a little mixed as it is not a fully featured format. For example, the SVG format has no native support for Inner or Outer Stroke and, as a consequence, different apps have different ways of working around this problem. For this reason parity may not be 100% when exchanging files between applications.

Known issues:

chunks.title: Vector artwork support
chunks.heading: Vector artwork support > Vector artwork support > Export
chunks.text:
* Clipping Paths/Masks/Compound Shapes are not currently supported.
* Gradients are not supported.
* Opacity is not supported.
* Blend Modes are not supported.
* Text is converted to a mesh (it is neither exported or imported as editable Text).
* Only **Centre** aligned Stroke is supported. While inner/outer is supported by the SVG format, they are not supported by most major browsers and so are not supported by Cavalry.

chunks.title: Working with Regex
chunks.heading: Working with Regex > Working with Regex > Intro
chunks.text:
Regular Expressions (shortened to Regex) can be used in various places in Cavalry including the [Regex String Manipulator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-manipulator/regex-string-manipulator/), Material/Style Behaviours like [Apply Font Size](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-font-size/) and the [JavaScript Layers](/docs/nodes/general/javascript-layers/).

Regex is a sequence of characters that specify a search pattern. A common use for regex is to match strings or parts of strings in order to do something with the result. For example, the expression `a+` will return all instances of the letters **a** found within the input string. So an input string of `Cavalry` would return `aa` because it contains two `a`s.

Online platforms like [Regex101](https://regex101.com/) are a great resource for learning and testing regular expressions.

Regex Flavours

[JavaScript Layers](/docs/nodes/general/javascript-layers/) use ECMAScript regex.

Text and Style Behaviours ([Apply Typeface](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-typeface/), [Apply Font Size](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-font-size/), etc.) use ICU regex, which supports [inline flags](#inline-flags) for case-insensitive matching and other options.

chunks.title: Working with Regex
chunks.heading: Working with Regex > Working with Regex > Examples > Use with the Regex String Manipulator
chunks.text:
The [Regex String Manipulator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-manipulator/regex-string-manipulator/) will return only the result of the regular expression.

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| String Regex Description Result|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Hello World. `\s` Remove Spaces HelloWorld.|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | As Capably as Cavalry. `C.....y` 7 letter words that start with **C** and end with **y** CapablyCavalry|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Is it Colour or Color? `Colou?r` Colour or Color ColourColor|  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 3 is the magic number. `\d` Any number 3 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

chunks.title: Working with Regex
chunks.heading: Working with Regex > Working with Regex > Examples > Use with the Style/Material Behaviours
chunks.text:
Style Behaviours ([Apply Typeface](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-typeface/), [Apply Font Size](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-font-size/) and Material Behaviours like [Apply Text Material](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-text-material/)) use the result of the regular expression to affect the font, appearance or character spacing.

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| String Layer Regex Description Result|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | How are you today? [Apply Typeface](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-typeface/) `\b(today)\b` Return the word 'today'. How are you **today**?| Animate in Cavalry [Apply Text Material](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-text-material/) `\b(Cavalry)\b` Return the word 'Cavalry' The word Cavalry will be colored with the Fill | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

chunks.title: Working with Regex
chunks.heading: Working with Regex > Working with Regex > Examples > Use with the Style/Material Behaviours > Capture Groups
chunks.text:
A capture group is a way to store and extract specific parts of the string being matched. Wrapping parts of a regular expression in parentheses creates groups which can then be filtered by entering their Ids into the **Capture Group Indices** attribute.

For example, given the string `hello@cavalry.studio`, the following regular expression can be used to separate the name, domain and top level domain - `\b(\w+)@(\w+)\.(\w+)\b`.

This will save capture groups with their indices set as follows:

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Index Contents|  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 hello|  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 2 cavalry|  |  | | --- | --- | | 3 studio | | | | | | | |

The capture groups can then be used by entering their Ids into the **Capture Group Indices** attribute. For example, entering `2` to an [Apply Typeface](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-typeface/) where a bold typeface is selected would result in - hello@**scenegroup**.co. Alternatively, setting **Capture Group Indices** of `1,3` would result in - **hello**@scenegroup.**co**.

chunks.title: Working with Regex
chunks.heading: Working with Regex > Working with Regex > Examples > Use with the Style/Material Behaviours > Capture Groups
chunks.text: Entering a value of `0` or leaving the **Capture Group Indices** attribute empty will return the full match.

chunks.title: Working with Regex
chunks.heading: Working with Regex > Working with Regex > Inline Flags
chunks.text:
Inline flags modify how the regex engine matches patterns by placing them at the start of an expression. These flags are supported in all Style and Material Behaviours.

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Flag Name Description Example|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `(?i)` Case Insensitive Matches regardless of upper/lower case `(?i)hello` matches "Hello", "HELLO", "hello"| `(?m)` Multiline `^` and `$` match at line boundaries, not just start/end of string `(?m)^Line` matches "Line" at the start of any line| `(?s)` Dot All `.` matches newline characters as well as other characters `(?s)a.b` matches "a", newline, "b"| `(?x)` Comments Allows whitespace and comments in the pattern for readability Useful for complex patterns | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

Flags can be combined: `(?im)` enables both case-insensitive and multiline modes.

chunks.title: Shapes
chunks.heading: Shapes > Shapes > Intro
chunks.text: **Shapes** are Layers that can be drawn in the viewport and animated using keyframes and/or [Behaviours](/docs/nodes/behaviours/).

chunks.title: Shapes
chunks.heading: Shapes > Shapes > Intro > Shapes
chunks.text:
A Shape is a type of Layer that contains a **Mesh** which can be styled using a **Fill** and **Stroke**.

Examples of Shape Layers in Cavalry are [Basic Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/), [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) and the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).

The [Particle Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/particle-shape/) is an outlier to this definition in order to handle high particle counts in a performant way.

A '**Shape**' can take two forms in Cavalry:

* **Shape** - A Shape contains custom attributes that can be edited to change its [Path](#paths). For example, a [Rectangle](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/rectangle/) includes a **Size** (Width/Height) attribute or the [Ellipse](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/ellipse/) includes a **Radius** attribute.
* **Editable Shape** - An [Editable Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/editable-shape/) is a non-procedural Shape containing an [Editable Path](#editable-paths) which can be edited using the [Edit Shape](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/edit-shape-tool/) tool.

chunks.title: Shapes
chunks.heading: Shapes > Shapes > Intro > Meshes
chunks.text:
A **Mesh** is a container made up of the following components:

* **Transform** - its Position, Rotation, Scale and Pivot.
* **Fill** - the color used to fill the inside of a closed path.
* **Stroke** - the color used for the outline of a path.
* **Path** - a geometry primitive made up of lines and curves. A Path can contain multiple **Contours** – parts of the Path that are not connected to each other.
* **Child Meshes** - children of the parent Mesh.

Meshes can contain children so that they can form hierarchies. For example, a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) contains a child for each line, then word and then character. Because each Mesh has its own Transform, Fill and Stroke, this is what makes it possible to animate Text on a per line/word/character basis.

* Text Shape
  + Line
    - Word
      * Character

A [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) Deformer can be used to edit each child-mesh by setting the depth within the hierarchy to affect. This idea also applies to a Mesh's **Fill**, **Stroke** and **Transform**.

Mesh Explorer

chunks.title: Shapes
chunks.heading: Shapes > Shapes > Intro > Meshes
chunks.text: The [Mesh Explorer](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/mesh-explorer/) can be used to expose a Shape's hierarchy and provide an understanding of the effect other Layers that can manipulate its child-meshes will have.

chunks.title: Shapes
chunks.heading: Shapes > Shapes > Intro > Paths
chunks.text:
A Path is a geometry primitive made up of lines and curves. It’s possible to have several unconnected contours inside a Path making features like holes possible. The lines and curves that form a Path can be made up of various different types of béziers, straight lines, or special signifiers which close a contour, or start a new one.

A Path is optimised for realtime drawing and so differs to an [Editable Path](#editable-paths) in that it cannot be edited by moving points in the viewport. A Path should be converted to an [Editable Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/editable-shape/) via the Shape Menu to allow for direct manipulation and **Path Animation**.

Paths and Editable Paths have a different appearance in the Viewport when selected using the [Edit Shape](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/edit-shape-tool/) tool. An Editable Path will display larger points to indicate they can be manipulated.

A Path (left) and Editable Path (right) when selected with the Edit Shape tool.

chunks.title: Shapes
chunks.heading: Shapes > Shapes > Intro > Editable Paths
chunks.text:
An **Editable Path** is part of a special type of Shape Layer called an [Editable Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/editable-shape/). It is a geometry primitive constructed using [Editable Points](#editable-points) to dictate the shape of the path. A [Path](#paths)'s shape is described by lines and curves with control points (a **curve** centric primitive), whereas an **Editable Path**'s Shape is described by points with handles (a **point** centric primitive). This distinction is what makes Editable Paths easier to work with as artistically, paths are generally thought of in terms of points with bézier handles rather than curves.

The purpose of an **Editable Path** is to make it easy and intuitive to draw and edit paths in the Viewport via the [Edit Shape](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/edit-shape-tool/) tool.

Because an Editable Path is an abstracted representation of the actual optimised Path being rendered in the Viewport, it's possible for a Path's visible point count to differ from its actual point count. Take this example of a simple triangle:

chunks.title: Shapes
chunks.heading: Shapes > Shapes > Intro > Editable Paths
chunks.text:
A triangle with **3** points is actually constructed from **4** points behind the scenes with the first and last point positioned in the same location.

A Shape with **3** visible points which also includes bézier points is actually constructed of **8** points.

This is important to understand if using the [Mesh Explorer](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/mesh-explorer/) to check the **Point Count** for a Shape.

chunks.title: Shapes
chunks.heading: Shapes > Shapes > Intro > Editable Points
chunks.text:
Editable Points dictate the shape of an Editable Path through various positions and settings:

* Position
* In Handle Position
* Out Handle Position
* Weight Locked
* Gradient Locked

When both **In Handle** and **Out Handle** are not set, a Point is treated as a **Corner Point**.

Point Count vs pointId

Note that **Point Count** and **pointId** should not be confused. **pointId** can be used by other Layers (Duplicator, Constraints, etc.) to position Shapes on the points of other Shapes. The first **pointId** is `pointId0` and increases in the direction of the Path based on the points that are visible in the Viewport – handles are ignored.

chunks.title: Cogwheel
chunks.heading: Cogwheel > Cogwheel > UI > Gear Example
chunks.text:
All rotation is driven by the medium Cogwheel.

In order to create a gear system there are some basic guides to follow:

* The **Module** of each Cogwheel must match. The module is a ratio which can be easily expressed as:
  Module=2∗PitchRadius/NumberOfTeethModule = 2 \* Pitch Radius / Number Of TeethModule=2∗PitchRadius/NumberOfTeeth
* The teeth must be the same shape/size.
* The **Pitch Circle** of each Cogwheel must be 'touching'.

In the example below:

* the **Medium** Cogwheel has a **Pitch Radius** of **200** and **12 Teeth**.
* the **Small** Cogwheel has a **Pitch Radius** of **100** and **6 Teeth**.
* the **Large** Cogwheel has a **Pitch Radius** of **400** and **24 Teeth**.

`200 / 12`, `100 / 6` and `400 / 24` all equal `16.66` so each Cogwheel has the same **Module**.

The math for the rotation is also quite simple. If:

* **r1** = Rotation of the Medium Cogwheel
* **t1** = Number of Teeth of the Medium Cogwheel
* **r2** = Rotation of the Small Cogwheel
* **t2** = Number of Teeth of the Small Cogwheel

r2=r1∗t1/t2r2 = r1 \* t1 / t2r2=r1∗t1/t2

In the case of **Medium** > **Small** that would be:

r2=r1∗12/6r2 = r1 \* 12/6r2=r1∗12/6

chunks.title: Cogwheel
chunks.heading: Cogwheel > Cogwheel > UI > Gear Example
chunks.text:
A [Jsmath](/docs/nodes/utilities/js-math/) Utility can be used to rig this equation up.

1. Create a [Jsmath](/docs/nodes/utilities/js-math/) Utility.
2. Add the expression `-n0 * n1/n2`
3. Add 3 indices.
4. Connect Medium.rotation→jsmath.index0
5. Connect Medium.teeth→jsmath.index1
6. Connect Small.teeth→jsmath.index2
7. Connect jsmath.id→Small.rotation

As he **Medium** Cogwheel rotates, the **Small** Cogwheel will rotate at the correct speed so they both mesh with each other. In order to position them correctly, move them 300 apart in X (the total of their **Pitch Radius** values).

chunks.title: Super Shape
chunks.heading: Super Shape > Super Shape > Intro
chunks.text:
Create an Super Shape primitive as part of a [Basic Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/).

The Super Shape is based on the 'superformula' –  a mathematical formula introduced by Johan Gielis that can generate a wide variety of shapes by adjusting its parameters.

chunks.title: Super Shape
chunks.heading: Super Shape > Super Shape > UI
chunks.text:
**Radius** - Set the outer radius of the circle the Shape is drawn within.

**Complexity** - Determines the number of 'petals' or 'lobes' in the shape. Increasing this increases the complexity of the shape. While any integer can be used, a value of 1 or any even number will produce the most visually pleasing shapes.

**n1** - Control the overall shape of the figure. It can make the Shape more circular or more star-like.

**n2** - Determines the sharpness of the edges. Higher values result in more defined edges.

**n3** - Similar to n2, this affects the sharpness of the edges but in a different direction.

**a** - A scaling factor that stretches or compresses the shape along the x-axis.

**b** - A scaling factor that stretches or compresses the shape along the y-axis.

**Divisions** - Set the number of divisions between points. This is particularly useful for creating smoother deformations.

**Randomise** - Click this to iterate through a random assignment of values for each attribute.

info

The For the record, it's even numbers, along with 1, that work well for this shape.

chunks.title: Cel Animation Shape
chunks.heading: Cel Animation Shape > Cel Animation Shape > Intro
chunks.text: The **Cel Animation Shape** can be used to create frame-by-frame animation. Rather than creating keyframes to animate a Shape, each frame is a new Shape.

chunks.title: Cel Animation Shape
chunks.heading: Cel Animation Shape > Cel Animation Shape > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Path** - Each keyframe represents a new frame. Where frames do not contain a keyframe, the Shape contained within the previous keyframe is drawn.

**Fill Rule** - Determine how holes are created when multiple Contours exist in one Editable Shape:

* **Even Odd** - Any Contour that intersects with another Contour will create a hole.
* **Winding** - In order to create a hole, an intersecting Contour must be drawn in the opposite direction to another.

**Onion Skinning** - When checked, the frames before or after the current frame are previewed in the Viewport. Ensure the [Onion Skinning](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#onion-skinning) Viewport option is also enabled.

**Frame tools**:

* **Keyframe** - Add a keyframe containing the contents of the previous keyframe.
* **Copy to Next** - Copy the contents of the current frame, move the timeline forward one frame and paste the contents into it.
* **Clear Key** - Create a blank keyframe or clear the contents of an existing keyframe.

Example

chunks.title: Cel Animation Shape
chunks.heading: Cel Animation Shape > Cel Animation Shape > UI
chunks.text:
1. Click the **Cel Animation Shape** icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
2. Draw in the Viewport with the [Pencil](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pencil-tool/) tool (auto selected).
3. Move forward one frame (`Cmd/Ctrl` + `⮕``).
4. Draw again.
5. Repeat steps 3-4!

When a new frame is created in the Cel Animation Shape, a new shape is created for that frame - the Paths are not being animated. it's possible to copy one frame to another and then move its points but each frame is a new 'drawing' and can have completely unique artwork including multiple paths if required.

If a frame is left empty it is considered a 'hold frame' and the previous frame containing any shape information will be drawn. To add a blank frame then an empty keyframe must be created – se **Clear Key** above.

Original artwork - https://dribbble.com/shots/6505762-Dust-Smoke

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Shapes)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Shapes) > Common Attributes (Shapes) > UI
chunks.text:
* Shape* Fill* Stroke* Masks* Advanced

**Position** - Set the Shape's position. 0,0 is in the centre of the Composition.

**Rotation** - Set the Shape's rotation (in degrees).

**Scale** - Set the Shape's scale.

**Skew** - Slant or shear the Shape along the X or Y axis.

**Pivot** - Define the pivot point for the shape. This is useful when animating rotation and scale.

**Opacity** - Set the Shape's opacity.

**Blend Mode** - Set the [blend mode](/docs/nodes/general/blend-modes/).

**Deformers** - A list of connected Deformers. Use the + button to create and connect a Behaviour or drag and drop an existing one to connect it.

**Filters** - A list of connected [Filters](/docs/nodes/effects/). Use the + button to create and connect a Filter or drag and drop an existing one to connect it.

**Motion Blur** - Enable/disable [motion blur](/docs/nodes/general/motion-blur/):

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Shapes)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Shapes) > Common Attributes (Shapes) > UI
chunks.text:
* **None** - No motion blur.
* **Full** - Enable [Full](/docs/nodes/general/motion-blur/#full) motion blur. Ensure **Motion Blur** is also enabled for the Composition by either clicking the icon at the top of the **Scene Tree** or checking Motion Blur in the [Composition Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/) window.
* **Transform Only (Fast)** - Enable [Transform Only](/docs/nodes/general/motion-blur/#transform-only) motion blur.

**Fill** - Enable/disable the fill. This can also be set by `Option/Alt` clicking the icon in the tab.

**Color** - Set the Shape's color using Hex or RGB values (only RGB values can be animated). Click the color swatch to set colors using HSV.

Auto-complete Hex

Where hex codes contain repeated sequences of characters or numbers, they will be auto-completed. For example, entering `AB` and then hitting `Return` will result in `#ABABAB`.

**Shaders** - A list of connected [Shaders](/docs/nodes/effects/).

**Alpha** - A master control for the opacity/alpha of the entire shader network.

**Stroke** - Enable/disable the stroke. This can also be set by `Option/Alt` clicking the icon in the tab.

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Shapes)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Shapes) > Common Attributes (Shapes) > UI
chunks.text:
**Color Mode** - Determine how the color is applied to the Stroke:

* **Single Color** - Use a single color.
* **Gradient** - Apply a gradient along the Stroke.

**Color** - When **Color Mode** is set to **Single Color**, set the Shape's color using Hex or RGB values (only RGB values can be animated). Click the color swatch to set colors using HSV.

Auto-complete Hex

Where hex codes contain repeated sequences of characters or numbers, they will be auto-completed. For example, entering `AB` and then hitting Enter will result in `#ABABAB`.

**Shaders** - When **Color Mode** is set to **Single Color**, connect [Shaders](/docs/nodes/effects/) to this list.

**Gradient Mode** - When **Color Mode** is set to **Gradient**, select an interpolation for the **Gradient**. See [Gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/).

**Gradient** - When **Color Mode** is set to **Gradient**, set the colors for that [gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/).

**Alpha** - A master control for the opacity/ alpha of the entire shader network.

**Width** - Set the width of the stroke.

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Shapes)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Shapes) > Common Attributes (Shapes) > UI
chunks.text:
**Cap Style** - Set the appearance of caps (each end of the stroke) on open paths:

* **Flat** - A flat end that terminates at the end point.
* **Round** - A hemispherical end with the end point at its centre.
* **Projecting** - A flat end that projects half the Stroke's **Width** beyond the end point.

Tapered Stroke

Note that **Projecting** caps are not supported when **Tapered Width** is checked. The **Cap Style** will fall back to **Round** in this instance.

**Join Style** - Set the appearance of joints:

* **Mitre** - Sharp corners.
* **Round** - Rounded corners.
* **Bevel** - Beveled/chamfered corners.

**Mitre Limit** - Sets the limit at which a sharp corner is drawn beveled.

**Dash Pattern Mode** - Determine how the **Dash Pattern** values are used:

* **Pixels** - The **Dash Pattern** values are used as lengths in pixels.
* **Percentage** - The **Dash Pattern** values are used as percentages of the length of the Path.

**Dash Pattern** - Enter a number sequence separated by commas. e.g. `dash, gap`. Where a single value is used, that value will be used for both the dash and the gap. e.g. `10` is the same as `10,10`.

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Shapes)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Shapes) > Common Attributes (Shapes) > UI
chunks.text:
**Dash Offset** - Offset the **Dash Pattern** along the path.

**Align** - Align the stroke along the path:

* **Centre** - Align the stroke along the centre of the path.
* **Inner** - Align the stroke along the inside of the path.
* **Outer** - Align the stroke along the outside of the path.

caution

Open paths only support **Centre** alignment. Where multiple contours appear in a single Path, any open contours will be set to **Centre** regardless of the Align setting.

info

If **Align** is set to **Inner** or **Outer** and **Trim** enabled, **closed paths** will be given a **Cap Style** of **Flat** regardless of their setting. Where multiple contours exist in one Shape, any open paths will respect the **Cap Style** setting.

**Trim** - When enabled the controls below are available.

**Start** - Wet the percentage along the Shape the Stroke will start.

**End** - Set the percentage along the Shape the Stroke will end.

**Travel** - Move the Stroke around the Shape.

**Reverse Path** - Reverse the direction of the Stroke.

---

**Tapered Width** - When checked, the Stroke is tapered from the start to end of the contour.

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Shapes)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Shapes) > Common Attributes (Shapes) > UI
chunks.text:
**Start Width** - A multiplier for the Stroke's **Width** at the contour's first point.

**End Width** - A multiplier for the Stroke's **Width** at the contour's last point.

**Double Taper** - When checked, the Taper's **Width** is set to 100% at a point along the contour determined by the **Taper From** attribute. The **Start Width** and **End Width** attributes can then, for example, be set to 0% to create a taper that starts at zero, increases to full width and then reduces to zero again.

**Cap Centres** - Offset the centre of **Round** caps.

**Taper From** - With **Double Taper** checked, set the point along the contour at which the **Width** is set to 100%.

**Middle Length** - Set the length of the Stroke either side of the **Taper From** point where the **Width** is 100%.

---

**Multi Stroke** - Add additional Strokes or Stroke Duplicators.

**Feather** - Add a blurred edge to the Shape.

**Clipping Masks** - Connect Shapes to be used as clipping masks. Clipping Masks are a geometry mask and so use the outline of a shape rather than its colour information.

List UI options:

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Shapes)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Shapes) > Common Attributes (Shapes) > UI
chunks.text:
* **Visibility** - Enable/disable the Clipping Mask.
* **Boolean options**:
  + **Union** - Combines the Shape.
  + **Subtract** - Clips the Shape.
  + **Intersect** - Clips everything outside the Shape.

**Clipping Mode** - Set the anti-aliasing quality for the Clipping Masks:

* **Best** - High quality anti-aliasing.
* **Normal** - Default anti-aliasing.
* **Fast** - No anti-aliasing.

**Feather Clipping Masks** - When checked, the **Feather** value is also applied to any Clipping Masks connected to the Shape.

info

When connecting a Shape as a Clipping Mask, its visibility will be set to hidden.

info

When using a [Composition](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/) as a Mask ensure that the Composition's [Background Alpha](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/) is set to **0** for the Composition bounds to **not** be included in the Mask.

**Track Mattes** - Connect Shapes to be used as track mattes. Track Mattes are image based masks.

List UI options:

* **Visibility** - Enable/disable the Track Matte.

**Track Matte Mode** - Choose an option to define the transparency of the Track Matte:

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Shapes)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Shapes) > Common Attributes (Shapes) > UI
chunks.text:
* **Alpha** - Opaque when the alpha channel's pixel value is 100%.
* **Alpha Inverted** - Opaque when the alpha channel's pixel value is 0%.

caution

It's not possible to use a Shape with a Track Matte as a Track Matte for another Shape.

**2.5D** - When checked, the Shape will draw in 2.5D if a [Camera](/docs/nodes/utilities/camera/) is added to the Composition.

**Lottie Export:**

* **Export if Visible** - Export a Shape if its visibility is set to on.
* **Always Export** - Export a Shape regardless of wether its visibility is set to on or off.
* **Never Export** - Do not export the shape regardless of whether its visibility is set to on or off.

**Lottie Baking:**

* **Automatic** - Automatically calculate if a Shape needs baking based on the connections in the scene.
* **Animated Mesh** - Bake the Shape information out for each frame. Materials will be static and changing point counts are not supported.
* **Animated Mesh & Materials** - Bake each Shape and any materials for every frame.
* **Nuclear** - This is the 'nuclear bake' option designed to work around shortcomings in Lottie.
* **Still** - The Shape will export as a still containing no animation.

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Shapes)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Shapes) > Common Attributes (Shapes) > UI
chunks.text:
**Wireframe** - Display the Shape as a wireframe in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/). This option can also be set by right clicking on a Shape in the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/). When checked, the Shape will not render.

**Hidden** - When checked, the Shape will be hidden from the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/). This is the equivalent of toggling the eye icon in the Scene Tree to off.

**Draw On Top Of Parent** - When checked (default), if the Shape is the child of another Shape, it will draw in front its parent. This is useful for situations where, for example, a character's eyes are the children of its head. Uncheck this to prevent this behaviour. Note that this attribute is ignored if a Shape has 2.5D enabled.

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Shapes)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Shapes) > Common Attributes (Shapes) > UI
chunks.text:
**Freeze Calculations** - When checked, any input connections to the Shape will be paused. This can be used to optimise a Composition where any connections to a Shape are no longer updating. For example, keyframing this attribute from **off** to **on** will prevent any further input calculations to the Shape and instead use the last known value. Reducing unnecessary calculations in this way can result in faster playback for heavier Compositions.

Freeze Calculations

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Shapes)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Shapes) > Common Attributes (Shapes) > UI
chunks.text:
* Checking **Freeze Calculations** blocks any input/downstream connections. Any output/upstream connections will continue to calculate but, because there are less overall calculations to consider, these will also be faster.
* Because any calculation in Cavalry is ultimately only required to render a Shape, **Freeze Calculations** only affects Shapes.
* Transformations (position, rotation, scale etc) have very little impact on performance and so freezing a Shape will not prevent it from transforming.
* **Freeze Calculations** is hierarchical. That means that if a parent is frozen then any child Shapes will also be frozen.
* **Freeze Calculations** is not supported when used on Shapes in **Composition References** (aka Pre-Comps).

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Shapes)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Shapes) > Common Attributes (Shapes) > UI
chunks.text:
In the image below, imagine **Freeze Calculations** has been keyframed from **off** on frame 24 to **on** on frame 25. At frame 25 the Duplicator will stop calculating the radii of the Ellipses which are being driven by the Noise. Even if the Noise had stopped changing at frame 25, Cavalry would still continue to 'listen' for any changes so, while the Shapes are not changing, playback might be affected. By checking Freeze Calculations any 'listening' is paused and so performance is greatly improved.

**Vertical Layout Alignment** - When a Shape is part of a [Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layouts-intro/), set the vertical alignment within its cell:

* **Ignore** - Respect the Shape's alignment (do not set any custom alignment).
* **Top** - Align the Shape to the top of its cell.
* **Middle** - Align the Shape to the middle of its cell.
* **Bottom** - Align the Shape to the bottom of its cell.

**Horizontal Layout Alignment** - When a Shape is part of a [Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layouts-intro/), set the horizontal alignment within its cell:

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Shapes)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Shapes) > Common Attributes (Shapes) > UI
chunks.text:
* **Ignore** - Respect the Shape's alignment (do not set any custom alignment).
* **Leading** - Align the Shape to the left of its cell.
* **Centre** - Align the Shape to the middle of its cell.
* **Trailing** - Align the Shape to the right of its cell.

**Exclude From Layout** - When checked, if a Shape is part of a [Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layouts-intro/), prevent it from being included in the layout's calculations. This can be useful for debugging layouts. Making a connection from **Exclude From Layout** to the **Hidden** attribute will result in the Shape also being hidden from the Viewport if preferred.

**Layout Based on Size at Frame** - When checked, the bounding box of a Shape that's part of a [Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layouts-intro/) can be set based on its size on a specific frame.
