**Layout Frame** - When **Layout Based on Size at Frame** is checked, set the frame to set the bounding box of a Shape that's part of a [Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layouts-intro/). This is useful to isolate the effect an animated Shape can have on a Layout Group.

chunks.title: Common Attributes (Shapes)
chunks.heading: Common Attributes (Shapes) > Common Attributes (Shapes) > UI
chunks.text:
**Scheduling Group Mode** - Determine the Shape's behaviour when part of a [Scheduling Group](/docs/nodes/utilities/scheduling-group/):

* **Use** - This Layer is used by Scheduling Group.
* **Ignore** - This Layer is excluded by Scheduling Groups.
* **Use Children** - This Layer is excluded, but its children are used.

**Guide Layer** - Determine whether or not a Shape is visible when rendered to file or when its parent Composition is a Layer within another Composition (Pre-Comp):

* **Off** - Do not set the Shape as a Guide Layer.
* **On (Visible in Pre-Compositions)** - A Shape **will** be visible when part of a Pre-Comp but **will not** appear when rendering to file.
* **On (Invisible in Pre-Compositions)** - A Shape **will not** be visible when part of a Pre-Comp and **will not** appear when rendering to file.

chunks.title: Component
chunks.heading: Component > Component > Intro
chunks.text:
Components are Layers that contain a collection of other Layers. Attributes from those Layers can be promoted to the Component in order to create a custom user interface.

By making other Layers children of a Component, those Layers can be hidden by the Component to create a simplified user interface. See [Edit Component](#edit-component).

Collapsing a Component to filter the promoted controls.

Supported Attributes

Any Attribute that can create a connection can be used within a Component.

Quick Start

1. Create a **Component**.
2. Create a **Rectangle**.
3. In the Attribute Editor, drag a connection from the Rectangle's **Size** attribute to the purple area at the top of the Component's UI in the **Control** tab.
4. Make the **Rectangle** a child of the **Component** in the Scene Window.
5. In the Attribute Editor, right click the **Size** attribute and choose **Rename**.
6. Give the attribute a custom label.
7. In the Attribute Editor, right click the Component's header.
8. Choose **Component** and uncheck **Edit Component**.
9. In the Attribute Editor, right click the Component's header.
10. Choose **Component** and check **Compact Layout**.

chunks.title: Component
chunks.heading: Component > Component > Intro
chunks.text: The Component's UI will simplify and the Rectangle will be hidden from the Layer stack.

chunks.title: Component
chunks.heading: Component > Component > UI > Edit Component
chunks.text:
Components have two modes that can be accessed by right clicking the Layer's header in the Attribute Editor and choosing from the options in the **Component** menu.

* **Checked** - Attributes from other Layers can be added to the Component. Any Layers that are children of the Component are visible in the Scene Window.
* **Unchecked** - Any Layers that are children of the Component are hidden from the Scene Window and adding or removing Attributes from other Layers is prevented.

chunks.title: Component
chunks.heading: Component > Component > UI > Add an Attribute to a Component
chunks.text: To add an attribute to a Component, in the Attribute Editor, drag a connection from a Layer's attribute to the purple area at the top of the Component's UI in the **Control** tab.

chunks.title: Component
chunks.heading: Component > Component > UI > Remove an Attribute from a Component
chunks.text:
To remove an attribute from a Component either:

* Right click on the attribute in the Component's **Control** tab and choose **Remove from Component**.
* Use the connection icon from the source attribute.

Custom Labels

Attribute labels can be customised by right clicking on an attribute and choosing 'Rename'.

chunks.title: Composition
chunks.heading: Composition > Composition > Intro
chunks.text:
The stage to compose Layers on.

To create a Composition either:

* Click the  button in the footer of the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).
* Drag an Asset in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) and drop it onto the  button.
* Via the `Composition > New Composition` menu.

To open a Composition, double click one in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).

Presets

Use a [Preset](/docs/user-interface/general/presets/) to set custom defaults (Resolution, Frame Rate etc.) for a new Composition.

It's possible to have multiple Compositions open at the same time but only one can be set as the active Composition. Use the tabs that appear at the top of the Scene Window to navigate between open Compositions.

chunks.title: Composition
chunks.heading: Composition > Composition > UI
chunks.text:
To load a Composition's UI, drag it from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) into the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).

**Position** - Set the Composition's position. 0,0 is in the centre of the Composition.

**Rotation** - Set the Composition's rotation. (in degrees).

**Scale** - Set the Composition's scale.

**Pivot** - Define the pivot point for the Composition. This is useful when animating rotation and scale.

**Opacity** - Set the Composition's opacity.

**Blend Mode** - Set the [Blend mode](/docs/nodes/general/blend-modes/).

**Deformers** - A list of connected Deformers.

**Filters** - A list of connected Filters.

**Motion Blur** - Enable [Motion Blur](/docs/nodes/general/motion-blur/).

**Preserve Frame Rate** - Where a Composition is used as a [Pre-Comp](#pre-comp), checking this will maintain its Frame Rate. For example, where a 12fps Composition is a Pre-Comp within a 24fps Composition, checking Preserve FPS will ensure the Pre-Comp plays back at 12fps. With this unchecked, Cavalry will re-interpolate the Pre-Comp's frame rate to match its parents 24fps frame rate.

chunks.title: Composition
chunks.heading: Composition > Composition > UI
chunks.text:
Composition Settings

Use these attributes to animate the Composition or affect its appearance. To adjust settings like **Resolution** or **Frame Rate** see [Composition Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/).

chunks.title: Composition
chunks.heading: Composition > Composition > Pre-Comp
chunks.text: A Composition used as a Layer within another Composition is also known as a **Pre-Comp**. Several Pre-Comps can be added to another Composition as a way to create copies with a single 'source of truth' – any changes made to the original Composition will propagate through to all its Pre-Comps.

chunks.title: Composition
chunks.heading: Composition > Composition > Pre-Comp > Create a Pre-Comp
chunks.text:
To create a Pre-Comp either:

* Drag a Composition from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) into the Viewport or Scene Tree into another Composition.
* Select several Layers within an existing Composition and either:
  + Right click > Pre-Compose Selection.
  + Use the `Composition > Pre-Compose` menu.

See [Pre-Comp Overrides](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/pre-comp-overrides/) for a method to use Compositions as a way to create editable 'templates'.

Where a **Pre-Comp** already exists in a **Composition**, it's possible to swap its reference to a different Composition in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/). To do this either:

chunks.title: Composition
chunks.heading: Composition > Composition > Pre-Comp > Create a Pre-Comp
chunks.text:
* Hold `Option/Alt`, drag a **Composition** from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) and drop it onto a **Pre-Comp**'s row in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) or;
* Select several **Pre-Comps** in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) and then, holding `Option/Alt`, drag a **Composition** from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) and drop it into the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).

Set a Pre-Comp as the Active Composition

Either clicking the `Open` button or `Option/Alt` + `Cmd/Ctrl` + double clicking a Composition Layer's row in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) will open that **Composition** (making it the active Composition).

note

The only way to create a new **Composition** is via the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) or the menus. It cannot be created via the [Add Layers Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/add-layers-window/).

chunks.title: Pre-Comp Overrides
chunks.heading: Pre-Comp Overrides > Pre-Comp Overrides > Intro
chunks.text:
A Composition used as a Layer within another Composition is also known as a Pre-Comp. Several Pre-Comps can be added to another Composition as a way to create copies with a single 'source of truth' – any changes made to the original Composition will propagate through to all of its Pre-Comps.

**Pre-Comp Overrides** can be used to promote a Layer's attributes so they can be accessed and overridden from the Pre-Comp itself. This makes it possible to add variation to several versions of the same Pre-Comp.

[Referencing→](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/referencing/)

Supported Attributes

A **Pre-Comp Override** can be added to any Attribute that can be keyframed with the exception of drop-downs.

Quick Start

chunks.title: Pre-Comp Overrides
chunks.heading: Pre-Comp Overrides > Pre-Comp Overrides > Intro
chunks.text:
1. In the Assets Window, rename the default Composition to "Pre-Comp".
2. Open the [Composition Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/) and set the **Resolution** to **500,500**.
3. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
4. Set the Text's **Alignment** to **Centre**.
5. In the Attribute Editor, right click on the **String** attribute and choose **Add Pre-Comp Override**.
6. Create a second **Composition** and name it "Main".
7. With the **Main** Composition active, drag **Pre-Comp** from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) into the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).
8. Duplicate **Pre-Comp** in the Scene Window (to create a Layer called **Pre-Comp 1**).
9. Move them apart so you can see both of them in the Viewport.
10. Double click or drag **Pre-Comp 1** from the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) into the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).
11. Open the **Overrides** tab.
12. Enter "Override" into the **String** attribute.
13. Double click either **Pre-Comp** to

chunks.title: Pre-Comp Overrides
chunks.heading: Pre-Comp Overrides > Pre-Comp Overrides > Intro
chunks.text:
load its parent Composition.
14. Change the Text Shape's **Font**.
15. Load the **Main** Composition.

chunks.title: Pre-Comp Overrides
chunks.heading: Pre-Comp Overrides > Pre-Comp Overrides > Intro
chunks.text:
The **Font** for both Pre-Comps has updated but the strings retain their overrides.

Two copies of the same Pre-Comp with overrides added.

chunks.title: Pre-Comp Overrides
chunks.heading: Pre-Comp Overrides > Pre-Comp Overrides > UI > Add/Remove Overrides
chunks.text:
To add a **Pre-Comp Override**:

1. Select an Attribute or multiple Attributes.
2. Right click on any selected Attribute's row.
3. Choose **Add Pre-Comp Override**.

To remove a **Pre-Comp Override**:

1. Select an Attribute or multiple Attributes with an Override.
2. Right click on an Attribute's row.
3. Choose **Remove Pre-Comp Override**.

If an attribute has a **Pre-Comp Override** applied, a purple dot will appear on the control row to signify this.

chunks.title: Pre-Comp Overrides
chunks.heading: Pre-Comp Overrides > Pre-Comp Overrides > UI > Setting Overrides
chunks.text:
Double click a **Pre-Comp** in the Scene Window to load it into the Attribute Editor, right click on an Attribute's row in the **Overrides** tab and choose **Override** to reveal the following options:

* **Reveal the Origin Layer** - Open the origin Composition and load the Attribute's parent Layer into the Attribute Editor.
* **Remove this Pre-Comp Override** - Remove the Pre-Comp Override. This is the equivalent of following the steps [above](#addremove-overrides) to remove a Pre-Comp Override.
* **Reset Value to Origin** - Reset the Attribute value to the one set in the origin Composition.

info

Note that **Reveal the Origin Layer** and **Remove this Pre-Comp Override** are not available when a Composition has been imported as a [Reference](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/referencing/).

chunks.title: Pre-Comp Overrides
chunks.heading: Pre-Comp Overrides > Pre-Comp Overrides > UI > Reorder Overrides
chunks.text: If a Composition contains Layers with Pre-Comp Overrides, a cog icon will appear on its row in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/). Clicking the cog will reveal a list of all the attributes with Pre-Comp Overrides. These can then be drag/dropped to customise the order they will appear in the **Overrides** tab of a Pre-Comp's Attribute Editor UI.

chunks.title: Pre-Comp Overrides
chunks.heading: Pre-Comp Overrides > Pre-Comp Overrides > UI > Naming Overrides
chunks.text:
By default, a Pre-Comp Override's label will appear as `layerNiceName`.`attrNiceName`. For example, if the **Position** Attribute of a Layer called **MyLayer** has been set as a Pre-Comp Override, it will appear as `MyLayer.Position` in the **Overrides** tab of a Pre-Comp.

Where a custom name is required, an Attribute can be renamed by [right clicking](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-interaction/#contextual-menu) an Attribute's label in the Attribute Editor and choosing `Rename...`. In this scenario, the label will appear as simply `attrNiceName`. For example, if the **Position** Attribute of a Layer called **MyLayer** has been renamed to '**My Custom Label**' and set as a Pre-Comp Override, it will appear as `My Custom Label` in the **Overrides** tab of a Pre-Comp.

chunks.title: Connect Shape
chunks.heading: Connect Shape > Connect Shape > Intro
chunks.text:
Connect distributions of points to create intricate patterns of lines.

Connect Shape connects the points generated by a [Distribution](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/) with straight or curved lines.

chunks.title: Connect Shape
chunks.heading: Connect Shape > Connect Shape > UI
chunks.text:
* Shape* Source* Target

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Mode** - Set the mode for the connections.

* **Within Range** - Create connections if points fall within a **Search Distance**.
* **Nearest** - Connect the **Source** points to the **Target** points closest to them.
* **Point Index** - Connect the point index of the **Source** to the **Target**.

**Time Offset** - Connect a Behaviour to this attribute (such as a Stagger) to offset any animation you have on the connection lines (e.g Stroke trim).

**Search Distance** - When points come within this range they will connect (depending on other settings).

**Connection Limit** - Set the maximum number of connections that can be made.

**Per Point Connection Limit** - Set the maximum number of connections that can be made from each point.

**Skip Points** - Ignore every nth point.

**Skip Offset** - Offset the skip by this value.

**Line Type** - Set the type of line for the connections:

* **Linear** - Create connections with straight lines.
* **Auto Bézier** - Create connections with curved lines.

**Auto Bézier Mode**:

chunks.title: Connect Shape
chunks.heading: Connect Shape > Connect Shape > UI
chunks.text:
* **Smooth** - Set equal bézier handles to form a shoulder shape at both ends of the connection.
* **Shoulder Target** - Set the bézier handles to form a shoulder shape at the target end of the connection.
* **Shoulder Source** - Set the bézier handles to form a shoulder shape at the source end of the connection.
* **Projection Vectors** - Project bézier control points towards a target. `0,0` is used if no **Projection Vector Target** is specified.

**Control Point Bias** - Adjust the shape of the bezier curves.

**Projection Vector Target** - Connect a Shape to use as a target when **Auto Bézier Mode** is set to **Projection Vectors**.

**Source Distribution** - Set the [Distribution Type](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/) to position the source points.

**Ignore Target Distribution** - When checked, the **Source** points will connect to each other rather than looking for a **Target**.

**Target Distribution** - Set the [Distribution Type](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/) to position the target points.

tip

chunks.title: Connect Shape
chunks.heading: Connect Shape > Connect Shape > UI
chunks.text: Set the **Source/Target Distribution** to **Sub-Mesh** and connect a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) as the **Input Shape** in order to draw the distributed points.

chunks.title: Convex Hull
chunks.heading: Convex Hull > Convex Hull > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Input Shapes** - Connect the shapes to draw a Convex Hull around.

**High Quality** - When enabled the resulting Shape will support **Input Shapes** containing bézier and/or quadratic curves.

Example

1. Create 2 [Polygons](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/).
2. Add some position keyframes to them both.
3. Create a **Convex Hull**.
4. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) the 2 polygons to the **Input Shapes** attribute.
5. Hit play.

Using a Duplicator as an Input Shape.

chunks.title: Corner Pin
chunks.heading: Corner Pin > Corner Pin > Intro
chunks.text:
The Corner Pin deforms a Shape and can be used to create the illusion of 3d perspective.

Photograph by Yüksel Göz via Unsplash

chunks.title: Corner Pin
chunks.heading: Corner Pin > Corner Pin > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Bind** - When checked, the Shape is deformed depending on the position of the Nulls. When unchecked, its **Size** can be adjusted.

**Size** - Set the dimensions of the Corner Pin Shape. This can be used as a guide

**Top Left** - Connect a transform (defaults to a Null).

**Top Left Offset** - Offset the connected transform.

**Top Right** - Connect a transform (defaults to a Null).

**Top Right Offset** - Offset the connected transform.

**Bottom Left** - Connect a transform (defaults to a Null).

**Bottom Left Offset** - Offset the connected transform.

**Bottom Right** - Connect a transform (defaults to a Null).

**Bottom Right Offset** - Offset the connected transform.

**Bind Selected Shape** (button) - Move each corner to the bounding box of the first selected Shape and Bind it to the Corner Pin.

Example

chunks.title: Corner Pin
chunks.heading: Corner Pin > Corner Pin > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a second Composition (Composition 2).
2. Double click Composition 2 in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) to load it into the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).
3. Set its **Resolution** to 600 x 800px via the [Composition Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/).
4. Add some Shapes to Composition 2 (as artwork).
5. Double click Composition 1 in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) to load it into the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).
6. Create a **Corner Pin**.
7. Uncheck **Bind**.
8. Set the **Width** and **Height** to `600` and `800`.
9. Move the **Nulls** to each corner of the Corner Pin Shape (use **Bounding Box** [Viewport Snapping](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#snapping) to help).
10. Check **Bind**.
11. Drag **Composition 2** from the **Assets Window** into the **Scene Window** and drop it on to the **Corner Pin** (the Shape, not the Group) to make it a child of the Shape.
12. With the Select tool, move the Nulls.

note

chunks.title: Corner Pin
chunks.heading: Corner Pin > Corner Pin > UI
chunks.text: Check out some example Scenes from [scenery.io](https://scenery.io/?node=cornerPinShape).

chunks.title: Custom Shape
chunks.heading: Custom Shape > Custom Shape > Intro
chunks.text: The Custom Shape is a Shape that inherits the properties of another Shape. It can be used to create 'instances' of other meshes.

chunks.title: Custom Shape
chunks.heading: Custom Shape > Custom Shape > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Bake Transform** - When checked, the Input Shape's transform will be applied to the Custom Shape's output meaning that if the Input Shape is e.g. scaled, the Custom Shape will output accordingly. This can also be used as a method to retain **Stroke Width** when scaling.

**Input Shape** - [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) a Shape to be instanced.

Example

1. Draw an Editable Shape with the Pen tool.
2. Create a **Custom Shape**.
3. Connect editableShape.id→customShape.inputShape.
4. Set the Custom Shape's **Scale X** to `-1`
5. With the Edit Shape tool, move the points on the Editable Shape.

The **Custom Shape** is now a mirror of the **Editable Shape**.

chunks.title: Duplicator
chunks.heading: Duplicator > Duplicator > Intro
chunks.text:
The Duplicator can be used to copy and distribute Shapes to create grids, circles and other patterns.

See Create > Demo Scenes > Generative Art > Axonometric

chunks.title: Duplicator
chunks.heading: Duplicator > Duplicator > UI
chunks.text:
* Shape* Advanced

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Input Shapes** - Connect Shapes to be duplicated. See [Input List](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-types/#input-list).

**Distribution** - Determine the layout of the duplicates. See [Distribution Types](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/).

**Shape Position** - Set positions on a per duplicate basis.

**Shape Rotation** - Set rotations on a per duplicate basis.

**Shape Scale** - Set scales on a per duplicate basis.

**Shape Visibility** - Set visibility on a per duplicate basis.

**Shape Opacity** - Set opacity on a per duplicate basis.

**Auto Id** - Automatically cycle through all of the Ids in the **Input Shapes** list.

**Shape Id** - Set the Id of the **Input Shape(s)** to be distributed. 0 is the first Id.

**Shape Time Offset** - Offset the animation curve for duplicates on a per shape basis. *Tip - connect a Stagger Behaviour.*

tip

chunks.title: Duplicator
chunks.heading: Duplicator > Duplicator > UI
chunks.text:
When using a **Stagger** Behaviour with **Shape Time Offset** you can use a negative **Minimum** value to ensure the animation starts at frame 0. e.g. use a **Minimum** of **-50** to offset the animation over 50 frames.

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Use Index Context** - When checked, the Duplicator will pull [Context](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/context/). This can be used to control how Ids are assigned when a Duplicator is the Input Shape to another Duplicator.

**Index Context** - Connecting this output to another layer will output the index for each duplicate at the relevant 'upstream depth'. See [Context](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/context/) for more information.

**Skip Invisible Duplicates** - When checked, the meshes for any duplicates hidden by **Shape Visibility** will also be removed. This will also effect the Duplicator's bounding box and can be used to optimise heavier Scenes.

Input Shape - Transforms

chunks.title: Duplicator
chunks.heading: Duplicator > Duplicator > UI
chunks.text:
In order to avoid the confusion that could be caused by Shapes not appearing at their expected place when part of a **Duplicator**, the transform information of an **Input Shape** is ignored. 'Transform information' includes the **Position**, **Rotation**, **Scale**, **Skew** and **Pivot** attributes of any Shape.

In the situation where a Shape with a **Position** of `100,100` is connected as the **Input Shape** of a **Duplicator**, that position will be ignored and reset to `0,0`. The result is that each duplicate is placed at the same position of each distributed point rather than offset by its `100,100` position. This is designed to prevent any confusion that might be introduced by adding offsets accidentally.

chunks.title: Duplicator
chunks.heading: Duplicator > Duplicator > UI
chunks.text:
This only applies to the parent Shape, the transform information of any of the Shape's children will be respected. This idea can be used to override the built in functionality via hierarchies. In the example below, the **Group** is connected as the **Input Shape** of the Duplicator and the **Shape** is a child of the Group. In this scenario the Shape's **Position** of `100,100` will be passed through which results in each duplicate being offset from the Duplicator's points by that amount. The Group remains at 0,0 but the Shape's position within the Group is respected.

* **Group** - the transform is ignored.
  + **Shape** - the transform is respected.

The Shapes are offset from the Duplicator's points (in red).

This technique can also be used to pass any transform **animation** through to the Duplicator. By adding an animating Shape to a Group and then adding that Group to a Duplicator, the Group will be positioned on a point and the Shape will then move around within the Group.

The animated Shapes move relative to the Duplicator's static points (in red).

chunks.title: Editable Shape
chunks.heading: Editable Shape > Editable Shape > Intro
chunks.text:
An Editable Shape is a non procedural shape which can be created using the [Pen](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pen-tool/) or [Pencil](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pencil-tool/) tools as well as by converting any of the procedural Shapes using the **Shapes > Make Editable** command (`Cmd/Ctrl` + `E`). They can also be created via the [Toolbar](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/toolbar/) by checking **Make Editable Primitives** in the tool options at the top.

Path Animation

You can animate the vertices of an **Editable Shape** using keyframes and the [Edit Shape tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/edit-shape-tool/). Also known as path animation.

1. Draw a Shape with the [Pen](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pen-tool/) tool (this creates an **Editable Shape**).
2. In the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/), click the keyframe icon on the **Path** attribute.
3. Move the timeline to a different frame.
4. With the [Edit Shape](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/edit-shape-tool/) tool, move any of the Shape's points in the Viewport.

chunks.title: Editable Shape
chunks.heading: Editable Shape > Editable Shape > Intro
chunks.text: Two keyframes will have been created in the Scene Window and, when scrubbing the timeline, the shape will animate. Any further changes made to the Shape's points will create new keyframes (or update existing ones).

chunks.title: Editable Shape
chunks.heading: Editable Shape > Editable Shape > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Path** - Once a keyframe is created any changes you make to the Shape's vertices will create new keyframes and the vertices will transform to each position between keyframes.

Path animation

Use the `Animate Path` button on an Editable Shape's row in the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/) to set an initial **Path** keyframe. The same button can be used to remove any keyframes if required.

**Fill Rule** - Determine how holes are created when multiple Contours exist in one Editable Shape:

* **Even Odd** - Any Contour that intersects with another Contour will create a hole.
* **Winding** - In order to create a hole, an intersecting Contour must be drawn in the opposite direction to another.

**Onion Skinning** - When checked the frames before or after the current frame are previewed in the Viewport. Ensure the [Onion Skinning](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#onion-skinning) Viewport option is also enabled.

chunks.title: Extract Sub-Meshes
chunks.heading: Extract Sub-Meshes > Extract Sub-Meshes > Intro
chunks.text:
Create a Shape by extracting specific child-meshes from another Shape. Any materials and animations are also copied across to the resulting **Extract Sub-Meshes** Shape.

This can be used to:

* Extract different sections of a Duplicator and place them within a [Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layouts-intro/).
* Extract part of a Duplicator to redistribute certain Ids using an [Apply Distribution](/docs/nodes/behaviours/apply-distribution/).
* Extract the Shapes contained within a Pre-Comp.

chunks.title: Extract Sub-Meshes
chunks.heading: Extract Sub-Meshes > Extract Sub-Meshes > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Input Shape** - Connect a Shape to extract the child-meshes from. See [Input List](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-types/#input-list).

**Indices** - The indices of the Shape to extract. The Ids can be seen in the [Mesh Explorer](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/mesh-explorer/) or by using the **Draw Debug Information** option in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

**Level Mode** - The level to extract the child-meshes from.

**Ignore Empty Sub-Meshes** - When extracting meshes - ignore any Ids that are empty.

Example

1. Create an **Ellipse**.
2. With the Ellipse selected, click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
3. Create an **Extract Sub-Meshes**.
4. Connect duplicator.id→extractSubMeshes.inputShape.
5. Hide the **Duplicator**.

Just the first and last indices of the Duplicator are extracted because those are the default indices specified. Try replacing `first,last` in **Indices** with `0:3` or `3, 6, 8`.

Materials

chunks.title: Extract Sub-Meshes
chunks.heading: Extract Sub-Meshes > Extract Sub-Meshes > UI
chunks.text: Materials are copied from the **Input Shape** but can be replaced by checking **Fill** or **Stroke** in the corresponding tabs in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).

chunks.title: Extrude
chunks.heading: Extrude > Extrude > Intro
chunks.text: Extrude Shapes to give the appearance of depth. For example, connecting an ellipse to an Extrude will create a cylindrical shape.

chunks.title: Extrude
chunks.heading: Extrude > Extrude > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Input Shapes** - Connect Shapes to be extruded. See [Input List](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-types/#input-list).

**Extrude Distance** - Set the distance of the extrusion.

**Extrude Angle** - Set the angle for the extrusion.

**Level Mode** - These presets set the Level value for you. See [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) for more info.

* **Custom...** - Manually set a **Custom Level**.
* **Text (Lines)** - Sets a Level value of 1.
* **Text (Words)** - Sets a Level value of 2.
* **Text (Characters)** - Sets a Level value of 3.
* **All** - Affects all sub-meshes, regardless of Level.

**Custom Level** - Manually set the Level value.

**Combine Meshes** - When checked, the individual meshes drawn to create the overall Shape are combined into a single mesh. When adding a Stroke to the Extrude this will isolate the Stroke to the outside edges. This can also be useful in order to remove the hairline gaps that can sometimes be visible between the meshes.

chunks.title: Extrude
chunks.heading: Extrude > Extrude > UI
chunks.text:
**Cap End** - When checked, a cap will be added to the end of the extrusion. This can be useful in order to remove the hairline gaps that can sometimes be visible between the meshes.

**Back-face Culling** - When checked, parts of the extrusion that are not visible wil not be drawn.

Example

1. Create an **Extrude**.
2. Create a **Polygon**.
3. Connect polygon.id→extrude.inputShapes.

chunks.title: Footage Shape
chunks.heading: Footage Shape > Footage Shape > Intro
chunks.text: A **Footage Shape** is created when dragging an image/video from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) or file system into the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) or [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/). It differs from a [Basic Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/) in that it inherits the size of the footage used to create it with.

chunks.title: Footage Shape
chunks.heading: Footage Shape > Footage Shape > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Shrink** - Decrease/increase the bounds of the image.

**Size** - A read only attribute with the dimensions of the image.

caution

The only way to create a **Footage Shape** is to drag an image from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) or file system into the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) or [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/). It cannot be created via the [Add Layers Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/add-layers-window/).

chunks.title: Collision Events
chunks.heading: Collision Events > Collision Events > Intro
chunks.text:
**Collision Events** can be used in combination with a [Forge Dynamics](/docs/nodes/shapes/forge-dynamics/forge-dynamics-shape/) simulation to change the appearance or properties of Shapes when they are involved in a collision with other Shapes.

They can be added via the [Add Layers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/add-layers-window/) window or via the `+` icon when viewing the settings under the **Bodies** tab of a [Forge Dynamics Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/forge-dynamics/forge-dynamics-shape/).

chunks.title: Collision Events
chunks.heading: Collision Events > Collision Events > Types of Collision Events
chunks.text:
[Body Setting Collision Event](/docs/nodes/utilities/body-settings-collision-event/) - Change the Density/ Friction/ Bounce etc of Shapes when they collide.

[Color Collision Event](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-collision-event/) - Change the Color of Shapes when they collide.

[Impulse Collision Event](/docs/nodes/utilities/impulse-collision-event/) - Add additional forces to Shapes when they collide.

[Sticky Collision Event](/docs/nodes/utilities/sticky-collision-event/) - Stick Shapes to each other when they collide.

[Visibility Collision Event](/docs/nodes/utilities/visibility-collision-event/) - Affect the Visibility of Shapes when they collide.

chunks.title: Constraints
chunks.heading: Constraints > Constraints > Intro
chunks.text:
**Constraints** can be used in combination with a [Forge Dynamics](/docs/nodes/shapes/forge-dynamics/forge-dynamics-shape/) simulation to bind the positions of Shapes.

They can be added via the [Add Layers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/add-layers-window/) window or via the `+` icon when viewing the settings under the **Bodies** tab of a [Forge Dynamics Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/forge-dynamics/forge-dynamics-shape/).

chunks.title: Constraints
chunks.heading: Constraints > Constraints > Types of Constraints
chunks.text:
[Bridge Constraint](/docs/nodes/utilities/bridge-constraint/) - Chain Shapes together.

[Distance Constraint](/docs/nodes/utilities/distance-constraint/) - Constrain Shapes to their original positions.

[Pin Constraint](/docs/nodes/utilities/pin-constraint/) - Fix Shapes to their position.

chunks.title: Fields
chunks.heading: Fields > Fields > Intro
chunks.text: Fields can be used to influence how Shapes move within a Forge Dynamics simulation.

chunks.title: Fields
chunks.heading: Fields > Fields > Types of Fields
chunks.text:
[Attractor Field](/docs/nodes/utilities/attractor-field/) - Pull or push Shapes towards or away from a target.

[Buoyancy Field](/docs/nodes/utilities/buoyancy-field/) - Create fluid containers within which dynamic bodies will float or sink based on their density.

[Direction Field](/docs/nodes/utilities/direction-field/) - Create a directional force to push Shapes along.

[Drag Field](/docs/nodes/utilities/drag-field/) - Apply a force counter to the Shapes' positional and rotational velocities.

[Path Field](/docs/nodes/utilities/path-field/) - Apply path following forces to dynamics bodies.

[Vortex Field](/docs/nodes/utilities/vortex-field/) - Apply spiral forces to rotate dynamic bodies around a centre point.

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > Intro
chunks.text:
Forge Dynamics is a 2d physics engine built on the amazing [Box2D](https://box2d.org/) by [Erin Catto](https://twitter.com/erin_catto)

Getting started with Forge Dynamics

Testing with a Starter licence

It's possible to test **Forge Dynamics** with a **Starter** licence by using the examples via the **Create > Demo Scenes > Dynamics** menu or the [Try Pro](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/#try-pro--pro-features) button. While it will be possible to experiment with the feature, saving and rendering will be blocked. See [Licence Types](/docs/tech-info/licensing/licence-types/#compatibility) for more information.

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > UI
chunks.text:
* Shape* Mask* Bodies* Initial State* Advanced

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Start Frame** - Set a frame for the simulation to start on.

**Gravity** - Set a strength for gravity.

**Ground Mode** - Determine how the simulation should react to the Composition boundary.

* **Off** - Ignore the Composition edges.
* **Composition Bottom** - Collide with the bottom of the Composition.
* **Composition Edges** - Collide with all edges of the Composition.

**Ground Friction** - Set a value to determine how much friction affects collisions with the Composition edges. A higher friction value will result in shapes losing their speed more quickly.

**Velocity Iterations** - How strongly to correct the forces applied to Shapes. The higher the value the more accurate the result.

**Position Iterations** - How strongly to correct the position of Shapes during collisions in order to reduce overlaps. The higher the value the more accurate the result.

**Fields** - Add a [Field](/docs/nodes/shapes/forge-dynamics/fields/) to the simulation.

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > UI
chunks.text:
**Collision Events** - Add a [Collision Event](/docs/nodes/shapes/forge-dynamics/collision-events/) to the simulation. Collision Events can also be added on a 'per body' basis via the settings under the **Body** tab.

info

Any Collision Events added to a **Body** will override Collision Events added to the **Forge Dynamics Shape**.

See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/)

**Bodies** - Connect Shapes to be included in the simulation. Shapes can be added by dragging them into this attribute via the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/), `right click > Add Body > select Shape` or via a [Connection Anchor](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/).

The list of Bodies includes options to enable/ disable them, set specific settings or remove them from the simulation.

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > Per Body Settings
chunks.text:
* **Input Shape** - The Shape being used as a Body.
* **Friction** - Set a value to determine the friction. A higher **Friction** value will result in Shapes losing their speed more quickly.
* **Bounce** - Set a value to determine how bouncy Shapes are. A higher **Bounce** value will result in Shapes bouncing higher/ further.
* **Density** - Set a value to determine how dense Shapes are. A higher **Density** value will give Shapes a heavier appearance and result in them requiring more force to move.
* **Gravity Scale** - Increase/ decrease the affect the Gravity attribute under the Shape tab has on Shapes. A value of `-1` would invert the Shape's Gravity setting or a value of`2` would double it.
* **Body Type**:
  + **Dynamic** - Bodies will move based on the properties set for the simulation.
  + **Still** - Bodies will remain in place and, while they will be included in collisions, their position or rotation will not be affected.
  + **Kinematic** - A Body's position and rotation will be dictated by any keyframe animation on the **Input Shape**.
  + **Kinematic Hybrid** - A Body's position and rotation will be dictated by any keyframe animation on the **Input Shape** until the la

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > Per Body Settings
chunks.text:
Kinematic Shapes

Only keyframe animation is supported for **Kinematic Shapes**. Procedural animation via Behaviours **is not** supported.

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > Per Body Settings
chunks.text:
* **Constrain Hybrids** - This setting will attach a spring to the Hybrid Body so that when the it comes to the end of its animation it will spring to a stop.
* **Hybrid Frequency** - Set the frequency of the spring in Hz.
* **Hybrid Damping** - Set how quickly the spring comes to a rest. A higher value will result in less secondary motion.
* **Sensor** - A Sensor is a shape that can trigger collision events, but will not trigger collisions.
* **Collision Shape Type** - Set the shape to be used for collisions. These are set automatically using a 'best guess' but can be set manually. Simpler shapes can help improve performance for more complicated scenarios but will decrease the accuracy of the simulation. Collision Shapes can be displayed in the Viewport by selecting a **Forge Dynamics Shape** with **Draw Debug Information** enabled in the [Viewport Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#viewport-settings) (ensure the Layer is unlocked).
  + **Box** - Use the bounding box of the Shape.
  + **Circle** - Use a circle that 'best fits' the Shape.
  + **Simple Polygon** - Use a polygon that 'best fits' the Shape. The polygon of up to a maximum of 12 sides can be used

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > Per Body Settings
chunks.text:
. If a 12 sided polygon can’t be used to approximate the Body then a box will be used instead.
  + **Complex Polygon** - Create a collision shape by dividing the shape up into smaller fixtures (sub-bodies) in order to support **concave** Shapes.
  + **Chain** - Use this setting for open contours/paths. This is a one sided collision and finding the correct setting will depend on how the contour is drawn. As a guide - when selecting a contour with the [Edit Shape](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/edit-shape-tool/) tool, the side of the contour the little arrow indicating the direction appears on, is the side that will collide.
  + **Chain (Reversed)** - Use this setting for open contours/paths. When **Chain** is not working for a contour it's likely that it is 'upside down' and so being excluded from collisions. Try this setting in that situation.
  + **Soft Body** - Use this setting to simulate deformable objects.

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > Per Body Settings
chunks.text:
info

The **Chain** Collision Shape Type is intended for use with open paths. Because open paths have no volume they can't have forces applied and so will always remain static regardless of their **Body Type**. While a closed Path can be set to **Chain**, the same principles apply.

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > Per Body Settings
chunks.text:
* **Max Fixtures Per Body** - When **Collision Shape Type** is set to **Complex Polygon**, set the maximum number of 'fixtures/sub-bodies' to create.
* **Stiffness** - When **Collision Shape Type** is set to **Soft Body**, set the spring frequency in Hz (vibrations per second). Higher values make the soft body stiffer.
* **Damping** - When **Collision Shape Type** is set to **Soft Body**, set the damping ratio to controls how quickly oscillations settle.
* **Pressure** - When **Collision Shape Type** is set to **Soft Body**, set the internal pressure for volume preservation. Higher values push particles outward to maintain the body's shape.
* **Shape Matching** - When **Collision Shape Type** is set to **Soft Body**, set an influence that will move the Soft Body particles back toward their original position helping to maintain shape coherence after collisions deform a Shape.
* **Particle Radius** - When **Collision Shape Type** is set to **Soft Body**, set the size of the particles that are used to simulate the soft body. Smaller values give finer detail but more particles but can also be harder to control.
* **Max Stretch** - When **Collision Shape Type** is set to **Soft Body**,

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > Per Body Settings
chunks.text:
set the maximum allowed stretch of spring connections as a multiple of rest length. Lower values maintain a better shape under impact but may be less flexible. A value of `2` would mean that springs can stretch to double their rest length.
* **Live Forever** - When checked, a Body is always included in the simulation.
* **Lifespan** - Set a duration (in seconds) after which the Body will be removed from the simulation.
* **Starts Asleep** - When checked, the Body will be dormant until another shape collides with it.
* **Allows Sleep** - When checked, a Body will be allowed to sleep when it becomes dormant. This can help performance.
* **Starting Velocity** - Set a velocity to be applied to the Body at the point it first appears.
* **Starting Rotational Velocity** - Set a rotational velocity to be applied to the Body at the point it first appears.
* **Position Damping** - Set damping for the Body's position. A higher value will result in faster declaration.
* **Rotation Damping** - Set damping for the Body's rotation. A higher value will result in faster rotational decelaration.
* **Use Maximum Velocity** - When checked, the velocity of all Bodies will be restricted to the **Maximum

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > Per Body Settings
chunks.text:
Velocity**.
* **Maximum Velocity** - Set the maximum velocity the Bodies can reach.
* **Use Maximum Rotational Velocity** - When checked, the rotational velocity of all Bodies will be restricted to the **Maximum Rotational Velocity**.
* **Maximum Rotational Velocity** - Set the maximum rotational velocity the Bodies can reach.
* **Collision Groups** - Assign collision groups by entering comma separated strings (e.g. `text, rocks`). These can be used to filter the affect Fields have on individual bodies or how bodies interact with other bodies.
* **Collides With** - Enter comma separated strings (e.g. `text, rocks`) to target specific Collision Groups for a body to collide with. The special token `none` can be used to omit a body from any collisions.
* **Level Mode** - choose which level(s) of a sub-mesh to affect. See [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) for more info.
  + **Custom...** - Manually set a **Custom Level**.
  + **Text (Lines)** - Used with a Text Shape, this will affect each **line**.
  + **Text (Words)** - Used with a Text Shape, this will affect each **word**.
  + **Text (Characters)** - Used with a Text Shape, this will affect each **character**.
  + **All

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > Per Body Settings
chunks.text:
** - Affects all sub-meshes, regardless of level.
* **Custom Level** - Manually set a custom level.
* **Constraints** - Add [Constraints](/docs/nodes/shapes/forge-dynamics/constraints/).
* **Collision Events** - Add [Collision Events](/docs/nodes/shapes/forge-dynamics/collision-events/).

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > Global Settings
chunks.text:
**Use Maximum Velocity** - When checked, the velocity of all Bodies will be restricted to a **Maximum Velocity**.

**Maximum Velocity** - Set the maximum velocity the Bodies can reach.

**Use Maximum Rotational Velocity** - When checked, the rotational velocity of all Bodies will be restricted to a **Maximum Rotational Velocity**.

**Maximum Rotational Velocity** - Set the maximum rotational velocity the Bodies can reach.

**Initial Position Strength** - Set a force to attract the Body back to its starting position. Keyframing this attribute can return Bodies back to their start position part way through a simulation.

**Initial Rotation Strength** - Set a force to attract the Body back to its starting rotation. Keyframing this attribute can return Bodies back to their start rotation part way through a simulation.

**Starting Velocity** - Set a velocity to be applied to all Bodies at the point they first appear.

**Starting Rotational Velocity** - Set a rotational velocity to be applied to all Bodies at the point they first appear.

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > Global Settings
chunks.text:
**World Scale** - Use this to adjust the world scale where there are very large or very small Shapes in the simulation to improve the simulation quality.

**Time Step** - Set how many times the simulation is stepped (calculated) per second. A higher value will result in higher quality simulation but may impact performance.

**Cache Solver** (button) - Cache the Forge Dynamics simulation. Cavalry will playback the Playback Range in order to save the cache file to disc. With a cache saved, this button will become an `Update Cache` button. This will overwrite any existing cache in use.

**Remove Cache** (button) - Remove the saved cache file. This **does not** delete the `.sdcache` file from the file system.

**Use File Cache** - When checked, the simulation can be saved to a `.sdcache` file. This can be useful for faster playback with heavier simulations or for retiming via the **Cache Offset**. It is also required for Motion Blur.

**Cache File Path** - Set the location the cache file is saved. This is determined when first caching a solver or use the folder icon to open a Finder/ Explorer window and navigate to an existing `.sdcache` file.

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > Global Settings
chunks.text:
**Cache Offset** - Set a time offset for the cache.

Looping

You can use the cache to 'rewind' a simulation and create a loop if required. To do this:

1. Cache the simulation.
2. Set a keyframe for **Cache Offset** just after the simulation ends.
3. If, for example, that keyframe was set on on frame **100** then move the playhead to frame **200** (e.g. forward another **100** frames) and then add a keyframe with a value of **-200**.

By setting a keyframe at frame 200 with a value of -200 you are effectively asking the cache to show you frame `200 + -200` which `= 0`. e.g. The cache is back to frame 0 (the start).

The table below illustrates how the **Cache Offset** creates the loop back to frame 0.

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Frame Cache Offset Value Equivalent Value|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 0 0 0|  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 100 0 100|  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | | 200 -200 0 | | | | | | | | | | | |

Unsupported features

chunks.title: Forge Dynamics Shape
chunks.heading: Forge Dynamics Shape > Forge Dynamics Shape > Global Settings
chunks.text:
It's not possible to update the geometry of a Shape during the simulation. For example:

* Animating **Scale**.
* Animating the attributes of primitive Shapes (e.g. the **Width** of a Rectangle or the **Radius** of an Ellipse).
* Animating vertices (aka **Path Animation**).
* Using **Deformers**.
* Animating Shapes like [Convex Hull](/docs/nodes/shapes/convex-hull/) or [Connect Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/connect-shape/).

chunks.title: Group
chunks.heading: Group > Group > Intro
chunks.text:
Collect Layers to organise them and/or create a common transform.

Groups are useful to perform several tasks including:

* Transform several Shapes together.
* Organise the Layers in a Composition.
* Pass Shape transforms through to the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) (the Duplicator ignores transforms for Input Shapes by design but by grouping animating objects and then adding the Group as an Input Shape the duplicates will animate).

chunks.title: Group
chunks.heading: Group > Group > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

* **Blending and Opacity Mode** - Determine how Shapes within the Group visually combine with each other:
  + **Artboard** - The Group's **Blend Mode** will only affect the Shapes within the Group – **Opacity** affects all Shapes as one.
  + **Individual Shapes** - The Group's **Blend Mode** will also affect Shapes outside the Group. **Opacity** affects each Shape individually.

Once a Group exists in the Composition, Layers can be dragged in to add them to the Group or dragged out to remove them.

info

Use the `Cmd/Ctrl` + `G` shortcut to group selected Layers. Use `Shift` + `Cmd/Ctrl` + `G` to un-group.

chunks.title: Group
chunks.heading: Group > Group > UI > Interacting with Groups in the Viewport
chunks.text:
* Using the [Select](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) tool, click + drag any Shape within a Group to transform the entire contents of the Group.
* Drill down to select Shapes within the Group's hierarchy by:
  + Double clicking a Shape within the Group.
  + Right clicking a Shape within the Group in the Viewport and choose **Select Hierarchy**. A list of parents within that Shape's hierarchy will be available to select.
  + `S` + click a Shape within a Group to select it directly, regardless of hierarchy level.
* When a Group is selected, a bounding box, annotated with the Group's layer name will appear in the Viewport. Note that this does not apply where non-Group Layers (e.g. Shapes) are parents.
* Non-drawables (e.g Behaviours) that form part of a hierarchy are ignored.

info

Other Shapes at the same hierarchy level as the selected Shape can be selected with a single click.

chunks.title: Image to Shapes
chunks.heading: Image to Shapes > Image to Shapes > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Image** - Connect an image asset. This can be directly from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) or via an [Asset Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/asset-array/) or [Asset from Smart Folder](/docs/nodes/utilities/asset-from-smart-folder/).

**Mode** - Determine the type of shapes to output:

* **Rectangles** - Output rectangles.
* **Circles** - Output circles.

**Iterations** - Set how many times the image is sampled. A higher number will create more shapes and a higher fidelity result.

**Filter** - These settings can improve image quality in both the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) and for renders – particularly when resizing images.

chunks.title: Image to Shapes
chunks.heading: Image to Shapes > Image to Shapes > UI
chunks.text:
* **None (Fastest)** - Use when speed is of paramount importance. No resampling will be performed when the images are resized – this is the lowest quality setting.
* **Bilinear** - Basic resampling is performed. This is low quality but it's very fast.
* **Mipmaps** - Mipmaps are pre-calculated, optimised, low resolution versions of the image created via Bilinear interpolation. These are used to get the best quality and performance when scaling images down.
* **Bicubic** - This is the slowest method but it produces the best quality when scaling images up.

chunks.title: Isolines Shape
chunks.heading: Isolines Shape > Isolines Shape > Intro
chunks.text:
Convert images or Shape Layers into Contours.

A Multi-Point Gradient Shader as the input to the Isoline Shape.

chunks.title: Isolines Shape
chunks.heading: Isolines Shape > Isolines Shape > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Mode** - Determine whether the Contours are generated from an Image Asset or Shape Layer:

* **Image** - Use an Image Asset as the source for the Contours.
* **Shape Layer** - Use a [Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/) (and [Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/)) as the source for the Contours.

**Input Shape** - When **Mode** is set to **Shape Layer**, connect a Shape.

**Input Shape** - When **Mode** is set to **Image**, connect an image asset. This can be directly from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/), via an [Asset Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/asset-array/) or an [Asset from Smart Folder](/docs/nodes/utilities/asset-from-smart-folder/) Utility.

info

**Image** mode is more performant than **Shape Layer** mode, particularly if [Filters](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/) are used. If performance is an issue, consider rendering the **Input Shape** to an image sequence and using that with **Image** mode.

**Looping** - When **Mode** is set to **Image** and **Looping** is checked, any video or image sequences assets will loop.

chunks.title: Isolines Shape
chunks.heading: Isolines Shape > Isolines Shape > UI
chunks.text:
**Levels** - Set the number of Contour levels to create (evenly distributed from black to white).

**Grid Size** - Set the size of the sampling grid size. Smaller values will result in more accurate/detailed results but may affect performance.

**Clean Up Path** - Removes points that are very close together from the output path.

**Output Béziers** - When checked, the output Contours are resampled as bézier curves.

**Filter Path Size** - Remove paths which are smaller than the **Path Size**. A path's 'size' is calculated as the longest dimension (width/height) of its bounding box.

**Path Size** - When **Filter Path Size** is checked, any paths with a 'size' smaller than this value will be removed.

chunks.title: JavaScript Shape
chunks.heading: JavaScript Shape > JavaScript Shape > Intro
chunks.text:
The **JavaScript Shape** is a Shape that can defined via a JavaScript expression.

For more information on how JavaScript can be used across all JavaScript Layers see [JavaScript Layers](/docs/nodes/general/javascript-layers/).

[See JavaScript Layers→](/docs/nodes/general/javascript-layers/)

info

See **Create > Demo Scenes > JavaScript > Heart Path** for an example.

chunks.title: JavaScript Shape
chunks.heading: JavaScript Shape > JavaScript Shape > UI
chunks.text:
* Shape* JavaScript

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/)

Enter the JavaScript expression to create the Shape. A mesh can be defined in [Scripting](/docs/tech-info/scripting/scripting-getting-started/) using the [Path Class](/docs/tech-info/scripting/cavalry-module/#path-class).

info

An equivalent to a **JavaScript Shape** can also be created by connecting a [JavaScript Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/javascript-utility/) to the **Input Shape** of a [Custom Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/custom-shape/).

Copying Shapes

Right clicking on a Shape in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) and choosing `Copy as JavaScript` will copy the Shape's information to the clipboard as JavaScript code.

chunks.title: Layout Shape
chunks.heading: Layout Shape > Layout Shape
chunks.text:
Deprecated Feature

This is a deprecated feature. See [Layouts](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layouts-intro/) for the replacement feature.

chunks.title: Layout Shape
chunks.heading: Layout Shape > Layout Shape > Intro
chunks.text: When you add Shapes to a Layout Shape, the Shapes are stacked next to each other (either vertically, horizontally or in a grid). The Layout Shape's size is then determined by the total size of the Shapes within it. The result is that as you animate a Shape contained in a Layout Shape the others will move in relation to it.

chunks.title: Layout Shape
chunks.heading: Layout Shape > Layout Shape > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Layout** - Select how Shapes are laid out:

* **Grid Layout** - see [Grid Layout](/docs/nodes/behaviours/apply-layout/grid-layout/).
* **Horizontal Layout** - see [Horizontal Layout](/docs/nodes/behaviours/apply-layout/horizontal-layout/).
* **Vertical Layout** - see [Vertical Layout](/docs/nodes/behaviours/apply-layout/vertical-layout/).

**Size** - set the dimensions of the Layout Shape. By default, this is connected to Composition's **Resolution** attribute. To manually set this value, delete this connection.

**Add Spacer** - spacers can be used to create gaps or blank cells in the Layout.

**Layout Items** - drag 'n' drop or connect Shapes to this area.There are further options within the **Layout Items** list. These differ depending on the **Layout** mode selected:

chunks.title: Layout Shape
chunks.heading: Layout Shape > Layout Shape > UI
chunks.text:
* - toggle whether a Shape appears in the Layout or not.
* **Settings**:
  + **Grid Layout**
    - **Column Span** - set how many columns a Shape will span. A setting of 2 will mean a Shape will be placed in a cell 2 columns wide.
    - **Row Span** - set how many rows a Shape will span. A setting of 2 will mean a Shape will be placed in a cell 2 rows tall.
    - **Fixed Position** - set a fixed cell for a Shape to be positioned in.
    - **Position** - set a cell for the Shape to be positioned in. For example, values of 2, 2 will position the Shape in the second column of the second row.
  + **Horizontal Layout**
    - **Baseline** - place Shapes on the baseline. This is useful for aligning Text and Shapes.
    - **Vertical Alignment** - set the vertical alignment for the Shape within its cell.
  + **Vertical Layout**
    - **Horizontal Alignment** - set the horizontal alignment for the Shape within its cell.
* - remove the Shape from the Layout Items.

chunks.title: Grid Layout Group
chunks.heading: Grid Layout Group > Grid Layout Group > Intro
chunks.text:
A **Grid Layout Group** can be used to organise the rows of a [Grid Layout Row](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-row/) into columns to create a grid.

[Introduction to Layouts→](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layouts-intro/)

While a [Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layout-group/) can also be used to create grids using the **Wrap** features, a **Grid Layout Group** can be used where each row requires a specific number of items.

Quick Start

1. Create 3 Shapes.
2. With all 3 Shapes selected, right click in the **Viewport** and choose **Layout > Embed selected in Grid Layout**.

This will create a hierarchy of:

```
Grid Layout Group

┠ Grid Layout Row

┠ Shape1

┠ Shape2

┠ Shape3
```

Rows

A **Grid Layout Group** requires [Grid Layout Row](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-row/)s as children. It is possible to add Shapes directly to a **Grid Layout Group** but without a [Grid Layout Row](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-row/), it’s just a more complex vertical layout.

chunks.title: Grid Layout Group
chunks.heading: Grid Layout Group > Grid Layout Group > Intro
chunks.text:
The columns of a **Grid Layout Group** are defined by the items placed within the [Grid Layout Row](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-row/)s. The number of items in rows do not need to match so one [Grid Layout Row](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-row/) containing 10 items can be nested within a **Grid Layout Group** along with a [Grid Layout Row](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-row/) containing 3 items. [Spacers](/docs/nodes/shapes/spacer/) can be used to create blank layout items within rows to build a grid with even columns.

A Grid Layout Group with Grid Layout Rows containing the same number of Shapes.

A Grid Layout Group with Grid Layout Rows containing a different number of Shapes.

Any Shape placed within a **Grid Layout Group** that is not within a [Grid Layout Row](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-row/) is treated as a full width layout items which spans all columns.

chunks.title: Grid Layout Group
chunks.heading: Grid Layout Group > Grid Layout Group > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

---

**Draw Extents** - When checked, a representation of the **Minimum** and **Maximum Size** will be drawn in the Viewport.

**Minimum Size** - Determine the minimum width and height the Layout occupies when within another Layout.

**Maximum Size** - Determine the maximum width and height Shapes can fill within the layout. Once the total width/height of the Shapes within the Layout Group exceed these values, the Shapes will start to overlap. By default, the **Maximum Size** is connected to the Composition's **Resolution** – remove the connection to set a custom value.

info

If the **Maximum Size** is set to a value less than the **Minimum Size**, the **Maximum Size** will be internally clamped to the **Minimum Size**'s value (and vice versa). This is not reflected in the **Attribute Editor** but can be seen in the **Viewport** with **Draw Extents** checked.

**Margins** - Set the space around the edges (top, bottom, left and right) of the layout.

**Spacing** - Set a space to appear between each layout item.

**Ordering Policy** - Determine the order **Grid Layouts Rows** are laid out within the Grid Layout Group:

chunks.title: Grid Layout Group
chunks.heading: Grid Layout Group > Grid Layout Group > UI
chunks.text:
* **Layer Order** - Order the Grid Layouts Rows based on their order within the Grid Layout Group. The Shape at the top of the hierarchy is considered the first layout item.
* **Alphabetical** - Order the Grid Layouts Rows alphabetically based on their **Layer Name**.
* **Shuffle** - Randomly order the Grid Layouts Rows.

**Flip Order** - Reverse the **Ordering Policy**.

**Shuffle Seed** - Set the random seed when the **Ordering Policy** is set to **Shuffle**.

chunks.title: Grid Layout Row
chunks.heading: Grid Layout Row > Grid Layout Row > Intro
chunks.text:
A **Grid Layout Row** can be used to arrange Shapes in a row for use within a [Grid Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-group/).

[Introduction to Layouts→](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layouts-intro/)

Each item placed under a **Grid Layout Row** will be placed into columns according to the size constraint handed down by the parent Grid Layout Group.

Rows are not influenced by other rows. One **Grid Layout Row** containing 10 items can be nested within a [Grid Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-group/) along with a **Grid Layout Row** containing 3 items. [Spacers](/docs/nodes/shapes/spacer/) can be used to create blank layout items within rows to build a grid with even columns.

caution

A Grid Layout Row is only useful when used in combination with a [Grid Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-group/). Without it, it does nothing.

chunks.title: Grid Layout Row
chunks.heading: Grid Layout Row > Grid Layout Row > Intro > Alignment
chunks.text:
A Shape's alignment within a cell can be set via the **Vertical/Horizontal Layout Alignment** options under its **Advanced** tab. See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) (Advanced tab).

Note that a Text Shape's **Alignment** and **Vertical Alignment** will be overridden by these settings.

chunks.title: Grid Layout Row
chunks.heading: Grid Layout Row > Grid Layout Row > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

---

**Minimum Column Width** - Set a minimum width for each column in the row. Connect a [Value Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/value-array/) to set individual values for each column.

**Ordering Policy** - Determine the order **Shapes** are laid out within the Grid Layout Row:

* **Layer Order** - Order the Shapes based on their order within the Grid Layout Row. The Shape at the top of the hierarchy is considered the first layout item.
* **Alphabetical** - Order the Shapes alphabetically based on their **Layer Name**.
* **Shuffle** - Randomly order the Shapes.

**Flip Order** - Reverse the **Ordering Policy**.

**Shuffle Seed** - Set the random seed when the **Ordering Policy** is set to **Shuffle**.

chunks.title: Layout Group
chunks.heading: Layout Group > Layout Group > Intro
chunks.text:
A **Layout Group** can be used to arrange Shapes in either a horizontal or vertical direction.

[Introduction to Layouts→](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layouts-intro/)

Quick Start

1. Create 3 Shapes.
2. With all 3 Shapes selected, right click in the **Viewport** and choose **Layout > Embed selected in Horizontal Layout**.

Try increasing the width/radius of a Shape.

chunks.title: Layout Group
chunks.heading: Layout Group > Layout Group > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

info

All Shapes have further **Layout Alignment** options under their **Advanced** tab which can be used to refine alignment within their cell.

---

**Direction** - Select the direction for the Layout:

* **Horizontal** - Stack Shapes side by side.
* **Vertical** - Stack Shapes above/below each other.

**Wrap Mode** - Determine what happens when the combined width/height of the Shapes within a Layout Group exceed its size:

* **No Wrap** - Shapes will remain on one row/column.
* **Wrap** - Shapes will wrap to the next row/column.
* **Wrap Reverse** - Shapes will wrap to the previous row/column.

Nested Wrapping

Note that **wrapping** is not currently supported for nested Layout Groups.

**Draw Extents** - When checked, a representation of the **Minimum** and **Maximum Size** will be drawn in the Viewport.

**Minimum Size** - Determine the minimum width and height the Layout occupies when within another Layout.

chunks.title: Layout Group
chunks.heading: Layout Group > Layout Group > UI
chunks.text:
**Maximum Size** - Determine the maximum width and height Shapes can fill within the layout. Once the total width/height of the Shapes within the Layout Group exceed these values, the Shapes will start to overlap. By default, the **Maximum Size** is connected to the Composition's **Resolution** – remove the connection to set a custom value.

info

If the **Maximum Size** is set to a value less than the **Minimum Size**, the **Maximum Size** will be internally clamped to the **Minimum Size**'s value (and vice versa). This is not reflected in the **Attribute Editor** but can be seen in the **Viewport** with **Draw Extents** checked.

**Margins** - Set the space around the edges (top, bottom, left and right) of the Layout.

---

**Spacing** - Set a space to appear between each layout item.

**Spacing Mode** - Determine how items are distributed within the available space:

chunks.title: Layout Group
chunks.heading: Layout Group > Layout Group > UI
chunks.text:
* **Manual Spacers** - See [Spacers](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layouts-intro/#spacers).
* **Flex Start** - Align the items to the left or top of the layout.
* **Flex End** - Align the items to the right or bottom of the layout.
* **Centre** - Align all items to the centre of the layout.
* **Space Between** - Distribute items so that the gap between each item is equal.
* **Space Around** - Distribute items so that each item is surrounded by an equal space or margin.
* **Space Evenly** - Distribute items so that the gap between each item is equal including the edges of the layout.

**Line Spacing** - When **Wrap Mode** is set to **Wrap** or **Wrap Reverse**, set the distance between rows/columns.

**Align Content** - When **Wrap Mode** is set to **Wrap** or **Wrap Reverse**, determine the cross axis alignment for the rows/columns. For example, if **Direction** is set to **Horizontal**, **Align Content** will affect the items vertical alignment:

chunks.title: Layout Group
chunks.heading: Layout Group > Layout Group > UI
chunks.text:
* **Flex Start** - Align the items to the left or top of the layout.
* **Flex End** - Align the items to the right or bottom of the layout.
* **Centre** - Align all items to the centre of the layout.
* **Space Between** - Distribute items so that the gap between each item is equal.
* **Space Around** - Distribute items so that each item is surrounded by an equal space or margin.
* **Space Evenly** - Distribute items so that the gap between each item is equal including the edges of the layout.

---

**Ordering Policy** - Determine the order the Shapes within the Layout Group are laid out:

* **Layer Order** - Order the Shapes from left to right/top to bottom based on their order within the Group. The Shape at the top of the hierarchy is considered the first layout item.
* **Alphabetical** - Order the Shapes alphabetically based on their **Layer Name**.
* **Shuffle** - Randomly order the Shapes.

**Flip Order** - Reverse the **Ordering Policy**.

**Shuffle Seed** - Set the random seed when the **Ordering Policy** is set to **Shuffle**.

tip

chunks.title: Layout Group
chunks.heading: Layout Group > Layout Group > UI
chunks.text: Connect a Shape's **Hidden** Attribute to its **Exclude from Layout** Attribute (Advanced tab) so that when it is hidden in the Viewport, the layout will also update accordingly.

chunks.title: Layouts
chunks.heading: Layouts > Layouts > Intro
chunks.text:
Layouts provide a way to stack Shapes by 'butting' them up against each other. This means that if the bounding box of one Shape in the stack changes, the others will move to accommodate the new space required for that Shape.

This is useful for creating dynamic layouts which need to respond to changes in size as well as being a fun, artistic feature.

chunks.title: Layouts
chunks.heading: Layouts > Layouts > Intro > Creating a Layout
chunks.text:
Layouts can be created by simply adding Shapes to one of the **Layout Group** types:

* [Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layout-group/) - Arrange Shapes in either a horizontal or vertical direction with options to wrap onto multiple rows/columns.
* [Grid Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-group/) - Arrange **Grid Layout Rows** into columns.
* [Grid Layout Row](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-row/) - Arrange Shapes in rows for use in a **Grid Layout Group**.

Quick Start

1. Create 3 Shapes.
2. With all 3 Shapes selected, right click in the **Viewport** and choose **Layout > Embed selected in Horizontal Layout**.

To create a simple horizontal layout:

1. Create 2 Shapes.
2. Create a [Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layout-group/).
3. Select both Shapes in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).
4. Click and drag both Shapes onto the **Layout Group**.
5. Release the mouse.

Both Shapes will be laid out side by side in a horizontal Layout. If the **Width** (Size W) of either Shape is changed, the layout will update accordingly.

chunks.title: Layouts
chunks.heading: Layouts > Layouts > Intro > Creating a Layout
chunks.text:
Layout Groups can be created via the [Add Layers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/add-layers-window/) window like any other Layer but they can also be created using the contextual menus in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) or [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/). Just select several Shapes, right click and choose **Layout > Embed selected in [Horizontal/Vertical/Grid] Layout**.

To remove a Shape from a Layout Group simply drag it out of the Layout Group.

chunks.title: Layouts
chunks.heading: Layouts > Layouts > Intro > Hierarchy
chunks.text:
Layout Groups are hierarchies with Shapes organised from top to bottom of the layer stack. Any child of a **Layout Group** will be included for placement but Shapes deeper than a child (e.g. grandchildren etc.) are ignored.

More complex layouts can be created by nesting Layout Groups within other Layout Groups.

In the example below, 2 **horizontal** Layout Groups are the children of a **vertical** Layout Group which itself is the child of another **horizontal** Layout Group.

Several Layout Groups nested within each other.

Exclude from Layout

A Shape within a Layout Group can be excluded from from the layout by checking **Exclude from Layout** under its **Advanced** tab in the Attribute Editor. See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/).

chunks.title: Layouts
chunks.heading: Layouts > Layouts > Intro > Transforms
chunks.text:
Once a Shape is added to a Layout Group its transforms (position/rotation/scale) can be adjusted meaning that it's possible to animate Shapes within a Layout Group. Note that the layout reads the [Bounding Box](#bounding-box) of a Shape and ignores 'top-level' transforms. So while a Shape may be rotated, the layout itself will not change as the Shape's bounding box has not changed.

Reset Position

When a Shape is added to a Layout Group, its **Position** will be reset to `0,0`. While Shapes do not have to be at 0,0, layouts can start to look broken if Shapes are unintentionally moved.

A Shape's transform will be maintained when removing it from a Layout Group.

chunks.title: Layouts
chunks.heading: Layouts > Layouts > Intro > Bounding Box
chunks.text:
A Shape's **world space bounding box** is used to calculate the space it occupies within the layout. Because the top-level [transforms](#transforms) are ignored, it's necessary for a Shape to be a child of another Shape in order for any transformations to affect the layout's bounding box calculation.

In the example below, because the yellow rectangle is the child of a [Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/group/) (bottom), its rotation changes the bounding box of the Group which, in turn, affects the layout of the other Shapes within the Layout Group.

The rectangle as the child of a Layout Group.

The rectangle as the child of a Group within a Layout Group.

info

Although Shapes below children (e.g. grandchildren etc) are ignored by the layout itself, as part of a hierarchy they are included in the bounding box calculation of their parent which can then affect the layout.

chunks.title: Layouts
chunks.heading: Layouts > Layouts > Intro > Spacers
chunks.text:
[Spacers](/docs/nodes/shapes/spacer/) can be used to fill any available space within layouts and so used to evenly space or align cells to the left/right/top/bottom of layouts.

In the examples below, note how the **Spacer** fills the available space within the layout which then forces the other cells to align themselves accordingly.
