A Spacer placed between the two Shapes.

A Spacer placed below the two Shapes.

To add a [Spacer](/docs/nodes/shapes/spacer/) to a layout simply create one via the [Add Layers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/add-layers-window/) window and drag it into a **Layout Group**.

A [Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layout-group/#ui)'s **Spacing Mode** must be set to **Manual Spacers** for [Spacers](/docs/nodes/shapes/spacer/) to be included in the layout calculation. In any other **Spacing Mode** they are ignored unless they are set to 'Fixed Size'.

chunks.title: Layouts
chunks.heading: Layouts > Layouts > Intro > Alignment
chunks.text:
A Shape's alignment within a cell can be set via the **Vertical/Horizontal Layout Alignment** options under its **Advanced** tab. See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) (Advanced tab).

Note that a Text Shape's **Alignment** and **Vertical Alignment** will be overridden by these settings.

chunks.title: Layouts
chunks.heading: Layouts > Layouts > Intro > Notes
chunks.text:
* A [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) with baseline alignment will be aligned to the bottom of its layout. This means that any descenders will sit outside of its 'cell'.
* A **Layout Group** shares the features of **Groups** so children will inherit any Transforms, Filters or Deformers added to it.
* When creating any of the **Layout Group** types, either via the [Add Layers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/add-layers-window/) window or the contextual menu, they will be **locked** in the Scene Window. This is to prevent adding any unintentional transforms for the Shapes within the Group when interacting with other Shapes in the Viewport.

chunks.title: Merge
chunks.heading: Merge > Merge > Intro
chunks.text:
Create a Shape containing a closed Path from two Shapes containing open Paths.

Loading Cavalry Player…

The Merge is used to join the First and Second Shape creating the 'fill' below the graph's line.

chunks.title: Merge
chunks.heading: Merge > Merge > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**First Shape** - Connect a Shape containing a single open Path.

**Second Shape** - Connect a Shape containing a single open Path.

**Reverse Second Shape** - Reverse the direction of the second Shape's Path.

chunks.title: Mesh Shape
chunks.heading: Mesh Shape > Mesh Shape > Intro
chunks.text:
Create a **mesh** by adding control vertices to deform images or Shaders.

Photo by charlesdeluvio on Unsplash

chunks.title: Mesh Shape
chunks.heading: Mesh Shape > Mesh Shape > UI
chunks.text:
* Shape* Mesh

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Size** - Set the size of the Shape.

**Mesh** - When checked, the Shape is converted to a mesh and so can be deformed by adding vertices. See [Mesh tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/mesh-tool/).

**Top Left Offset** - Set a position offset for the Shape's top left corner.

**Top Right Offset** - Set a position offset for the Shape's top right corner.

**Bottom Left Offset** - Set a position offset for the Shape's bottom left corner.

**Bottom Right Offset** - Set a position offset for the Shape's bottom right corner.

**Vertices** - Open a popover window containing a list of the mesh vertices:

* Add - Use this button to add more vertices to the mesh. See [Mesh tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/mesh-tool/).
* Each index contains the position information for each vertex:
  + **Bind Position** - Set the starting position for the vertex.
  + **Offset Position** - Set values to offset the vertex's position from its **Bind Position**.

Use the `x` to remove a Vertex from the list.

chunks.title: Mesh Shape
chunks.heading: Mesh Shape > Mesh Shape > UI
chunks.text:
**Controllers** - Add [Falloffs](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/) which can be used to affect groups of vertices.

Controllers

While a Falloff can be added as a Controller by right clicking in the Controllers list, it may be preferable to:

1. Manually create a [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/).
2. Position it over the vertices to affect.
3. Connect it to the **Controllers** input.

If a Controller is already bound to vertices:

1. Click the active icon in the Controllers list to disable the Falloff.
2. Move the Falloff.
3. Click **Rebind**.
4. Click the active icon in the Controllers list to enable the Falloff.

Image Assets

Right click on an image asset in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) and choose `Add to Composition as Mesh` to quickly add an image to a **Mesh Shape**.

Alternatively, drag an image from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) to the **Shaders** input of a Mesh Shape's **Fill** tab. A dialogue will appear asking if the **Mesh Shape** should be resized to fit the image asset's resolution.

Example

chunks.title: Mesh Shape
chunks.heading: Mesh Shape > Mesh Shape > UI
chunks.text:
1. Import an image to the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).
2. Right click on the image and choose `Add to Composition as Mesh`.
3. Enable the [Mesh tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/mesh-tool/).
4. Click on the **Mesh Shape** to ensure it is selected.
5. Hold `Option/Alt` and click in the centre of the **Mesh Shape** to create a vertex.
6. Release `Option/Alt` and click and drag the vertex.

**Offset Position** keyframes can be set by either right clicking on a vertex and choosing `Set Keyframe` or via the **Vertices** popover.

chunks.title: Outline
chunks.heading: Outline > Outline > Intro
chunks.text: Create a geometry stroke using the path of another Shape. The Outline Shape is similar to a stroke but rather than being a render effect it actually creates geometry. This means it can be deformed and be used as a clipping mask on other Shapes.

chunks.title: Outline
chunks.heading: Outline > Outline > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Input Shapes** - Connect Shapes to create an Outline around.

**Width** - Set the width of the Outline.

**Offset** - Set the distance away from the Input Shapes to draw the Outline.

**Cap Style** - Select the shape for the ends of open Paths:

* **Flat** - Set the caps to be flat.
* **Projecting** - Set the caps to project.
* **Round** - Set the caps to be rounded.

**Join Style** - Select the shape for the 'corners' of a Path:

* **Mitre** - Set joints to be mitred.
* **Bevel** - Set joints to be bevelled.
* **Round** - Set the joints to be rounded.

**Mitre Limit** - Set a limit for the length of a mitred corner. This is useful to prevent very long mitres when angles between edges are very acute.

**Dash Pattern** - Enter a number sequence separated by commas (dash, gap, dash, gap...).

**Dash Offset** - Offset the **Dash Pattern** along the path.

**Align** - Align the stroke along the path.

* **Centre** - Align the stroke along the centre of the path.
* **Inner** - Align the stroke along the inside of the path.
* **Outer** - Align the stroke along the outside of the path.

caution

chunks.title: Outline
chunks.heading: Outline > Outline > UI
chunks.text:
Open paths only support **Centre** alignment. Where multiple contours appear in a single Path, any open contours will be set to **Centre** regardless of the Align setting.

**Trim** - When enabled the controls below are available.

**Start** - Set the percentage along the Input Path the Outline will start.

**End** - Set the percentage along the Input Path the Outline will end.

**Travel** - Move the Outline around the Input Shape.

**Reverse Path** - Reverse the direction the Outline travels around the Input Path.

**Clean Up** - Outline can create unwanted geometry in some cases. While this can usually be safely ignored, checking Clean Up will remove any geometry that may be causing issues with the resulting mesh. *Note - using this feature will have an impact on performance.*

**Preserve Materials** - When checked, the Fill or Stroke Color from the Input Shapes will be applied to the Outline. Where both a Fill and Stroke are present, the Stroke Color will be used.

info

An Outline is not a stroke. While it can be used as such it is actually a Shape and so can be used in the same way as any other shape (i.e. it can be deformed or used as a distribution path etc)

chunks.title: Particle Shape
chunks.heading: Particle Shape > Particle Shape
chunks.text:
Experimental Feature

This is an experimental feature. To enable, check **Enable Experimental Features** in [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/). Experimental features are only available as part of a **Professional** licence.

chunks.title: Particle Shape
chunks.heading: Particle Shape > Particle Shape > Intro
chunks.text:
Technical Preview

⚠️ Note that this is a technical preview. It's possible Scenes may not be 100% compatible with future versions of Cavalry.

Features may change so documentation is currently very light. Jump on Discord to ask any questions.

The Particle system consists of several Layers:

chunks.title: Particle Shape
chunks.heading: Particle Shape > Particle Shape > Intro
chunks.text:
* **Particle Shape** - The 'core' which hosts the other features.
* **Emitters** - Defines where Particles appear from and how many are added to the Composition:
  + [Distribution Emitter](/docs/nodes/utilities/distribution-emitter/)
  + [JavaScript Emitter](/docs/nodes/utilities/javascript-emitter/)
  + [Particle Emitter](/docs/nodes/utilities/particle-emitter/)
* **Modifiers** - Fields which can be used to change a Particle's Attributes.
  + [Data Modifier](/docs/nodes/utilities/data-modifier/)
  + [Flow Field Modifier](/docs/nodes/utilities/flow-field-modifier/)
  + [Force Modifier](/docs/nodes/utilities/force-modifier/)
  + [Goal Modifier](/docs/nodes/utilities/goal-modifier/)
  + [Image Modifier](/docs/nodes/utilities/image-modifier/)
  + [JavaScript Modifier](/docs/nodes/utilities/javascript-modifier/)
  + [Magnetic Modifier](/docs/nodes/utilities/magnetic-modifier/)
  + [Path Modifier](/docs/nodes/utilities/path-modifier/)
  + [Speed Modifier](/docs/nodes/utilities/speed-modifier/)
  + [Turbulence Modifier](/docs/nodes/utilities/turbulence-modifier/)
  + [Visual Modifier](/docs/nodes/utilities/visual-modifier/)
  + [Vortex Modifier](/docs/nodes/utilities/vortex-modifier/)

chunks.title: Particle Shape
chunks.heading: Particle Shape > Particle Shape > Intro
chunks.text:
A quick way to get started is to click the **Particle Shape** icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/) and hit **play**. This will add a **Particle Shape** and a connected [Particle Emitter](/docs/nodes/utilities/particle-emitter/) to the Composition.

Particle Distribution

The [Particle Distribution](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/particle-distribution/) can be used to attach geometry to each Particle or, for example, to use a Particle Shape as the input to a [Connect Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/connect-shape/) (or any Layer that uses a [Distribution](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/)).

chunks.title: Particle Shape
chunks.heading: Particle Shape > Particle Shape > UI
chunks.text:
* Shape* Masks* Visual* Advanced

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Time** - This attribute is connected to the Composition's **Time** to animate the Particles on each frame. The connection can be replaced with keyframes or another Behaviour if required.

**Start Frame** - Set the frame the Particle simulation will start on.

**Seed** -

**Lifespan** - Set

**Emitters** - Connect Emitters to this attribute to define where Particles will spawn from.

**Modifiers** - Modifiers can be used to manipulate the Particles movements and properties. They can be 'stacked' where each Modifier adds to the one below it.

**Turbulence** - Add noisy movement to the Particles.

**Gravity** - Set the strength and direction of a force to accelerate the Particles along.

**Drag Force** - Set the strength of a force acting opposite to the relative motion of the Particles.

**Mass** - The mass of a Particle determines its rate of acceleration when a force is applied. A Particle with a higher mass will accelerate more slowly.

**Number of Particles** - (Read only) The current number of Particles being emitted.

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

chunks.title: Particle Shape
chunks.heading: Particle Shape > Particle Shape > UI
chunks.text:
**Shape Style** - Set the shape for the Particles:

* **Square** - Emit square Particles.
* **Circle** - Emit circular Particles.
* **Input Shape** - Emit Particles as custom Shapes.

**Particle Radius** -

**Input Shape** - When Shape Style is set to Input Shape, connect a Shape to be used for the Particles.

**Scale Over Lifespan** - Use a graph to set a Particle's scale over its lifespan where the top left of the graph is a multiplier of 1 at the Particle's birth and the bottom right is a multiplier of 0 at the Particle's death.

**Scale Strength** - A multiplier for a Particle's scale.

**Start Rotation** - Set an angle for a Particle at its birth.

**Rotation Over Lifespan** - Set an angle each Particle will rotate in over the course of its lifespan.

**Rotation Scalar** - Use a graph to set the interpolation of a Particles rotation over the course of its lifespan where the bottom left of the graph is the start rotation at the Particle's birth and the top right is the end rotation at at the Particle's death.

**Color Mode** - Determine whether a Particle's color is effected by its lifespan

chunks.title: Particle Shape
chunks.heading: Particle Shape > Particle Shape > UI
chunks.text:
* **Color** - Set a color for the Particles.
* **Color Over Lifespan** - Use a [gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/) to set a Particle's color based on its age.

**Gradient Mode** - Select an interpolation for the [gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/).

**Color Over Lifespan** - A Particle's color will evolve from the left to the right of the the gradient over its lifespan. See also [Visual Modifier](/docs/nodes/utilities/visual-modifier/) for more options.

**Image Blend Mode** - Where at Input Image is used, set its [Blend Mode](/docs/nodes/general/blend-modes/).

**Image Quality** -

**Input Image** -

**Image Sequence Animation** -

* **Static** -
* **Animating** -

**Loop Sequence** -

**Image Index** -

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**World Scale** -

**Time Step** -

**Use Cache** -

**Cache File Path** -

Particles as a mesh

chunks.title: Particle Shape
chunks.heading: Particle Shape > Particle Shape > UI
chunks.text:
A **Particle Shape** differs in certain ways from other Shapes in order to handle high particle counts in a performant way. For example, it does not include a **Fill** or **Stroke** tab. Instead, the visual appearance can be affected via the **Visual** tab or using the [Visual Modifier](/docs/nodes/utilities/visual-modifier/). It also doesn't output a **Path** which means it cannot be deformed, used with Layers like the [Component Constraint](/docs/nodes/utilities/component-constraint/) or rendered to **SVG**.

In order to use a **Particle Shape** in this way, the [Particle Distribution](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/particle-distribution/) can be used alongside a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) which does output a Path.

chunks.title: Points to Path
chunks.heading: Points to Path > Points to Path > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Point Source** - See [Distribution Types](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/).

**Close** - Close the path.

**Bézier** - When checked, bézier paths will be created between points.

Example

1. Create a **Points to Path**.
2. Set **Point Source** to **Array**.
3. Create 3 [Nulls](/docs/nodes/utilities/null/).
4. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) null1.position→pointsToPath.array.0.
5. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) null2.position→pointsToPath.array.1
6. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) null3.position→pointsToPath.array.2
7. Move/animate the Nulls.

chunks.title: Quad Tree Shape
chunks.heading: Quad Tree Shape > Quad Tree Shape > Intro
chunks.text: Quad Tree uses a distribution of points to subdivide a square into smaller squares depending on the density of points.

chunks.title: Quad Tree Shape
chunks.heading: Quad Tree Shape > Quad Tree Shape > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Source Distribution** - Select a [Distribution Type](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/).

**Size** - Set the dimensions of the source square [x,y].

**Max. Iterations** - The maximum number of times to attempt to subdivide the square.

Example

1. Create a **Quad Tree Shape**.
2. Set the **Source Distribution** to **Random**.
3. Reduce the **Count** to **5**.
4. Create a [Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/).
5. Give it a different color (use the Fill tab in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/)).
6. With the **Shape** selected, `Option/Alt` + click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
7. Set the **Distribution** type on the **Duplicator** to **Sub Mesh**.
8. Connect the **Quad Tree** to the **Input Shape** of the Duplicators Sub Mesh Distribution.
9. Adjust the **Seed** on the **Quad Tree** to adjust the subdivision.

You can extend this idea by using other Compositions in place of the Shape. There's an example here - <https://www.instagram.com/p/B3H8j9THWpz/>

chunks.title: Ray
chunks.heading: Ray > Ray > Intro
chunks.text: A Ray is a line that starts in its centre and radiates out to an infinite length unless it collides with other shapes.

chunks.title: Ray
chunks.heading: Ray > Ray > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Collision Shapes** - Connect Shapes to be used as collisions.

**Collision Margin** - Increase/ decrease the depth of a collision.

**Bidirectional** - When checked, the Ray will travel out from its centre in both directions along a horizontal axis.

**Border** - Set a value that will crop the Ray inside the Composition boundary.

**Divisions** - Set the number of divisions along the length of the Ray.

chunks.title: Rectangle Pattern
chunks.heading: Rectangle Pattern > Rectangle Pattern > Intro
chunks.text:
The **Rectangle Pattern Shape** can be used to create stacked bar charts and pie charts. Input values are normalised to fit its width or angle.

A bar chart with a Bevel Deformer used to create the rounded corners.

chunks.title: Rectangle Pattern
chunks.heading: Rectangle Pattern > Rectangle Pattern > UI
chunks.text:
* Shape* Advanced

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Pattern Mode** - Set the distribution for the pattern:

chunks.title: Rectangle Pattern
chunks.heading: Rectangle Pattern > Rectangle Pattern > UI
chunks.text:
* **Line** - Distribute the rectangles along a line.
  + **Use Fixed Size** - When checked the bars will be scaled to fit the **Size**.
  + **Orientation** - Set the direction of the line:
    - **Horizontal** - Bars are oriented along the X axis.
    - **Vertical** - Bars are oriented along the Y axis.
  + **Size** - Set a fixed size for the Shape.
  + **Gap Type** - Set the gap style:
    - **Alternating** - Each gap is set by the **Bar Size**. In this mode, **Count** includes rectangles and gaps.
    - **Fixed Width** - Each gap is set by the **Fixed Gap Width**. In this mode, the gaps are in addition to the **Count**.
  + **Fixed Gap Width** - Set a fixed width for each gap.
  + **Alignment** - Align the Shape to a position between its left (0) and right (1) edges.
* **Ring** - Distribute the rectangles along a ring.
  + **Outer Radius** - Set the outer radius of the ring.
  + **Inner Radius** - Set the inner radius of the ring.
  + **Start Angle** - Set the start angle.
  + **End Angle** - Set the end angle.
  + **Gap Type** - Set the gap style:
    - **Alternating** - Each gap is set by the **Bar Size**. In this mode, **Count** includes rectangles and gaps.
    - **Fixed Angl

chunks.title: Rectangle Pattern
chunks.heading: Rectangle Pattern > Rectangle Pattern > UI
chunks.text:
e** - Each gap is set by the \*\*Fixed Gap Angle. \*\*In this mode, the gaps are in addition to the **Count**.
  + **Fixed Gap Angle** - Set a fixed angle for each gap.

chunks.title: Rectangle Pattern
chunks.heading: Rectangle Pattern > Rectangle Pattern > UI
chunks.text:
**Count** - Set the total number of rectangles and gaps.

**Dynamic Bar Size** - Connect a Behaviour to set the size of the rectangles. The values are normalised to fit the **Size**.

info

Note that a 'gap' is actually an empty rectangle so connecting, for example, a [Random Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/random/) to the **Dynamic Bar Size** will create randomly sized rectangles and gaps.

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Use Index Context** - When checked, the Rectangle Pattern Shape will pull [Context](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/context/). This can be used to control how Ids are assigned and so affect each rectangle individually – for example, adding a [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/) via a [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) to the Rectangle Pattern Shape's **Fill Color**.

Example

chunks.title: Rectangle Pattern
chunks.heading: Rectangle Pattern > Rectangle Pattern > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a **Rectangle Pattern Shape**.
2. Set the **Gap Type** to **Fixed Width**.
3. Set the **Count** to **5**.
4. Create a [Value Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/value-array/).
5. Add 4 more indices (for a total of 5) to the **Value Array** and set different values for each one.
6. Connect valueArray.id→rectanglePatternShape.dynamicBarSize.

The values in the **Value Array** are normalised to fit the width of the **Rectangle Pattern Shape**. Try changing the **Pattern Mode** to **Ring**.

A [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) can be used to add colors to each section of the **Rectangle Pattern Shape**:

1. Click the `+` next to the Rectangle Pattern Shape's **Deformers** attribute.
2. Select [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) from the list.
3. On the Sub-Mesh's **Fill** tab, check **Replace Fill**.
4. Right click on the Sub-Mesh's **Color** attribute and choose `Add Array > Color Array`.
5. Add 4 more indices (for a total of 5) to the [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/) and set different colors for each one.

chunks.title: Segment Path
chunks.heading: Segment Path > Segment Path > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Input Shapes** - Connect Shapes to split into segments.

**Mode** - Determine how Paths are segmented:

* **Number of Cuts** - The **Input Shapes** will be evenly split into [Count] parts.
* **Automatic Cuts** - The **Input Shapes** will be automatically split at their points.

**Count** - Set how many segments to create from the **Input Shapes**.

**Extension Mode** -

* **Start** - Extend the trim paths from the start of the segment.
* **End** - Extend the trim paths from the end of the segment.
* **Both** - Extend trim paths from both the start and the end of the segment.

**Extend** - Set the amount to extend the segments by.

Example

chunks.title: Segment Path
chunks.heading: Segment Path > Segment Path > UI
chunks.text:
1. Draw an open path with the [Pencil](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pencil-tool/) tool.
2. Create a **Segment Path**.
3. Connect path.id→segmentPath.inputShapes
4. On the Segment Path, click the + on the Deformers attribute and select [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) from the list.
5. On the **Sub-Mesh**, open the **Stroke** tab and enable **Replace Stroke**.
6. Right click on the **Stroke Color** attribute and select `Add Array > Color Array`.
7. Add three more indices to the [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/) and set different colors for each.

The original path should be segmented into four different colors.

chunks.title: Shortest Path
chunks.heading: Shortest Path > Shortest Path > Intro
chunks.text:
Generates Paths by finding the shortest path between a start and end position via a [Distribution](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/) of Points.

The algorithm calculates the shortest path by:

1. Starting at a given position along an **Input Path**.
2. Searching for neighbouring points within a **Distribution**. By default this is the nearest 10 points but can also be based on a **Search Distance**.
3. Choosing the neighbouring point closest to the end position and moving to it.
4. Looping through steps 2 and 3 until the path reaches the end position.

Using a Text Shape to generate several Shortest Paths.

chunks.title: Shortest Path
chunks.heading: Shortest Path > Shortest Path > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Input Shape** - Connect a Shape to generate the start and end positions from.

**Count** - Set the number of Paths to generate.

**Start Travel** - Set the position along the **Input Shape** for the start of the Shortest Path. If **Count** is greater than 1, connect a Behaviour to vary the positions for each path.

**End Travel** - The position along the **Input Shape** for the end of the Shortest Path. If **Count** is greater than 1, connect a Behaviour to vary the positions for each path.

**Use Search Radius** - By default, the closest 10 points are used to calculate the shortest path – with **Use Search Radius** checked, the **Search Radius** can be used for greater control.

**Search Radius** - Set a maximum radius to search within to find 'the next point' the shortest path should travel along.

**Use Levels** - When checked, determine which level of the **Input Shape** to use to create start/end positions from.

**Level Mode** - Choose which level(s) of a Mesh's hierarchy to affect.

chunks.title: Shortest Path
chunks.heading: Shortest Path > Shortest Path > UI
chunks.text:
* **Custom...** - Manually set a **Custom Level**.
* **Text (Lines)** - Used with a Text Shape, this will affect each **line**.
* **Text (Words)** - Used with a Text Shape, this will affect each **word**.
* **Text (Characters)** - Used with a Text Shape, this will affect each **character**.

Sub-Meshes

If using a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) with the string `TEXT` as an **Input Shape**, the **Level Mode** can be used to determine where the start/end positions are created from/to. For example, if set to **Text (Characters)**, the start and end points must both be positioned along each individual letter (`T`, `E`, `X` or `T`) whereas if set to **Text (Words)**, the start and end points can be generated anywhere along the whole word. For example, the start could be positioned along the first `T` with the end being positioned somewhere along the `X`.

**Custom Level** - Set a custom level.

**Points Distribution** - Select a [Distribution](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/) to create the points for the Shortest Path algorithm to search within.

Draw Debug Information

chunks.title: Shortest Path
chunks.heading: Shortest Path > Shortest Path > UI
chunks.text:
**Shortest Path** supports the **Draw Debug Information** option in the [Viewport settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#viewport-settings) which can be used to preview the Points within the **Points Distribution**.

Example

1. Create an **Ellipse**.
2. Set its **Radius** to `200,200`.
3. Create a **Shortest Path**.
4. Connect ellipse.id→shortestPath.inputShape.
5. Set the Shortest Path's **Count** to `20`.
6. Right click on the **Start Travel** Attribute and choose `Add Behaviour > Random`.
7. Set the Random's **Maximum** to `1`.
8. Change the Random Distribution's **Seed** value on the Shortest Path.

Mask Distribution

A [Mask Distribution](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/mask-distribution/) can be used to ensure only the points inside the Shape will be considered for the Shortest Path.

chunks.title: Spacer
chunks.heading: Spacer > Spacer > Intro
chunks.text: A **Spacer** is simply an empty mesh and can be used in combination with [Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layout-group/), [Grid Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-group/) or [Grid Layout Row](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-row/) to create gaps or blank cells.

chunks.title: Spacer
chunks.heading: Spacer > Spacer > UI
chunks.text:
**Used Fixed Size** - When checked, a **Fixed Size** can be set for the Spacer.

**Fixed Size** - Set a width and height for the Spacer.

chunks.title: Sub-Mesh Bounding Box
chunks.heading: Sub-Mesh Bounding Box > Sub-Mesh Bounding Box
chunks.text:
Experimental Feature

This is an experimental feature. To enable, check **Enable Experimental Features** in [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/). Experimental features are only available as part of a **Professional** licence.

chunks.title: Sub-Mesh Bounding Box
chunks.heading: Sub-Mesh Bounding Box > Sub-Mesh Bounding Box > Intro
chunks.text: Create rectangles using the bounding boxes of sub-meshes (Duplicator, Text, SVG etc). See [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) for more info on sub-meshes.

chunks.title: Sub-Mesh Bounding Box
chunks.heading: Sub-Mesh Bounding Box > Sub-Mesh Bounding Box > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Input Shape** - Connect any other Shape containing sub-meshes.

**Level** - Set the level within the sub-mesh's hierarchy to affect.

**Expand** - Increase/ decrease the size of the bounding boxes generated.

**Fixed Size** - By default, the size of each bounding box is set by the size of each child-mesh (e.g. each character in a text string). By unchecking the **Auto** (Width/Height) checkboxes, the bounding boxes can be set to a fixed width and height.

**Specific Indices** - Enter specific ids for each sub-mesh to create a bounding box around. Enter comma separated values (e.g. `0, 4, 7`) or create ranges using colons (e.g. `1:4`) or a combination of both (e.g. `2, 3:5`).

**Sequences Keep Gaps** - When checked, where the **Specific Indices** attribute contains ranges (e.g. `0:3`), they will be converted to a sequence (e.g. `0,1,2,3`). This can be used as a way to unify the heights of individual bounding boxes across letters with ascenders/descenders (e.g. `h` and `y`). Note that this feature only works across one row – mutli-line text/sub-meshes are not supported.

info

chunks.title: Sub-Mesh Bounding Box
chunks.heading: Sub-Mesh Bounding Box > Sub-Mesh Bounding Box > UI
chunks.text:
Remember that Ids start at 0 so the first word in a string would be `id0`.

Example

1. Create a **Sub-Mesh Bounding Box** Shape.
2. Set its **Fill Color** to green.
3. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
4. Enter `Sub-Mesh Bounding Box` into the **Text** attribute.
5. Connect textShape.id→subMeshBoundingBox.inputShape.
6. Set the **Level** to **2** (Words are the 2nd level of the sub-mesh within a Text Shape).
7. Enter `0,2` into the **Specific Indices** attribute.

Green boxes will be drawn around the words **Sub-Mesh** and **Box**.

Specific Indices across line breaks

When entering ranges into **Specific Indices** be aware that where that range includes characters or words across line breaks, the resulting bounding box will encompass all characters or words. In the image below, despite the both examples incorporating the same indices, note how the range `0:3` creates a bounding box that encompasses `Enter indices across a`, whereas `0,1,2,3` creates a bounding box for each individual word.

chunks.title: SVG
chunks.heading: SVG > SVG > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**File** - Drag in a .svg file from the [Asset Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).

**SVG Materials** - Uncheck this attribute to ignore the SVG's materials. Enable \*\*Fill \*\*under the Fill tab to replace the Fill Color.

**SVG Strokes** - Uncheck this attribute to ignore the SVG's stroke. Enable **Stroke** under the Fill tab to replace the Stroke Color.

Working with SVG

See [Vector Artwork Support](/docs/nodes/general/vector-artwork-support/) for tips on working with SVG data.

chunks.title: Text Shape
chunks.heading: Text Shape > Text Shape > Intro
chunks.text:
Create and format text.

tip

A **Text Shape** can also be created in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) using the [Text](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/text-tool/) tool. With the Text tool selected, click and drag to draw a **Text Box**. If you `Option/Alt` + click on the Text tool or, with the Text tool selected, click once in the Viewport, the **Text Shape** will be created with **Auto Width** and **Auto Height** checked. This results in the text box fitting the text rather than the text fitting within the **Text Box**.

Style Inheritance

When creating a Text Shape, some of its settings will be inherited from the last interaction with another Text Shape. For example, if the last interaction with a Text Shape set the **Font** to `Arial` and the **Font Size** to `100`, the next Text Shape created will also match those settings. This affects the following attributes:

* Font
* Font Style
* Font Size
* Alignment
* Vertical Alignment
* Character Spacing
* Word Spacing
* Line Spacing
* Paragraph Spacing

chunks.title: Text Shape
chunks.heading: Text Shape > Text Shape > Intro
chunks.text:
Use the [Presets](/docs/user-interface/general/presets/) feature too set a 'default' Text Shape. If a Preset is `Set as Default Settings` then the Preset will override the above.

This does not apply to Text created via [Scripting](/docs/tech-info/scripting/scripting-getting-started/) or when pasting in text from the clipboard.

chunks.title: Text Shape
chunks.heading: Text Shape > Text Shape > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

* Shape* Background* Advanced

**String** - Enter text, numbers or symbols here.

Generator - Add and connect a [String Generator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/) from a list.

OpenType - Open a popover window to enable/disable the font's **OpenType** features. If the current string (or selection) does not contain a combination of glyphs that could be affected by a particular option, that option will be dimmed. OpenType can be applied to the entire string or via selections and combined with rich text features. Note that **OpenType** is not supported if the **String** attribute has an **input connection**. In this scenario, use an [Apply OpenType](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-opentype/) Style Behaviour instead.

Reset - Clear any rich text or **OpenType** styling to return the text to its default.

chunks.title: Text Shape
chunks.heading: Text Shape > Text Shape > UI
chunks.text:
Glyphs - Open a popover version of the [Glyph Browser](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/glyph-browser/). Double click glyphs to add them to the **String**. Note that adding glyphs is not supported if the **String** attribute has an **input connection**. In this scenario, open the [Glyph Browser](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/glyph-browser/) and add glyphs to the input directly.

**Font** - Select the Font and Weight.

Variable Fonts

If a **Variable Font** is selected, a small disclosure icon (three dots) will appear to the right of the **Font** attribute. Click this icon to load a pop over window in order to access the font's axes. Drag the pop over window's header to detach it in order to make connections to the axes.

**Typeface** - Connect a [Typeface](/docs/nodes/utilities/typeface/). This is a way to connect different Text Shapes to the same typeface.

**Font Size** - Set the size of the font.

**Style** - Apply Underline, Strikethrough, Subscript, Superscript and/or All Caps styling to text. Use the gear icon to set options:

chunks.title: Text Shape
chunks.heading: Text Shape > Text Shape > UI
chunks.text:
* **Line Style** - Specify how **underline** and **strikethrough** render a space character between words:
  + **Through** - Create a continuous line through spaces.
  + **Gaps** - Create gaps in the line where spaces exist.
* **Decorator Shape** - When adding styling to a Text Shape a new 'decorator' Shape is created.

**Alignment** - Align text horizontally to the Left, Centre, Right or Justified. Justified text increases the spaces between words aligning the text to both the left and right margins except the last line of a paragraph which is aligned to the left.

**Vertical Alignment** - Align text vertically to the Top, Centre, Bottom or Baseline.

**Character Spacing** - Set the distance between characters.

**Word Spacing** - Set an offset for the distance between words.

**Line Spacing** - Set an offset for the distance between lines.

**Paragraph Spacing** - Set an offset for the distance between paragraphs. A paragraph is defined by a line break.

**Text Box Size** - Set the size of the area the text wraps within.

chunks.title: Text Shape
chunks.heading: Text Shape > Text Shape > UI
chunks.text:
* **Auto Width** - When checked, the Text Box is sized to the width of the text.
* **Auto Height** - When checked, the Text Box is sized to the height of the text.

**Shrink to Fit Text Box** - When checked, the Font Size will be automatically reduced at the point the String overflows the **Text Box**. Note - this requires **Auto** to be unchecked on the **Text Box Size** Attribute. The scale factor applied to the Text can be accessed via the **Font Scale** attribute under the Advanced tab.

**Allow Word Breaks** - When unchecked and with **Shrink to Fit Text Box** checked, words are prevented from wrapping over lines. This is useful for automated templates to prevent long words being split across lines where they would otherwise extend outside the text box. Instead, the text will be scaled appropriately.

Hyphens

Hyphenated words (e.g. Sub-Mesh) will be treated as separate words unless they contain a NON-BREAKING HYPHEN character ([U+2011](https://www.fileformat.info/info/unicode/char/2011/index.htm)).

**Avoid Orphans** - When checked, ensure that wrapping text within a **Text Box** does not result in single words being 'orphaned' on the last line.

chunks.title: Text Shape
chunks.heading: Text Shape > Text Shape > UI
chunks.text:
**Force Monospacing** - Click the checkbox to remove any kerning from non monospace fonts (useful when animating text strings but need to maintain each character's position). Use the **Monospace Multiplier** to increase or decrease the space between monospaced characters.

**String Manipulators** - Add a [String Manipulator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-manipulator/).

**Style Behaviours** - Add a Style Behaviour. Style Behaviours allow for the procedural manipulation of text strings. For an example, see the [Apply Font Size](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-font-size/) Utility.

**Material Behaviours** - Add a Material Behaviour. Material Behaviours allow for the procedural manipulation of text strings. For an example, see the [Apply Text Material](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-text-material/) Utility.

**Formatting Inputs** - Inject a String/Text into the Text Shape. This allows you to set up Text containing different styles, colours or sizes. Any connected Text or String can then be referenced by its index within curly brackets. For example, a Text Shape containing the Text string `Cavalry {0}` will inject the text from another Text Shape connected to **Formatting Inputs** index **0**.

chunks.title: Text Shape
chunks.heading: Text Shape > Text Shape > UI
chunks.text:
Example

**Formatting Inputs**

1. Create a **Text Shape** (Text Shape 1).
2. Using the `+` icon on the **Formatting Inputs** attribute row, add a second **Text Shape** (Text Shape 2).
3. Set the **Font Weight** for **Text Shape 2** to **Bold**.
4. On the **Fill** tab, set **Text Shape 2**'s **Color** to blue.
5. Change the **Text** input for **Text Shape 2** to `rules`.
6. On **Text Shape 1**, insert a space character between `Cavalry` and `{0}`

Text Shape 1 now displays 'Cavalry **rules**' (with rules in blue).

**Text Path** - Connect a Shape to position the Text Shape along.

Paths and Alignment

When **Text** is placed along a path its **Alignment** will be set based on the path's start/centre/end. Text will be positioned as follows depending on the **Alignment**:

* **Left** - its left edge (first character) is positioned at the path's first point.
* **Centre** - its centre is positioned half way along the path.
* **Right** - its right edge (last character) is positioned at the path's last point (for closed paths this will be the same as the first point).

**Path Loop** - When checked, the Text Shape will loop around the Path.

chunks.title: Text Shape
chunks.heading: Text Shape > Text Shape > UI
chunks.text:
**Path Travel** - Move the Text Shape along the Path.

**Path Push** - Move the Text Shape along the Path's normals.

Text along a Path

Use the `Shape > Reverse Contour(s)` command or [Reverse Path](/docs/nodes/behaviours/reverse-path/) Behaviour to position Text on the other side of a Path.

**Background Shape** - Add a [Custom Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/custom-shape/) to be used as the background. Note - this is an output connection. To reconnect, connect the Text Shape's **Background Shape** attribute to the Custom Shape's **Input Shape** attribute.

**Mode** - Set the level for the **Background Shape** to be based on:

* **Document** - Create a Shape to encompass the entire String.
* **Paragraph** - Create a Shape for each paragraph found within the String. Note - a paragraph is defined by an empty line (e.g. two line returns).
* **Line** - Create a Shape for each line found within the String.
* **Word** - Create a Shape for each word found within the String.
* **Character** - Create a Shape for each character found within the String.

chunks.title: Text Shape
chunks.heading: Text Shape > Text Shape > UI
chunks.text:
**Specific Indices** - Manually enter the indices to determine which paragraphs/lines/words/characters are selected. Enter comma separated values (e.g. `0, 4, 7`) or create ranges using colons (e.g. `1:4`) or a combination of both (e.g. `2, 3:5`). Entering the string `first` or `last` will procedurally select those indices. Negative values can also be used to select indices working backwards from the end of the string. e.g. `-1` = last, `-2` = penultimate, `-3` = third to last, etc.

**Padding** - Increase/decrease the padding of the Custom Shape around the Text Shape.

**Ascender Adjustment** - Offset the vertical padding of the Custom Shape above the ascenders (e.g. t, d, l) within the font.

**Descender Adjustment** - Offset the vertical padding of the Custom Shape below the descenders (e.g. g, y, j) within the font.

**Corner Radius Mode** - Determine whether to set the corner radius globally on on a per corner basis:

* **All** - The **Corner Radius** setting will set all corner radii.
* **Individual** - Set each corner individually via **Top** and **Bottom Radii**.

**Corner Radius** - Set a radius for the rectangle’s corners.

chunks.title: Text Shape
chunks.heading: Text Shape > Text Shape > UI
chunks.text:
**Top Radii** - Set a radius for the top corners [l, r].

**Bottom Radii** - Set a radius for the bottom corners [l, r].

**Chamfer** - Chamfer the corners of the rectangle.

**Font Scale** - Output the scale factor applied to the Text when **Shrink to Fit Text Box** is checked.

**Automatic Naming** - When checked, a Text Shape's 'nice name' is inherited from its **String** unless it has been manually set by renaming it in the Scene Window.

Per-Character Animation

See [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) for animating **Text** by character/word/line.

Order of Operations

When using a combination of features with Text they will affect the output in the follow order:

chunks.title: Text Shape
chunks.heading: Text Shape > Text Shape > UI
chunks.text:
1. **Text input** (includes [String Generators](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/) and [String Manipulators](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-manipulator/))
2. **Style Behaviours** ([Apply Character Spacing](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-character-spacing/), [Apply Font Size](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-font-size/), [Apply Typeface](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-typeface/))
3. **Standard Materials** (Fill, Stroke)
4. **Material Behaviours** ([Apply Text Material](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-text-material/))
5. **Formatted Inputs**

Naming Text Shape Layers

By default, a Text Shape's 'nice name' is inherited from its **String** unless it has been manually set by renaming it in the Scene Window. This can be disabled by unchecking **Automatic Naming** in the **Advanced** tab.

chunks.title: Trails
chunks.heading: Trails > Trails > Intro
chunks.text:
Generate trails (lines) from the movement of other Shapes.

Experimental Feature

This is an experimental feature. To enable, check **Enable Experimental Features** in [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/). Experimental features are only available as part of a **Professional** licence.

chunks.title: Trails
chunks.heading: Trails > Trails > UI
chunks.text:
* Shape* Stroke* Advanced

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Input Shapes** - Connect a shape or shapes to create trails from.

**Limit Length** - When checked the Trail's length will be limited to a maximum **Length** value.

**Length** - Set the maximum length for the Trail's. Note - inactive when **Limit Length** is unchecked.

**Start Frame** - Set the first frame for the Trails to appear.

**Path Type** - Select the curve type:

* **Béziers** - Trails will be created as bézier curves.
* **Lines** - Trails will be created as polygonal lines.

**Time Offset** - Offset the time for any animation that has been added to the Trails. For example, if an [Oscillator](/docs/nodes/behaviours/oscillator/) is connected to the Stroke's **Width**, connecting a [Stagger](/docs/nodes/behaviours/stagger/) to the **Time Offset** can be used to offset the animation for each trail.

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Use Particle Color** - When checked, the Trails will inherit their color from a [Particle Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/particle-shape/) used as an **Input Shape**.

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

chunks.title: Trails
chunks.heading: Trails > Trails > UI
chunks.text:
**Use Index Context** - When checked, the Trails will pull [Context](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/context/). This can be used to control how Ids are assigned and so affect each Trail individually – for example, adding a [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/) to the Trails Shape's **Stroke Color**.

Example

1. Create a [Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/).
2. With the Shape selected, click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
3. In the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/), right click on the Duplicator's **Shape Position** attribute and select `Add Behaviour > Noise`.
4. Load the **Noise's** Attribute Editor UI.
5. Increase the **Strength** to e.g. **500**.
6. Create a **Trails Shape**.
7. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) duplicator.id→trails.inputShapes.
8. Hide the **Duplicator**.
9. Press Play.

chunks.title: Utilities
chunks.heading: Utilities > Utilities
chunks.text: Utilities are general purpose building blocks that can be used to create custom set-ups.

chunks.title: Accumulator
chunks.heading: Accumulator > Accumulator > Intro
chunks.text:
Create 'stacks' of Shapes or custom layouts.

When connected to a Duplicator or Sub-Mesh Deformer, the Accumulator will add the number in **Value** for each Mesh being calculated.

chunks.title: Accumulator
chunks.heading: Accumulator > Accumulator > UI
chunks.text:
**Value** - Set a value to accumulate or connect a Behaviour.

**Padding** - Add a gap between each Shape.

**Offset** - Add or subtract a value to the output.

Example

1. Create a Rectangle.
2. Click the  on the **Deformers** attribute and select [Align](/docs/nodes/behaviours/align/).
3. Set the Align's **X** attribute to **1**.
4. With the Rectangle selected, click the Duplicator icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/) to add it to a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).
5. Set the **Duplicator**'s **Distribution** to **Point**.
6. In the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/), right click on the Rectangle's **Size** attribute and choose `Add Behaviour > Random`.
7. Set the [Random](/docs/nodes/behaviours/random/) Behaviour's **Minimum** to `50` and **Maximum** to `150`.
8. Uncheck the Random's **Use Layer as Seed** attribute.
9. Create an **Accumulator**.
10. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) accumulator.id→duplicator.shapePosition.x.
11. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) rectangle.size.w→accumulator.value.

chunks.title: Accumulator
chunks.heading: Accumulator > Accumulator > UI
chunks.text: The Rectangles are positioned side by side, respecting each others width. Try increasing **Count** on the Duplicator or changing the **Seed** on the Random Behaviour.

chunks.title: Animation Control
chunks.heading: Animation Control > Animation Control > Intro
chunks.text:
Remap an attribute's **animation curve** (e.g. from the first to the last keyframe) to a percentage.

The **Animation Control** can be thought of as a way to horizontally 'scale' the **animation curve**. For example, if an attribute had several keyframes spanning over a total of 100 frames, connecting an **Animation Control** to that attribute and setting keyframes for...

* **Amount** = **0** at frame 0
* **Amount** = **100** at frame 50

...would result in the same animation happening in half the time, therefore doubling in speed. This is the equivalent of using the [Transform tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/#transform-tool) in the [Time Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/) to scale the keyframes.

Animation Curve

An **animation curve** is best visualised in the [Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/). It's the line connecting the keyframes which starts at the first keyframe and ends at the last. In the [Time Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/) it is represented by the coloured line that connects the keyframes.

chunks.title: Animation Control
chunks.heading: Animation Control > Animation Control > Intro
chunks.text: Using an **Animation Control** means that one attribute can be rigged to trigger another attributes animation. For example, by connecting a Shape's **position.y** attribute to an Animation Control's **Amount** attribute, when that Shape moves up, it can be used to drive the animation curve of another Shape.

chunks.title: Animation Control
chunks.heading: Animation Control > Animation Control > UI
chunks.text:
**Active** - When checked, the **Animation Control** is active.

**Amount** - A value between 0 and 100 where `0 = the first keyframe` and `100 = the last keyframe`.

Example

1. Create 4 keyframes on the **Position X** channel of a **Basic Shape**.
2. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) ***animationControl.id*** > ***basicShape.position.x***.
3. Scrub **Amount** on the **Animation Control** layer.

As you move the **Amount** from 0 to 100, the Basic Shape will animate between its first and last (4th) keyframe.

caution

It's not possible to edit keyframes on an attribute connected to an active Animation Control. Uncheck **Active** to allow this.

chunks.title: Apply Character Spacing
chunks.heading: Apply Character Spacing > Apply Character Spacing > Intro
chunks.text: **Apply Character Spacing** can be used as a **Style Behaviour** on a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) to create procedural kerning pairs. This prevents the need to manually set this up on a case-by-case basis and is ideal for situations where the string may change (e.g. in automated workflows).

chunks.title: Apply Character Spacing
chunks.heading: Apply Character Spacing > Apply Character Spacing > UI
chunks.text:
Add - Add a new index.

**Match String** - Enter the characters to affect.

**Character Spacing** - Set the Character Spacing for the matched string.

Example

1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/)
2. In the Attribute Editor, click the  on the **Style Behaviour** attribute.
3. Select **Apply Character Spacing**.
4. Scrub the **Apply Character Spacing**'s **Character Spacing** attribute in the Attribute Editor.

Note how the spacing between the `v` and `a` in Ca**va**lry updates but the other characters are unchanged. Change the string in **Match String** to `ly` to only affect those letters or add a new index using the Add button.

chunks.title: Apply Font Size
chunks.heading: Apply Font Size > Apply Font Size > Intro
chunks.text: **Apply Font Size** can be used as a **Style Behaviour** on a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) and makes it possible to set different Font Sizes for characters, lines, words or partial strings in a procedural way.

chunks.title: Apply Font Size
chunks.heading: Apply Font Size > Apply Font Size > UI
chunks.text:
**Mode** - Choose a mode for the selection:

* **Regex** - Set a **Regular Expression** to determine which parts of the string will be selected. There are several presets available at the top of the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) UI.
* **Specific Indices** - Manually enter the indices to determine which lines/words/characters are selected.
* **All** - Use this setting when using a [Range Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/range-falloff/) via another Behaviour. See example below.

**Index Mode** - When the **Mode** is set to **Specific Indices**, select which level is affected:

* **Line** - Fill each line within the string defined by **Specific Indices**.
* **Word** - Fill each word within the string defined by **Specific Indices**.
* **Character** - Fill each character within the string defined by **Specific Indices**.

chunks.title: Apply Font Size
chunks.heading: Apply Font Size > Apply Font Size > UI
chunks.text:
**Specific Indices** - When the **Mode** is set to **Specific Indices**, set the indices to select. Values should be comma `,` separated for lists or colon `:` separated for ranges. e.g. `0,1:3,8` will select indices 0, 1, 2, 3 and 8. You can also enter `first` or `last` to procedurally select those indices. Note that a space character is included as an index.

**Regex** - Enter a **Regular Expression**. See [Working with Regex](/docs/nodes/general/working-with-regex/) for more information.

**Capture Group Indices** - Where a Regular Expression includes capture groups, determine which groups are returned. Values should be comma `,` separated for lists or colon `:` separated for ranges. See [Working with Regex](/docs/nodes/general/working-with-regex/#capture-groups) for more information.

**Font Size** - Set the size of the font within the selection.

**Falloffs** - Add a [Range Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/range-falloff/).

Example

chunks.title: Apply Font Size
chunks.heading: Apply Font Size > Apply Font Size > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. Using the `+` button on the **Style Behaviours** attribute and add an **Apply Font Size**.
3. Set the **Apply Font Size**'s **Mode** to **All**.
4. Right click in the **Apply Font Size**'s **Falloff** input > Add Falloff > Range Falloff.

The [Range Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/range-falloff/) can now be used to set each character's color from either end of the Color Blend's **gradient**.

chunks.title: Apply Font Style
chunks.heading: Apply Font Style > Apply Font Style > Intro
chunks.text: **Apply Font Style** can be used as a **Style Behaviour** to dynamically set styling features like **Underline**, **Strikethrough**, **Subscript** and **Superscript** used within a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) in a procedural way. For example, set the last word to underline or set the word `Cavalry` to strikethrough each time it appears in a string.

chunks.title: Apply Font Style
chunks.heading: Apply Font Style > Apply Font Style > UI
chunks.text:
**Underline** - When checked, an underline style will be applied.

**Strikethrough** - When checked, a strikethrough style will be applied.

**Supers Inferiors Mode** - Select a Superscript or Subscript style:

* **None** - No style.
* **Superscript** - Set to Superscript.
* **Subscript** - Set to Subscript.

**Mode** - Choose a mode for the selection:

* **Regex** - Set a **Regular Expression** to determine which parts of the string will be selected. There are several presets available at the top of the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) UI.
* **Specific Indices** - Manually enter the indices to determine which lines/words/characters are selected.
* **All** - Use this setting when using an Apply Typeface with a Behaviour. See **Create > Demo Scenes > Text > Variable Font**.

**Index Mode** - When the **Mode** is set to **Specific Indices**, select which level is affected:

* **Line** - Fill each line within the string defined by **Specific Indices**.
* **Word** - Fill each word within the string defined by **Specific Indices**.

chunks.title: Apply Font Style
chunks.heading: Apply Font Style > Apply Font Style > UI
chunks.text:
**Specific Indices** - When the **Mode** is set to **Specific Indices**, set the indices to select. Values should be comma `,` separated for lists or colon `:` separated for ranges. e.g. `0,1:3,8` will select indices 0, 1, 2, 3 and 8. You can also enter `first` or `last` to procedurally select those indices. Note that a space character is included as an index.

**Regex** - Enter a **Regular Expression**. See [Working with Regex](/docs/nodes/general/working-with-regex/) for more information.

**Capture Group Indices** - Where a Regular Expression includes capture groups, determine which groups are returned. Values should be comma `,` separated for lists or colon `:` separated for ranges. See [Working with Regex](/docs/nodes/general/working-with-regex/#capture-groups) for more information.

Example

1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. Enter the string `First and last`.
3. Click the `+` to the right of the **Style Behaviours** attribute.
4. Select **Apply Font Style** from the list.

chunks.title: Apply Font Style
chunks.heading: Apply Font Style > Apply Font Style > UI
chunks.text:
An underline style will be added to the words `First` and `last`. Double click the **Apply Font Style** layer in the Scene Window and try replacing `first,last` in the **Indices** attribute with `1`.

info

When adding styling to a Text Shape a new 'decorator' Shape is created.

chunks.title: Apply OpenType
chunks.heading: Apply OpenType > Apply OpenType > Intro
chunks.text: **Apply OpenType** can be used as a **Style Behaviour** to dynamically enable OpenType features used within a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) in a procedural way.

chunks.title: Apply OpenType
chunks.heading: Apply OpenType > Apply OpenType > UI

**Mode** - Choose a mode for the selection:

* **Regex** - Set a **Regular Expression** to determine which parts of the string will be selected. There are several presets available at the top of the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) UI.
* **Specific Indices** - Manually enter the indices to determine which lines/words/characters are selected.
* **All** - Use this setting when using an Apply Typeface with a Behaviour. See **Create > Demo Scenes > Text > Variable Font**.

**Index Mode** - When the **Mode** is set to **Specific Indices**, select which level is affected:

* **Line** - Fill each line within the string defined by **Specific Indices**.
* **Word** - Fill each word within the string defined by **Specific Indices**.
* **Character** - Fill each character within the string defined by **Specific Indices**.

chunks.title: Apply OpenType
chunks.heading: Apply OpenType > Apply OpenType > UI
chunks.text:
**Specific Indices** - When the **Mode** is set to **Specific Indices**, set the indices to select. Values should be comma `,` separated for lists or colon `:` separated for ranges. e.g. `0,1:3,8` will select indices 0, 1, 2, 3 and 8. You can also enter `first` or `last` to procedurally select those indices. Note that a space character is included as an index.

**Regex** - Enter a **Regular Expression**. See [Working with Regex](/docs/nodes/general/working-with-regex/) for more information.

See [Working with Regex](/docs/nodes/general/working-with-regex/#capture-groups) for more information.

Add - Use this button to add more rows (indices) to the UI.

**Font Feature** - Select an OpenType feature from the list. Note that this list in not filtered based on the font so ensure the font in use supports the feature.

**Enabled** - When checked, the OpenType feature is enabled.

Example

chunks.title: Apply OpenType
chunks.heading: Apply OpenType > Apply OpenType > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. Set the **Font** to [Inter](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Inter).
3. Enter the string `I heard the store is open from 1st June to 3rd July.`.
4. Click the `+` to the right of the **Style Behaviours** attribute.
5. Select **Apply OpenType** from the list.
6. Double click the **Apply OpenType** layer in the Scene Window to load its UI into the Attribute Editor.
7. Set the **Mode** to **Regex**.
8. Enter the string `(\d+)(st|nd|rd|th)` into the **Regex** control.
9. Enter `2` into the **Capture Group Indices** control.
10. Select '**Superscript**' from the **Font Feature** list.

Only where `st` or `rd` appear after a number are those characters are set to Supertype.

chunks.title: Apply Text Material
chunks.heading: Apply Text Material > Apply Text Material > Intro
chunks.text: **Apply Text Material** can be used as a **Material Behaviour** on a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) to set the materials of characters, lines, words or partial strings in a procedural way. For example, set the last word's color to blue or set the word `Cavalry` to green each time it appears in a string.

chunks.title: Apply Text Material
chunks.heading: Apply Text Material > Apply Text Material > UI
chunks.text:
* Behaviour* Fill* Stroke

**Mode** - Choose a mode for the selection:

* **Regex** - Set a **Regular Expression** to determine which parts of the string will be selected. There are several presets available at the top of the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) UI.
* **Specific Indices** - Manually enter the indices to determine which lines/words/characters are selected.
* **All** - Use this setting when using a [Range Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/range-falloff/) via another Behaviour. See example below.

**Index Mode** - When the **Mode** is set to **Specific Indices**, select which level is affected:

* **Line** - Fill each line within the string defined by **Specific Indices**.
* **Word** - Fill each word within the string defined by **Specific Indices**.
* **Character** - Fill each character within the string defined by **Specific Indices**.

chunks.title: Apply Text Material
chunks.heading: Apply Text Material > Apply Text Material > UI
chunks.text:
**Specific Indices** - When the **Mode** is set to **Specific Indices**, set the indices to select. Values should be comma `,` separated for lists or colon `:` separated for ranges. e.g. `0,1:3,8` will select indices 0, 1, 2, 3 and 8. See [Working with Regex](/docs/nodes/general/working-with-regex/#capture-groups) for more information.

**Overwrite Blend Mode** - When checked, a **Blend Mode** can be set for the selection.

**Blend Mode** - Set the [blend mode](/docs/nodes/general/blend-modes/).

**Filters** - A list of connected [Filters](/docs/nodes/effects/). Use the  to create and connect a Filter or drag and drop an existing one to connect it.

See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) (Fill tab).

chunks.title: Apply Text Material
chunks.heading: Apply Text Material > Apply Text Material > UI
chunks.text:
Removing Fill

Any existing Fill must be overridden to remove it. To do this, enable the **Fill** and set the **Alpha** to `0`.

See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) (Stroke tab).

Removing Stroke

Any existing Stroke must be overridden to remove it. To do this, enable the **Stroke** and set the **Alpha** to `0`.

Use with Falloffs

1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. Using the `+` button on the **Material Behaviours** attribute and add an **Apply Text Material**.
3. Set the **Apply Text Material**'s **Mode** to **All**.
4. Go to the **Apply Text Material**'s **Fill** tab, right click on the **Color** attribute > Add Behaviour > Color Blend.
5. Go the [Color Blend](/docs/nodes/behaviours/color-blend/)'s **Falloff** tab and right click > Add Falloff > Range Falloff.

The **Range Falloff** can now be used to set each character's color from either end of the Color Blend's **gradient**.

chunks.title: Apply Typeface
chunks.heading: Apply Typeface > Apply Typeface > Intro
chunks.text: **Apply Typeface** can be used as a **Style Behaviour** to dynamically set the typeface used within a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) in a procedural way. For example, set the last word's font to Times New Roman or set the word `Cavalry` to Helvetica each time it appears in a string.

chunks.title: Apply Typeface
chunks.heading: Apply Typeface > Apply Typeface > UI
chunks.text:
**Font** - Select a typeface and weight.

**Mode** - Choose a mode for the selection:

* **Regex** - Set a **Regular Expression** to determine which parts of the string will be selected. There are several presets available at the top of the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) UI.
* **Specific Indices** - Manually enter the indices to determine which lines/words/characters are selected.
* **All** - Use this setting when using an Apply Typeface with a Behaviour. See **Create > Demo Scenes > Text > Variable Font**.

**Index Mode** - When the **Mode** is set to **Specific Indices**, select which level is affected:

* **Line** - Fill each line within the string defined by **Specific Indices**.
* **Word** - Fill each word within the string defined by **Specific Indices**.
* **Character** - Fill each character within the string defined by **Specific Indices**.

chunks.title: Apply Typeface
chunks.heading: Apply Typeface > Apply Typeface > UI
chunks.text:
**Specific Indices** - When the **Mode** is set to **Specific Indices**, set the indices to select. Values should be comma `,` separated for lists or colon `:` separated for ranges. e.g. `0,1:3,8` will select indices 0, 1, 2, 3 and 8. You can also enter `first` or `last` to procedurally select those indices. Note that a space character is included as an index.
