chunks.title: JavaScript Utility
chunks.heading: JavaScript Utility > JavaScript Utility > UI
chunks.text:
**Expression Window** - Enter a JavaScript expression here.

**`+` Button** - Add a new Variable.

**n0** - A default (double) Variable.

Example

Making a [String Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-array/) in JavaScript.

1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. With the **Text Shape** selected, click the **Duplicator** icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
3. Create a **JavaScript Utility**.
4. Copy and paste the below into the expression window.

```
var animation = [

"2d",

"3d",

"Cel"

];

animation[ctx.index]
```

5. Connect `javaScript.id > text.string`

The first three Text Shapes in the Duplicator will read 2d, 3d and Cel.

In order to loop each index within the array, edit the last line to read `animation[ctx.index % animation.length]`

It's possible to add line breaks by adding `\n` to a string. e.g. `2d\nrules` will output:

```
2d

rules
```

[See Scripting→](/docs/tech-info/scripting/scripting-getting-started/)
[Example JavaScript Expressions→](/docs/tech-info/scripting/example-expressions/)

chunks.title: Jsmath
chunks.heading: Jsmath > Jsmath > UI
chunks.text:
**Expression** - An area to input mathematical operations/JavaScript expressions.

**Result** - A read only attribute previewing the result of the **Expression**.

**Add** - Use this button to add more indices to the UI.

**0: Number** - The first index in the array.

info

To reference a row in the expression use the syntax `n[index number]`. For example, to reference the index labelled **0: Number** use the syntax **n0**.

Any strings with `n` followed by a `value` will be coloured to help visually identify them within an expression.

Example

Adding the values of two attributes together.

1. Create 3 Shapes.
2. Create a **Jsmath** Utility.
3. Connect basicShape1.position.x→jsmath.number0.
4. Connect basicShape2.position.x→jsmath.number1.
5. Enter `n0 + n1` into the **Expression** input.
6. Connect jsmath.id→basicShape3.position.x to output the result.

Example

Move Shape1 in X at a value of Shape2\sqrt{Shape2}Shape2​.

1. Create 2 Shapes.
2. Create a **Jsmath** Utility.
3. Connect basicShape1.position.x→jsmath.number0
4. Enter `Math.sqrt(n0)` into the **Expression** input.
5. Connect jsmath.id→basicShape2.position.x

info

chunks.title: Jsmath
chunks.heading: Jsmath > Jsmath > UI
chunks.text:
See <https://htmlcheatsheet.com/js/> for some JavaScript syntax.

info

To remove indices from the array, select a row or rows, right click and choose **Delete Selected Attribute(s)**.

Right click on an index row and select **Rename** to rename an index.

Reorder indices by right clicking on a index row and select **Reorder**.

If Statement

It's possible to write **If Statements** with the Jsmath Layer. For example...

`if (n0 > n1) {1} else {0}` or the equivalent ternary `n0 > n1 ? 1 : 0`

...translate to "If `n0` is greater than `n1` then output `1`. If not, output `0`"

chunks.title: Lattice Controller
chunks.heading: Lattice Controller > Lattice Controller > Intro
chunks.text: Manipulate the position, rotation and scale of multiple [Lattice](/docs/nodes/behaviours/lattice/) points.

chunks.title: Lattice Controller
chunks.heading: Lattice Controller > Lattice Controller > UI
chunks.text:
**Strength** - Increase/decrease the influence of the Controller on the Lattice points. This can be used to blend the points between their original position and the offsets applied by the Controller.

**Pivot Offset** - Offset the Controller from its original position.

**Position** - Offset the Lattice points in the X and Y axes.

**Rotation** - Rotate the Lattice points around the Controller's centre.

**Scale** - Rotate the Lattice points from the Controller's centre.

caution

When manually connecting a Lattice Controller to a [Lattice](/docs/nodes/behaviours/lattice/), ensure some Lattice points are selected before making the connection. Using the Lattice's **Add Controller to Selection** button is the recommended workflow.

Example

chunks.title: Lattice Controller
chunks.heading: Lattice Controller > Lattice Controller > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a Rectangle.
2. Set **Edge Divisions** to `1,1`.
3. Click the  button on the Deformers attribute and choose [Lattice](/docs/nodes/behaviours/lattice/).
4. With the **Lattice** selected and the [Select](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) tool active, marquee select the Lattice points in the top right quadrant of the rectangle.
5. Click `Add Controller to Selection` at the bottom of the Lattice UI.
6. Use the [Select](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) tool to move/rotate/scale the Controller.

chunks.title: Layer Seed
chunks.heading: Layer Seed > Layer Seed > Intro
chunks.text:
The **Layer Seed** can be connected to an attribute in order for that attribute's parent Layer to pass unique values to its output connections.

Layers such as the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) can automatically 'seed' random numbers to its **Input Shapes** but this is not true for individual Layers where, for example, 3 [Random Behaviours](/docs/nodes/behaviours/random/) are required to generate 3 random numbers. Rather than managing several Layers, a **Layer Seed** can, for example, be connected to a single [Random Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/random/)'s **Seed** attribute to generate different random numbers for each of the Layers it's connected to.

chunks.title: Layer Seed
chunks.heading: Layer Seed > Layer Seed > UI
chunks.text:
**Offset** - Offset the value to generate new seeds.

Example

1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. Click the Text Shape's Generator button and choose [Random Date](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/random-date-generator/).
3. Select the **Text Shape** and then `Cmd/Ctrl` + `D` twice to create two duplicates.
4. Move them apart in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).
5. Right click on the **Random Date** String Generator's **Seed** attribute > `Add Utility > Layer Seed`.

The **Random Date** passes a different seed to each **Text Shape** which renders a unique date.

Example

chunks.title: Layer Seed
chunks.heading: Layer Seed > Layer Seed > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create an [Ellipse](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/ellipse/).
2. Create a [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/).
3. On the Color Array, click the `+ Add` button 3 times to add 3 indices.
4. Set a unique color for each index.
5. Connect colorArray.id→ellipse.fillColor.
6. Uncheck **Auto Index**.
7. Right click on the Color Array's **Index** attribute > `Add Utility > Layer Seed`.
8. Right click on the Color Array's **Index** attribute > `Add Expression...`
9. Enter `%4`.
10. With the **Ellipse** selected, hit `Cmd/Ctrl` + `D` several times to create several duplicates of the Ellipse.
11. Move the **Ellipses** apart in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

Each **Ellipse** is given a random **Fill Color** from the **Color Array**.

The `%4` [Attribute Expression](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-interaction/#attribute-expressions) (modulo 4) converts the values from the **Layer Seed** to a value between 0 and 3 to match the number of ids in the **Color Array**.

chunks.title: Length Context
chunks.heading: Length Context > Length Context > Intro
chunks.text: Length Context allows you to read the length of a path or paths and pass values through to affect any other attribute.

chunks.title: Length Context
chunks.heading: Length Context > Length Context > UI
chunks.text:
**Remapping** - Remap the incoming values.

* **None** - Do not remap values.
* **Area Range** - See [Area Range](/docs/nodes/behaviours/area-range/).
* **Number Range** - See [Number Range](/docs/nodes/behaviours/number-range/).
* **Number Range to Color** - See [Number Range to Color](/docs/nodes/behaviours/number-range-to-color/).

Example

1. Create some [Trails](/docs/nodes/shapes/trails/) as per the example usage on the Trails page.
2. Add a [Random](/docs/nodes/behaviours/random/) Behaviour to **trails.length**
3. Set the Random Behaviour's **Minimum** to **10** and the **Maximum** to **200**.
4. Create a **Length Context**.
5. Set:
   1. **Source Minimum** to **0**
   2. **Source Maximum** to **200**
   3. **Minimum** to **1**
   4. **Maximum** to **40**
6. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) lengthContext.id→trails.strokeMaterial.width\*.
7. Press Play.

As the **Trails** grow in length their Stroke Width will increase (1px when they have a length of 0, 40px at 200).

Try a similar thing with **Color** (adjust the remap values accordingly) or [Connect Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/connect-shape/).

chunks.title: Local Time
chunks.heading: Local Time > Local Time > Intro
chunks.text:
Output the current time.

Rendering

Note that **Local Time** is primarily a playback feature and so may not always render to file as expected. The value is the ‘real clock value’ so if it takes 1 second to render 150 frames, each of those 150 frames will be given the same second value. In this example, if the Composition's **Frame Rate** is 25fps, the output will update every 25 frames in playback whereas the render will only update every 150 frames.

The [Frame Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/frame/) can be used to create a 'counter'.

chunks.title: Local Time
chunks.heading: Local Time > Local Time > UI
chunks.text:
**Strength** - A multiple for the output. Setting this to 50% will result in time progressing half as quickly.

**Mode** - Select the unit of time to output:

* Milliseconds through Second -
* Seconds through Minute -
* Seconds through Hour -
* Seconds through Day -
* Seconds through Week -
* Seconds through Month -
* Seconds through Year -
* Minutes through Hour -
* Minutes through Day -
* Minutes through Week -
* Minutes through Month -
* Minutes through Year -
* Day of the Week -
* Day of the Month -
* Day of the Year -
* Month of the Year -

**Output Mode** -

* **Unit** - Output the time as a unit/value.
* **Ratio** - Output the time as a ratio. e.g. if it's half way through the year output **Day of the Year** as 0.5.

**Offset** - Add/subtract values to the output.

Example

1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. Using the `+` to the right of the **Text** attribute add a [String Generator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/).
3. Set the **Generator** to **Value**.
4. Add a **Local Time**.
5. Set **Mode** to **Day of the Month**.
6. Connect localTime.id→stringGenerator.number.

If today is the 11th August the Text Shape will output `11`.

chunks.title: Logic
chunks.heading: Logic > Logic > UI
chunks.text:
**First** - Set the first boolean to be used in the operation. When using input connections, a value less than **0.5** is considered `false` and a value greater than or equal to **0.5** is `true`.

**Operation** - Determine the logical operation:

* **AND (both)** - The **Result** is `true` if **First** and **Second** are both `true`.
* **OR (one or both)** - The **Result** is `true` if **First** and/or **Second** are `true`.
* **XOR (one but not both)** - The **Result** is `true` if either **First** or **Second** is `true` but not if both are `true`.

**Second** - Set the second boolean to be used in the operation. When using input connections, a value less than **0.5** is considered `false` and a value greater than or equal to **0.5** is `true`.

**Result** - A read only preview of the output. The **Logic Utility** will output a value of **1** when the result is `true` and a value of **0** when the result is `false`.

Example

chunks.title: Logic
chunks.heading: Logic > Logic > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create an Ellipse.
2. Create two [Comparison Utilities](/docs/nodes/utilities/comparison/).
3. Set **Second** to **0** for both.
4. Connect ellipse.position.x→comparison1.first.
5. Connect ellipse.position.y→comparison2.first.
6. Create a **Logic Utility**.
7. Connect comparison1.id→logic.first.
8. Connect comparison2.id→logic.second.
9. Create a [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/).
10. Using the Add button add a second index to the **Color Array** and set a different color.
11. Connect logic.id→colorArray.index.
12. Connect colorArray.id→ellipse.fill.color.

Using the **Select** tool, move the **Ellipse** around the **Viewport**. When the Ellipse is positioned in the bottom left quadrant of the Viewport it will change color because;

* Its position in both **X** and **Y** is less than **0** which means both **Comparisons** return `true`.
* This means the **Logic** also returns `true`.
* Which sets the **Color Array**'s **Index** to **1**.

chunks.title: Measure Text
chunks.heading: Measure Text > Measure Text > Intro
chunks.text: An optimised method to output the bounding box of a string without rendering in the Viewport. By not rendering a Text Shape in the Viewport this can be a faster approach for setting up rigs that need to know the width/height of a Text Shape.

chunks.title: Measure Text
chunks.heading: Measure Text > Measure Text > UI
chunks.text:
**String** - Enter a string to measure.

`+` - Add a [String Generator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/).

**Font** - Select the Font and Weight.

**Typeface** - Connect a Typeface. See [Typeface](/docs/nodes/utilities/typeface/).

**Font Size** - Set the size of the font.

**Out Text Size** - Output the dimensions of the resulting Text. These represent the size of the text over one line and ignores the **Text Box Size**.

**Text Box Size** - Set the size of the area the text wraps within if it was being drawn within a Text Box. Changing this will affect the **Out Font Scale** but not the **Out Text Size**.

**Allow Word Breaks** - When unchecked, words are prevented from wrapping over lines. Instead, they remain in-tact and the Text is shrunk to fit accordingly.

**Out Font Scale** - Output the scale factor applied to the Text in order to fit within the **Text Box Size**. The **Shrink to Fit Text Box** feature from the Text Shape is enabled behind the scenes.

chunks.title: Measure
chunks.heading: Measure > Measure > UI
chunks.text:
**First Target** - Connect a Shape.

**Second Target** - Connect a second Shape.

**Distance** [read only] - The resulting distance between **First Target** and **Second Target**.

Example

1. Create three [Basic Shapes](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/)
2. Create a **Measure**.
3. Connect basicShape1→measure.firstTarget.
4. Connect basicShape2→measure.secondTarget.
5. Connect measure.id→basicShape3.position.y.

As Basic Shape 1 and Basic Shape 2 move, Basic Shape 3 moves up and down.

info

[Distance](/docs/nodes/behaviours/distance/) can also be used to calculate the distance between two Shapes/transforms and it's drive either of the Input Shape's transforms. This is not possible using **Measure** as it would cause a cycle.

chunks.title: Null
chunks.heading: Null > Null > Intro
chunks.text: Nulls are drawable (visible in the viewport) but not renderable (won't show up in any output). They are most commonly used in rigging but often find uses in many other applications.

chunks.title: Null
chunks.heading: Null > Null > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Shape** - Set the type of Null.

* **Cross** - Set the Null to a crosshair.
* **Circle** - Set the Null to circle shape.
* **Square** - Set the Null to a rectangular shape.

**Custom Color** - By default a Null will use its label color but with **Custom Color** checked the Null will use the color set by the **Color** attribute.

**Color** - Set a custom color for the **Null**.

**Limit Position** - When enabled the Null will be limited to values between the **Minimum** and **Maximum Position** values.

**Minimum Position** - Set a value to limit the Null's minimum position [x,y].

**Maximum Position** - Set a value to limit the Null's maximum position [x,y].

**Draw Position Limits** - Show the position limits in the viewport.

**Limit Rotation** - When enabled the Null will be limited to values between the **Minimum** and **Maximum Rotation** values.

**Minimum Rotation** - Set a value to limit the Null's minimum rotation.

**Maximum Rotation** - Set a value to limit the Null's maximum rotation.

**Limit Scale** - When enabled the Null will be limited to values between the **Minimum** and **Maximum Scale** controls.

chunks.title: Null
chunks.heading: Null > Null > UI
chunks.text:
**Minimum Scale** - Set a value to limit the Null's minimum scale [x,y].

**Maximum Scale**- Set a value to limit the Null's maximum scale [x,y].

info

The hotkey `Shift` + `Cmd/Ctrl` + `=` will create a **Null**.

chunks.title: Particle Emitter
chunks.heading: Particle Emitter > Particle Emitter
chunks.text:
Experimental Feature

This is an experimental feature. To enable, check **Enable Experimental Features** in [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/). Experimental features are only available as part of a **Professional** licence.

chunks.title: Particle Emitter
chunks.heading: Particle Emitter > Particle Emitter > Intro
chunks.text: Emit [Particles](/docs/nodes/shapes/particle-shape/) from a Point, Shape or Path.

chunks.title: Particle Emitter
chunks.heading: Particle Emitter > Particle Emitter > UI
chunks.text:
* Transform* Emitter

[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Custom Color** - A representation of the **Emitter** is drawn in the Viewport – when **Custom Color** is checked it will been drawn using the value set in **Color**. When unchecked the **Label Color** is used (this is the color used for the row in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/)).

**Color** - Set a **Custom Color** for the Emitter's Viewport draw.

**Emitter Shape** - Select a shape to emit from:

* **Point** - Emit Particles from a point.
* **Circle** - Emit Particles from within a circle.
* **Square** - Emit Particles from within a square.
* **Input Shape** - Emit Particles from within a Shape.
* **Input Shape Perimeter** - Emit Particles from a Shape's Path.

**Input Shape** - Connect a Shape to emit Particles from.

**Size** - Set the width and height of the **Circle** or **Square Emitter Shape**.

chunks.title: Particle Emitter
chunks.heading: Particle Emitter > Particle Emitter > UI
chunks.text:
**Use Single Position** - When unchecked, Particles will emit from a random position within the Input Shape or along its Path 'per Particle'. When checked, the positions are set 'per frame' so where 20 Particles will emit within 1 frame, each Particle will emit from the same position. This can be useful to create an explosion type effect.

**Maximum Particles** - The maximum number of Particles emitted.

**Emitter Type** - Determine whether Particles are emitted over Time or Distance:

* **Time** - Emit Particles on every frame (or sub-frame).
* **Distance** - Emit Particles whenever the Emitter's position changes.

**Particles per Pixel** - When **Emitter Type** is set to **Distance**, set how many Particles will be emitted for every pixel the Emitter moves.

**Rate** - When **Emitter Type** is set to **Time**, set the number of Particles emitted per second.

**Duration** - Define the period of time Particles will be emitted for.

chunks.title: Particle Emitter
chunks.heading: Particle Emitter > Particle Emitter > UI
chunks.text:
**Interval** - Define a time (in seconds) the Emitter will pause for before starting the next emission cycle. A **Duration** of **2** and an **Interval** of **1**, will result in 'bursts' of Particles emitting for 2 seconds and then pausing for 1 second before repeating the cycle.

**Probability** - When using emission cycles, set the probability of Particles emitting during the **Duration** time. This can be used to create a less uniform feel to each burst.

**Direction Type** - Determine the direction Particles will emit in:

* **Angle** - Emit Particles along the angle set by the **Initial Direction**.
* **Inwards** - Emit Particles along the normals that face towards the inside of the **Emitter Shape**'s Path.
* **Outwards** - Emit Particles along the normals that face towards the outside of the **Emitter Shape**'s Path.

**Initial Direction** - Set an angle for the Particles to emit along. Behaviours (e.g. [Random](/docs/nodes/behaviours/random/)) can be connected to set the angle on a 'per Particle' basis.

chunks.title: Particle Emitter
chunks.heading: Particle Emitter > Particle Emitter > UI
chunks.text:
**Initial Speed** - Set a speed to assign to the Particles as they are emitted. Behaviours (e.g. [Random](/docs/nodes/behaviours/random/)) can be connected to set the speed on a 'per Particle' basis.

**Perimeter Margin** - When the **Emitter Shape** is set to **Input Shape Perimeter**, expand the width of the Path used for emission. For example, this can be used to create a ring of Particles from an Ellipse Shape.

**Use Path Normals** - When the **Emitter Shape** is set to **Input Shape Perimeter**, emit Particles along the **Input Shape**'s normals.

**Normal Angle** - When the **Emitter Shape** is set to **Input Shape Perimeter**, offset the direction the Particles emit in from the Path's normals.

**Use Emitter Velocity** -

**Emitter Velocity Strength** -

**Override Lifespan** - When checked, the value in **Lifespan** will override the [Particle Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/particle-shape/)'s **Lifespan**. This can be useful when more than one Emitter is connected to a Particle Shape.

**Lifespan** - Override the [Particle Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/particle-shape/)'s **Lifespan** with this value.

chunks.title: Particle Emitter
chunks.heading: Particle Emitter > Particle Emitter > UI
chunks.text:
**Time** - This attribute is connected to the Composition's **Time** to animate the Particles on each frame. The connection can be replaced with keyframes or another Behaviour if required.

**Seed** - Set the random seed used to position Particles within the **Emitter Shape**.

chunks.title: Path Field
chunks.heading: Path Field > Path Field > Intro
chunks.text: Apply path following forces to dynamics bodies within a [Forge Dynamics](/docs/nodes/shapes/forge-dynamics/forge-dynamics-shape/) simulation.

chunks.title: Path Field
chunks.heading: Path Field > Path Field > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) +

**Path to Follow** - Connect a Shape to define the path that bodies will follow.

**Capture Force** - Strength of the force pulling bodies towards the path.

**Flow Force** - Strength of the force moving bodies along the path tangent.

**Capture Margin** - Distance from the path where capture forces apply.

**Flow Margin** - Distance from the path where flow forces apply.

**Flow Variance** - Add randomness to flow direction for more natural motion.

**Capture Curve** - Control how capture force attenuates with distance from the path.

**Flow Curve** - Control how flow force attenuates with distance from the path.

**Velocity Damping** - Opposes body velocity to prevent oscillation and instability. Higher values create more stable but slower motion.

chunks.title: Path Length
chunks.heading: Path Length > Path Length > UI
chunks.text:
**Input Shape** - Connect a Shape to output the length of.

**Strength** - Determine the strength of the Behaviour.

**Offset** - Add/subtract a value to the output.

**Length** [read only] - The output of the layer. e.g. the length of the **Input Shape**.

chunks.title: Path Modifier
chunks.heading: Path Modifier > Path Modifier
chunks.text:
Experimental Feature

This is an experimental feature. To enable, check **Enable Experimental Features** in [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/). Experimental features are only available as part of a **Professional** licence.

chunks.title: Pin Constraint
chunks.heading: Pin Constraint > Pin Constraint > Intro
chunks.text: Pin Shapes to their original position in a [Forge Dynamics](/docs/nodes/shapes/forge-dynamics/forge-dynamics-shape/) simulation while allowing them to rotate. Shapes can also be driven by a **motor** meaning they can be used for concepts like gears, wheels, or crankshafts.

chunks.title: Pin Constraint
chunks.heading: Pin Constraint > Pin Constraint > UI
chunks.text:
**Horizontal Alignment** - Align the position of the Constraint to the left (-1) or right (1) edge of the Body.

**Vertical Alignment** - Align the position of the Constraint to the top (1) or bottom (-1) edge of the Body.

**Motor** - When checked, a pinned Shape is given a rotational force.

**Motor Speed** - Set the speed in which the pinned Shape rotates.

**Maximum Torque** - Set the torque or force for the Motor. A higher value will mean the pinned Shape is capable of acting against Shapes with a greater density.

**Limit Rotation** - When checked, the Constraint's rotation will be never go above or below the **Rotational Limits**.

**Rotational Limits** - Set an upper (`U`) and lower (`L`) angle to clamp the Constraint's rotation.

**Tension** - When this value is greater than 0, the Constraint will attempt to return to its original angle with a spring-like behaviour where a higher value will result in a stronger spring. When this value is set to 0, the Constraint will rotate freely.

**Damping Ratio** - Increase/decrease the damping of a Constraint's rotational 'spring' where a value of `0` = bouncy oscillation and `1` = smooth return with no bounce.

chunks.title: Pin Constraint
chunks.heading: Pin Constraint > Pin Constraint > UI
chunks.text:
**Breakable** - When enabled, the Constraint can be broken by other forces.

**Breaking Mode** - Set a condition for the Constraint to break under:

* **Force** - The Constraint will break when a force is above the **Breaking Force**.
* **Distance** - The Constraint will break when it moves beyond its **Stretch Limit**.
* **Time** - The Constraint will break when a force above the **Breaking Force** is sustained for a number of consecutive frames above the **Breaking Duration**.

**Breaking Force** - Set the amount of force required to break the Constraint.

**Stretch Limit** - Set a multiple of the **Rest Length** a Constraint is moved by before it breaks. For example, if the **Rest Length** is `100` and the **Stretch Limit** is `2`, the Constraint will break when stretched to 100×2=200100 \times 2 = 200100×2=200.

**Breaking Duration** - Set the number of consecutive frames a Constraint must be under a force above the **Breaking Force** before breaking.

**Stress Threshold** - Set a threshold as a percentage of the **Breaking Force** within which a Constraint will break.

Example

chunks.title: Pin Constraint
chunks.heading: Pin Constraint > Pin Constraint > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a **Rectangle**.
2. Set **Width** to `600` and **Height** to `30`.
3. Create an **Ellipse**.
4. Set the Ellipse's **Position** to `100,400`.
5. Select both Shapes and click the **Forge** icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
6. Under the Forge Dynamics **Bodies** tab, click the gear icon for the **Rectangle**.
7. Click the + next to the **Constraints** attribute towards the bottom of the window and choose **Pin Constraint**.
8. Hit Play

The **Ellipse** will fall and hit the **Rectangle** causing it to rotate in place.

chunks.title: Radius
chunks.heading: Radius > Radius > Intro
chunks.text:
Generate the radius for a circle which encompasses several Shapes.

info

Note that the **Radius Utility** outputs values and does not generate a Shape. Connect the outputs to a Shape (e.g. an Ellipse) to see the results in the Viewport.

chunks.title: Radius
chunks.heading: Radius > Radius > UI
chunks.text:
**Input Shapes** - Connect a Shape or Shapes to generate a radius around.

**Centre Mode** - Determine where the centre of the radius is calculated from:

* **Custom Centre** - Manually set a position for the radius' centre.
* **Shapes' Centre** - The radius' centre is positioned at the centre of the Input Shapes.
* **Smallest Circle** - The radius' centre is positioned by calculating the smallest circle that can encompass the Input Shapes.

**Centre** - Set a position for the radius' centre when the **Centre Mode** is set to **Custom Centre**.

**Expand** - Add an offset to the **Radius** and **Inner Radius**. A positive value will increase the **Radius** and decrease the **Inner Radius**.

**Centre Position** - An output for the Radius' centre.

**Radius** - An output for the radius.

**Inner Radius** - An output for the radius of a circle that can be drawn inside the Input Shapes.

Example

chunks.title: Radius
chunks.heading: Radius > Radius > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create 3 Shapes.
2. Move them apart from each other.
3. Create a **Radius Utility**.
4. Connect the 3 Shapes to the Radius Utility's **Input Shapes** attribute.
5. Create an **Ellipse**.
6. Disable the Ellipse's **Fill** and enable **Stroke**.
7. Connect radius.centrePosition→ellipse.position.
8. Connect radius.radius→ellipse.radius.
9. Move the Input Shapes in the Viewport.

The Ellipse will increase/decrease in size as the Shapes are moved.

chunks.title: Range Falloff
chunks.heading: Range Falloff > Range Falloff > Intro
chunks.text: The **Range Falloff** is similar to the [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/) in that it can be used to isolate the strength of most [Behaviours](/docs/nodes/behaviours/) but rather than using a shape, it uses a range.

chunks.title: Range Falloff
chunks.heading: Range Falloff > Range Falloff > UI
chunks.text:
[Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/common-attributes-behaviours/) +

**Strength** - A multiplier for the **Falloff Graph** attribute.

**Mode** - Determine how the indices within the range are selected:

* **Specific Indices** - Manually enter the indices to determine which lines/words/characters are selected.
* **Percentage** - The indices will be worked out as a percentage of the total range.
* **Transition** - Create a sequential 'sweep' through the indices.

**Indices** - When the **Mode** is set to **Specific Indices**, set the indices to select. Values should be comma `,` separated for lists or colon `:` separated for ranges. e.g. `0,1:3,8` will select indices 0, 1, 2, 3 and 8. You can also enter `first` or `last` to procedurally select those indices. Note that a space character is included as an index when working with Text.

**Start** - When the **Mode** is set to **Percentage**, set a value for the start percentage.

**End** - When the **Mode** is set to **Percentage**, set a value for the end percentage.

chunks.title: Range Falloff
chunks.heading: Range Falloff > Range Falloff > UI
chunks.text:
**Offset** - When the **Mode** is set to **Offset** or **Percentage**, set a value to add/subtract from the indices. This can be used to travel/loop the effect of the Range Falloff.

**Transition Size** - When the **Mode** is set to **Transition**, set the number of indices within the transition window.

**Completion** - When the **Mode** is set to **Transition**, set how complete the transition is.

**Use Graph** - When the **Mode** is set to **Percentage**, check this to attenuate the values using the **Falloff Graph**.

**Falloff Graph** - See [Graph Attribute](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/graph-attribute/). The X axis of the Graph represents the total indices within the range.

Example

chunks.title: Range Falloff
chunks.heading: Range Falloff > Range Falloff > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create an [Ellipse](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/ellipse/).
2. Create a [Value](/docs/nodes/behaviours/value/) Behaviour.
3. Set:
   1. **Value** to `20`.
   2. **Offset** to `20`.
4. Connect value.id→ellipse.radius.
5. Select the **Ellipse** and click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) button in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
6. In the Value's **Falloff** tab, right click > Add Falloff > Range Falloff.
7. Set the Range Falloff's **Mode** to **Percentage**.
8. Adjust the **Start/End** values.

Example

1. Create an [Ellipse](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/ellipse/).
2. Create a [Value](/docs/nodes/behaviours/value/) Behaviour.
3. Set:
   1. **Value** to `20`.
   2. **Offset** to `20`.
4. Connect value.id→ellipse.radius.
5. Select the **Ellipse** and click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) button in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
6. In the Value's **Falloff** tab, right click > Add Falloff > Range Falloff.
7. Set the Range Falloff's:
   1. **Mode** to **Transition**.
   2. **Transition Size** to **5**.
8. Scrub the **Completion** value between 0 and 100%.

chunks.title: Rig Control
chunks.heading: Rig Control > Rig Control > Intro
chunks.text:
A 2d controller (or joystick by any other name) which can be used for pose-based rigging.

Loading Cavalry Player…

Use the X and Y controls as a joystick.

Keyframe Layers

The **Rig Control** uses a dedicated [Keyframe Layer](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/keyframe-layers/) to set keyframes for the poses so that they can be set without affecting the main timeline.

chunks.title: Rig Control
chunks.heading: Rig Control > Rig Control > UI
chunks.text:
**Active** - Toggle the **Control** mode.

**Control** - This UI is dependent on the **Active** state:

* **Active unchecked** - This is the mode to set up the rig in. The five dots on the joystick represent the five keyframes necessary to set up the rig. Clicking each dot will move the timeline to the following corresponding frames:
  + Centre (neutral pose) - Frame 0
  + Left - Frame 1
  + Right - Frame 2
  + Top - Frame 3
  + Bottom - Frame 4
* **Active checked** - This is the mode to animate the rig in. Moving the dot translates between the poses set in **Inactive mode**.

Example

chunks.title: Rig Control
chunks.heading: Rig Control > Rig Control > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a [Basic Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/) and a **Rig Control**.
2. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) rigControl.id→basicShape.position.
3. A new [Keyframe Layer](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/keyframe-layers/) will be created and 5 keys set for you on frames 0-4.
4. Set the following keys on the Basic Shape for Position [x,y]:
5. Frame 0 = 0, 0
6. Frame 1 = -50, 0
7. Frame 2 = 50, 0
8. Frame 3 = 0, 50
9. Frame 4 = 0, -50
10. Check **Active** on the Rig Control.
11. Move the dot on the Control.
12. To animate the rig, set the [Keyframe Layer](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/keyframe-layers/) to **Default** and set [keyframes](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-interaction/#setting-keyframes) by using the x, y controls.

See the demo scene in the [Example Files](/docs/getting-started/example-files/).

chunks.title: Scheduling Group
chunks.heading: Scheduling Group > Scheduling Group > Intro
chunks.text:
Procedurally position child layers in time.

A **Scheduling Group** provides a way to group a collection of Layers and affect their time offsets in a procedural way. In the example below a [Stagger Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/stagger/) is connected to the **Child Offset** attribute. The **first** to **last** Layer's time offsets are being set by the Stagger's **Minimum** and **Maximum** values respectively. By adjusting the Stagger's **Maximum** attribute Layer's can be moved in time.

Procedurally offsetting Layers in time using a Stagger Behaviour

If Layers are added/removed from the Scheduling Group then the Stagger will automatically update their time offsets.

When Layers are dragged out of a **Scheduling Group** they will retain any time offset that has been applied.

Hierarchy

Where a Group or a hierarchy of Layers is included within a Scheduling Group, only the parent will be affected. All children will inherit the parent's offset but not be offset in time themselves.

It's also possible to 'sequence' Layers. In this example, extending the Clip of one Layer 'ripples' on to the other Layers in the Scheduling Group.

Dynamically sequencing Layers.

chunks.title: Scheduling Group
chunks.heading: Scheduling Group > Scheduling Group > UI
chunks.text:
**Child Offset** - Add a time offset to each layer in the Scheduling Group.

**Sequencing** - When checked, layers will be positioned one after the other.

**Overlap** - Add an overlap to sequenced layers (or use a negative value to add a gap).

**Schedule from End** - When checked, scheduling will start from the end of the Composition.

**Start Frame** - When **Schedule From End** is unchecked, set the frame for the scheduling to start on. By default, this is connected to the Composition's **Frame Range**.

**End Frame** - When **Schedule From End** is checked, set the frame for the scheduling to start on. By default, this is connected to the Composition's **Frame Range**.

**Ordering Policy**:

* **Layer Order** - Order any offsets based on layer order.
* **Alphabetical** - Order any offsets alphabetically based on the Layer's nice name. This will not swap actual layer order.

**Flip Order** - Reverse the order Layers are scheduled in. When checked, Layers will be ordered from bottom to top.

**Shapes Only** - When checked, all Layer Types other than Shapes will be excluded from scheduling.

Example

chunks.title: Scheduling Group
chunks.heading: Scheduling Group > Scheduling Group > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create 3 Basic Shapes.
2. With all 3 Shapes selected, click the **Schedule selected Layers** [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/) button.
3. Adjust the **Minimum** and **Maximum** attributes of the [Stagger](/docs/nodes/behaviours/stagger/) Behaviour that is created.

info

A small icon will appear on the left or right hand side (depending on the **Show Names** setting) of a Layer's Clip to indicate that it's part of a **Scheduling Group**.

tip

Controls for customising the behaviour of Shapes within a Scheduling Group can be found under a Shape's [Advanced](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) tab.

chunks.title: Seconds to Frames
chunks.heading: Seconds to Frames > Seconds to Frames > Intro
chunks.text: Convert a given number of seconds to the equivalent number of frames based on a frame rate.

chunks.title: Seconds to Frames
chunks.heading: Seconds to Frames > Seconds to Frames > UI
chunks.text:
**Seconds** - Enter the number of seconds.

**FPS** - Enter the frame rate. By default, this is connected to the Composition's **Frame Rate**.

**Frames** - An output for the equivalent number of frames. The calculation is simply FPS∗SecondsFPS\*SecondsFPS∗Seconds.

Example

1. Create a [Time Marker](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-markers/).
2. Create a **Seconds to Frames**.
3. Set **Seconds** to `2`.
4. Connect secondsToFrames.frames→timeMarker.absoluteTime.
5. Open the [Composition Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/).
6. Change the **Frame Rate**.

The **Time Marker** will move to the correct frame that represents 2 seconds at the current **Frame Rate**.

chunks.title: Sequence
chunks.heading: Sequence > Sequence > Intro
chunks.text:
Generate random (or non-random), non-repeating number sequences.

A random sequence of 0-3.

chunks.title: Sequence
chunks.heading: Sequence > Sequence > UI
chunks.text:
**Auto Index** - When checked the layer will automatically output all values within the **Sequence** range.

**Index** - Manually select an index within the **Sequence** range.

**Sequence** - Set a range of values to create a sequence within.

**Offset** - Add/subtract a value to the sequence. e.g. a value of 1 will convert `0,1,2,3` to `1,2,3,4`.

**Travel** - Use a value to offset the order of the sequence. e.g. a value of 1 will convert `0,1,2,3` to `3,0,1,2`.

**Randomize** - When checked the values set in **Sequence** will be randomized.

**Seed** - Set the seed used for **Randomize**.

**Skip Indices** - Enter values which you want to omit from the range set within **Sequence**. Indices can be entered as comma or colon separated values. For example, entering `1, 5, 7:9` would omit the values 1, 5, 7, 8 and 9.

Example

chunks.title: Sequence
chunks.heading: Sequence > Sequence > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. Add a [String Generator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/) to the Text.
   1. Set **Precision** and **Padding** to **0**.
3. Add the **Text Shape** to a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).
   1. Set the Duplicator's **Distribution** to **Linear**.
   2. Set the **Count** to **4**.
4. Create a [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/).
   1. Add 3 more colors to the **Array** and give each a different color.
   2. Connect colorArray.id→>.
5. Create a **Sequence**.
   1. Set values for the Sequence of **0** and **3**.
   2. Connect sequence.id→stringGenerator.number.
   3. Connect sequence.id→colorArray.index.

Scrubbing **Seed** on the **Sequence** Utility will generate random values but the same value (or color) will never appear twice.

chunks.title: Shader Array
chunks.heading: Shader Array > Shader Array > Intro
chunks.text: Create a list of Shaders that can be assigned to other Layers via their indices.

chunks.title: Shader Array
chunks.heading: Shader Array > Shader Array > UI
chunks.text:
**Auto Index** - Automatically output all indices within the array.

**Index** - Manually output an index within the array (uncheck Auto Index to enable).

**Reverse** - Invert the order the indices are output in. For example, where there are 3 indices `0,1,2`, their order will be reversed to `2,1,0`.

**Count** - Output the number of indices in the array.

Add - Use this button to add more rows (indices) to the array.

**0: Shader** - The first index in the array. Connect a Shader to each index.

Example

1. Create an [Ellipse](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-line/).
2. Select the Ellipse.
3. Click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
4. Create 3 [Gradient Shaders](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/gradient-shader/).
5. Create a **Shader Array**.
6. Use the Add button to create 2 more indexes on the **Shader Array**.
7. Connect the **Gradient Shaders** to each **Shader Array** index.
8. Connect the **Shader Array** to the **Shaders** attribute on the **Shape** (under the Fill tab).

Double click to set Index

Double clicking on a indices' row will set the **Index** to that value.

chunks.title: Shape Array
chunks.heading: Shape Array > Shape Array > Intro
chunks.text: Create a list of Shapes (Shapes/Compositions/Groups) that can be assigned to other Layers via their indices.

chunks.title: Shape Array
chunks.heading: Shape Array > Shape Array > UI
chunks.text:
**Auto Index** - Automatically output all indices within the array.

**Index** - Manually output an index within the array (uncheck Auto Index to enable).

**Reverse** - Invert the order the indices are output in. For example, where there are 3 indices `0,1,2`, their order will be reversed to `2,1,0`.

**Count** - Output the number of indices in the array.

Add - Use this button to add more rows (indices) to the array.

**0: Shape** - The first index in the array. Drag a Shape, Composition or Group into this attribute.

Example

1. Create 3 different Shapes.
2. Create a **Shape Array**.
3. Click the Add button to add 2 more indices to the Array.
4. Connect each **Shape** to each index on the **Shape Array**.
5. Create a [Custom Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/custom-shape/).
6. Connect shapeArray.id→customShape.inputShape.
7. Select the **Custom Shape** and click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).

Double click to set Index

Double clicking on a indices' row will set the **Index** to that value.

chunks.title: Speed Modifier
chunks.heading: Speed Modifier > Speed Modifier
chunks.text:
Experimental Feature

This is an experimental feature. To enable, check **Enable Experimental Features** in [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/). Experimental features are only available as part of a **Professional** licence.

chunks.title: Spreadsheet Lookup
chunks.heading: Spreadsheet Lookup > Spreadsheet Lookup > Intro
chunks.text:
Lookup values in spreadsheet data based on related text strings (keys). This could be useful, among other things, for creating **design systems** where many layers share common attributes. For example, in the table below, the **key** `corner-radius` would return a **value** of `10`.

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Key Value|  |  | | --- | --- | | corner-radius 10 | | | |

The advantage of using a lookup is that the row can be moved for organisational purposes without losing the link to the value.

chunks.title: Spreadsheet Lookup
chunks.heading: Spreadsheet Lookup > Spreadsheet Lookup > UI
chunks.text:
**File** - Connect a .csv or Google Sheet [Asset](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).

**Excel Sheet** - Select a sheet (tab) from an `.xlsx` asset.

**Lookup Column** - Select the column in the data to search for a key.

**Lookup Key** - Specify the key (text) to find within the **Lookup Column**.

**Value Column** - Select the column to match against the **Lookup Key**.

Example

chunks.title: Spreadsheet Lookup
chunks.heading: Spreadsheet Lookup > Spreadsheet Lookup > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a Rectangle.
2. Right click in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) and select **Import Google Sheet...**
3. Paste in this url - [**https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1DB4Yv0W\_sT1nIlKiQFUBeQyXZoz88tdQt8YvLzXYwbU/edit?usp=sharing**](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1DB4Yv0W_sT1nIlKiQFUBeQyXZoz88tdQt8YvLzXYwbU/edit?usp=sharing)
4. Create a **Spreadsheet Lookup**.
5. Drag the Google Sheet from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) to the **File** attribute on the **Spreadsheet Lookup**.
6. Select the `Key` column for **Lookup Column**.
7. Select the `Value` column for **Value Column**.
8. Enter `corner-radius` in the **Lookup Key**.
9. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) spreadsheetLookup.id→rectangle.cornerRadius.

info

Any changes to the data in the spreadsheet will need to updated by right clicking on the spreadsheet Asset in the [Asset Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) and selecting **Reload**.

chunks.title: Spreadsheet
chunks.heading: Spreadsheet > Spreadsheet > Intro
chunks.text: Read data from a [Google Sheet](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/google-sheets-asset/), `.csv` or `.xlsx` file.

chunks.title: Spreadsheet
chunks.heading: Spreadsheet > Spreadsheet > UI
chunks.text:
**File** - Drag in a `Google Sheet`, `.csv` or `.xlsx` asset from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).

**Excel Sheet** - Select a sheet (tab) from an `.xlsx` asset.

**Column Title** - Select a column from the spreadsheet. The first row of the spreadsheet is reserved and used to populate this list.

info

A **Spreadsheet** Utility can only output data from a single column. In order to use several columns from the same asset, create a **Spreadsheet** Utility for each column to output.

**Factorize** - When checked, a column of text can be converted into values. For example, a column of data containing the text `Summer, Spring, Summer, Summer` can be converted to a list of values `1, 0, 1, 1`. The resulting list is ordered alphabetically.

caution

When using Factorize, the asset must also be 'factorized' for performance reasons. Right click on the asset in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) and check **Factorize**.

chunks.title: Spreadsheet
chunks.heading: Spreadsheet > Spreadsheet > UI
chunks.text:
**Remapping** - Remap numerical values relative to the lowest and highest number in the data. For example, if you want to create a bar chart and need a value of 1 to be represented by a rectangle with a height of 300px, you can.

* **None** - Remapping disabled.
* **Area Range** - See [Area Range](/docs/nodes/behaviours/area-range/).
* **Number Range** - See [Number Range](/docs/nodes/behaviours/number-range/).
* **Number Range to Color** - See [Number Range to Color](/docs/nodes/behaviours/number-range-to-color/).

info

If you have a minimum value of 0 and a maximum of 10 within the data and a simple black to white gradient, a value of 0 will be Black, a value of 10 will output White and a value of 5 will be remapped to 50% grey.

**Fixed Row** - When checked it will output the contents of the row specified in **Row Index** (not including the title row). Useful for [Dynamic Rendering](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/).

**Row Index** - Specify the row to output. A value of 0 outputs row 1 of the spreadsheet (row 0 is reserved for **Column Title**).

**Row Offset** - Add or subtract a value to **Row Index**.

chunks.title: Spreadsheet
chunks.heading: Spreadsheet > Spreadsheet > UI
chunks.text:
**Use Every Nth Row** - Only sample the first and then every **Nth** row where **N** = the value.

**Row Count** - A read only attribute that outputs the number of rows in the selected column.

**Column Count** - A read only attribute that outputs the number of columns in the data. Note that the count starts at the first column and ends on the last column that contains data. For example, if importing the data below via a [Google Sheet](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/google-sheets-asset/), a **Column Count** of `7` (columns A-G) would be returned:

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A B C D E F G H I|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 1 1 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

Note this may vary for a .csv file where empty columns can still be defined. For example, the columns defined by the commas after 'ColumnB' in `ColumnA,ColumnB,,,,,` would be included in the **Column Count**.

chunks.title: Spreadsheet
chunks.heading: Spreadsheet > Spreadsheet > UI
chunks.text:
**Interpolate** - When checked, data can be blended across columns. This requires the **Column Title** to be animated which can be achieved by connecting a [Value Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/value/) to the **Column Title** and keyframing the Value's **Value** attribute. Note - a value of 0 represents the first column.

**Output Mode** - Set the output of the Layer:

* **Data** - Output the raw data.
* **Sort Order (Ascending)** - Output the sort order of the column's data from the smallest to the largest value.
* **Sort Order (Descending)** - Output the sort order of the column's data from the largest to the smallest value.

Sort Order

**Sort Order** takes the values within a column and outputs their sort order. For example, if a column called **Data** contains the values below and the **Output Mode** is set to **Sort Order (Ascending)**, the Spreadsheet will output the values in **Sort Order**.

chunks.title: Spreadsheet
chunks.heading: Spreadsheet > Spreadsheet > UI

chunks.title: Spreadsheet
chunks.heading: Spreadsheet > Spreadsheet > UI
chunks.text:
The output can then be used, for example, to set **Shape Position Y** of a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) in order to position the largest bar of a bar chart at the top and the smallest at the bottom of a Linear Distribution. **Remapping** can then be used to convert the Sort Order into meaningful position values. For example, convert the Sort Order of `0, 1, 2` to values of `0, 50, 100`.

Example

1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/), a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) and a **Spreadsheet** Utility.
2. Create a `.csv` file containing a row titled 'Name' with several names listed below.

```
Name,

Ringo,

John,

George,

Paul
```

chunks.title: Spreadsheet
chunks.heading: Spreadsheet > Spreadsheet > UI
chunks.text:
1. Import the `.csv` file to the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).
2. Drag the `.csv` into the **File** attribute of the **Spreadsheet** Utility.
3. Set **Column Title** to 'Name' on the **Spreadsheet** Utility.
4. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) textShape.id→duplicator.inputShapes.
5. Set the Duplicator's **Distribution** to **Linear**.
6. Set the Duplicator's **Direction** to **Vertical**.
7. Set the Duplicator's **Count** to **4**.
8. [Connect](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) spreadsheet.id→textShape.string.

The first 4 names from the .csv (not including the title) will appear. For more or less than 4 names just adjust **Count Y** on the Duplicator.

Example

1. Create a `Google Sheet`, `.csv` or `.xlsx` containing the data below:

chunks.title: Spreadsheet
chunks.heading: Spreadsheet > Spreadsheet > UI

chunks.title: Spreadsheet
chunks.heading: Spreadsheet > Spreadsheet > UI
chunks.text:
1. If using a Google Sheet, ensure **Link Sharing** is set to **Anyone with the link**.
2. Import the `Google Sheet`, `.csv` or `.xlsx` via the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).
3. Drag the asset into the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) (this will create a **Spreadsheet Utility** and connect the asset).
4. On the Spreadsheet Utility, set **Column Title** to **Value**.
5. Create a [Rectangle](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/).
6. Connect spreadsheet.id→rectangle.size.height.
7. Select the **Rectangle** and click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
8. Set **Distribution** to **Linear**.
9. Set **Count** to **5**.

At this point you should have 5 rectangles each with a height set as per each row of the **Value** column in the data. In order to pin the rectangles to a 'floor' you can use an [Align](/docs/nodes/behaviours/align/) Behaviour.

11. Create an [Align](/docs/nodes/behaviours/align/).
12. Connect align.id→rectangle.deformers.
13. On the **Align** Behaviour, set **Y** to **1**.

chunks.title: Spreadsheet
chunks.heading: Spreadsheet > Spreadsheet > UI
chunks.text:
If the data contains small/large values then you may need to remap the values to something that produces results that better fit your Composition.

14. On the **Spreadsheet** Utility set **Remapping** to [Number Range](/docs/nodes/behaviours/number-range/).
15. Set **Source Minimum** to **0**.
16. Set **Source Maximum** to **2500**. These two values roughly contain the range of the data.
17. Set **Minimum** to **0**.
18. Set **Maximum** to **500**.

A value of 0 in the data will now output as 0 while a value of 2500 will be output at 500. In this example, we are effectively dividing all values by 2500/500 = 5 so a value of 1000 would be remapped to 200.

info

Fields that contain currency symbols (e.g. `£` `€` `$`) are recognised as numeric values. For example, `£123.45` will be interpreted as `123.45` when connected to a numeric attribute.

If values are suffixed by a `k`, `M` or `B` then the the result is multiplied by a thousand, million or billion respectively. For example, `1.5k` will be converted to `1500` when connected to a numeric attribute.

chunks.title: Sticky Collision Event
chunks.heading: Sticky Collision Event > Sticky Collision Event > UI
chunks.text:
**Stiffness** - The rotational stiffness.

**Damping** -The rotational damping.

**Breakable** - When enabled, the Constraint can be broken by other forces.

**Breaking Force** - Set the amount of directional force required to break the Constraint.

**Rotational Force** - Set the amount of rotational force required to break the Constraint.

chunks.title: String Array
chunks.heading: String Array > String Array > Intro
chunks.text: Create a list of strings which can be assigned to other layers via their indices. For example, if connected to a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) which is the Input Shape to a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/), each string in the list will be assigned to the pointIds of the Duplicator.

chunks.title: String Array
chunks.heading: String Array > String Array > UI
chunks.text:
**Mode** - Set which index/indices are output:

* **Index** - Output all indices within the array.
* **Longest** - Output the index with the longest string.
* **Shortest** - Output the index with the shortest string.

**Auto Index** - Automatically output all indices within the array.

**Index** - Manually output an index within the array (uncheck **Auto Index** to enable).

**Reverse** - Invert the order the indices are output in. For example, where there are 3 indices `0,1,2`, their order will be reversed to `2,1,0`.

**Count** - Output the number of indices in the array.

Add - Use this button to add more rows (indices) to the array.

**0: String** - The first index in the array. By default, this is a single line input but entering a soft return (`Shift` + `Return`) will convert the UI to a multi-line input.

Example

Start with a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) in a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).

chunks.title: String Array
chunks.heading: String Array > String Array > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create 3 indices (**Add** button) and enter some text for each index.
2. Connect stringArray.id→textShape.string.
3. Connect a [Random](/docs/nodes/behaviours/random/) Behaviour to the **Array Index** of the **String Array**.
4. Set **Min and Max** on **Random** to **0** and **2** (to match the 3 indices in the array - 0,1,2)

Each duplicated Text Shape will be randomly set one of the three strings you entered for each index.

Double click to set Index

Double clicking on a indices' row will set the **Index** to that value.

chunks.title: String From Asset
chunks.heading: String From Asset > String From Asset > Intro
chunks.text: The **String From Asset** Utility can be used to read strings from Text Assets imported into the Assets Window.

chunks.title: String From Asset
chunks.heading: String From Asset > String From Asset > UI
chunks.text:
**Asset** - Drag in a text asset from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).

Example

1. Import a `.txt` (plain text) file into the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/)
2. Create a **String From Asset** Utility
3. Drag the `.txt` file from the Assets Window into the String From Asset's **Asset** attribute.
4. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
5. Connect stringFromAsset.id→text.string.

The Text Shape will show the contents of the `.txt` file.

chunks.title: String Generator
chunks.heading: String Generator > String Generator > Intro
chunks.text: Create procedurally generated strings such as dates and time, hashes, numbers and timecodes.

chunks.title: String Generator
chunks.heading: String Generator > String Generator > UI
chunks.text:
**Generator** - Select the type of generator:

* [Block](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/block-generator/)
* [Formatted Date and Time](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/formatted-date-time-generator/)
* [Formatted String](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/formatted-string-generator/)
* [Hash](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/hash-generator/)
* [Hexadecimal](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/hexadecimal-generator/)
* [Random Date](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/random-date-generator/)
* [Random Number](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/random-number-generator/)
* [Timecode Generator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/timecode-generator/)
* [Value](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/value-generator/)

**Prefix** - Set the characters to appear before the number.

**Suffix** - Set the characters to appear after the number.

**String Manipulators** - Connect a [String Manipulator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/).

Example

chunks.title: String Generator
chunks.heading: String Generator > String Generator > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a Text Shape
2. Click the `+` button on the **String** attribute and choose **String Generator**.
3. Set the **Generator** to **Random Date**.
4. With the **Text Shape** selected, click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).

Each duplicated Text Shape is given a randomly generated date.

chunks.title: Block Generator
chunks.heading: Block Generator > Block Generator > Intro
chunks.text:
Create text blocks and optionally use Behaviours to populate paragraphs, lines, words and characters.

This can be used for many use cases including with pictographic fonts and for FUI text generation.

chunks.title: Block Generator
chunks.heading: Block Generator > Block Generator > UI
chunks.text:
**Paragraphs** - Number of paragraphs to generate.

**Lines** - Number of lines per paragraph.

**Words** - Number of words per line.

**Characters** - Number of characters per word.

**Mode** - Select a mode for the generator:

* **Unicode Code Point** - Enter values used to define a font's code point.
* **String** - Enter a string.

**Code Point** - When **Mode** is set to **Unicode Code Point**, enter a value to define the code point for the character. For example, 33 for "!" is the first code point for most western fonts.

**String** - When **Mode** is set to **String**, enter the string.

**Word Delimiter** - Enter a string to appear between words.

**Line Delimiter** - Enter a string to appear between lines.

chunks.title: Block Generator
chunks.heading: Block Generator > Block Generator > Code point guide > Basic Latin

chunks.title: Block Generator
chunks.heading: Block Generator > Block Generator > Code point guide > Extended Characters

chunks.title: Block Generator
chunks.heading: Block Generator > Block Generator > Code point guide > Symbols & Shapes

chunks.title: Block Generator
chunks.heading: Block Generator > Block Generator > Code point guide > Symbols & Shapes
chunks.text:
1. Create [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. Click the Generator button and select `Block`.
3. Set:
   1. **Words** to `3`.
   2. **Characters** to `1`.
   3. **Mode** to **String**.
4. Right click on the **String** attribute and choose `Add Array > String Array`.
5. Click the Add twice on the [String Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-array/) to add two new indices.
6. Enter `Y` and `Z` into the two new indices.
7. Enter a `,` (comma) into the **Word Delimiter** attribute of the **Block String Generator**.

This will create the string `X,Y,Z`. Try replacing the [String Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-array/) with a [Value Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/value-array/) (via a **Value** String Generator). This will create a string like `1,2,3` which can then be connected to attributes that accept comma separated strings like the **Indices** attribute of an [Apply Font Size](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-font-size/).

Example

chunks.title: Block Generator
chunks.heading: Block Generator > Block Generator > Code point guide > Symbols & Shapes
chunks.text:
1. Create [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. Click the Generator button and select `Block`.
3. Right click on the **Characters** attribute and choose `Add Behaviour > Random`.
4. Set the Random's **Minimum** to `2` and **Maximum** to `6`.
5. Set the Block String Generator's **Words** attribute to `5`.
6. Right click on the Block String Generator's **Code Point** attribute and choose `Add Behaviour > Random`.
7. Set this Random's **Minimum** to `8678` and **Maximum** to `8681`.
8. Enter several `space` characters into the **Word Delimiter** attribute of the **Block String Generator**.

This will create a string similar to `⇦⇨ ⇧⇦⇧⇩⇧ ⇩⇨⇩ ⇦⇨ ⇨⇧⇦⇧ ⇦⇨⇨⇧⇨`. Try changing the **Seed** of either of the [Random](/docs/nodes/behaviours/random/) Behaviours.

chunks.title: Formatted Date and Time Generator
chunks.heading: Formatted Date and Time Generator
chunks.text:
* * Layers* Utilities* String Generator* Formatted Date and Time Generator

On this page

chunks.title: Formatted Date and Time Generator
chunks.heading: Formatted Date and Time Generator > Formatted Date and Time Generator > UI
chunks.text:
**Formatted String** - Enter a string. See [Date and Time Tokens](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/render-tokens/#date-and-time-tokens) for options.

tip

Right click in the **Formatted String** input and choose **Date and Time** to insert preset tokens.

caution

Only **Date and Time** tokens are supported with the Date and Time Generator. For example, `<Composition>` is not valid. Use a [Formatted String Generator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/formatted-string-generator/) for that.

chunks.title: Formatted String Generator
chunks.heading: Formatted String Generator
chunks.text:
* * Layers* Utilities* String Generator* Formatted String Generator

On this page

chunks.title: Formatted String Generator
chunks.heading: Formatted String Generator > Formatted String Generator > UI
chunks.text:
**Formatted String** - Enter a string. Use `{<indexNumber>}` to reference an index. By default, this is a single line input but entering a soft return (`Shift` + `Return`) will convert the UI to a multi-line input.

Add - Use this button to add more rows (indices) to the array.

**0:String** - The first index in the array.

chunks.title: Formatted String Generator
chunks.heading: Formatted String Generator > Formatted String Generator > Formatting Strings
chunks.text:
Each string within the array can be referenced within the **Formatted String** by wrapping its index in curly brackets. The output string generated will replace `{0}` with the contents entered into **0:String**.

Example

1. Create a [String Generator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/).
2. Set the **Generator** to **Formatted String**.
3. Enter `Here's to the {0} ones.` into the **Formatted String**.
4. Enter `crazy` into **0:String**.
5. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
6. Connect stringGenerator.id→textShape.string.

`{0}` from the **Formatted String** has been replaced with `crazy` so the Text Shape outputs "**Here's to the crazy ones.**".

chunks.title: Formatted String Generator
chunks.heading: Formatted String Generator > Formatted String Generator > Formatting Strings > Values
chunks.text: The **Formatted String Generator** only accepts strings as inputs but a [Value String Generator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/value-generator/) can be used to convert values into a string. For example, the **Width** of a [Rectangle](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/rectangle/) can be added to a **Formatted String Generator** by first connecting it to a [Value String Generator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/value-generator/) and then connecting the [Value String Generator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/value-generator/) to an index of the **Formatted String Generator**.

chunks.title: Formatted String Generator
chunks.heading: Formatted String Generator > Formatted String Generator > Formatting Strings > Dynamic File Names
chunks.text:
The **Formatted String Generator** is also a good way to generate dynamic file names. This can be useful in combination with [Dynamic Rendering](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/dynamic-rendering/). Simply connect the **Formatted String Generator** to the **File Name** of a **Render Queue Item** in the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/) – each time the **Dynamic Index** increments, a new file name is generated.

The **Formatted String Generator** can be used to combine various inputs including data from a [Spreadsheet Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/), [Render Tokens](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/render-tokens/) and values from the Composition to create bespoke, unique file names.

If external data via a [Spreadsheet Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/) or the **Index** of an Array is already connected to the Render Manager's **Dynamic Index**, each render will be given a unique file name generated by the **Formatted String Generator**.

Example

chunks.title: Formatted String Generator
chunks.heading: Formatted String Generator > Formatted String Generator > Formatting Strings > Dynamic File Names
chunks.text:
1. Import a .csv or Google Sheet Asset containing the following data to the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/):

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Colour Hex|  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Red #ff0000|  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Green #00ff00|  |  | | --- | --- | | Blue #0000ff | | | | | | | |

2. Drag the Asset into the Viewport to create a [Spreadsheet Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/).
3. Set the Spreadsheet's **Column Title** to **Colour**.
4. Check **Fixed Row**.
5. Connect the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/)'s **Dynamic Index** to the Spreadsheet's **Row Index**.
6. Create a [String Generator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/).
7. Set the **Generator** to **Formatted String**.
8. Enter `Colour-{0}` into the **Formatted String**.
9. Connect spreadsheet.id→stringGenerator.array.0 (the **0:String** attribute).
10. Connect the **String Generator** to the [Render Queue Item](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/)'s **File Name**.

chunks.title: Formatted String Generator
chunks.heading: Formatted String Generator > Formatted String Generator > Formatting Strings > Dynamic File Names
chunks.text:
When [Dynamic Rendering](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/dynamic-rendering/), each file will be named `Colour-Red`, `Colour-Green`, `Colour-Blue`.

Render Tokens

Note that [Render Tokens](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/render-tokens/) do not inherit the styling that confirms they are valid within a **Formatted String Generator** so ensure they are spelt and formatted correctly. The styling will appear when connected to a Render Queue Item's **File Name** so this can be used to ensure they have been correctly entered.

info

Non indexed entries (empty curly brackets) are enumerated on based on their position in the string. For example, a string containing `{} {} {}` is the equivalent of `{0} {1} {2}`. This is also true where indexed and non indexed entries exist in the same string. For example, `{2} {} {1} {}` would be interpreted as `{2} {0} {1} {1}`

chunks.title: Hash Generator
chunks.heading: Hash Generator > Hash Generator > UI
chunks.text:
**Number of Lines** - Set the number of lines.

**Line Offset** - Move each line up by x lines.

**Random Seed** - Set the seed.

chunks.title: Hexadecimal Generator
chunks.heading: Hexadecimal Generator > Hexadecimal Generator > UI
chunks.text:
**Length** - Set the length of the string.

**Number of Lines** - Set the number of lines.

**Line Offset** - Move each line up by x lines.

**Random Seed** - Set the seed.

chunks.title: Random Date Generator
chunks.heading: Random Date Generator > Random Date Generator > UI
chunks.text:
**Start Date** - Set the start date.

**End Date** - Set the end date.

**Formatting** - Set the date format.

**Padding** - When unchecked e.g. 05 will be converted to 5.

**Delimiter** - Set the character(s) used to separate days, months, years.

**Seed** - Set the seed.

chunks.title: Random Number Generator
chunks.heading: Random Number Generator > Random Number Generator > UI
chunks.text:
**Minimum** - Set the smallest number to generate.

**Maximum** - Set the largest number to generate.

**Precision** - Set the number of decimal places to display.

**Padding** - Set the minimum number of digits to appear before the decimal place.

**Multiplier** - Multiply your number by this value.

**Whole Numbers** - When checked only whole numbers will be generated.

**Clamp Minimum** -

**Clamp Maximum** -

**Random Seed** - Set the seed.

**Delimiter** - Set a character used to separate thousands. e.g. 10000 > 10,000

chunks.title: Timecode Generator
chunks.heading: Timecode Generator > Timecode Generator > UI
chunks.text:
**Frame** - By default this is connected to the [Composition](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/)'s Time.

**Frame Offset** - Add/ subtract a value to the output.

**Frames per Second** - By default this is connected to the [Composition](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/)'s FPS.

**Delimiter** - Enter a character to separate the hour, minute, second and frame of the timecode.

chunks.title: Value Generator
chunks.heading: Value Generator > Value Generator > UI
chunks.text:
**Number** - Set a value to generate.

**Precision** - Set the number of decimal places to display.

**Padding** - Set the minimum number of digits to appear before the decimal place.

**Thousands Separator** - Set the symbol used to separate thousands. (e.g. `,` in `1,000`).

**Decimal Separator** - Set the symbol used to separate the integer part from the fractional part of a number. (e.g. `.` in `12.75`).

**Multiplier** - Output the **Number** multiplied by this value. This can also be keyframed to animate the **Number**.

chunks.title: String Length
chunks.heading: String Length > String Length > UI
chunks.text:
**Mode** - Set the parts of the string to count:

* **Characters** - Count how many characters there are in the string.
* **Words** - Count how many words there are in the string.
* **Lines** - Count how many lines there are in the string.

**String** - Enter or connect a string to count.

**Out** - A read only attribute displaying the output value.

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.heading: Introduction > Introduction > UI
chunks.text:
* [Change String Case](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-manipulator/change-string-case-manipulator/) - Change the case of a string.
* [Join String](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-manipulator/join-string-manipulator/) - Concatenate strings.
* [Regex](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-manipulator/regex-string-manipulator/) - Use a regular expression to match strings or parts of strings in order to do something with the result.
* [Replace String](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-manipulator/replace-string-manipulator/) - Find and replace sections of a string with another string.
* [Resize String](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-manipulator/resize-string-manipulator/) - Change the length of the string.
* [Shuffle String](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-manipulator/shuffle-string-manipulator/) - Jumble up a string.
* [Sub-String](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-manipulator/sub-string-manipulator/) - Clip start/end points of a string.
* [Transition String](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-manipulator/transition-string-manipulator/) - Transition from one string to another.
* [Unicode Offset](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-manipulator/unicode-offset-string-manipulator/) - Offset characters in a string by Unicode code p

chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.heading: Introduction > Introduction > UI
chunks.text:
info

String Manipulators can be stacked together to affect a single String. They can be reordered by clicking the yellow input connection icon on the Text Shape's **String Manipulators** attribute and dragging them above/below each other.

chunks.title: Change String Case Manipulator
chunks.heading: Change String Case Manipulator
chunks.text:
* * Layers* Utilities* String Manipulator* Change String Case Manipulator

On this page

chunks.title: Change String Case Manipulator
chunks.heading: Change String Case Manipulator > Change String Case Manipulator > UI
chunks.text:
**Mode** - Set the mode:

* **Lower Case** - Convert all characters to `lower case`.
* **Upper Case** - Convert all characters to `UPPER CASE`.
* **Proper Case** - Convert all characters to `Proper Case`. Proper case will capitalise the first letter of every word. See **Word Exclusion List** below.
* **Sentence Case** - Convert all characters to `Sentence case`. **Sentence Case** will search for punctuation typically marking the end of a sentence ( `.` `!` `?` ) and capitalise the first letter of the next word. Use the **New Line as Sentence Delimiter** option if you want the first letter after a line break to be capitalised.

**Word Exclusion List** - When using the **Proper Case** mode you can add comma separated strings (words) to be excluded. For example, if the source string was `this is a string` then adding `is,a` to the **Word Exclusion List** would mean the words **is** and **a** would not be capitalised resulting in `This is a String`. By excluding words in this way you are able to create your own custom **Title Case**.

caution

chunks.title: Change String Case Manipulator
chunks.heading: Change String Case Manipulator > Change String Case Manipulator > UI
chunks.text:
The **Word Exclusion List** is case sensitive. In the example above, if the source string was `this iS a string` then the result would be `This IS a string` because `iS` would not match the `is` entered in the list.

**New Line as Sentence Delimiter** - When checked, the first letter after a line break will be capitalised when the **Mode** is set to **Sentence Case**.

chunks.title: Join String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Join String Manipulator
chunks.text:
* * Layers* Utilities* String Manipulator* Join String Manipulator

On this page

chunks.title: Join String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Join String Manipulator > Join String Manipulator > UI
chunks.text:
**Delimiter** - Enter a character(s) to appear between the **strings**.

**Start Delimiter** - Add the delimiter character before the first **string**.

**End Delimiter** - Add the delimiter character after the last **string**.

**0:String** - The first string in an array. Use the Add button to add more.

info

The delimiter will only appear in-between strings (and not the text on your Text/Type Shape). If you want e.g. `text`,`string` then check the **Start Delimiter** attribute.

chunks.title: Regex String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Regex String Manipulator
chunks.text:
* * Layers* Utilities* String Manipulator* Regex String Manipulator

On this page

chunks.title: Regex String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Regex String Manipulator > Regex String Manipulator > Intro
chunks.text:
A regular expression (shortened as regex) is a sequence of characters that specifies a search pattern. A common use for regex is to match strings or parts of strings in order to do something with the result. For example, the default expression of `a+` will return all instances of the letters **a** found within the input string. So the string `Cavalry` would output `aa` because the word C`a`v`a`lry has two `a`s.

[Working with Regex→](/docs/nodes/general/working-with-regex/)

chunks.title: Regex String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Regex String Manipulator > Regex String Manipulator > UI
chunks.text:
**Regex** - Enter a **Regular Expression**. The result of the expression will be returned by the String Manipulator. See [Working with Regex](/docs/nodes/general/working-with-regex/) for more information.

**Capture Group Indices** - Where a Regular Expression includes capture groups, determine which groups are returned. Values should be comma `,` separated for lists or colon `:` separated for ranges.
