See [Working with Regex](/docs/nodes/general/working-with-regex/#capture-groups) for more information.

chunks.title: Regex String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Regex String Manipulator > Regex String Manipulator > Examples

chunks.title: Replace String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Replace String Manipulator
chunks.text:
* * Layers* Utilities* String Manipulator* Replace String Manipulator

On this page

chunks.title: Replace String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Replace String Manipulator > Replace String Manipulator > UI
chunks.text:
**Replace** - Enter the part of the string to be replaced.

**With** - Enter the string to replace the contents of **Replace**.

info

The `.` (full-stop/period) symbol is a special character in regex which means 'match anything'. In order to match a `.` it needs to be escaped with a forward slash like `\.`

chunks.title: Resize String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Resize String Manipulator
chunks.text:
* * Layers* Utilities* String Manipulator* Resize String Manipulator

On this page

chunks.title: Resize String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Resize String Manipulator > Resize String Manipulator > UI
chunks.text:
**Grouping** - Determine which parts of the string are affected:

* **Character** - Erase the string per character.
* **Word** - Erase the string per word.
* **Line** - Erase the string per line.
* **Paragraph** - Erase the string per paragraph.

**Progress Mode** - Set the mode to erase the string by:

* **Percentage** - Set the remaining length of the string as a percentage.
* **Fixed Length** - Explicitly set the remaining length of the string.

**Percentage** - Set a percentage of the string to remain.

**Length** - Set the number of characters/words/lines/paragraphs to remain.

**Direction Mode** - Set which direction to erase the string from:

* **Erase from Start** - Decreasing the **Length/Percentage** will erase the string starting with its first character/word/line/paragraph.
* **Erase from End** - Decreasing the **Length/Percentage** will erase the string starting with its last character/word/line/paragraph.
* **Erase Randomly** - Decreasing the **Length/Percentage** will randomly erase the string's characters/words/lines/paragraphs.

chunks.title: Shuffle String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Shuffle String Manipulator
chunks.text:
* * Layers* Utilities* String Manipulator* Shuffle String Manipulator

On this page

chunks.title: Shuffle String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Shuffle String Manipulator > Shuffle String Manipulator > UI
chunks.text:
**Mode** - Determine which part of the string is shuffled:

* **All** - Shuffle the entire string.
* **Regex** - Shuffle strings that match a regular expression.

**Regex** - When **Mode** is set to **Regex**, enter a **Regular Expression**. The result of the expression will be returned by the String Manipulator. See [Working with Regex](/docs/nodes/general/working-with-regex/) for more information.

**Capture Group Indices** - When **Mode** is set to **Regex**, and where a Regular Expression includes capture groups, determine which groups are returned. Values should be comma `,` separated for lists or colon `:` separated for ranges. See [Working with Regex](/docs/nodes/general/working-with-regex/#capture-groups) for more information.

**Grouping** - Determine which part of the String is affected by the **Percentage** value:

chunks.title: Shuffle String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Shuffle String Manipulator > Shuffle String Manipulator > UI
chunks.text:
* **Word** - A **Percentage** value of `50` will result in half of each word being scrambled
* **Line** - A **Percentage** value of `50` will result in half of each line being scrambled. Note that a line is defined by a 'line break' and not wrapping within a Text Box.
* **Paragraph** - A **Percentage** value of `50` will result in half of each paragraph being scrambled.
* **Document** - A **Percentage** value of `50` will result in half the document being scrambled.

**Percentage** - The percentage of the string that will be shuffled.

**Time Offset** - Offset any animation on a 'per group' basis. For example, connect a Behaviour like [Stagger](/docs/nodes/behaviours/stagger/) to create a word-by-word shuffle.

**Direction Mode** - Determine how a **Group** is scrambled:

* **Start** - Shuffle from the beginning of the string. A **Percentage** of `50` will result in the first half of the word/line/paragraph/document being shuffled.
* **End** - Shuffle from the end of the string. A **Percentage** of `50` will result in the second half of the word/line/paragraph/document being shuffled.
* **Random** - Shuffle each Group's string randomly.

chunks.title: Shuffle String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Shuffle String Manipulator > Shuffle String Manipulator > UI
chunks.text:
**Shuffle Type** - Determine the shuffle method:

* **Unicode Offset** - Offset the letters by a unicode code point. For example, an offset of 1 will result in an `a` character being shuffled to `b`. This mode is useful for non-latin characters.
* **Random Alphanumeric** - Shuffle using alphanumeric characters.
* **Custom String** - Shuffle from the original string using only the characters entered into the **Custom String** attribute.

**Unicode Offset** - The number of code points to offset when **Shuffle Type** is set to **Unicode Offset**

**Keep Punctuation** - When checked, `Space` characters and/or any punctuation marks (`.,-` etc) will not be shuffled if the **Shuffle Type** is set to **Unicode Offset**.

**Random Seed** - Change the seed used to randomise the shuffle.

**Custom String** - When **Shuffle Type** is set to **Custom String**, use the characters from the string entered here instead.

chunks.title: Sub-String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Sub-String Manipulator > Sub-String Manipulator > Intro
chunks.text:
The **Sub-String Manipulator** can be used to output a specified range of characters. The range is set in the same way all arrays work in Cavalry. For example, the text string `Cavalry` has 7 letters and so would be represented by a range between 0 and 6.

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 1 2 3 4 5 6|  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | C a v a l r y | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

chunks.title: Sub-String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Sub-String Manipulator > Sub-String Manipulator > UI
chunks.text:
**Start Position** - Set the index of the first character.

**End Position** - Set the index of the last character.

**Exclude End** - When checked, the index of the **End Position** will be removed from the range. For example, a **Start Position** and **End Position** of `0` will leave 1 character visible (`Id0` is in the range 0,0). Checking **Exclude End** will remove it.

tip

To output `ava` from the string `Cavalry` use a **Start Position** of `1` and an **End Position** of `3`.

chunks.title: Transition String Maniplulator
chunks.heading: Transition String Maniplulator
chunks.text:
* * Layers* Utilities* String Manipulator* Transition String Maniplulator

On this page

chunks.title: Transition String Maniplulator
chunks.heading: Transition String Maniplulator > Transition String Maniplulator > UI
chunks.text:
**Final String** - The string to transition to.

**Mode** - Set the mode:

* **Percentage** - Transition the string by a percentage.
* **Fixed Length** - Explicitly set the length of the transition.

**Percentage** - Set the percentage of the **Final String** for the transition.

**Length** - Set the length along the **Final String** (in characters) for the transition.

**Transition from end** - Clip the string from the beginning.

chunks.title: Unicode Offset String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Unicode Offset String Manipulator
chunks.text:
* * Layers* Utilities* String Manipulator* Unicode Offset String Manipulator

On this page

chunks.title: Unicode Offset String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Unicode Offset String Manipulator > Unicode Offset String Manipulator > Intro
chunks.text: Offset characters in a string by Unicode code point. This can be useful for working with picture fonts.

chunks.title: Unicode Offset String Manipulator
chunks.heading: Unicode Offset String Manipulator > Unicode Offset String Manipulator > UI
chunks.text:
**Offset** - Code point delta to add to each character.

**Clamp to Range** - Constrain results to a code point range. This is useful for ensuring only known characters are used.

**Code Point Range** - When **Clamp to Range** is checked, set the range of code point positions to clamp. (default: 33-126).

**Keep Punctuation** - When checked, punctuation characters are not affected by the Manipulator.

**Keep Whitespace** - When checked, whitespace characters are not affected by the Manipulator.

chunks.title: String
chunks.heading: String > String > Intro
chunks.text: A simple utility that creates a string (aka text) which can be used to pass a string through to another Layer.

chunks.title: String
chunks.heading: String > String > UI
chunks.text:
**String** - Enter a string. By default, this is a single line input but entering a soft return (`Shift` + `Return`) will convert the UI to a multi-line input.

**String Manipulators** - Connect a [String Manipulator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-manipulator/).

chunks.title: Stroke Duplicator
chunks.heading: Stroke Duplicator > Stroke Duplicator > Intro
chunks.text:
The **Stroke Duplicator** can be used to create complex combinations of Strokes.

A Capsule Shape with a Stroke Duplicator.

chunks.title: Stroke Duplicator
chunks.heading: Stroke Duplicator > Stroke Duplicator > UI
chunks.text:
**Stroke Count** - Set the number of Strokes to add.

See [Common Attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) (Stroke tab)

Example

1. Draw a path with the [Pen](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pen-tool/) tool.
2. On the **Stroke** tab, click the `+` button on the **Multi Stroke** attribute and choose **Stroke Duplicator**.
3. Set **Stroke Count** to `3`.
4. Right click on the **Color** attribute > Add Array > Color Array.
5. On the Color Array, use the Add button to add 2 more indices and set colors for each.
6. Back on the **Stroke Duplicator**, right click on the **Width** attribute > Add Behaviour > Stagger.
7. Set the Stagger's **Minimum** to `30` and **Maximum** to `100`.
8. Open the Stagger's **Graph** and use the buttons in the bottom right to flip the graph.

chunks.title: Stroke
chunks.heading: Stroke > Stroke > Intro
chunks.text:
The **Stroke Utility** can be connected to multiple Shapes to control their Stroke Color. By doing this, many Shapes can share the same color and so be updated in a single interaction from one Layer.

info

Once Shape's are connected to a **Stroke Utility**, the color of all connected Shapes can be changed from any of those Shapes or via the **Stroke Utility** itself.

chunks.title: Stroke
chunks.heading: Stroke > Stroke > UI
chunks.text:
**Color** - Set the Shape's color using Hex or RGB values (only RGB values can be animated). Click the color swatch to set colors using HSV.

Auto-complete Hex

Where hex codes contain repeated sequences of characters or numbers, they will be auto-completed. For example, entering `AB` and then hitting Enter will result in `#ABABAB`.

**Shaders** - A list of connected [Shaders](/docs/nodes/effects/).

**Alpha** - A master control for the opacity/ alpha of the entire shader network.

**Width** - Set the width of the stroke.

**Cap Style** - Set the appearance of caps (each end of the stroke) on open paths.

* **Flat** - A flat end that terminates at the end point.
* **Round** - A hemispherical end with the end point at its centre.
* **Projecting** - A flat end that projects half the Width beyond the end point.

Tapered Stroke

Note that **Projecting** caps are not supported when **Tapered Width** is checked. The **Cap Style** will fall back to **Round** in this instance.

**Join Style** - Set the appearance of joints.

* **Mitre** - Sharp corners.
* **Round** - Rounded corners.
* **Bevel** - Beveled/chamfered corners.

chunks.title: Stroke
chunks.heading: Stroke > Stroke > UI
chunks.text:
**Mitre Limit** - Sets the limit at which a sharp corner is drawn beveled.

**Dash Pattern** - Enter a number sequence separated by commas (dash, gap, dash, gap...).

**Dash Offset** - Offset the **Dash Pattern** along the path.

**Align** - Align the stroke along the path.

* **Centre** - Align the stroke along the centre of the path.
* **Inner** - Align the stroke along the inside of the path.
* **Outer** - Align the stroke along the outside of the path.

caution

Open paths only support **Centre** alignment. Where multiple contours appear in a single Path, any open contours will be set to **Centre** regardless of the Align setting.

info

If **Align** is set to **Inner** or **Outer** and **Trim** enabled, **closed paths** will be given a **Cap Style** of **Flat** regardless of their setting. Where multiple contours exist in one Shape, any open paths will respect the **Cap Style** setting.

**Trim** - When enabled the controls below are available.

**Start** - Wet the percentage along the Shape the Stroke will start.

**End** - Set the percentage along the Shape the Stroke will end.

**Travel** - Move the Stroke around the Shape.

chunks.title: Stroke
chunks.heading: Stroke > Stroke > UI
chunks.text:
**Reverse Path** - Reverse the direction of the Stroke.

**Tapered Width** - When checked, the Stroke is tapered from the start to end of the contour.

**Start Width** - A multiplier for the Stroke's **Width** at the contour's first point.

**End Width** - A multiplier for the Stroke's **Width** at the contour's last point.

**Double Taper** - When checked, the Taper's **Width** is set to 100% at a point along the contour determined by the **Taper From** attribute. The **Start Width** and **End Width** attributes can then, for example, be set to 0% to create a taper that starts at zero, increases to full width and then reduces to zero again.

**Cap Centres** - Offset the centre of **Round** caps.

**Taper From** - With **Double Taper** checked, set the point along the contour at which the **Width** is set to 100%.

**Middle Length** - Set the length of the Stroke either side of the **Taper From** point where the **Width** is 100%.

Example

chunks.title: Stroke
chunks.heading: Stroke > Stroke > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create 2 Shapes.
2. Create a **Stroke Utility**.
3. Select both Shapes in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).
4. In the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/), hold `Option/Alt` and connect stroke.id→shape.stroke (holding `Option/Alt` will make a connection to both selected Shapes at the same time).
5. Adjust the Stroke Utility's **Color**.

The stroke color of both Shapes will update.

chunks.title: Timeline Counter
chunks.heading: Timeline Counter > Timeline Counter > Intro
chunks.text: Use [Time Markers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-markers/) or [Pacing Markers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/#pacing-markers) to accumulate or trigger a value over time.

chunks.title: Timeline Counter
chunks.heading: Timeline Counter > Timeline Counter > UI
chunks.text:
**Count** - `Read only` A preview of the current output.

**Count Target** - Choose which type of marker to count:

* **Time Markers** - Trigger when passing a [Time Marker](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-markers/).
* **Beats per Minute** - Trigger when passing a [Pacing Marker](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/#pacing-markers) set to **Beats per Minute**.
* **Seconds** - Trigger when passing a [Pacing Marker](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/#pacing-markers) set to **Seconds**.

**Time** - The current time. This is connected to the Composition's Time attribute by default.

**Count Mode** - Choose what should happen when a marker is passed:

chunks.title: Timeline Counter
chunks.heading: Timeline Counter > Timeline Counter > UI
chunks.text:
* **Accumulate** - Add 1 to the **Count** each time the playhead passes a [Time Marker](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-markers/) or [Pacing Marker](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/#pacing-markers).
* **Trigger** - Set the **Count** to `1` when the playhead is on a [Time Marker](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-markers/) or [Pacing Marker](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/#pacing-markers) or `0` when it's not.

**Convolution Size** - Increase the duration over which changes to values occur when a Marker is hit.

**Convolution Offset** - Move the time the convolution occurs forward or backward in time relative the the Markers.

**Convolution Graph** - Shape or ease the convolution over its Size (duration).

**Filter Marker Color** - When using Time Markers, only count a specific color of Time Marker.

**Marker Color** - Choose a color to filter.

Example

chunks.title: Timeline Counter
chunks.heading: Timeline Counter > Timeline Counter > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create a Shape.
2. Create a **Timeline Counter**.
3. Add several [Time Markers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-markers/) to the Timeline.
4. Connect timelineCounter.id→shape.position.y.
5. Add an [Attribute Expression](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-interaction/#attribute-expressions) of `*50` to the Shape's **Position Y** attribute.
6. Hit Play.

Each time the playhead passes a **Time Marker** the Shape will move up 50px.

chunks.title: Transform Constraint
chunks.heading: Transform Constraint > Transform Constraint > UI
chunks.text:
**Target** - The Shape to constrain to.

**Offset** - Add/subtract a value to the Shape's original position.

**Rest Position** - The position a Shape will return to when **Position Strength** is set to 0.

**Rest Offset** - Add/subtract a value to the **Rest Position**.

**Rest Rotation** - The rotation your Shape will return to when **Rotation Strength** is set to 0.

**Rotated Offset** - Add/subtract a value to the **Rest Rest Rotation**.

**Position Strength** - A multiplier to **Out Position**. Adjusting this value will determine the position of your Shape along a vector between 0, 0 and the transform of your **Target**.

**Out Position** [read only] - Shows the [x, y] values being output by the Constraint. Where the **Id** connection combines both the x and y positions this attribute allows you to connect the separate [x, y] attributes to other layers.

**Rotation Strength** - A multiplier to **Out Rotation**.

**Out Rotation** - Connect this attribute to the rotation of another Shape.

Example

Pick up a Shape with another Shape:

**The quick way:**

chunks.title: Transform Constraint
chunks.heading: Transform Constraint > Transform Constraint > UI
chunks.text:
1. Follow steps 1-6 below (the long way).
2. Move to frame 50.
3. Select the Constraint.
4. Navigate to **Animation > Constraints > Transform Constraint Tools > Pick Up.**
5. Move to frame 150.
6. Navigate to **Animation > Constraints > Transform Constraint Tools > Drop**

Now Hand should 'pick up' Ball at frame 50 and then 'drop' it again at frame 75.

**The long way:**

1. Create 2 Shapes
2. Name one 'Hand' and the other 'Ball'.
3. Create a **Transform Constraint**.
4. Connect constraint.outPosition→ball.position.
5. Connect **Hand** as your **Target**. on the **Constraint**.
6. Set 2 position.x keys (fr0 = -200, fr200 = 200) for **Hand** (animate it horizontally).
7. Set **Position Strength** on the Constraint to **0** for both X and Y.
8. On frame 50, copy Hand's Position X value and paste it into the Constraint's Rest Position X.
9. Set a key on **Rest Position X**.
10. Go back one frame.
11. Set a key on **Position Strength X** with a value of 0.
12. Go forward one frame.
13. Set a key on **Position Strength X** with a value of 100.
14. Go to the first frame.
15. Hit play.

At frame 50 Hand should 'pick up' Ball.

chunks.title: Transform Constraint
chunks.heading: Transform Constraint > Transform Constraint > UI
chunks.text:
1. Move to frame 74.
2. Set a key for **Position Strength X** (should be a value of 100).
3. Move to frame 75.
4. Copy Hand's **Position X** value and paste it into the Constraint's **Rest Position X**.
5. Set a key on **Rest Position X**.
6. Set a key for **Position Strength X** with a value of 0.
7. Go to the first frame.
8. Hit play.

Now Hand should 'pick up' Ball at frame 50 and then 'drop' it again at frame 75.

chunks.title: Turbulence Modifier
chunks.heading: Turbulence Modifier > Turbulence Modifier
chunks.text:
Experimental Feature

This is an experimental feature. To enable, check **Enable Experimental Features** in [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/). Experimental features are only available as part of a **Professional** licence.

chunks.title: Turbulence Modifier
chunks.heading: Turbulence Modifier > Turbulence Modifier > Intro
chunks.text: Use noise to influence a particle's position and velocity to add interest to a simulation.

chunks.title: Typeface Array
chunks.heading: Typeface Array > Typeface Array > Intro
chunks.text: Create a list of typefaces that can be assigned to other Layers via their indices.

chunks.title: Typeface Array
chunks.heading: Typeface Array > Typeface Array > UI
chunks.text:
**Auto Index** - When checked the node will automatically output all indices.

**Index** - Select the index within the array.

**Reverse** - Invert the order the indices are output in. For example, where there are 3 indices `0,1,2`, their order will be reversed to `2,1,0`.

**Count** - Output the number of indices in the array.

Add - Use this button to add more rows (indices) to the UI.

**0: Typeface** - The first index in the array.

Example

1. Create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
2. Select the **Text Shape** and click the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) icon in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/).
3. Set **Count.x** to **1**.
4. Create 3 [Typeface](/docs/nodes/utilities/typeface/) Utilities.
5. Set a different font for each one.
6. Create a **Typeface Array**.
7. Click the Add button twice to add 2 more indices.
8. Connect each **Typeface** to each index on the **Typeface Array**.
9. Connect typefaceArray.id→textShape.typeface.

Each word in the Duplicator should now have a different typeface.

Double click to set Index

Double clicking on a indices' row will set the **Index** to that value.

chunks.title: Typeface
chunks.heading: Typeface > Typeface > Intro
chunks.text: Define a font and its weight to be used as part of a [Typeface Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/typeface-array/).

chunks.title: Value Array
chunks.heading: Value Array > Value Array > UI
chunks.text:
**Mode** - Set which value(s) is output:

* **Index** - Output all indices within the array.
* **Minimum** - Output the smallest value of all the values within the Array.
* **Maximum** - Output the largest value of all the values within the Array.
* **Average** - Output the mean of all the values within the Array.
* **Accumulate** - Output the total of all the values within the Array.

**Auto Index** - When checked the layer will automatically output all indices.

**Array Index** - Select the index within the array.

**Reverse** - Invert the order the indices are output in. For example, where there are 3 indices `0,1,2`, their order will be reversed to `2,1,0`.

**Count** - Output the number of indices in the array.

Add - Use this button to add more rows (indices) to the UI.

**0: Value** - The first index in the array.

Example

Start with a simple [Basic Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/) (Polygon) in a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).

chunks.title: Value Array
chunks.heading: Value Array > Value Array > UI
chunks.text:
1. Create 3 indices (**Add** button) and set values of 3, 5 and 8 for each index.
2. Connect valueArray.id→basicShape.sides.
3. Connect a [Random](/docs/nodes/behaviours/random/) node to the **Array Index** of the **Value Array.**
4. Set **Min and Max** on **Random** to **0** and **2**

Each duplicate will randomly be a 3, 5 or 8 sided polygon.

Also see [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/).

chunks.title: Value2 Array
chunks.heading: Value2 Array > Value2 Array > Intro
chunks.text: Create a list of two dimensional values that can be assigned to other Layers via their indices.

chunks.title: Value2 Array
chunks.heading: Value2 Array > Value2 Array > UI
chunks.text:
**Auto Index** - When checked the Layer will automatically output all indices.

**Array Index** - Select the index within the array.

**Reverse** - Invert the order the indices are output in. For example, where there are 3 indices `0,1,2`, their order will be reversed to `2,1,0`.

**Count** - Output the number of indices in the array.

Add - Use this button to add more rows (indices) to the UI.

**0: Value** - The first index in the array. Set two dimensional values.

Example

1. Create a **Value2 Array**.
2. Click the Add button to create a second index.
3. Set values for **X, Y** of `1920, 1080` and `720, 720` for each index.
4. Open the [Composition Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/) and, by clicking and dragging its header, make the window persistent.
5. Connect value2Array.id→composition1.resolution.
6. Uncheck **Auto Index** on the **Value2 Array**.
7. Set the Array Index to a value of 1.

As the **Array Index** is toggled between values of **0** and **1** the **Composition Resolution** will change from 1920 x 1080px to 720 x 720px.

Double click to set Index

chunks.title: Value3 Array
chunks.heading: Value3 Array > Value3 Array > Intro
chunks.text: Create a list of three dimensional values that can be assigned to other Layers via their indices.

chunks.title: Value3 Array
chunks.heading: Value3 Array > Value3 Array > UI
chunks.text:
**Auto Index** - When checked the Layer will automatically output all indices.

**Array Index** - Select the index within the array.

**Reverse** - Invert the order the indices are output in. For example, where there are 3 indices `0,1,2`, their order will be reversed to `2,1,0`.

**Count** - Output the number of indices in the array.

Add - Use this button to add more rows (indices) to the UI.

**0: Value** - The first index in the array. Set 3 dimensional values.

Example

1. Create a **Value3 Array**.
2. Click the Add button to create a second index.
3. Set values for **X, Y, Z** of `0, 0, 0` and `100, 100, 100` for each index.
4. Add a [Camera](/docs/nodes/utilities/camera/).
5. Create a Basic Shape.
6. Connect value3Array.id→basicShape.position.
7. Uncheck **Auto Index** on the **Value3 Array**.
8. Set the **Array Index** to a value of **1**.

As the **Array Index** is toggled between values of **0** and **1** the Shape's position will change from `0,0,0` to `100,100,100`.

Double click to set Index

Double clicking on a indices' row will set the **Index** to that value.

chunks.title: Visibility Collision Event
chunks.heading: Visibility Collision Event > Visibility Collision Event > Intro
chunks.text: Affect the Visibility or Opacity of Shapes when they collide within a [Forge Dynamics](/docs/nodes/shapes/forge-dynamics/forge-dynamics-shape/) simulation.

chunks.title: Visibility Collision Event
chunks.heading: Visibility Collision Event > Visibility Collision Event > UI
chunks.text:
**Mode** -

* **Visibility** - Hide Shapes when they collide. Note that this does not remove the Shapes from the collision.
* **Opacity** - Set the Shape's Opacity when it collides.

**Visibility** - If a Body starts with its visibility off, checking this attribute will set the Body's visibility to on after its first collision.

**Opacity** - Set the Opacity to be applied to a Shape when it collides.

**Specific Collisions** - When checked, use the **Collision Numbers** attribute to define which collisions are used.

**Collision Numbers** - Enter a value to specify which collision(s) are used to trigger the event. 0 is the first collision and use comma separated values to include multiple collisions. For example, entering `0,2` would include the first and third collisions.

**Fade Changes** - When checked, the Shape will return to its original settings.

**Fade Time** - Define the time (secs) it takes for a Shape to return to its original settings.

chunks.title: Visibility Collision Event
chunks.heading: Visibility Collision Event > Visibility Collision Event > UI
chunks.text: **Use Collision Index** - When checked, each collision will add 1 to its index. This can be used, for example, in combination with a Value Array connected to the **Opacity** – each time a Shape collides its Opacity will be change to the next value in the Array.

**Radius** - Size of the vortex influence area.

**Angular Strength** - Spin/rotation force applied to bodies on their own axis. Makes bodies rotate as they move through the vortex.

**Clockwise** - Direction of vortex rotation.

**Noise Generator** - Modulate forces based on noise.

**Noise Affects** - Which force component the noise modulates.

chunks.title: Cavalry Licence Types
chunks.heading: Cavalry Licence Types > Cavalry Licence Types > Legacy
chunks.text:
Cavalry offers 3 types of licence via the website:

* [Starter](#starter) - Requires no payment or credit card details to use.
* [Professional](#professional) - A paid version available as an annual subscription which includes additional features.
* [Team](/docs/tech-info/licensing/team/) - Purchase and manage licensing for a team.

See the website for information on [Team](https://cavalry.scenegroup.co/teams/) and [Education](https://cavalry.scenegroup.co/education/) licenses.

The [Enterprise](#enterprise) licence offers headless rendering via the [CLI](/docs/applications/cavalry-cli/).

chunks.title: Cavalry Licence Types
chunks.heading: Cavalry Licence Types > Cavalry Licence Types > Legacy > Starter
chunks.text:
The Starter licence is intended for learning or evaluation but can also be used for commercial purposes. It has no expiry so can be used for as long as you like and it's feature packed bar a few exceptions:

* Renders and exports are restricted to **1920 x 1080px**. You can work in a Composition of any size but any output will be resized to a maximum of either of those dimensions.
* Certain features are not available (see below).

chunks.title: Cavalry Licence Types
chunks.heading: Cavalry Licence Types > Cavalry Licence Types > Legacy > Professional
chunks.text:
The Professional licence increases the render resolution to a maximum of **15360 × 8640px** and includes access to the following features:

Try Pro

Most of the Professional features can be evaluated via the **Try Pro** button at the top of the UI. When signed in with a [Starter](#starter) licence, loading a Try Pro example will enable **Restricted Mode** which prevents saving or rendering. Removing the Professional feature(s) or signing in with a Professional licence will disable Restricted Mode.

The button is labelled **Pro Features** when signed in with a Professional licence as these scenes are useful as demo scenes.

chunks.text:
Legacy

This page only applies to Cavalry 2.6.1 and earlier. It's no longer possible to create new Teams but support for pre-existing Teams continues.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Intro
chunks.text:
Deploy Cavalry throughout an organisation with unified billing and volume licence management.

Several individual licences can be grouped as part of a Team providing organisations with a way to consolidate multiple licences under one invoice. Any user assigned a licence will have access to the same features as a [Professional](/docs/tech-info/licensing/licence-types/#professional) licence.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Intro > Team Hierarchy
chunks.text:
A Team consists of users with the following roles:

* **Owner** - The owner of the team.
* **Admin** - Add and assign licences.
* **Member** - Licences can be assigned to Team Members by Admins/Owners.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Onboarding
chunks.text:
To create a new team:

1. Go to [welcome.scenegroup.co](https://welcome.scenegroup.co).
2. Enter the **email** for the team's **Owner**.
3. Enter a **name** and set a **password**.
4. This will trigger a verification step. Enter the **code** sent via email to confirm your identity.
5. Enter the **Team Name** and optionally add a **domain**.
6. Enter **payment details** for any future payments. There are no charges made on this step.
7. Confirm the **number of licences** required. Your card will be charged at this point.
8. Optionally invite **Members** to the team and assign licences. This will send emails to the Members and onboard them if they do not already have an account. Click `Add Myself` to assign a licence to the Owner. Alternatively, this step can also be completed via the [Team Portal](#team-portal).

EU VAT Numbers

EU customers registered for 'intracommunity operations' should enter valid VAT/tax information including a country code (e.g. GB123456789). Any tax is applied on a 'reverse-charge' basis (removed from your invoice).

This information can be retrospectively updated via the [Profile](#profile) section of the [Team Portal](#team-portal).

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Team Portal
chunks.text:
The [Team Portal](https://team.scenegroup.co) is accessible to users with the **Owner** or **Admin** role and can be used to manage a team.

Active user

A green profile icon indicates that user is currently signed in.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Team Portal > Team > Add/remove Users
chunks.text:
Click the '**Add Users**' button to invite new users to join the team. Invited users will be sent an email which includes an invite. Once redeemed, they will appear in the list of users in the Team Portal.

If '**Assign available Licences**' is checked when inviting users then a licence will be assigned to a user if one is available at the time the invite is redeemed.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Team Portal > Team > Add/remove Licences
chunks.text: Click the '**Add Licences**' button at the top of the window to manage the number of licences available to the Team. On opening this window, the value in the `Qty` column will represent the current number of licences.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Team Portal > Team > Add/remove Licences > Adding Licences
chunks.text: To add more licences, increase the value in the `Qty` column. As this value increases, the payment information will update. Additional licences are charge on a [pro-rated](#what-happens-if-a-new-licence-is-added-part-way-through-a-subscription) basis meaning that charges are based on a percentage of the remaining time between now and the renewal date.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Team Portal > Team > Add/remove Licences > Removing Licences
chunks.text: To reduce the number of licences available in the Team's pool, decrease the value in the `Qty` column. There will be no charges or refunds at this stage. Any existing licences will remain active until the renewal date at which point the number of available licences will be reduced. If any of those licences are assigned to users, the Member(s) with the least recent activation date will lose access to the Pro features (you snooze, you lose).

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Team Portal > Team > Assign licences
chunks.text:
To assign a licence to a user either:

* Click the '**Assign licence**' button on a user's row.
* Use the `...` icon to the right of the row and choose **Assign Licence**.

If there are unused licences available one will be assigned to that user. If there are no licences available then an inline checkout will appear. On completion of the checkout the new licence will be assigned.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Team Portal > Team > Unassign licences
chunks.text:
To unassign a licence, use the `...` icon to the right of the row and choose **Unassign Licence**. This will return the licence to the pool of available licences.

Licence type status

The **Licence type** column indicates the licence type assigned to a Member:

* `Team` - A **Team** licence is assigned from the team's pool.
* `BYOL` - A Member has a licence assigned outside of the team's pool (**B**ring **Y**our **O**wn **L**icence).
* `-` - A Member either has a [Starter](/docs/tech-info/licensing/licence-types/#starter) licence or **no** licence assigned. In short, they do not have access to the [Professional](/docs/tech-info/licensing/licence-types/#professional) features.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Team Portal > Team > Assign Admin role (Owner only)..")
chunks.text: To assign [Admin](#team-hierarchy) permissions to a user, Owners can use the `...` icon to the right of the row and choose **Assign Admin Role**.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Team Portal > Team > Preview invites
chunks.text: Click the ⓘ icon above the **Members** list to preview a list of any unredeemed invites. Note that invites expire after 30 days and will be removed from the list shortly afterwards. New invites can be sent at any time and, where multiple invites for the same member exist, any one of their active invites can be redeemed.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Team Portal > Billing
chunks.text:
Review details of the current subscription including renewal date, number of licences and future costs.

Use the link to the **Stripe customer portal** to manage billing information including payment method, billing address and tax and access **invoices**.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Team Portal > Profile > Team Profile
chunks.text: Click the '**Edit Team profile**' button to update the **Team Name** or **Team Domain**.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Team Portal > Profile > Your Profile
chunks.text: To update details related specifically to your user, use the '**Manage User profile**' button to link to your [Account](http://account.scenegroup.co).

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > FAQs > Can I add a different email to send invoices to?
chunks.text: This is not currently possible via the Team Portal but can be requested via [email](mailto:support@cavalry.studio) by an admin user. Please ensure you provide details of the team in your request.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > FAQs > What happens if a new licence is added part way through a subscription?
chunks.text: Additional licences are charged on a pro-rata basis meaning that if the annual subscription is half way through then the remaining 6 months of the annual subscription will be charged. This keeps renewal dates in sync across the team. When the renewal date arrives, that licence will be charged at full price for the following year.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > FAQs > What happens if a licence is cancelled part way through a subscription?
chunks.text: The licence will be removed on the renewal date. It will remain active until that time and not be charged going forward. There are no refunds offered.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > FAQs > What happens if all licences are cancelled?
chunks.text: All licences will expire on the renewal date and the team will be removed. If you change your mind before the renewal date, add 1 or more licences via the Team Portal.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > FAQs > How can I delete a Team?
chunks.text: Either reduce the **number of licences** to **0** in the Team Portal or click the **Cancel Subscription** button in the **Stripe customer portal** via the **Billing** section of the Team Portal. The team and all licences will remain active until the renewal date at which point the team will be removed. If you change your mind before the renewal date, add 1 or more licences via the Team Portal and/or click the **Renew Subscription** button in the **Stripe customer portal**.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > FAQs > Do you offer PO/Invoicing?
chunks.text: Use of the Team Portal requires card payment but please [contact us](mailto:support@cavalry.studio) if invoicing is required.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > FAQs > Do you offer payment in other currencies?
chunks.text: Use of the Team Portal currently requires card payment in GBP but please [contact us](mailto:support@cavalry.studio) if you would like to discuss payment in EUR or USD.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > FAQs > How can I transfer ownership of the Team?
chunks.text: This is not possible directly via the Team Portal so please [contact us](mailto:support@cavalry.studio) from the Owner's email with details of the new owner.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > FAQs > How can we resolve a payment that has failed 3D Secure?
chunks.text: Where a payment has failed 3D Secure, the Team **Owner** will receive an email with instructions on how to resolve the problem. **Admin** users should contact the **Owner**.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Notes > Scenario 1
chunks.text:
* 4 licences are added to a subscription and assigned to team members.
* The number of licences is later reduced to `3` via the Team Portal.

**Result** - All 4 licences remain active but, on the renewal date, the Member with the least recent activation date will lose access to the Pro features (you snooze, you lose). Use the [Team](#team) section of the Team Portal to make any changes.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Notes > Scenario 2
chunks.text:
* A big project ends so the number of licences is reduced from `10` to `0` via the Team Portal.
* Later, a new project comes in which is expected to remain active beyond the renewal date so the number of licences is increased to `5`.

**Result** - On the renewal date, the number of available licences will be reduced from 10 to 5 and charged accordingly. Any assigned licences will be removed from the Members with the least recent activation dates (you snooze, you lose). Use the [Team](#team) section of the Team Portal to make any changes.

chunks.title: Cavalry for Teams
chunks.heading: Cavalry for Teams > Cavalry for Teams > Notes > Scenario 3
chunks.text:
* The number of licences is reduced from `5` to `3` via the Team Portal.
* The number of licences is later increased to `6`.

**Result** - A additional licence is charged at a pro-rated amount and the number of available licences will increase from `5` to `6`. On the renewal date, a charge will be made for `6` licences.

chunks.title: Logs
chunks.heading: Logs > Logs
chunks.text:
Cavalry saves logs when ending sessions (e.g. closing Cavalry). These can sometimes be useful when attempting to debug any problems.

Full session logs can be found in:

* **macOS** - `~/Library/Application Support/Cavalry/logs`
* **Windows** - `C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Roaming\Cavalry\logs`

info

**AppData** and **~/Library** are hidden folders. To find them:

* Windows - check '**Hidden Items**' in the **View options** for **Explorer**.
* macOS - in **Finder**, **Library** will appear when holding `Option/Alt` when opening the **Go** menu.

chunks.title: Mathematical Expressions
chunks.heading: Mathematical Expressions > Mathematical Expressions
chunks.text: Use the [ExptrTk](http://www.partow.net/programming/exprtk/index.html) language to write mathematical expressions when working with [Attribute Expressions](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-interaction/#attribute-expressions) and the [Math Distribution](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/math-distribution/).

* [String Length\*\*](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-length/) Utility - counts the number of characters in a string an outputs it as a number.
* **Composition Preferences** - you can now set a default resolution, frame rate and composition range via th

e new tab in the Preferences window.

You can add and remove attributes by right clicking on them in the Attribute Editor and selecting **Add to Control Centre** or **Remove from Control Centre**.

chunks.title: 1.1 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 1.1 Release Notes > 1.1 Release Notes > **Shape Editing**
chunks.text:
* **Join Contours** - where you have multiple open contours within a path, with any two end points selected, you can now use the Shape > Join Contours command to connect the two.
* **Open Contour** - running the Shape > Open Contour command on a closed contour will open it at the ‘first point’. Note - currently requires at least one point to be selected.
* **Set First Point** - running Shape > Set First Point will set the last selected point as Point Index: 0. Also available in the right click contextual menu in the Edit Shape tool.
* **Enable/ Disable Bezier Weight Locking** - you can now toggle between weighted and unweighted bezier handles (currently only available from the right click contextual menu for Edit Shape).
* **Point Snapping** - a new Snapping option in the Viewport. When enabled you can snap to other points on a path (any selected shape will be available for point snapping).
* **Onion Skinning** - Editable Shapes now have an Onion Skinning attribute (on by default). With Onion Skinning enabled in the Viewport you can now preview pre/post frames for any path animation. Use the settings in the Viewport button to customise the look.
* **Points Transform Tool** - you ca

chunks.text:
n now transform selected points with the Edit Shape tool. This is currently enabled using the checkbox in the tool’s options at the top of the Viewport. Note - rotate and scale are not working for path animation.
* **Delete point and edges** - Hold alt when deleting a point on a path to split the path at the deleted point. This will open closed paths.
* **Pencil Tool improvements** - the Pencil now draws more optimised (cleaner) paths.
* The **Pen tool** now supports angle snapping, snapping to the points on the shape being edited, and the other settings in the Snapping popover.
* Drawing with the **Pen/Pencil** will now add to any selected Editable Shape.
* You can now copy/paste paths between **Editable Shapes**.
* **Make Editable Primitives** checkbox in the **Shapes menu**.

* **Make Editable copy** (`Shift` + `Cmd/Ctrl` + `E`) will preserve the old behaviour of also keeping the original shape.
* **Make Editable** will now attempt to preserve materials. This does not currently support shaders.
* **Separate to Editable** has been added to the \*\*Shape menu. \*\*

chunks.title: 1.1 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 1.1 Release Notes > 1.1 Release Notes > Edit Shape Tool
chunks.text:
* The **Edit Shape tool** has been completely re-written and now supports editing very dense paths.
* The **Edit Shape tool** has an updated UI. Handles are now circular and points are square for corner points or circular for bezier points.
* You can now edit multiple shapes at once with the **Edit Shape tool.**
* **Tooltips** for hovered points when in the Edit Shape tool to reveal the point index.
* The first point in a contour is now highlighted yellow when in the Edit Shape tool.
* Double clicking on a point will select all the points in that contour.
* Shift double clicking on a point will select all the points in that path.
* Points for non-editable shapes have a new look in the Edit Shape tool.
* You can now select shape points with a Lasso tool (hold alt and drag to draw a selection).
* **The Edit Shape tool** now has a contextual menu (more commands being added here).
* Holding x and clicking on a bezier handle in the Viewport will delete (zero) that handle.

ays Visible**” this will disable the Visibility Bar completely for this layer, meaning it will always be visible. This means for example, you will not need to manage the visibility bar for this item if you increase the comp length.

chunks.title: 1.4 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 1.4 Release Notes > 1.4 Release Notes
chunks.text:
`Release date: 17th Oct 2022`

File Version Bump

Scenes created in Cavalry 1.3.1 or older will be converted when opening them in Cavalry 1.4. The file will be copied to a new scene which will need saving – you'll notice the legacy scene will be named `<yourSceneName> [Converted].cv` on opening. Any scenes saved in 1.4 onwards **will not be compatible** with previous versions of Cavalry.

CPU Renderer

Due to performance issues with Filters and Shaders we have removed the CPU backend in Cavalry 1.4.

* **Scale to Fit Text Box** - A new feature on the [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/). This scales the font size to keep large amounts of text inside the text box.
* New **Freeze Calculations** attribute for Shapes. This can be found under the Advanced tab and can be used to 'pause' calculations in order to optimise Compositions.

chunks.title: 1.4 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 1.4 Release Notes > 1.4 Release Notes > Notes
chunks.text:
* Importing video formats (MP4, HEVC, WebM, APNG and GIF files) is now 5x faster. There is still more work to be done here.

Cycles

We have made some changes to the graph in order to better handle cycles (e.g. creating connections/ hierarchies where a child can effect its parent, which then affects its child...). We are aware of some instances where connections that were allowed in 1.3.1 (and previous) are now no longer allowed so this may break some old scenes. There is no easy way to 'unpick' this as it's hard to predict every scenario but, while it should only affect a handful of people, please let us know if you suspect this may have affected any of your scenes in order to help us improve how we handle any such scenarios.

Legacy Scenes and the Image Smart Folder

On opening a file saved in **1.3.1** or previous where an **Image Smart Folder** is missing (e.g. is no longer in its original location on the file system), the scene will open but the **Image Smart Folder** will not appear in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/). Unfortunately there is no automatic way to recover this but following the steps below will reinstate the scene:

chunks.title: 1.4 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 1.4 Release Notes > 1.4 Release Notes > Notes
chunks.text:
1. Reimport the **Image Smart Folder** to the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).
2. Load the [Asset From Smart Folder](/docs/nodes/utilities/asset-from-smart-folder/) Utility into the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).
3. Drag the **Image Smart Folder** from the **Assets Window** into the **Asset From Smart Folder Utility**'s **Smart Folder Asset** attribute.

If you have trouble locating the missing folder then you can find the original file path in the scene file. Open the .cv file in a Text Editor and at the top of the file you'll see some entries like:

```
{

"data": {

"filePath": "@assets/Cans"

},

"nodeId": "asset#10",

"type": "file"

},
```

The `filePath` entry shows the folder's name and its location when the file was last saved.

In the event that an Image Smart Folder is missing in scenes saved in 1.4, they will be marked as such and can be relinked as expected.

* `alt/opt + clicking` the disclosure arrow in the Attribute Editor now opens/closes all Layers (this was actually a regression from a very early beta in...2018!).
* Dragging Layers into an empty space within the **Tag Drawer** will create a new tag and assign the dragged Layers to it. The tag is named after the first selected Layer.

* Web API - `post` no longer returns a 'null terminated string'.
* Some vertical misalignment between the Scene Tree and the Time Editor when isolating Layers with the **Animation Layer Filter** has been resolved.

chunks.text:
* **Text Backgrounds** now support the `last` token in the **Specific Indices** input.
* **Text Backgrounds** now support negative values for **Specific Indices** to select the last, penultimate, third-to-last etc paragraph/line/word/character.
* Enabling/disabling **Fill/Stroke** on selected Layers at the same time is now supported. Note - ensure you have the Fill/Stroke tab open before selecting the other Layers (clicking the tab will change selection).
* Connections to Attributes from other Compositions are now labelled as such.
* Deleting Layers by selecting them in the **Time Editor** is now supported again.
* When adding Random, Oscillator or Stagger Behaviours to Attributes via the `right click > Add Behaviour` workflow, Cavalry attempts to be more helpful in certain cases. For example:
  + Adding a **Random** to a default Ellipse's **radius.x** will set the Random's **Maximum** to **100** (the Ellipse's width).
  + Adding an **Oscillator** to a default Ellipse's **radius.x** will set the Oscillator's **Minimum** to **-100** and **Maximum** to **100**.
  + Adding a **Random** to the **Index** of a **Color Array** with **4** colors will set the Random's **Maximum** to **4**.

* Various issues with Text Backgrounds using Specific Indices have been resolved.
* A performance drop relating to Gradients in Duplicators has been improved.
* Where a Pre-Comp contained a Layer with a Shape Time Offset, time remapping the Pre-Comp was creating unwanted time offsets. This has been resolved.
* Fixed a crash undoing creating Ellipses or Rectangles after adding keyframes (required quite specific steps).

chunks.text:
* A long standing macOS bug where a single undo could undo multiple steps has now finally been reproduced and, we hope, confined to the annals of history. This has been a very illusive issue but we believe it related to right clicking in the Time Editor and then, without closing the context menu, left clicking in the Viewport – this corrupted the undo queue. It's possible we haven't found every instance of this issue yet so please let us know if it ever rears its ugly head again.
* Fixed a crash caused when deleting a **Forge Dynamics Shape** created via the **Shelf**.
* The **Replace Fill/Stroke** checkboxes were broken on the **Sub-Mesh Behaviour**.

chunks.title: 2.0 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.0 Release Notes > 2.0 Release Notes
chunks.text:
`Release date: 10th January 2024`

File Version Bump

Scenes created in Cavalry 1.5.6 or older will be converted when opening them in Cavalry 2.0. The file will be copied to a new scene which will need saving – you'll notice the legacy scene will be named `<yourSceneName> [Converted].cv` on opening. Any scenes saved in 2.0 onwards **will not be fully compatible** with any previous versions of Cavalry.

macOS Version Bump

Minimum requirements on **macOS** have been bumped to **macOS 11** for the 2.0 release.

chunks.title: 2.0 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.0 Release Notes > 2.0 Release Notes > What's new in Cavalry 2.0?
chunks.text:
Introducing:

* [Cameras](/docs/nodes/utilities/camera/) - Create a 2.5D environment to add depth to Compositions.
* [Pre-Comp Overrides](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/pre-comp-overrides/) - Override attributes contained within Compositions to create templates.
* [Component Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/component-shape/) - Collect Layers and promote attributes to create a simplified, custom container.
* **Background Rendering** - Hand off rendering to continue working in parallel.
* **Tapered Strokes** - Taper the width of a stroke along a Path.
* Big performance improvements.
* A new [Particle](/docs/nodes/shapes/particle-shape/) system is now available as an **Experimental Feature**.
* And much more...

chunks.title: 2.0 Release Notes

chunks.text:
* [Pre-Comp Overrides](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/pre-comp-overrides/)  - Promote a Layer's attributes so they can be accessed and overridden from the Pre-Comp itself making it possible to add variation to several versions of the same Pre-Comp.
* **Track Mattes** - mask Shapes with Alpha Mattes.
* A new [Transform Only](/docs/nodes/general/motion-blur/#transform-only) **Motion Blur** option for Shapes.
* [Particle Distribution](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/particle-distribution/) to position Shapes onto Particles.
* [Animation Offsets](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/#animation-offsets) - layer additional animation on top of any existing keyframe animation.
* **Increment and Save** added to the [File](/docs/user-interface/menus/file-menu/) menu.
* **Palette Generator** in the [Color Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/palettes/).

* Upgrades to the [JavaScript Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/javascript-editor/) :
  + Find and Replace text.
  + Auto-indentation.
  + Helpers for inserting matching brackets and double quotes.

* When hovering Shapes in the Viewport, **Pre-Selection Highlighting** now appears. The level of detail is adaptive to the complexity of the Shapes being hovered. For example, rather than highlighting every character in a paragraph, simply show bounding boxes for the words or the entire Text Shape.

chunks.text:
* The [Frame Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/frame/) has a new 'Seconds' interpolation.
* **Beta Features** have been renamed to **Experimental Features** to try and avoid the confusion between beta builds (e.g. Cavalry 2.0 beta 7 ) and the features.
* **Sorting** is now supported in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).
* [Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/group/) selection/interaction in the Viewport has been improved:
  + Clicking and dragging any Shape within a Group will now move the whole Group.
  + Double clicking a Shape will drill down to that hierarchy level.
  + Hold `S` to select a child of a Group.
  + Right click a Shape within a Group to select a parent within that hierarchy.
* `EXPERIMENTAL` [Trails](/docs/nodes/shapes/trails/) can now automatically inherit colours from a [Particle Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/particle-shape/).
* A Shape's **Opacity** is now respected when used as the **Input Shape** to a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).
* The [Mesh Explorer](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/mesh-explorer/) has had a facelift and now includes thumbnail previews.
* The **Notes** feature in the Scene Window now has a yel

chunks.text:
low background colour to improve contrast.
* When creating a Pre-Comp from the `Composition > Pre-Compose` menu (or via the contextual menu in the Scene Window) the new Pre-Comp will inherit the parent Composition's FPS.
* New **Flow Rows/Columns** attribute for the [Grid Distribution](/docs/nodes/general/distribution-types/grid-distribution/).

Previously, constraints imposed on moving bezier handles (e.g. moving a handle past other keyframes) were overly aggressive which could result in the 'double clicking an animation curve to add a new keyframe' feature resulting in inaccurate curves in certain cases. Similar improvements have also been made to the Graph Attribute curves (e.g. Falloffs).

chunks.heading: 2.0 Release Notes > 2.0 Release Notes > Enhancements > Performance
chunks.text:
* Many optimisations have been made in Cavalry 2.0. Speed improvements will be dependent on the Scene but on average you can expect to see ~200% increase in playback speed. Performance improvements will be most noticeable in complex scenes where we have observed up to ~600% speed improvements. Simple Scenes should see at least a 10% improvement in playback performance.
* Opening large Scenes is now much faster. In our tests a 2000 Layer Scene load time is now ~22x faster.
* Selecting large numbers of Layers is now ~100x faster.

chunks.text:
📣 **Make some noise!!** 📣

**Cavalry 2.1** is all about audio including **audio export**, **multi-track audio playback** and big improvements to the [Sound Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sound/).

chunks.title: 2.1 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.1 Release Notes > 2.1 Release Notes > New Features > General
chunks.text:
* New **Label Palettes** tab in the [Color Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/) which can be used to set custom **Label Colors** for Layers, Keyframes and Time Markers.
* New [Audio Monitor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/audio-monitor/) window.
* The [Audio Smart Folder](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/audio-smart-folder/) is now a  feature.
* Users with **`Starter`** licences can now export the **first selected Layer** to [Lottie](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/lottie-export/) to evaluate the feature.
* New **Try Pro** window. This can be accessed from the button in the [Shelf](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/) and is intended to provide simple examples that use the **Professional features**. Note that **`Starter`** users will be switched into 'Restricted Mode' which prevents saving and rendering – deleting the Pro Layer(s) will restore saving and rendering.

chunks.title: 2.1 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.1 Release Notes > 2.1 Release Notes > New Features > General > Audio Import
chunks.text:
The list of supported audio file types has been expanded to include:

* **.mp3** audio files.
* **.aac** audio files.
* **.caf** (aka Apple Loops) audio files.

See [here](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/#supported-file-types) for the full list of supported audio file types.

chunks.title: 2.1 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.1 Release Notes > 2.1 Release Notes > New Features > General > Audio Export
chunks.text:
Audio can now be exported to the following formats:

* New **Audio Only** Format (.aac).
* **MP4** (h264).
* **QuickTime** (Motion JPEG, Uncompressed 422, ProRes 422, ProRes 422 HQ, ProRes 422 LT, ProRes 422 Proxy, ProRes 4444, ProRes 4444 XQ).
* **WebM** (VP8, VP9).

chunks.title: 2.1 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.1 Release Notes > 2.1 Release Notes > New Features > General > Audio Playback
chunks.text:
More controls for handling audio playback:

* **Multi-track** audio playback support.
* The [Sound Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sound/) now has **in/out** points (aka Clips).
* A new toggle in the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/) can be used to **enable/disable audio playback** independently of the [Sound Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sound/)'s output.
* A new **Playback Volume** control has been added to the [Viewport Audio settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#audio-playback) popover.

Embedded audio

Note that audio contained within video assets is not supported.

chunks.title: 2.1 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.1 Release Notes > 2.1 Release Notes > New Features > General > CLI
chunks.text: * Support for **audio export** has been added to the [CLI](/docs/applications/cavalry-cli/).

chunks.title: 2.1 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.1 Release Notes > 2.1 Release Notes > New Features > Behaviours
chunks.text:
* The [Sound Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sound/) is now a **`Starter`** feature and includes the following improvements:
  + **Frequency Scale** - Choose a model to sample the audio file's frequencies with.
  + **Frequency Range Hz** - Customise the range of frequencies to sample the file within.
  + **Band Weighting Graph** - Control the contribution of individual frequency bands to the output value.
  + **Active Bands** (Output) - The number of active frequency bands selected in the **Equaliser**.
  + **Volume Adjustment** - Animate the volume of the audio track.
  + **Pan** - Bias audio to the left/right channel.
  + **Play Audio** - Animate audio playback on/off.

* **Loading video** Assets is now much **faster** in many cases.

* The **Import Google Sheet...** dialogue has been visually improved.
* Loading [Google Sheet Assets](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/google-sheets-asset/) is now **multi-threaded** meaning multiple Assets will now load concurrently and no longer block interactions while calling the data from Google's API.
* When duplicating a **Composition** in the Assets Window, [Guides](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/rulers/) are now also **duplicated**.
* The [Timeline](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/timeline/) now displays a **timecode** ruler when the Frame Indicator is in that mode.
* [Dynamic Rendering](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/dynamic-rendering/) - The **Number of Renders** attribute is now **Dynamic Range** meaning ranges can be set per RQI and it's now possible (wit

h scripting) to render an arbitrary set of sequences.
* A modal window now warns of any **missing fonts** when loading a Scene.
* **Missing fonts** are now marked as such in the Attribute Editor.
* It's now possible to **delete all** selected **Render Queue Items** in the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/).
* It's now possible to **delete** the **active Composition** from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/). Note that if the Composition that becomes the new active Composition is within an hierarchy, it will be moved up to the root level (this needs improving!).
* **Inactive** Behaviours now output 0 or their input value (this is not exhaustive across all Behaviours just yet).
* New **Circular** generator type in the [Color Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/).
* The [Value Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/value-array/) can now output the total of all its values.
* Support for mice with **horizontal scroll**.
* **Freeform scrolling** with a **trackpad** is now supported in the [Time Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/).
* A [Group](/docs/nodes/shapes

/group/) now has **options** to determine how Shapes within it **visually combine** with each other and other Shapes outside the Group.

* New '**Bind Selected Shape**' button added to the [Corner Pin](/docs/nodes/shapes/corner-pin/) Shape.
* New '**Create and Connect Rectangle**' button added to the [Bounding Box](/docs/nodes/utilities/bounding-box/) Utility.

Note that this bug will still occur when making the connection via the pop up menu in the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/).

chunks.text: We're aware of a situation where previously deleted Compositions (and their Layers) could persist within the .cv file. This is harmless but meant that these Layers appeared as tags on [scenery.io](https://scenery.io). These hidden Compositions will now appear when opening Scenes so they can be cleaned up. In the meantime, we're still on the hunt for the root cause so if this affects one of your Scenes, we'd love to hear from you.

File Version Bump

Scenes created in Cavalry 2.1.1 or earlier will be converted when opening them in Cavalry 2.1.2. The file will be copied to a new Scene which will need saving – you'll notice the legacy Scene will be named `<yourSceneName> [Converted].cv` on opening. chunks.text:
* Holding `Q` and scrubbing anywhere in the app now also supports timecodes.
* New **Select Attribute Keyframes** in the [Time Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/) and [Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/) contextual menus. Select an attribute in the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/) or by clicking the attribute's keybar and then right click in the Time Editor to reveal the option.
* The modal window to notify of **missing fonts** when opening a Scene will now only list **each font once** rather than for each Layer a missing font is used on.
* The examples in **Create > Demo Scenes** are now added to a **new** Composition rather than the **active** Composition.
* **Blend Mode** and **Opacity** attributes have been added to the [Distortion Filter](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/distortion-filter/).
* [Flatten Shape Layers](/docs/nodes/behaviours/flatten-shape-layers/) has a new **Maintain Transforms** attribute.

chunks.title: 2.1.2 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.1.2 Release Notes > 2.1.2 Release Notes > Notable Bug Fixes
chunks.text:
* Fixed an issue with the [Glow Filter](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/glow-filter/) rendering incorrectly with non-centre aligned **Text Shapes** and frozen Shapes with offset pivots.
* Fixed a specific issue where importing a .cvc could trigger a crash.
* Fixed a regression with the [Timeline Counter](/docs/nodes/utilities/timeline-counter/) where the **Filter Marker Color** was being ignored and the **Marker Color** UI was not updating correctly.
* Fixed an issue with occasional crashes related to running Cavalry on a second display which has been woken from sleep mode.
* The **Create > Demo Scenes > JavaScript > Closest Point** example now works again – this was an issue with the API.
* Fixed a crash with [Extrude](/docs/nodes/shapes/extrude/) using **Combine Meshes** in combination with a [Travel Deformer](/docs/nodes/behaviours/travel-deformer/).

docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/javascript-editor/) and [JavaScript Layers](/docs/nodes/general/javascript-layers/).

* Various issues around exporting/importing `.cvc` files have been resolved. Note that `.cvc` files exported before 2.1.3 may still have issues.
* **Clip Ends** were being positioned one frame too early when **snapping** to the **playhead** or the **Playback Range**.
* Using `Option/Alt` to replace Compositions that contained [Pre-Comp Overrides](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/pre-comp-overrides/) now update correctly.

red by setting certain ranges in the [Sequence](/docs/nodes/utilities/sequence/)'s **Skip Indices** field.

chunks.title: 2.2 Release Notes

chunks.text:
* The **Transform tool** has been added to the [Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/).
* **Proportional Easing** - When using the Transform tool in the [Time Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/) and [Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/), scaling keyframes also scales any bézier handles.
* **Maintain Proportional Easing** - When moving keyframes in the [Time Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/) and [Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/), any bézier handles surrounding the keyframe are adjusted to maintain similar easing. This can optionally be turned off in [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/).

nus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).

/docs/nodes/shapes/component-shape/). Along with the ability to rename attributes introduced in Cavalry 2.1.3 this provides a further simplified option for the UI.

* New **Justify** alignment option for the [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
* New **Paragraph Spacing** option for the [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/).
* The [Asset from Smart Folder](/docs/nodes/utilities/asset-from-smart-folder/) now has a **Count** attribute.
* When `View > Draw Outside Composition Boundary` is active, complex Shapes are now converted to bounding boxes to improve performance.
* **Verb Count** has been added to the [Mesh Explorer](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/mesh-explorer/). This is useful when working with the [Blend Shape](/docs/nodes/behaviours/blend-shape/) Behaviour.

e](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) now supports **looping** for Text Paths.

chunks.title: 2.2 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.2 Release Notes > 2.2 Release Notes > Notable Bug Fixes
chunks.text:
* Holding `Option/Alt` when using the **Run Script** button in the [JavaScript Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/javascript-editor/) is working again.
* **Disabled audio** playback now remains disabled when playback loops.
* The [Sound Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sound/)'s **Frequency Bands** as now set to a minimum of 2 to avoid a crash on Windows.
* The [Glow Filter](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/glow-filter/) no longer produces 'blocky' results.
* The **Text Background** now treats a single line break as a paragraph in line with the new **Paragraph Spacing** feature. The previous behaviour or a double line break was considered a bug so backward compatibility is not included – any legacy files will need updating.
* The **Input List** UIs seen in Forge Bodies/Shaders/Falloffs etc. now correctly update the list item Ids when removing from the list. This was causing different issues dependent on the context.
* **Hidden Guides** can no longer be double clicked.
* The styling of the `Animate Path` button in the Scene Tree has been restored.
* Holding `Cmd/Ctrl` when **parenting** Layers is now blocked.
* **Dimming** for **contextual menus** in the Attribute Editor has

chunks.title: 2.2 Release Notes

chunks.text:
been restored.
* **Auto-complete** in the [JavaScript Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/javascript-editor/) is now case sensitive.
* Fixed an issue affecting animation triggered by a [Timeline Counter](/docs/nodes/utilities/timeline-counter/) when contained within a **Pre-Comp**.
* Where a Stroke's **Dash Pattern** was a **decimal** value without a gap defined, the auto-generated gap is no longer rounded to the nearest integer.
* Fixed an issue with certain Cyrillic glyphs not rendering correctly as Layer labels causing a crash.
* The [Blend Shape](/docs/nodes/behaviours/blend-shape/) now behaves correctly in **Delta** mode.
* The [Math](/docs/nodes/utilities/math/) Utility can now be connected to an enum (dropdown).
* The **Time Offset** for [Value](/docs/nodes/behaviours/value/), [Value2](/docs/nodes/behaviours/value2/) and [Value3](/docs/nodes/behaviours/value3/) is now working again.
* The [Noise Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/noise/)'s `Context > Filter Position` option available within the contextual menu now retains its state between sessions.

* Exported **ProRes 4444** or **4444 XQ*

chunks.text:
* files that contain **alpha** but where the first frame is fully opaque now import to Adobe After Effects/Premiere Pro.
* The **Convolution Graph** for the [Timeline Counter](/docs/nodes/utilities/timeline-counter/) is now the correct way round. Note that legacy Scenes will not auto-update. In order to update a file either create a new Timeline Counter to replace the existing one or run `api.set(layerId, {"legacyGraph": false});` (replace `layerId` with the Timeline Counter's layerId) and then flip the **Convolution Graph** horizontally.
* Compositions with **non-integer frame rates** now report timecodes correctly to the **Frame/Timecode Display** and [Timecode String Generator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/timecode-generator/).

e rate will be rounded so reinterpreting the footage may be required.
* A hidden [Merge Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/merge/) being used as a **Clipping Mask** now behaves when opening saved Scenes.
* It's no longer possible to accidentally apply transformations to selected Groups or Comps in the Assets Window.
* A crash when rendering higher resolutions to **MP4** has been fixed and the limitations when rendering to MP4 have been clarified [here](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/#format-features).
* `isAttrReadOnly` now returns correctly when using [getAttributeDefinition()](/docs/tech-info/scripting/api-module/#getattributedefinition)

* [setVerticalToolbar()](/docs/tech-info/scripting/script-uis/#setverticaltoolbar) now renders correctly.
* Fixed a regression where **child Layers** where not returning when searching in the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/#search).
* Fixed a crash when interacting with [Trails](/docs/nodes/shapes/trails/) with **t

apered strokes** in the Viewport via a [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/).
* Fixed the situation on Windows where **Directory Junctions** with a missing origin in the **Scripts** directory could cause Cavalry to crash on startup.
* A [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) on a **Text Path** now correctly positions the characters around sharp corners.

chunks.title: 2.2 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.2 Release Notes > 2.2 Release Notes > Notes
chunks.text:
* NFT.Storage are no longer supporting uploads to their NFT.Storage Classic product and so this upload preset has been removed from the [Upload Preset Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/upload-preset-manager/) for new Cavalry installs. The `uploadPresets.json` file can be safely deleted from the [Preferences](/docs/tech-info/user-preferences/) directory to update this for existing installs but be aware this will also affect any changes made to the Web3.Storage preset.

* The **Falloffs** tab for the [Blend Sub-Mesh Positions](/docs/nodes/behaviours/blend-sub-mesh-positions/) has been removed as it is unsupported. We hope to reinstate this in future versions.
