chunks.title: 2.3.2 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.3.2 Release Notes > 2.3.2 Release Notes > Enhancements
chunks.text:
* The **Show Scripts Folder** command is now available from the [Scripts](/docs/user-interface/menus/scripts-menu/) menu.
* New inline button for the `File > Show Project Folder` command in the footer of the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).
* A **Starter** user can now reinstate the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) from the [Windows menu](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/) without using 'Reset to Default Workspace'.
* The [CLI](/docs/applications/cavalry-cli/#auth) now supports specifying a path to a CA certificate when working with Docker instances.

chunks.title: 2.3.2 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.3.2 Release Notes > 2.3.2 Release Notes > Notable Bug Fixes
chunks.text:
* **Windows** will now automatically select the **'High performance' GPU**. This fixes an issue where the Viewport and Time Editor could appear white. Windows laptops may have been previously been auto-selecting the 'low power' GPU so users may also experience **performance improvements**. Note that if the graphics card is not supported this issue may still occur.
* Fixed a crash when rendering **WebM** using the **VP9 Codec**.
* Fixed a regression with Text and **misaligned diacritic marks** (accents).
* The **Use Layer as Seed** attribute (Noise and Random Behaviour) no longer produces different results across **Pre-Comps**.
* Hitting `Cmd/Ctrl` + `D` when focus is in a **String** Attribute's field no longer triggers a crash.
* Scenes containing **Assets** located on a **missing NAS drive** no longer trigger a crash.
* A crash triggered by copying a Layer with a **label** containing certain **non-Latin characters** has been resolved.
* An **SkSL error** generated by the [Venetian Blinds Filter](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/venetian-blinds-filter/) no longer appears.
* [ui.onClose](/docs/tech-info/scripting/script-uis/#onclose) is now working.
* A crash with **Live Mode** and the [

chunks.title: 2.3.2 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.3.2 Release Notes > 2.3.2 Release Notes > Notes
chunks.text: * The Context Index Utility has been renamed to [Index Context](/docs/nodes/utilities/index-context/) for consistency with the Duplicator's Index Context attribute. This is a cosmetic change so will not affect legacy scenes.

chunks.title: 2.4 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.4 Release Notes > 2.4 Release Notes > New Features > General
chunks.text:
* New [Dependency Graph](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/dependency-graph/) window providing an interactive schematic view or map of the connections within a Composition. Starter users can preview but not create or edit. This replaces the **Flow Graph**.
* New [Mesh Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/mesh-shape/) for **deforming images/shapes** by adding vertices to create a **mesh**.
* A new [Mesh tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/mesh-tool/) for use with the [Mesh Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/mesh-shape/).
* [Third-party plugins](/docs/tech-info/third-party-plugins/) - developers can now create and distribute native Filters and Shaders.
* **Excel** (`.xlsx`) file import including an option to choose sheets/tabs on the [Spreadsheet Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/) and [Spreadsheet Lookup](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet-lookup/).

chunks.title: 2.4 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.4 Release Notes > 2.4 Release Notes > New Features > Behaviours
chunks.text:
* The [Oscillator](/docs/nodes/behaviours/oscillator/) has been upgraded. New features include:
  + **Seamless loops** when used as **deformer**.
  + New **Seconds** and **Minutes (BPM)** Time Modes.
  + Create a **custom Wave Type**.

Legacy scenes will use the 'old' Oscillator for backwards compatibility. These can be manually replaced but note that feature parity is not guaranteed so some settings may need adjusting.

chunks.title: 2.4 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.4 Release Notes > 2.4 Release Notes > New Features > Effects > Shaders
chunks.text: * New [SLA Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/sla-shader/). Big thanks to **David Farmer** for contributing his SLA noise shaders in celebration of the life of [Mark Coleran](https://www.pushing-pixels.org/coleran/).

chunks.title: 2.4 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.4 Release Notes > 2.4 Release Notes > New Features > Effects > Filters
chunks.text: * [SkSL Filter](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/sksl-filter/). Write custom filters in SkSL ("Skia Shading Language").

chunks.heading: 2.4 Release Notes > 2.4 Release Notes > New Features > Utilities

* [Apply Font Style](/docs/nodes/utilities/apply-font-style/) Style Behaviour. Dynamically set text styling features like **Underline**, **Strikethrough**, **Subscript** and **Superscript**.
* [Seconds to Frames](/docs/nodes/utilities/seconds-to-frames/) - Convert seconds to frames.

  + A **Regular** grid's **origin** can now be specified (e.g top left).
  + Creating **non-uniform** grids is now supported.
  + 2D Grids are now saved **per Composition**.
  + Grids can be **copied** and **past

chunks.text:
* Several issues with removing Pins from the Forge Dynamics [Pin Constraint](/docs/nodes/utilities/pin-constraint/) have been resolved.

n issue causing problems with saved attributes in legacy files has been resolved. This was reported in relation to 'Use Layer as Seed' on the Noise Behaviour.

chunks.title: 2.4 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.4 Release Notes > 2.4 Release Notes > Notes
chunks.text:
* The **Mesh Array** has been renamed to [Shape Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/shape-array/) to avoid any confusion with the new [Mesh Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/mesh-shape/) feature.
* The **hamburger** icon has been replaced with a disclosure (`...`) icon. This is used in the Color Window and Text Shape (variable fonts).
* In order for the default swatch names in the palettes that ship with Cavalry to appear they will need to be regenerated. To do this:
  1. Close Cavalry.
  2. Rename the `Palettes` folder to `Palettes-old`.
  3. Open Cavalry.
  4. Manually move any custom palettes from the `Palettes-old` folder to the new `Palettes` folder that will be (re)generated
  5. The `Palettes-old` folder can be deleted once complete.

chunks.title: 2.4.1 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.4.1 Release Notes > 2.4.1 Release Notes > Notable Bug Fixes
chunks.text:
* **Viewport Quality** = **Balanced** performance had regressed since Cavalry 2.3.2. The fix should mean that Viewport rendering in all modes is now slightly faster.
* [Image to Shapes](/docs/nodes/shapes/image-to-shapes/) is now working again on **Windows**.
* Clicking the **Project** palette tab in the [Color Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/) no longer triggers a crash on **Windows** if the `@project/Assets/Palettes/` directory is empty.
* Support for `.ase` import has been restored.
* The UI now updates correctly when making a connection to a 'generator' (e.g. Fill Color) in the [Dependency Graph](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/dependency-graph/).
* Deleting certain Layers from the [Dependency Graph](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/dependency-graph/) no longers triggers a crash.
* The [Background Blur Filter](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/background-blur-filter/) supports world transforms for the **Blur Shape** again.
* `.psd` Asset support has been restored.
* The [Stagger](/docs/nodes/behaviours/stagger/) Behaviour no longer prints (harmless) warnings to the console.
* `ui.Modal` no longer returns `false` for both buttons/options.

* Issues with `mesh.childMeshCount()` and `mesh.getChildMeshAtIndex` that broke the `Demo Scenes > JavaScript > Line Chart` example have been resolved.

chunks.title: 2.4.2 Release Notes
chunks.heading: 2.4.2 Release Notes > 2.4.2 Release Notes > Notes
chunks.text: * **File paths** have been unified across macOS and Windows to use `/` (slash) as a separator in the UI. A `\` (backward slash) can be used on Windows but these will resolve as `/`. For example, entering `\my\path\file` to **File Name** will preview as `/my/path/file.png` in the RQIs path preview. This includes any paths returned by the [JavaScript APIs](/docs/tech-info/scripting/scripting-getting-started/).

chunks.heading: 2.5 Release Notes > 2.5 Release Notes
chunks.text:
`Release date: 1st October 2025`

File Version Bump

Scenes created in Cavalry 2.4.3 or earlier may be converted when opening them in Cavalry 2.5. If converted, the file will be copied to a new Scene which will need saving – you'll notice the legacy Scene will be named `<yourSceneName> [Converted].cv` on opening. Any Scenes saved in 2.5 onwards **may not be fully compatible** with any previous versions of Cavalry.

chunks.text:
* The [Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layout-group/) now includes options for **Wrapping** and a new **Spacing Mode**.
* Importing **ProRes** files on **macOS** now uses **hardware acceleration**.
* **MP4 Export** now uses hardware encoding on **macOS** for improved export quality and speed.
* [Pre-Comp Overrides](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/pre-comp-overrides/) (also related to [Referencing](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/referencing/)):
  + The order [Pre-Comp Overrides](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/pre-comp-overrides/#reorder-overrides) appear in Pre-Comps can now be customised.
  + By default an Override's label is defined as `layerNiceName`.`attrNiceName` but where an attribute has been renamed, just the `attrNiceName` is now shown.
  + New compact UI design.
  + New **Reset Value to Origin** command.
* **Drag/drop** re-orderable Arrays/Compounds.
* [Components](/docs/nodes/shapes/component-shape/):
  + Any animated attributes are now revealed when any child Layers are hidden (i.e. the Component is in non-edit mode).
  + The 'spacious/compact' UI option has been removed now that re-ordering is possible.
* '**All Caps**' has been added as a

* **Constrain proportions** UI added for the **Box** and **Circle** [Arrows](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/arrow/).
* [Presets](/docs/user-interface/general/presets/) now support adding Layers from the Menus, Shelf and via drag and drop. For example, an Image Shader's **Scale Mode** can be set to **Fit Cover** when an image is dropped into the Viewport.
* The 'splitter' position for the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) and [JavaScript Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/javascript-editor/) is now saved between sessions.
* Holding `Shift` when importing Assets now opens Finder/Explorer to the `Scenes` directory defined in [Project Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/project-settings/) – useful when working with [References](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/referencing/).

ene-window/#close-compositions).

* An issue where adding **Feather** to **Clipping Masks** could offset the original Shape has been resolved.
* Fixed an edge case where **individual** Attribute Expressions for 2.5D transforms were not working.
* An issue with the [Stroke Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/stroke/), **Inner Alignment** and the **Composition Boundary** has been resolved.
* A **crash** relating to **Live Mode** and loading a [Range Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/range-falloff/) has been resolved.

mponents](/docs/nodes/shapes/component-shape/) could be lost has been resolved.

chunks.text:
* **Editable Motion Paths** - manipulate [motion paths](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/motion-paths/) in the **Viewport**.
* Enable **Color Management** for Scenes. See [Color Management](/docs/user-interface/general/color-management/).
* [Pivot tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pivot-tool/) - The addition of the Manipulator and editable Motion Paths has meant a new tool is required to edit pivots. Note that this replaces the previous workflows when using the Select tool.
* **Manipulator** - A new 3d-like Viewport manipulator for the [Select](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) tool. It's used with the new [Lattice](/docs/nodes/behaviours/lattice/) and [Lattice Controller](/docs/nodes/utilities/lattice-controller/) and can be optionally enabled for use with Shape Layers.
* [File](/docs/user-interface/menus/file-menu/) > **Reduce Scene** - Remove any unused Compositions and Assets from the Scene.
* New **Systems Diagnostics** window available via the [Help](/docs/user-interface/menus/help/) menu. This can be used to help debug any issues and share useful information in support tickets when troubleshooting.

Cavalry joined the team at  in February 2026. As part of their mission to empower the world to design, the paid 'Professional' features in Cavalry are now **free**!

chunks.title: API Module
chunks.heading: API Module > API Module > Introduction
chunks.text:
The following APIs are all in the `api` namespace. They are **ONLY** available in the [JavaScript Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/javascript-editor/) and not available when writing expressions in the [JavaScript Layers](/docs/nodes/general/javascript-layers/).

All commands in this namespace must be prefixed with `api.` e.g `api.create("null", "My Null");`

The API can communicate with the Web (see [Web APIs](/docs/tech-info/scripting/web-apis/)) and execute shell commands. See [runProcess](#runprocess) below.

tip

When working with Layers and Attributes it is important to know their `layerId` and `attrId`.

To find the **layerId**:

1. Right click on a layer in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/), [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) or its header bar in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).
2. Select `Copy Layer Id`.

This will copy the Layer's Id to the clipboard.

To find the **attrId**:

chunks.title: API Module
chunks.heading: API Module > API Module > Introduction
chunks.text:
1. Right click on an attribute in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).
2. Choose `Copy Scripting Path` from the contextual menu.
3. Select and click an option from the list.

This will copy the attribute's Id to the clipboard.

These Ids can then be used within a script. In the example below, **basicShape#1** is the `layerId` and **position.x** is the `attrId`.

```
api.get("basicShape#1", "position.x");
```

* `attrId` // the attribute's Id

* `isCompound` // true if the attribute is a compound (for example a point within a Graph attr

chunks.heading: API Module > API Module > Member Functions > Working with Attributes > modifyKeyframeTangent(layerId:string, data:object)
chunks.text:
Modify the keyframe tangents.
The supplied object must include a `frame` key.
Both the in and out handle will be affected unless a handle is specified and the handle is not weight and angle locked.

* `inHandle` // An optional boolean value used to specify the inHandle to be affected.
* `outHandle` // An optional boolean value used to specify the outHandle to be affected.
* `angleLocked` // Boolean stating if the key tangents are angle locked or not (optional).
* `weightLocked` // Boolean stating if the key tangents are weight locked or not (optional).
* `angle` // Set a new angle for the keyframe tangent, 0 is flat (optional).
* `weight` // Set a new weight for the keyframe tangent (optional).
* `xValue` // The absolute value for the bezier handle's X position (frame).
* `yValue` // The absolute value for the bezier handle's Y position (value).

chunks.heading: API Module > API Module > Member Functions > Working with Attributes > magicEasing(layerId:string, attrId:string, frame:int, easingName:string, expression:string)
chunks.text:
Apply **Magic Easing** to an Attribute's keyframe and optionally add an expression.

```
// Add SlowOut Magic Easing

var shapeId = api.create("basicShape");

api.keyframe(shapeId, 0, {"position.x": 0})

api.keyframe(shapeId, 24, {"position.x": 200})

api.magicEasing(shapeId, "position.x", 0, "SlowOut");
```

```
// Add Custom Magic Easing

var shapeId = api.create("basicShape");

api.keyframe(shapeId, 0, {"position.x": 0})

api.keyframe(shapeId, 24, {"position.x": 200})

api.magicEasing(shapeId, "position.x", 0, "Custom", "1 - pow(1 - x, 5)");
```

Valid **Magic Easing** names are:

* "SlowIn"
* "SlowOut"
* "SlowInSlowOut"
* "VerySlowIn"
* "VerySlowOut"
* "VerySlowInVerySlowOut"
* "SpringIn"
* "SpringOut"
* "SpringInSpringOut"
* "SmallSpringIn"
* "SmallSpringOut"
* "SmallSpringInSmallSpringOut"
* "AnticipateIn"
* "OvershootOut"
* "AnticipateInOvershootOut"
* "BounceIn"
* "BounceOut"
* "BounceInBounceOut"
* "Custom" // This must be used if adding an expression
* "None"

chunks.text:
Like `load`, `exec` will load and run JavaScript but it does not require a saved file.

The first argument is a `scriptId`. The `scriptId` exists because Cavalry asks for permission to perform certain tasks (like using the WebAPIs or writing to the hard drive) on a per-script basis. This information is stored using the `scriptId` so that permission will only be requested once per Id.

We recommend using reverse domain notation `com.<yourCompany>.<yourScript>` as a basis for `scriptId`s.

```

api.exec("com.scenegroup.scriptName", myScript)
```

chunks.heading: API Module > API Module > Member Functions > Files and Paths > writeToFile(filePath:string, content:string, overwriteExisting:bool=false) → bool
chunks.text:
Write a string to a file. Returns if the write was successful. If a file already exists, an error is returned. Set the 'overwriteExisting' argument to `true` to override the error and replace the existing file - proceed with caution.

Binary data cannot be written from this API, for that, please use `writeEncodedToBinaryFile`. [filePathExists](#filepathexists) can also be used to add any additional success/warning messages to the console.

Backslashes

JavaScript does not support single backslashes (`\`) in file paths (it is an escape character) but slashes (`/`) are valid on Windows. Alternatively, replace single backslashes with double backslashes (`\\`).

chunks.title: Cavalry Module
chunks.heading: Cavalry Module > Cavalry Module > Introduction
chunks.text:
This module gives access to the Path class, functions for creating `noise` and `random` numbers along with a number of utilities to make working with color easier, and, a whole host of maths functions such as `clamp`, `norm`, `map` and `dist`.
The following methods are available to the [JavaScript Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/javascript-utility/), and the [JavaScript Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/javascript-editor/).
Everything in this module is in the `cavalry` namespace and so methods need prefixing with `cavalry.` e.g `var distance = cavalry.dist(0,0,100,200);`

The examples given are for use in the [JavaScript Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/javascript-editor/) (less setup required to run examples).

JavaScript Deformers also have access to the [`def` module](/docs/tech-info/scripting/deformer-module/), which provides methods for accessing and modifying the geometry being deformed.

chunks.title: Cavalry Module
chunks.heading: Cavalry Module > Cavalry Module > Member Functions > Path Class
chunks.text:
The Cavalry module contains a Path class which can be used to construct paths which can then be drawn on screen. Path itself contains several methods.

Several of these methods use the word 'param' or 'parameter'. This is a number between 0..1 which represents a progression along the curve's control cage from 0 (the beginning) to 1 (the end). The control cage, formed by the curve's control points, outlines the basic shape of the curve. Note that a 'param' value of 0.5 does not necessarily represent a position half way along the curve. This is because the relationship between the param value and the curve's length is not linear due to the influence of the curve's control points and its resulting shape. To convert length values into param values, use [paramAtLength](#paramatlength).

Copying Shapes

Right clicking on a Shape in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) and choosing `Copy as JavaScript` will copy the Shape's information to the clipboard as JavaScript code.

chunks.title: Cavalry Module
chunks.heading: Cavalry Module > Cavalry Module > Member Functions > Path Class > Drawing a path:

chunks.title: Cavalry Module
chunks.heading: Cavalry Module > Cavalry Module > Member Functions > Path Class > conicTo(cp1X:number, cp1Y:number, endX:number, endY:number, weight:number)
chunks.text:
Adds a conic to the path. Where weight:

* `= 1` - the curve is a quadratic bézier curve (a conic with a weight of 1 is mathematically equivalent to a quadratic curve).
* `< 1` - the curve approximates an ellipse. The smaller the weight, the more the curve leans towards being circular, with smaller weights resulting in sharper curves.
* `> 0` - the curve begins to resemble a hyperbola. As the weight increases, the curve opens up more.
* `= 0` (or a very low value) - these may produce degenerate cases or curves that don't visually change much from a straight line or a very sharp curve.

chunks.heading: Cavalry Module > Cavalry Module > Member Functions > Path Class > pathData() → object → object")
chunks.text:
This returns an array of dictionaries and provides a convenient way to iterate and change an existing path as opposed to creating a new [Path Class](#path-class). Each dictionary contains the verb `type` variable e.g. `moveTo` or `lineTo` along with any 'point' objects relevant to the verb.

The dictionary will contain different objects depending on the verb type:

* `moveTo`: contains a `point` object (with x and y variables).
* `lineTo`: contains a `point` object (with x and y variables).
* `quadTo`: contains a `cp1` object representing the control point (with x and y variables) along with a `point` object (with x and y variables). This is the end point of the `quadTo` verb.
* `cubicTo`: contains `cp1` and `cp2` objects representing the first and second control points (both with x and y variables) along with a `point` object (with x and y variables). This is the end point of the `cubicTo` verb.
* `close`: contains no points.

Represent a line defined by two points with various geometric operations.

chunks.text:
Returns an object representing the bounding box of some text without the need to actually create a text shape.

* **width** - The width of the text
* **height** - The height of the text

chunks.title: Cavalry Module
chunks.heading: Cavalry Module > Cavalry Module > Member Functions > Text > fontMetrics(fontFamily:string, fontStyle:string, fontSize:int) → {top:number, ascent:number, descent:number, bottom:number, leading:int, averageCharacterWidth:number, maxCharacterWidth:number, xMin:number, xMax:number, xHeight:number, capHeight:number}
chunks.text:
Returns an object containing information about the given font. The resulting metrics are scaled by the font size.

* **top** - greatest extent above origin of any glyph bounding box, typically negative; deprecated with variable fonts
* **ascent** - distance to reserve above baseline, typically negative
* **descent** - distance to reserve below baseline, typically positive
* **bottom** - greatest extent below origin of any glyph bounding box, typically positive; deprecated with variable fonts
* **leading** - distance to add between lines, typically positive or zero
* **averageCharacterWidth** - average character width, zero if unknown
* **maxCharacterWidth** - maximum character width, zero if unknown
* **xMin** - greatest extent to left of origin of any glyph bounding box, typically negative; deprecated with variable fonts
* **xMax** - greatest extent to right of origin of any glyph bounding box, typically positive; deprecated with variable fonts
* **xHeight** - height of lower-case 'x', zero if unknown, typically negative
* **capHeight** - height of an upper-case letter, zero if unknown, typically negative

chunks.title: Cavalry Module
chunks.heading: Cavalry Module > Cavalry Module > Member Functions > Utilities > versionLessThan(version:string) → bool
chunks.text:
This will return `true` if the version of Cavalry in use is less than the specified version. This is useful to add support for features in scripts that depend on the version of Cavalry.

```
// This will return true in Cavalry 1.3.1, and false in Cavalry 1.5.0

console.log(cavalry.versionLessThan("1.4.0"));
```

SEMVER

Cavalry uses [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) for version numbers.

`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` (e.g. 1.5.0) is used for official releases.

`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.PRE-RELEASE-TYPE.NUMBER` (e.g. 2.0.0-beta.1) is used for pre-release builds.

chunks.title: Render Scripts
chunks.heading: Render Scripts > Render Scripts > Introduction
chunks.text:
Cavalry can execute scripts:

* To setup a **Render Queue Item**.
* Before every render performed by a **Render Queue Item**.
* After every render performed by a **Render Queue Item**.

The following APIs are all in the `render` namespace. They are **ONLY** available in a Render Queue Item. Scripts can be added to the corresponding editor on the Render Queue Item's **Scripts** tab in the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/).

Dynamic Rendering

When using [Dynamic Rendering](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/dynamic-rendering/), the **Dynamic Index** can be accessed using the [api.getDynamicIndex()](/docs/tech-info/scripting/api-module/#getdynamicindex) member.

Any JavaScript execution will block further rendering until the script finishes running. This is by design so that any processes like downloading/replacing Assets or altering the Scene in some way can complete before starting the next render.

Image Sequences

Scripts are executed before and after the entire sequence is rendered and not before and after each individual image.

chunks.text: Add a script that runs before any render setup begins and so can be used to affect the **Render Queue Item** itself.

chunks.text:
Add a script that runs once a **Render Queue Item** has completed.

info

Scripts can include using the JavaScript API to perform tasks such as modify attributes, to pull new information from the web, or the replacement and reloading of Assets.

Pro Feature

Pro features are only available with a **Professional** licence. **Starter** licences can evaluate most Professional features via the [Try Pro](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/shelf/#try-pro--pro-features) button at the top of the Viewport. chunks.title: Script UIs
chunks.heading: Script UIs > Script UIs > Introduction
chunks.text:
Scripts with user interfaces (UIs) can be built to make them easier to use or share with other people. They can be tested from the [JavaScript Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/javascript-editor/) and then saved to the file system meaning they can be opened as a Window and so docked and saved as part of a [Workspace](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/general/workspaces/).

For Scripts to appear in the [Scripts](/docs/user-interface/menus/scripts-menu/) menu they should be saved with the extension `.js` or `.jsc` to:

* **macOS** - `~/Library/Application Support/Cavalry/Scripts`
* **Windows** - `C:\Users\<USERNAME>\AppData\Roaming\Cavalry\Scripts`

Encryption

`.jsc` is an encrypted JavaScript format. Scripts can be saved to this format using the `Save Encrypted...` button in the JavaScript Editor. Once in this format, scripts can only be read by Cavalry – an end user will not be able to see the source. Remember to keep a copy of a script in its unencrypted form as this is a one-way operation.

Location

**AppData** and **~/Library** are hidden folders. To find them:

chunks.title: Script UIs
chunks.heading: Script UIs > Script UIs > Introduction
chunks.text:
* Windows - check '**Hidden Items**' in the **View options** for **Explorer**.
* macOS - in **Finder**, **Library** will appear if you hold `option` as you open the **Go** menu.

A quick way navigate to this folder is to use the `Help` or `Scripts > Show Scripts Folder` command. Scripts saved to this location will then appear under the `Scripts` menu.

Scripts can be organised into folders within the **Scripts** folder. These folders will appear as a nested hierarchy under the `Scripts` menu.

tip

Scripts are 'hot loaded' so there's no need to restart the application in order to update scripts. Simply close and reopen the script's window. This includes adding new scripts to the Scripts folder — these will appear the next time the `Scripts` menu is opened.

chunks.title: Script UIs
chunks.heading: Script UIs > Script UIs > Assets
chunks.text:
If a script has assets (for example images), these should be placed inside a folder with the suffix `_assets`. Any directory ending with `_assets` will be hidden when navigating the `Scripts` menu.

For example:

A script's location can be accessed using the property `ui.scriptLocation` which will return the script's parent folder. This can then be used to build relative paths when adding images or other assets to a script's UI.

For example:

```
// Create a button and set an image

var buttonTop = new ui.Button("Top");

buttonTop.setImage(ui.scriptLocation + "/scriptName_assets/icon.png");
```

Testing Assets

Assets can only be referenced via **absolute** file paths when running scripts from the [JavaScript Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/javascript-editor/), In order to use `ui.scriptLocation`, the script must be saved to the **Scripts** folder and run from the [Scripts](/docs/user-interface/menus/scripts-menu/) menu.

chunks.heading: Script UIs > Script UIs > UI Module > registerDragDropMimeType(mimeType:string)
chunks.text:
UI windows support drag and drop functionality. The [Container](#container) Widget can also be used to create multiple, distinct (noncontiguous) drag and drop areas within the same UI window – meaning the event will only occur within the Container rather than the entire UI window. At least one `MIME type` for the UI window to accept **must** be registered. To register multiple MIME types, add each on a separate line.

Valid `MIME type` values are:

* `layerIds` // Accepts a Layer(s). Returns `{"layerIds":[layerId:string]}`
* `assetIds` // Accepts an Asset(s) from the Assets Window. Returns `{"assetIds":[assetId:string]}`
* `url` // Accepts a file or web URL. Returns `{"text":URL:string,"url":URL:string}`
* `color` // Accepts a color swatch. Returns `{"colorHexA":hexA:string,"colorHex":hex:string}`
* `text` // Accepts a string. Returns `{"text":text:string}`

A Container can be used in several scenarios such as:

* setting a background color for a [Layout](#layouts).
* making separate controls look like they're related.
* detecting drag and drop events and/or respond to mouse events (e.g. trigger a context menu). See [addMenuItem](#addmenuitem) for more information on creating context menus.

chunks.text:
Draw custom shapes via [cavalry.Path](/docs/tech-info/scripting/cavalry-module/#path-class).
Paths can be described by using the `paint` object (examples below).

chunks.title: Script UIs
chunks.heading: Script UIs > Script UIs > Widgets > Draw > Functions
chunks.text:
* `addPath(pathObject:object, paintInfo:object)` // adds a path to be drawn.
* `clearPaths()` // erase all paths from the draw store.
* `redraw()` // ask for an update, use this if you update the paths once the UI has been created.
* `saveImage(filePath:string, int:width, int:height)` // save the contents of the draw to the filesystem. Use width and height to scale the output to your desired size.
* `useHoverEvents(use:bool)` // if set to true, mouseMoveEvents will fire even when the mouse isn't pressed.

chunks.title: Script UIs
chunks.heading: Script UIs > Script UIs > Widgets > Draw > Callbacks
chunks.text:
* `onMousePress(position:{"x":number, "y":number}, button:string)` // fire when the mouse is pressed
* `onMouseRelease(position:{"x":number, "y":number}, button:string)` // fire when the mouse is released
* `onMouseDoubleClick(position:{"x":number, "y":number}, button:string)` // fire when the mouse is double clicked
* `onMouseMove(position:{"x":number, "y":number})` // only fires when the mouse is pressed unless `useHoverEvents` is true

Possible values for `button` are:

* left
* right
* middle

The `pathObject` is an object made from a `cavalry.Path()` object when calling `.toObject()`, for example:

```
var path = new cavalry.Path();

var paint = { color: "#4fac3c", stroke: true, strokeWidth: 5 };

draw.addPath(path.toObject(), paint);
```

If you wish for a path to have a fill and a stroke, add the path via `addPath()` twice, first with a fill paint object, and then with a stroke object.
The paint object has keys for `color`, `stroke` (to determine if the paint is a stroke or fill, it's fill by default), and `strokeWidth`. e.g:

```
// Create a stroke paint

var examplePaint = { color: "#4ffd7a", stroke: true, strokeWidth: 4 };
```

Timers can be used in UI scripts and can be useful for polling Web APIs. When the Timer is triggered it will call an `onTimeout()` function on the Timer object. Implement this function for a Timer to execute logic when this happens. See [Timer](/docs/tech-info/scripting/api-module/#timer) for more information.

caution

Timers should **not** be used to detect changes to the scene, please use [Application Callbacks](#application-callbacks) for this purpose.

Notes

* Each script has its own JavaScript sandbox so pollution of the global namespace is not possible.
* When testing UI Scripts in the JavaScript Editor only one UI Script window can be loaded at a time.

chunks.title: Getting Started with Scripting
chunks.heading: Getting Started with Scripting > Getting Started with Scripting > Introduction
chunks.text:
**JavaScript** in Cavalry provides access to layers and data within a Scene so that it's possible to write scripts that perform custom workflows. This includes creating Layers, setting Attributes, making [Connections](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) and much more.

The easiest way to get started is by taking a look at the examples in the `Create > Demo Scenes > JavaScript` menu.

Here's an example script that will create a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) and animate it. This script can be run in the [JavaScript Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/javascript-editor/) by copy and pasting it into a tab and pressing the `Run Script` button.

chunks.title: Getting Started with Scripting
chunks.heading: Getting Started with Scripting > Getting Started with Scripting > Introduction

chunks.title: Getting Started with Scripting
chunks.heading: Getting Started with Scripting > Getting Started with Scripting > Introduction

chunks.title: Getting Started with Scripting
chunks.heading: Getting Started with Scripting > Getting Started with Scripting > Installing UI Scripts
chunks.text: To install a [UI Script](/docs/tech-info/scripting/script-uis/), go to `Help > Show Scripts Folder` then drag the Script file into this folder. Nested folders are allowed and will appear as sub-menus. Scripts saved to this folder will be immediately available from the `Window > Scripts` menu without the need to restart Cavalry.

chunks.title: Getting Started with Scripting
chunks.heading: Getting Started with Scripting > Getting Started with Scripting > Cavalry Scenes
chunks.text: Every Cavalry Scene consists of several trees of layers. There is an Asset tree, which contains all of the Asset layers in a Scene, and beyond that, every Composition in Cavalry has its own tree of layers. JavaScript can be used to walk these trees to access (almost) every layer in Cavalry. Each tree can be made up of any number of layers, at any number of levels.

chunks.title: Getting Started with Scripting
chunks.heading: Getting Started with Scripting > Getting Started with Scripting > Accessing Layers and Attributes
chunks.text: To access Layers and Attributes in a Composition, their `LayerId` and/or `AttributeId`s are required.

chunks.title: Getting Started with Scripting
chunks.heading: Getting Started with Scripting > Getting Started with Scripting > Accessing Layers and Attributes > Layer Ids
chunks.text: To get the `layerId`, which can be used to access a **Layer** when scripting, right click on the Layer in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/), [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) or [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) and choose `Copy Layer Id` from the contextual menu.

chunks.title: Getting Started with Scripting
chunks.heading: Getting Started with Scripting > Getting Started with Scripting > Accessing Layers and Attributes > Layer Type
chunks.text: The `layerType` is part of the `layerId` so can be accessed in the same way as above. `layerType` is the part of the `layerId` that comes before the `#`. For example, if the `layerId` is **basicShape#1**, then the `layerType` is **basicShape**.

chunks.title: Getting Started with Scripting
chunks.heading: Getting Started with Scripting > Getting Started with Scripting > Accessing Layers and Attributes > Attribute Ids
chunks.text:
To get the `attrId` which can be used to access an **Attribute** in scripting, right click on an **Attribute** in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) and choose `Copy Scripting Path` from the contextual menu. For example:

1. Create a [Basic Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/).
2. In the Attribute Editor, right click on the `Position` attribute.
3. Choose `Copy Scripting Path` from the contextual menu.

This will copy `position` to the clipboard which can then be used as a argument within a script:

```
api.get("basicShape#1", "position");
```

chunks.title: Getting Started with Scripting
chunks.heading: Getting Started with Scripting > Getting Started with Scripting > Modules
chunks.text: JavaScript can be used in several places and Cavalry includes 4 modules providing access to data from the Scene. A number of convenience methods are also provided to make working with that data easier. Note that not all the JavaScript modules that Cavalry provides are available everywhere.

* The prefix for this module is `api`.

* The prefix for this module is `ctx`.

chunks.title: Getting Started with Scripting
chunks.heading: Getting Started with Scripting > Getting Started with Scripting > Logging
chunks.text:
Use `console.<method>()` to write a message to Cavalry's [JavaScript Console](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/javascript-console/). The methods below can be used to print context specific messages which include different coloured accents for faster recognition.

```
console.log("This is a test."); // Typically used in testing (green).

console.info("Confirming this happened as expected."); // Confirm when something expected has happened (green).

console.warn("Just to let you know..."); // Warn a user when they've done something unexpected (yellow).

console.error("Something went wrong."); // Flag when something has gone wrong (red).

console.debug("I am a developer."); // Print a message to Terminal/Cmd Prompt.
```

chunks.title: Getting Started with Scripting
chunks.heading: Getting Started with Scripting > Getting Started with Scripting > Glossary
chunks.text:
Many Member Functions can accept arguments as inputs and/or will return values of different types:

* `int` - An integer is a number without a decimal point. e.g. `4`.
* `number` - A number with decimal digits. e.g. `4.153`. |
* `string` - A String can contain alphanumeric characters and symbols and should be wrapped in double quotes. e.g.
* `"string"`.
* `bool` - A boolean value can be `true` or `false`.
* `array` - An array is a list of items. e.g. `["one", "two", "three"]` or `[1, 2, 3]`.
* `object` - An object is a collection of properties (a name (or key) and a value). e.g. `{width:10, height:10}`.

chunks.title: Web APIs
chunks.heading: Web APIs > Web APIs > Introduction
chunks.text:
Cavalry provides a way to interact with API endpoints on the web by creating a `WebClient` object and interacting with its methods to `get`, `post` or `put`. These API calls are blocking meaning they must successfully complete before progressing to the next part of a script.

Further to the `WebClient`, Cavalry also provides a simple `WebServer`. You can call `/get` to retrieve whatever response you have set on the server, or, for those of an adventurous persuasion, you can use `/post`. To aid when using `/post` the `WebServer` can poll for new data and will fire a callback function when a data drop has been detected.

chunks.title: Web APIs
chunks.heading: Web APIs > Web APIs > WebServer > getNextPost() → object → object")
chunks.text:
As many `/post` events may happen before you have a chance to react, Cavalry will queue them for you.
This function will get the next (the oldest) post and will pop the post from the queue meaning once you get it, you can no longer access it from the server.
The object will contain a `result` string, and an `headers` array, each header is an object with a `name` and `value`. Please note only non binary data is supported for `/post` events.

chunks.heading: Web APIs > Web APIs > WebServer > getNewestPost() → object → object")
chunks.text: This is just like the above method, only instead of getting the oldest unprocessed `/post`, it will skip to the newest and pop that from the queue.

chunks.heading: Web APIs > Web APIs > WebServer > postCount() → int → int")
chunks.text: Returns the number of unprocessed `/post` events. Process posts using the `getNextPost()` or `getNewestPost()` functions.

chunks.title: Third Party Plugins
chunks.heading: Third Party Plugins > Third Party Plugins > Introduction
chunks.text:
Write custom [Shaders](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/), [Filters](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/) and [JavaScript Layers](/docs/nodes/general/javascript-layers/) which can be loaded as native Layers in Cavalry.

Creating a product

Cavalry recursively searches the 'Third Party' directory so plugins can be packaged in arbitrary directories but it's recommended that each 'product' is published within a single folder containing one [strings](#node-strings)/[definition](#definitions-json-file).json file.

A product could be a single Shader or it might be a bundle of 10. Package and distribute each product accordingly.

[Download the Plugin SDK.↓ Download](/docs/files/Cavalry Plugin SDK.zip)

chunks.title: Third Party Plugins
chunks.heading: Third Party Plugins > Third Party Plugins > Installation
chunks.text:
To install a third party Layer drag the plugin's [folder](#anatomy-of-a-plugin) or a `.zip` of the folder anywhere into the Cavalry window.

If the files within the folder are valid a confirmation dialogue will appear.

This will add the [folder](#anatomy-of-a-plugin) containing the Shader's/Filter's files to:

* **macOS** - `~/Library/Application Support/Cavalry/Third-Party/Plugins`
* **Windows** - `C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Roaming\Cavalry\Third-Party\Plugins`

The Layer will then be available within Cavalry.

info

**AppData** and **~/Library** are hidden folders. To find them:

* Windows - check '**Hidden Items**' in the **View options** for **Explorer**.
* macOS - in **Finder**, **Library** will appear when holding `Option/Alt` when opening the **Go** menu.

chunks.title: Third Party Plugins
chunks.heading: Third Party Plugins > Third Party Plugins > Anatomy of a Plugin
chunks.text:
Third party Layers consist of several files.

```
📁 Layer

┠ definitions.json

┠ layer.sksl

┠ layerIcon.png

┠ layerIcon@2x.png

┠ setup.js

┠ strings.json

┠ welcome.js

┠ versioning.js
```

chunks.title: Third Party Plugins
chunks.heading: Third Party Plugins > Third Party Plugins > Anatomy of a Plugin > Layer SkSL file
chunks.text: This contains the SkSL code defining the Layer. These files can be encrypted using [encryptFile](/docs/tech-info/scripting/api-module/#encryptfile) from Cavalry's API Module. Encrypted Layers should use the extension `.skslc`.

chunks.title: Third Party Plugins
chunks.heading: Third Party Plugins > Third Party Plugins > Anatomy of a Plugin > Definitions JSON file
chunks.text: This contains the information used to create the Attributes for the Layer, along with the UI order, icon name, and other useful information. Definitions for multiple Layers can be present in the same file. See the [example](#example-layers) below.

chunks.title: Third Party Plugins
chunks.heading: Third Party Plugins > Third Party Plugins > Anatomy of a Plugin > Definitions JSON file > Author
chunks.text:
Both the `definitions.json` and `strings.json` files must include an "author" key as an identifier for the creator of the Layer (e.g. company name) which is used internally in the registration of plugins. This identifier must not contain any space or period (full stop) characters and is preferably written in camelCase.

```
"author": "sceneGroup",
```

The third-party Layer `superTypes` are:

chunks.title: Third Party Plugins
chunks.heading: Third Party Plugins > Third Party Plugins > Anatomy of a Plugin > Versioning
chunks.text:
If `versioning.js` is present in a plugin's folder it will be run when opening any Scene that contains one of the plugins Layers. This can be used to add backwards compatibility for users with Scenes containing previous versions of a plugin.

versioning.js has access to two member variables via a plugin module:

chunks.title: Third Party Plugins
chunks.heading: Third Party Plugins > Third Party Plugins > Writing Layers
chunks.text:
When adding Attributes to the Definition, these values will become available as uniforms in the Layer automatically. Note that not all Attribute types are supported.

Adding the line...

```
uniform float2 resolution;
```

...to the top of a Shader will cause Cavalry to set this uniform to the size of the Shape being rendered.

Child Shaders are supported and can be created via the [setup script](#javascript-setup-script) and then sampled in the code much like they can be for [SkSL Shaders](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/sksl-shader/).

Child Shaders should be connected to a Shader’s `childShaders` Attribute (this Attribute is added automatically).

Multi-pass Filters are supported.

chunks.title: Third Party Plugins
chunks.heading: Third Party Plugins > Third Party Plugins > Missing Plugins
chunks.text:
Opening a Scene containing missing plugins will trigger Cavalry to create a copy of the Scene. This copy removes the missing plugins from the Scene as there is currently no way for a user to fix this via the UI.

A warning dialogue will also appear. To resolve the issue a user should install the missing plugins and then reopen the original Scene file.

chunks.title: User Preferences
chunks.heading: User Preferences > User Preferences
chunks.text:
If you experience any problems with preferences you can safely delete the files contained within the **Cavalry** directory.

It's recommended to temporarily **rename** the Cavalry directory or files (e.g. `preferences_temp.json`) to retain a backup. Once a problem has been identified/resolved, those renamed files can then be optionally restored or deleted.

danger

* Ensure Cavalry is closed before deleting/resetting any of these files.
* Deleting these files will result in default files being recreated on startup.
* You will lose any saved preferences previously set by those files.

Application and workspace preference files are saved in:

* **macOS** - `~/Library/Preferences/Cavalry/`
* **Windows** - `C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Local\Cavalry\`

info

**AppData** and **~/Library** are hidden folders. To find them:

* **Windows** - Check '**Hidden Items**' in the **View options** for **Explorer**.
* **macOS** - In **Finder**, **Library** will appear by holding `Option/Alt` when opening the **Go** menu.

chunks.title: Input Shapes - Transforms
chunks.heading: Input Shapes - Transforms > Input Shapes - Transforms > Intro
chunks.text: Several features including the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) ignore the transform information of a parent Shape that's connected as an **Input Shape**. This is by design to prevent confusing offsets that would otherwise occur.

chunks.title: Input Shapes - Transforms
chunks.heading: Input Shapes - Transforms > Input Shapes - Transforms > Details
chunks.text:
In order to avoid the confusion that could be caused by Shapes not appearing at their expected place when part of a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/), the transform information of an **Input Shape** is ignored. 'Transform information' includes the **Position**, **Rotation**, **Scale**, **Skew** and **Pivot** attributes of any Shape.

In the situation where a Shape with a **Position** of `100,100` is connected as the **Input Shape** of a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/), that position will be ignored and reset to `0,0`. The result is that each duplicate is placed at the same position of each distributed point rather than offset by its `100,100` position. This is designed to prevent any confusion that might be introduced by adding offsets accidentally.

chunks.title: Input Shapes - Transforms
chunks.heading: Input Shapes - Transforms > Input Shapes - Transforms > Details
chunks.text:
This only applies to the parent Shape, the transform information of any of the Shape's children will be respected. This idea can be used to override the built in functionality via hierarchies. In the example below, the **Group** is connected as the **Input Shape** of the Duplicator and the **Shape** is a child of the Group. In this scenario the Shape's **Position** of `100,100` will be passed through which results in each duplicate being offset from the Duplicator's points by that amount. The Group remains at 0,0 but the Shape's position within the Group is respected.

* **Group** (transform ignored)
  + **Shape** (transform respected)

The Shapes are offset from the Duplicator's points (in red).

This technique can also be used to pass any transform **animation** through to the Duplicator. By adding an animating Shape to a Group and then adding that Group to a Duplicator, the Group will be positioned on a point and the Shape will then move around within the Group.

The animated Shapes move around the Duplicator's static points (in red).
