chunks.title: Color Management
chunks.heading: Color Management > Color Management
chunks.text:
caution

Color Management is 'opt in' and currently considered a technical preview.

chunks.title: Color Management
chunks.heading: Color Management > Color Management > Intro
chunks.text:
**Color management** ensures designs look consistent across different devices and export formats. Cavalry uses a pipeline approach where colors flow through distinct stages.

Color management can be enabled via [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/) or overridden per-project via [Project Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/project-settings/). It can also be enabled/disabled via the [Viewport Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#color-management).

What "Disabled" Actually Means

When Color Management is disabled, Cavalry still performs color operations — it simply uses **sRGB** for both the **Working Space** and Viewport [Display Color Space](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#viewport-settings). This is equivalent to enabling Color Management, setting the **Working Color Space** to **sRGB** and setting the Viewport's [Display Color Space](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#viewport-settings) to **sRGB** meaning that even with color management disabled, colors remain predictable.

chunks.title: Color Management
chunks.heading: Color Management > Color Management > Working Color Space
chunks.text:
The **Working Color Space** determines the color space used for all internal rendering operations — blending, anti-aliasing, gradients, and compositing.

What Color Management **does not** affect:

* Colors are always entered or color picked in sRGB.
* Colors are always stored with the Scene (.cv) in sRGB.
* The final appearance of flat, solid colors is unaffected.

chunks.title: Color Management
chunks.heading: Color Management > Color Management > Viewport Display Color Space
chunks.text: The Viewport's [Display Color Space](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#viewport-settings) controls how a Composition is displayed on screen. This is a preview transform that converts from the Working Space to a target display profile.

chunks.title: Color Management
chunks.heading: Color Management > Color Management > Viewport Display Color Space > Color Wheel Appearance
chunks.text: The Viewport's [Display Color Space](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#viewport-settings) intentionally affects how the color wheel appears so that the available color range for the target display is shown when picking colors.

chunks.title: Color Management
chunks.heading: Color Management > Color Management > Rendering
chunks.text:
The formats below are automatically embedded with the working color space for rendering. This ensures any exports display correctly in other applications:

* PNG
* JPEG
* WebP
* Quicktime
* WebM
* MP4

chunks.title: Color Management
chunks.heading: Color Management > Color Management > Assets
chunks.text:
All image/video **assets** and **renders** will be color managed with the exception of GIF, SVG and Lottie which all convert to sRGB regardless of the working space.

This is set automatically based on the color profile of the asset but can be overridden by right clicking on an asset in the Assets window and choosing `Color Settings...`. This will open a new window with the following options:

**Interpret As** - Select a color profile to override the detected color profile.

When to use:

* When the footage has no embedded profile.
* When the embedded profile is incorrect.
* When footage has been shot in a different color space and needs to be reinterpreted.

**Linearise** - Replace the transfer function with linear (gamma 1.0) while keeping the color gamut.

**Preserve RGB** - When checked, color management is bypassed and raw RGB values pass through without conversion.

When to use:

* Where brightness values from assets are being sampled by other Layers like the [Image Sampler](/docs/nodes/utilities/image-sampler/).

chunks.title: Color Management
chunks.heading: Color Management > Color Management > FAQ > Why are colors stored as sRGB?
chunks.text: This is a current limitation but support for a wider range of gamuts is planned for the future.

chunks.title: Color Management
chunks.heading: Color Management > Color Management > FAQ > GIF/Lottie export looks different. Why?
chunks.text: These web formats are always converted to sRGB regardless of the Working Color Space.

chunks.title: Color Management
chunks.heading: Color Management > Color Management > FAQ > Gamma 2.4 and Rec.709
chunks.text:
* **Rec.709** is the camera encoding standard.
* **Gamma 2.4 (BT.1886)** is the display standard for broadcast monitors.

Cavalry uses Gamma 2.4 for display when content is tagged as Rec.709. This can be overridden via the Asset's `Color Settings...`.

chunks.title: Presets
chunks.heading: Presets > Presets > Intro
chunks.text: Presets provide a way to save and apply pre-configured settings and set defaults for **Layers**, [Compositions](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/) and [Render Queue Items](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/#render-queue-item).

chunks.title: Presets
chunks.heading: Presets > Presets > Working with Presets
chunks.text:
Presets can be set or accessed via the header row of a Layer's [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) UI, the header of the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/#header) or the header row of a [Render Queue Item](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/#render-queue-item).

Quick Start

How to use a **Preset** to set a default [Composition](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/):

1. Open the [Composition Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/) window and define your Composition's settings (Resolution, FPS, Background Color etc.).
2. Click the **Preset**  button at top of the Scene Window and choose `Save Preset...`.
3. Give the **Preset** a name.
4. Click the **Preset**  button again and choose '**Manage Presets...**'
5. Right click on the **Preset** row and choose '**Set as Default Settings**'.

Each time a new Composition is created, it will inherit its settings from the Preset.

chunks.title: Presets
chunks.heading: Presets > Presets > Working with Presets > Saving a Preset
chunks.text:
To save a Preset:

1. Change a Layer's attribute value/setting.
2. Click the Preset  button in the header row of the Layer's Attribute Editor UI.
3. Choose `Save Preset...`.
4. Enter a 'Preset Name'.
5. Click `Save`.

chunks.title: Presets
chunks.heading: Presets > Presets > Working with Presets > Saving a Preset > Save Options
chunks.text:
* **Reset Layer** - When checked, the Preset is saved so that when it's applied to a Layer, it will also reset any non-default attributes.
* **Include Primitive Type** (Basic Shape only) - When checked, if this Preset is later applied to a [Basic Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/), it will also set the **Primitive Type**. Leave this unchecked to create a preset that applied exclusively to affect [common attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/).
* **Include Transforms** (Shape Layers only) - When checked, transform settings (Position/Rotation/Scale/Pivot) are included in the Preset.
* **Include Path** (Editable Shape Layers only) - When checked, the Path is also included in the Preset.
* **Availability** (Shape Layers only) - Determine whether a saved Preset can be later applied to all Shape Layers or just the specific Shape type being saved:
  + **This Shape Type** - The preset will be exclusively available on the specific Shape type being saved.
  + **All Shapes** - The preset will be available on all Shape Layers. This is useful when making Presets that affect [common attributes](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) like Fill or Stroke.
* **Include File Name and

chunks.title: Presets
chunks.heading: Presets > Presets > Working with Presets > Saving a Preset > Save Options
chunks.text: Path** (Render Queue Items only) - When checked, the **File Name** and **Path** are also included in the Preset. When unchecked, note that if **Reset Layer** if checked the **File Name** and **Path** will be cleared when applying the Preset. Uncheck **Reset Layer** to retain any existing **File Name** and **Path**.

chunks.title: Presets
chunks.heading: Presets > Presets > Working with Presets > Apply a Preset
chunks.text:
To apply a Preset:

1. Load a Layer's [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) UI.
2. Click the **Preset**  button in the header row of the Layer's Attribute Editor UI.
3. Choose the **Preset** from the list.

chunks.title: Presets
chunks.heading: Presets > Presets > Working with Presets > Managing Presets
chunks.text:
To rename, delete or set a Preset as a default:

1. Click the **Preset**  button in the header row of the Layer's Attribute Editor UI.
2. Choose `Manage Presets...`. This will open a **Manage Presets** popover window.

chunks.title: Presets
chunks.heading: Presets > Presets > Working with Presets > Managing Presets > Options > Rename a Preset
chunks.text:
To **rename** a **Preset** either:

* Select a Preset's row and hit `Return`.
* Double click a Preset's row.
* Click the '...' icon on a Preset's row and choose 'Rename'.
* Right click on a Preset's row and choose 'Rename'.

chunks.title: Presets
chunks.heading: Presets > Presets > Working with Presets > Managing Presets > Options > Remove a Preset
chunks.text:
To **remove** a **Preset** either:

* Click the '...' icon on the Preset's row and choose 'Delete'.
* Right click on a Preset's row and choose 'Delete'.

A confirmation dialogue will appear – this can be bypassed by holding `Option/Alt` when deleting the Preset.

chunks.title: Presets
chunks.heading: Presets > Presets > Working with Presets > Managing Presets > Options > Set a default Preset
chunks.text:
Presets can be used to override default settings. For example, when creating a Basic Shape, this can be set to a blue rectangle with a width of 400.

To use a Preset as a Layer's **default** settings either:

* Click the '...' icon on the Preset's row and choose 'Set as Default Settings'.
* Right click on a Preset's row and choose 'Set as Default Settings'.

Default Presets will be marked with a green icon.

To **remove** a Layer's custom **default** settings either:

* Click the '...' icon on the Preset's row already set to default and choose 'Remove as Default Settings'.
* Right click on a Preset's row already set to default and choose 'Remove as Default Settings'.

chunks.title: Presets
chunks.heading: Presets > Presets > Sharing Presets
chunks.text:
Presets are saved to `presets.json` in the `Presets` directory within the [Preferences](/docs/tech-info/user-preferences/) folder.

Adding other valid .json files to the `Presets` directory will result in the Presets contained within those files being available when applying or deleting Presets. If the .json is invalid (contains syntax errors) the Presets will not be loaded.

chunks.title: Presets
chunks.heading: Presets > Presets > Notes
chunks.text:
[Connections](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) are not saved with Presets. This includes **Compositions** added to a [Render Queue Item](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/#render-queue-item).

Attributes with system **default** values **are not saved** with a Preset.

Presets are not supported when using the [Tools](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/) to **drag out** Primitives and/or Text but they are when `Option/Alt` clicking a Tool to create a 'default' Shape.

chunks.title: Animation menu
chunks.heading: Animation menu > Animation menu
chunks.text:
**Set Transform Keyframes** - Set transform keyframes:

* **Position** - Set **position.x** and **position.y** keyframes for all selected layers at the current frame.
* **Rotation** - Set **rotation** keyframes for all selected layers at the current frame.
* **Scale** - Set **scale.x** and **scale.y** keyframes for all selected layers at the current frame.
* **All** - Set keyframes for **all** transforms at the current frame.

---

**Magic Easing** - Add [Magic Easing](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/#magic-easing) to the selected keyframes.

---

**Constraints** - Add constraints to the Composition:

chunks.title: Animation menu
chunks.heading: Animation menu > Animation menu
chunks.text:
* **Transform Constraint** - Add a [Transform Constraint](/docs/nodes/utilities/transform-constraint/).
* **Transform Constraint Tools** >
  + **Pick Up** - Automatically set the keys needed to pick up a shape when using a [Transform Constraint](/docs/nodes/utilities/transform-constraint/). See example on the Transform Constraint page.
  + **Drop** - automatically set the keys needed to drop a shape when using a [Transform Constraint](/docs/nodes/utilities/transform-constraint/). See example on the Transform Constraint page.
* **Point Constraint** - Add a [Component Constraint](/docs/nodes/utilities/component-constraint/) set to **Point Constraint**.
* **Edge Constraint** - Add a [Component Constraint](/docs/nodes/utilities/component-constraint/) set to **Edge Constraint**.
* **Composition Constraint** - add a [Composition Constraint](/docs/nodes/utilities/comp-constraint/).

---

**Add Null** - Add a [Null](/docs/nodes/utilities/null/) to the current Composition.

---

**Create Rubber Hose Limb** - Add a [Rubber Hose Limb](/docs/nodes/behaviours/rubber-hose-limb/) to the current Composition.

chunks.title: Animation menu
chunks.heading: Animation menu > Animation menu
chunks.text:
**Attach Rubber Hose Limb** - Attach a [Rubber Hose Limb](/docs/nodes/behaviours/rubber-hose-limb/) to the selected Shape.

---

**Add Animation Control** - Add an [Animation Control](/docs/nodes/utilities/animation-control/) to the current Composition.

**Add Rig Control (Joystick)** - Add a [Rig Control](/docs/nodes/utilities/rig-control/) to the current Composition.

**Add Look At** - Add a [Look At](/docs/nodes/behaviours/look-at/) constraint to the current Composition.

**Add Time Marker** - Add a [Time Marker](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-markers/) at the playhead.

---

**Animate Along Path** - Run commands relating to animating shapes along Paths:

chunks.title: Animation menu
chunks.heading: Animation menu > Animation menu
chunks.text:
* **Move along Path** - Using the first two selected shapes this will set up the first to move along the second. For example, select a **Shape** and then a **Path** and then run this command. A [Pathfinder](/docs/nodes/behaviours/pathfinder/) will be created and connected to the **Position** and **Rotation** of the **Shape** and the **Path** will be added as its **Input Path**.
* **Deform along Path** - using the first two selected shapes this will deform the first along the second. For example, select a **Shape** and then a **Path** and then run this command. A [Pathfinder](/docs/nodes/behaviours/pathfinder/) will be created and connected as a **Deformer** to the **Shape** and the **Path** will be added as its **Input Path**.

---

**Nudge Backward** - Nudge layers/ keyframes backward in time.

**Nudge Forward** - Nudge layers/ keyframes forward in time.

---

**Go to Next Keyframe** - Move the playhead to the next keyframe. Keyframes can be filtered by selection.

**Go to Previous Keyframe** - Move the playhead to the previous keyframe. Keyframes can be filtered by selection.

---

**Move Layer Start to Current Frame** - Offset the entire Clip so it starts at the playhead.

chunks.title: Animation menu
chunks.heading: Animation menu > Animation menu
chunks.text:
**Move Layer End to Current Frame** - Offset the entire Clip so it ends at the playhead.

---

**Set Layer In Point to Current Frame** - Crop the Clip so it starts at the playhead.

**Set Layer Out Point to Current Frame** - Crop the Clip so it ends at the playhead.

---

**Bake Animation** - Sample an animation curve and redraw it based on the chosen settings under the **Bake Animation** section of the [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/) window. These settings can be used to reduce or increase the number of keyframes created when using the command. This command can also be used to convert procedural animation via Behaviours or Magic Easing to keyframed animation.

**Reverse Animation** - Reverse the animation curves of selected attributes/keyframes. Select attributes or keyframes in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) and hit the button.

**Delete Animation** - Remove all keyframes from selected attributes. Select a layer to remove all animation from all attributes.

chunks.title: Animation menu
chunks.heading: Animation menu > Animation menu
chunks.text:
**Align Keyframes** - Align selected keys to each other. This works in the same way [aligning shapes](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/align-window/) does. Imagine a rectangle bordering each 'group' of selected keys on each attribute and then aligning those rectangles to each other.

* **Align Left** - Align keys to the key nearest to the beginning (left) of your timeline.
* **Align Centre** - Centrally align keys.
* **Align Right** - Align keys to the key nearest to the end (right) of your timeline.

chunks.title: Composition menu
chunks.heading: Composition menu > Composition menu
chunks.text:
**New Composition** - Add a new [Composition](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/) to the Scene.

**New Composition from Preset** - Add a new [Composition](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/) to the Scene and apply a [Preset](/docs/user-interface/general/presets/). This command can also be run by right clicking on the Composition icon in the footer of the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/#footer).

**Composition Settings...** - Adjust Composition related attributes including Resolution, Start/End Frame, FPS and [Motion Blur](/docs/nodes/general/motion-blur/). See [Composition Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/).

---

**Pre-Compose** - Create a new [Composition](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/), add any selected Layers to it and place the new Composition within the active Composition. The new Composition will inherit its Resolution, Frame Range and Frame Rate from the active Composition.

chunks.title: Composition menu
chunks.heading: Composition menu > Composition menu
chunks.text:
**Pre-Compose based on Selection Bounds** - Create a new [Composition](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/), add any selected Layers to it and place the new Composition within the active Composition. The new Composition will inherit its **Resolution** from the bounding box of any selected Shapes and be positioned in the active Composition so that they remain in place.

---

**Close Composition** - Close the current Composition. Note - this requires more than one Composition to be open in the Scene Window.

**Close Other Compositions** - Close all other open Compositions except for the active one.

---

**Set Composition to Playback Range** - Set the Composition Start and End Frames to the Playback Range.

**Set Playback Range to [Selection/Composition]** - This menu item is dependent on selection:

* **Selection** - Set the **Playback Range** to the earliest and latest frame of any selected layers.
* **Composition** - If nothing is selected then set the **Playback Range** to the Composition's Start and End Frame.

**Solo Selection in Viewport**/**Clear Viewport Soloing** - This menu item is dependent on selection:

chunks.title: Composition menu
chunks.heading: Composition menu > Composition menu
chunks.text:
* **Solo Selection in Viewport** - Add any selected Layers to the **Quicklist** and set the mode to **Filter Viewport**. See [Tags](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/tags/).
* **Clear Viewport Soloing** - With nothing selected this command will deselect the **Quicklist** to remove all Viewport filtering. See [Tags](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/tags/).

---

**Clear Quicklist** - Remove all layers from the Quicklist.

---

**Enable Time Remapping** - With a Composition selected in the Scene Window, running this command will add a **Time Remapping** attribute with keyframes on the first and last frame of the Composition. The first keyframe is set to a value of 0% and the last to a value of 100%. These represent a percentage along the Compositions duration. These keyframes can then be edited to increase or decrease the original playback speed of the Composition. For example, repositioning the last keyframe to half way along the Composition's length (e.g. dragging it towards the first keyframe) will double its speed in playback.

Looping Compositions

chunks.title: Composition menu
chunks.heading: Composition menu > Composition menu
chunks.text:
When one Composition is placed within another Composition (also know as a Pre-Comp), **Time Remapping** can be used to loop its animation. To do this:

1. Select the Composition to loop in the Scene Window.
2. Go **Composition > Enable Time Remapping**.
3. Select the **Time Remapping** animation curve (either select the attribute in the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/) or select the **keybar** (the line connecting the keyframes) in the [Time Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/) or [Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/)).
4. Right click > **Loop After > Looping**.
5. Extend the Clip of the Pre-Comp in the [Time Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/) as needed.

---

**Toggle Background Alpha** - Set the current Composition's Background Alpha to 0 or 255.

chunks.title: Create menu
chunks.heading: Create menu > Create menu
chunks.text:
**Quick Add...** - Open the [Add Layers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/add-layers-window/) window.

---

**Create Editable Primitives** - When creating **Primitives** (e.g. an ellipse) via the [tools](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/toolbar/), convert them to geometry.

**Primitives** - Create a primitive (ellipse, rectangle, polygon...)

---

**Background** - Add a [Background Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/background-shape/) to the current Composition.

---

**Shapes** - Select a [Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/) to add to the current Composition.

**Behaviours** - Select a [Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/) to add to the current Composition.

**Effects** - Select an [Effect](/docs/nodes/effects/) to add to the current Composition.

**Utilities** - Select a [Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/) to add to the current Composition.

---

**Layout** - Add the current selection to a [Layout](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layouts-intro/).

---

**Text Animation Presets** - Select a Text Shape Layer and then select a Preset to apply animation to it.

chunks.title: Create menu
chunks.heading: Create menu > Create menu
chunks.text: **Demo Scenes** - Select a Scene to add to the current Composition as an example to inspire or learn from. Not all examples are set up to animate but holding `Cmd/Ctrl` when selecting a menu item will automatically start playback.

chunks.title: Dynamics menu
chunks.heading: Dynamics menu > Dynamics menu
chunks.text:
**Make Dynamic** - Create a [Forge Dynamics Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/forge-dynamics/forge-dynamics-shape/) and connect the selected Shapes to it.

---

**Active Forge Solver** - Choose a Solver (Forge Dynamics Shape) to be affected.

---

**Add Field** - Add a Field to the **Active Solver**.

**Add Collision Event** - Add a Collision Event to the **Active Solver**.

---

**Cache Solver** - Generate a cache file for the **Active Solver**.

chunks.title: Edit menu
chunks.heading: Edit menu > Edit menu
chunks.text:
**Undo** - Go back in the undo queue.

**Redo** - Go forward in the undo queue.

---

**Cut** - Copy the selected Layers to the clipboard and remove them from the composition.

**Copy** - Copy the selected Layers to the clipboard.

**Copy as SVG** - Copy the selected Shapes to the clipboard as SVG code.

**Paste** - Copy the clipboard into the current Composition.

**Delete** - Delete the selected Layers.

---

**Group** - Add the selected Layers to a new [Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/group/).

**Group and Flatten** - Group any selected Layers and flatten any existing hierarchies.

**Un-Group** - Un-group any selected [Groups](/docs/nodes/shapes/group/).

**Add to Group** - Add the selected Layers to an existing [Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/group/).

---

**Connect to Frame Range** - Create and connect relative [Time Markers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-markers/) positioned at the start and end of the Composition to the ends of a Shape's Clip so that they are always visible in the Viewport if the Composition's **Frame Range** changes.

---

chunks.title: Edit menu
chunks.heading: Edit menu > Edit menu
chunks.text:
**Show/ Hide Selected** - Toggle the visibility of any Layers in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).

**Show/Hide Channels** - Toggle the visibility of any animation channels for the selected Layers in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/)

---

**Duplicate** - Duplicate the selected Layers and keep any input connections.

**Duplicate (Options)...** - Open a modal window with the following options:

* **All Inputs** - Duplicate the selected Layers plus any Layers connected as inputs.
* **Keep Connections** - Duplicate the selected Layers and keep any input connections (this is the same as **Duplicate** above).

**Duplicate and Split** - Duplicate a Layer and clip the end of the original Layer and the start of the new Layer to the current frame.

---

**Arrange**

* **Bring to Front** - Move the selected Shape to the top of its hierarchy in the Scene Tree.
* **Bring Forward** - Move the selected Shape up one level in the Scene Tree.
* **Send Backward** - Move the selected Shape down one level in the Scene Tree.
* **Send to Back** - Move the selected Shape to the bottom of its hierarchy in the Scene Tree.

---

chunks.title: Edit menu
chunks.heading: Edit menu > Edit menu
chunks.text:
**Select All** - Select all the Layers in the current composition.

**Invert Selection** - Deselect any selected Shapes and select any deselected Shapes.

**Clear Selection** - Deselect everything. It's also possible to clear the selection by clicking in the header of the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/).

**Select by Label Color** - Select all Layers with the same Label Color.

**Select by Type** - Select all Layers of the same Type.

**Select by Tag** - Select all Layers assigned to a [Tag](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/tags/).

---

**Show in Attribute Editor** - Reveal or load the selected Shape's [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) UI.

**Show in Scene Window** - Reveal or load the selected Shape in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).

---

**Preferences...** - Open the [Preferences Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/) to customise select features. Note that this menu item is under the **Cavalry** menu on macOS.

---

chunks.title: Edit menu
chunks.heading: Edit menu > Edit menu
chunks.text: **Emoji Symbols** - [macOS only] A standard OS menu item which opens a window providing access to emoji symbols. Note that the majority of emoji symbols are bitmap but only vector based emojis will work in Cavalry. Unfortunately there is no way to filter bitmap vs emoji so there is an element of trial and error when using emojis.

chunks.title: File menu
chunks.heading: File menu > File menu
chunks.text:
**New Scene** - Create a new empty Scene.

**Open...** - Open a previously created Scene.

**Open Recent** - Open any of the last five opened Scenes.

**Restore Autosave** - Open a previously autosaved file. Requires the **Autosave** [preference](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/) to be set to **Autosave**.

**Save** - Save the Scene.

**Save As...** - Save the current Scene to a new location or filename.

**Increment and Save** - Create a new Scene file in the same location as the current Scene file, increment the file name's suffix by one and then open the newly created Scene. See the info box below for more details.

File Format

Cavalry's native file format is `.cv`. Files are saved in a compact `JSON` format by default with options that can be adjusted via the [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/) window.

---

**Import Assets...** - Open the Finder/Explorer import dialogue.

**Import Reference...** - Import another `.cv` file as a [Reference](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/referencing/).

**Import Scene...** - Import another `.cv` or `.cvc` file.

chunks.title: File menu
chunks.heading: File menu > File menu
chunks.text:
**Import Google Sheet...** - Open the Import Google Sheet window. See [Google Sheets](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/google-sheets-asset/).

**Import Image Smart Folder...** - Open the Finder/Explorer import dialogue and select a folder containing image assets. See [Image Smart Folder](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/image-smart-folder/)

**Import Audio Smart Folder...** - Open the Finder/Explorer import dialogue and select a folder containing audio assets. See [Audio Smart Folder](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/audio-smart-folder/)

---

**Export Selected...** - Export any selected (and connected) Layers to a `.cvc` file.

**Export Lottie...** - Export the scene to a [Lottie](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/lottie-export/) (`.json`) file.

Evaluate Lottie

When a **Starter** licence is in use, the `File > Export Lottie` menu item will appear as `Export Lottie... (Demo Mode)`. This allows for the **first selected Layer** to be exported to Lottie and so can be used to evaluate the resulting file size and compatibility of specific Layers.

chunks.title: File menu
chunks.heading: File menu > File menu
chunks.text:
**Export as Project...** - Export the Scene or selected Compositions along with any connected Assets to a new [Project](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/project-settings/) directory. This can be used for archiving and/or sharing Projects with clients or colleagues.

* **Mode** - Select which Compositions to export to the new Project:
  + **All Compositions** - Export all the Scene's Compositions.
  + **Selected Compositions** - Export any selected Compositions.
* **Include Fonts** - When checked, any fonts imported to the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) will be copied to the new Project's `/Assets` directory. ⚠️ Ensure fonts are correctly licenced for sharing.
* **Include Palettes** - When checked, and if a Project is set, any `.pal` files found in the `/Palettes` directory (by default `/Assets/Palettes`) will be save to the new Project.

---

**Project Settings** - Open the [Project Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/project-settings/) window.

**Set Project** - Select any of the last five Projects.

**Show Project Folder** - Open the Project's root directory on the file system.

---

chunks.title: File menu
chunks.heading: File menu > File menu
chunks.text:
**Render Manager** - Open the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/).

**Render Current Frame...** - Render the current frame to a `.png` file.

**Render Current Frame to SVG...** - Export the current frame to a `.svg` file.

---

**Reduce Scene** - Remove any unused Compositions and Assets from the Scene.

Increment and Save

If a file has been saved and its file name includes a valid 'counter' then running **Increment and Save** will happen without interruption.

If the current Scene has either not been saved or its file name does not contain a 'counter', running **Increment and Save** will trigger a 'Save As...' dialogue. Entering a file name that includes a valid 'counter' will result in any subsequent use of the command happening without interruption.

If a Scene has been saved but its file name does not include a 'counter', the 'Save As...' dialogue will suggest one (e.g. `file.cv` > `file 2`.cv) but any custom 'counter' can be added at this point.

A 'counter' is a delimiter followed by a number. Valid delimiters are space, period (full-stop), underscore or hyphen. Examples of valid file names are:

chunks.title: File menu
chunks.heading: File menu > File menu

chunks.title: Help menu
chunks.heading: Help menu > Help menu
chunks.text:
**About** - Open the [About](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/about-window/) window containing information about the current Cavalry version, email and licence type. On **macOS** this can be found under the **Cavalry** menu.

**Onboarding** - Launch the Onboarding window with some tips to get started.

**Documentation** - View the documentation.

**Tips and Tricks** - Open the Tips and Tricks window.

**Video Tutorials** - Find tutorials on our [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL3ZRk7VwZVnifyfZXOipWb4Hcfny_Pbhr) channel.

**Report a Bug** - Report a bug via our [GitLab](https://gitlab.com/mfn-public/cavalry/-/issues) page.

---

**System Diagnostics** - Launch a window to review system diagnostics. This can be useful to share in support tickets when troubleshooting any issues.

---

**Send Anonymised Analytics** - Allow Cavalry to send anonymised analytics data to help us understand how it is being used.

**Send Anonymised Crash Reports** - In the event of a crash, Cavalry will send an anonymised report to sentry.io which helps us resolve issues for future versions of Cavalry.

---

chunks.title: Help menu
chunks.heading: Help menu > Help menu
chunks.text:
**Show Preferences Folder** - Open the directory on the file system where [Preferences](/docs/tech-info/user-preferences/) are stored.

**Show Scripts Folder** - Open the directory on the file system where scripts are stored. Any scripts saved in this location will appear under the `Scripts` menu item. See [Script UIs](/docs/tech-info/scripting/script-uis/) for more info.

**Show Plugins Folder** - Open the directory on the file system where plugins are stored. See [Third Party Plugins](/docs/tech-info/third-party-plugins/) for more info.

**Show Logs Folder** - Open the directory on the file system where logs are stored. This can be useful if asked to send logs as part of a support ticket.

---

**View Account...** - Open your Canva account in a browser.

---

**Sign Out...** - Sign out of your user account – this will open the **Sign In** window.

chunks.title: Scripts menu
chunks.heading: Scripts menu > Scripts menu
chunks.text:
The Scripts menu can be used to load scripts with UIs or directly run scripts saved in the **Scripts** directory. This can be found here:

* **macOS** - `~/Library/Application Support/Cavalry/Scripts`
* **Windows** - `C:\Users\<USERNAME>\AppData\Roaming\Cavalry\Scripts`

Scripts with user interfaces (UIs) can be docked and saved as part of a [Workspace](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/general/workspaces/) just like any other dockable window.

See [Scripting - Getting Started](/docs/tech-info/scripting/scripting-getting-started/) for more information on writing Scripts and [Script UIs](/docs/tech-info/scripting/script-uis/) for how to install and create user interfaces for Scripts.

chunks.title: Scripts menu
chunks.heading: Scripts menu > Scripts menu > UI
chunks.text: **Show Scripts Folder** - Open the directory on the file system where scripts are stored. Any scripts saved in this location will appear under the `Scripts` menu item. See [Script UIs](/docs/tech-info/scripting/script-uis/) for more info.

chunks.title: Shape menu
chunks.heading: Shape menu > Shape menu
chunks.text:
**Make Editable** - Convert a **Primitive** (e.g. an ellipse) into geometry.

**Make Editable Copy** - Copy and convert a **Primitive** (e.g. an ellipse) into geometry.

**Bake Selected Shape** - Make a copy of a Shape with any deformation baked into it.

---

**Separate** - Convert all closed paths into separate shapes.

**Separate to Editable** - Convert all closed paths into separate shapes and convert to editable shapes.

**Merge** - Combine multiple shapes into one shape. Note - this is not a boolean.

**Merge to Editable** - Combine multiple shapes into one editable shape. Note - this is not a boolean.

---

**Centre Pivot** - Move the pivot to the centre of a Shape's bounding box.

**Centre Pivot (Centroid)** - Move the pivot to the Shape's centre of mass. This can also be useful for finding the optical centre of shapes.

---

**Freeze Transform** - Set the selected Shape's current transformations to zero.

**Reset Transform** - Reset the transform (position, rotation, scale, skew and pivot) to defaults.

---

chunks.title: Shape menu
chunks.heading: Shape menu > Shape menu
chunks.text:
**Add Background to Selected** - Create a [Bounding Box](/docs/nodes/utilities/bounding-box/) connected to a Rectangle for each selected Shape and add each selected Shape to each Bounding Box's **Input Shapes** attribute.

---

**Swap Fill/Stroke** - Swap the state and Color of a Shape's Fill and Stroke. For example, if a Shape has a red Fill and no Stroke, running this command will result in a Shape with no Fill and a red Stroke. Note that this does not apply to Shaders.

---

**Close Contour** - Close an open Contour.

**Open Contour** - Open a closed Contour.

**Join Contours** - Join two end points of separate Contours on the same path to make one contour.

**Split Path at Selection** - Split a Path based on the selected points (maximum of 2).

* Open Paths:
  + With a single point selected, split the Path into two open Contours at that point.
* Closed paths:
  + With a single point selected, open the Path at that point.
  + With two points selected, split the Path into two closed Contours across those points.

**Reverse Contour(s)** - Reverse the direction of a Contour.

---

**Set First Point** - Set the selected point to Point Index 0.

---

chunks.title: Shape menu
chunks.heading: Shape menu > Shape menu
chunks.text:
**Join Bézier Handle** - If a bézier handle(s) is unlocked/broken, join it with its opposite handle so that moving one with also move the other.

**Break Bézier Handle** - If a bézier handle(s) is locked/joined to its opposite handle, break it so that the two can be moved independently.

---

**Convert to Corner Point** - Convert a bézier point to a corner point.

**Convert to Bézier Point** - Convert a corner point to a bézier point.

---

**Delete Selected Points** - Remove all selected points.

**Delete Selected Points and Split Path** - Remove all selected points and their associated edges.

---

**Boolean (Union)** - Combine the selected Shapes together.

**Boolean (Subtract)** - Remove the selected Shapes from the first selected Shape.

**Boolean (Intersection)** - Remove everything outside of the first selected Shape to leave only the overlapping areas.

**Boolean (Exclude)** - Show only the areas that do not overlap (the opposite of Intersect).

tip

Booleans create a new [Editable Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/editable-shape/) from the result of a selection of Shapes. The first Shape is affected by any subsequent Shapes added to the selection.

chunks.title: Tool Menu
chunks.heading: Tool Menu > Tool Menu > Intro
chunks.text: Tools can be used to interact or create Layers in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

chunks.title: Tool Menu
chunks.heading: Tool Menu > Tool Menu > Tool Settings
chunks.text:
Each tool has its own settings which can be found in the [Tool Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/tool-settings/) Window. When drawing Shapes it's possible to draw a **Primitive** or an [Editable Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/editable-shape/). A Primitive is a Shape that has attributes like Radius or Size whereas an Editable Shape is a Shape that consists of points or vertices that can be moved.

Enable **Create Editable Primitives** to create **Editable Shapes**. Editable Shapes can be edited with the [Edit Shape](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/edit-shape-tool/) tool.

chunks.title: Tool Menu
chunks.heading: Tool Menu > Tool Menu > Shortcuts
chunks.text:
The following hotkeys can be used to perform various tasks when drawing Shapes:

* Hold `Shift` to constrain proportions.
* Hold `Option/Alt` to draw the Shape outwards from the start position of the cursor.
* A single click in the Viewport with a tool selected will create a default Shape centred on the cursor.

You can alternatively `Option/Alt` + click an icon in the [toolbar](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/toolbar/) to create a default Shape.

chunks.title: Arc tool
chunks.heading: Arc tool > Arc tool
chunks.text: Click and drag in the viewport to interactively create an [Arc](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/arc/).

chunks.title: Arrow tool
chunks.heading: Arrow tool > Arrow tool
chunks.text: Click and drag in the viewport to interactively create an [Arrow](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/arrow/).

chunks.title: Camera tool
chunks.heading: Camera tool > Camera tool > Intro
chunks.text: Manipulate [Cameras](/docs/nodes/utilities/camera/) in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

chunks.title: Camera tool
chunks.heading: Camera tool > Camera tool > Shortcuts
chunks.text:
caution

The Camera tool currently only supports the **Look At** Camera.

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shortcut Description|  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `Option/Alt` + click + drag Track in X and Y.|  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `Shift` + click + drag up/down Dolly/Track in Z.|  |  | | --- | --- | | `Cmd/Ctrl` + click + drag Orbit. | | | | | | | |

chunks.title: Capsule tool
chunks.heading: Capsule tool > Capsule tool
chunks.text: Click and drag in the viewport to interactively create a [Capsule](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/capsule/).

chunks.title: Cogwheel tool
chunks.heading: Cogwheel tool > Cogwheel tool
chunks.text: Click and drag in the viewport to interactively create a [Cogwheel](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/cogwheel/).

chunks.title: Edit Shape tool
chunks.heading: Edit Shape tool > Edit Shape tool > Intro
chunks.text:
The **Edit Shape** tool can be used to select and manipulate points on [Editable Shapes](/docs/nodes/shapes/editable-shape/).

To make an Editable Shape either check the **Make Editable Primitives** option when using the [Rectangle](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/rectangle-tool/), [Ellipse](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/ellipse-tool/), [Polygon](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/polygon-tool/) or [Star](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/star-tool/) Tools or use the **Make Editable** command from the [Shape](/docs/user-interface/menus/shape-menu/) menu (`Cmd/Ctrl` + `E`). The [Pen](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pen-tool/), [Pencil](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pencil-tool/) and [Line](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/line-tool/) tools all make Editable Shapes by default.

chunks.title: Edit Shape tool
chunks.heading: Edit Shape tool > Edit Shape tool > Intro > Select
chunks.text:
To select a point(s) click a shape and then either:

* Click a point.
* Click + drag to marquee select several points (pre-selection highlighting to come).
* `Option/Alt` + click + drag to lasso select several points.
* Hold `Cmd/Ctrl` + click to add points to the selection.
* Double click a point to select all the points on a Contour.
* `Shift` + double click a point to select all the points on a Shape (where there are multiple Contours within a Shape).

Clicking anywhere outside a Shape will **deselect** all points.

chunks.title: Edit Shape tool
chunks.heading: Edit Shape tool > Edit Shape tool > Intro > Move
chunks.text:
To move a point simply click + drag one or select a point and then use the arrow keys to nudge it by 1px or 5px when holding `Shift`.

info

Holding `Option/Alt` when nudging points will switch from moving points in the Shape's local space to world space. For example, if nudging a point of an Editable Shape with 90° rotation, hitting the `⬆︎` arrow key will move the point to the **left** (along the direction of its local transform) by default. Holding `Option/Alt` will mean the point will move up instead.

chunks.title: Edit Shape tool
chunks.heading: Edit Shape tool > Edit Shape tool > Intro > Edit
chunks.text:
Points can be either **corner** or **bézier** points.

To convert a point or points from corner to bézier, use the **Shape > Convert to Bézier Point** command. To convert a point or points from bézier to corner, use the **Shape > Convert to Corner Point** command.

A quicker way to do this is to simply `Option/Alt` + click a point (or points) to toggle between bézier and corner points (e.g. a corner will become a bézier and vice versa).

When converting from corner to bézier you can also control the length of the bézier handles by using `Option/Alt` + click + drag. This will convert a corner point to a bézier point and drag the bézier handles out until the mouse is released.

Where **bézier** points exist, bézier **handles** will appear. These handles can exist in two states:

* **Locked** - When a handle is moved, the opposing handle also moves in an opposing direction.
* **Unlocked** - Each handle can be moved independently of the other.

The **Lock/Unlock bézier Handle** commands under the **Shape** menu can be used to convert points to either state.

chunks.title: Edit Shape tool
chunks.heading: Edit Shape tool > Edit Shape tool > Intro > Edit
chunks.text:
Alternatively, a quicker way to do this on a point by point basis is to `Option/Alt` + drag a handle. If a bézier handle is **locked**, `Option/Alt` + dragging one side of the handle will **unlock** it. And conversely, if a bézier handle is **unlocked**, `Option/Alt` + dragging one side of the handle will **lock** it.

info

Within a certain range, any bézier handles will appear automatically. Rather than having to click on a point first and then grabbing a handle it can be selected immediately. To provide a better visual picture of how other handles are determining the shape of the path, incoming handles from the previous/next point will also be shown when handles or points are selected.

Open paths can be closed by simply dragging one end of the path onto the other. As the cursor approaches a point, a small circle will appear in the Viewport to indicate the path will be closed. Use the **Close Distance** option in the [Tool Settings](#tool-settings) to adjust the threshold.

chunks.title: Mesh tool
chunks.heading: Mesh tool > Mesh tool > Intro
chunks.text:
Create a mesh by adding control vertices which can be used to deform raster graphics (images) and/or other [Shaders](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/).

Support

The Mesh tool is only supported for use with the [Mesh Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/mesh-shape/).

chunks.title: Mesh tool
chunks.heading: Mesh tool > Mesh tool > UI > Add a vertex
chunks.text:
With a [Mesh Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/mesh-shape/) selected, hold `Option/Alt` and click on the Shape.

Keep holding `Option/Alt` and clicking to create more vertices with connecting edges.

chunks.title: Mesh tool
chunks.heading: Mesh tool > Mesh tool > UI > Edit a vertex
chunks.text:
Vertices have two positions, **Bind** and **Offset**. See the [Mesh Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/mesh-shape/#ui) (Mesh tab) for more information.

Hold `Option/Alt` and click and drag a vertex to move its **Bind Position**.

Click and drag a vertex to move its **Offset Position**. A 'ghosted' vertex will also appear to indicate its **Bind Position**.

When holding `Option/Alt`, the vertices will return to their **Bind Position**s in the Viewport. This is the equivalent of unchecking th [Mesh Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/mesh-shape/)'s **Mesh** checkbox.

chunks.title: Mesh tool
chunks.heading: Mesh tool > Mesh tool > UI > Create an edge
chunks.text:
The direction of triangles within the mesh can be customised by:

1. Holding `Shift`.
2. Clicking on a vertex.
3. Dragging to another vertex and releasing the mouse.

This is useful for refining the resulting deformation. For example, in the situation where 4 individual vertices have been added to form a rectangle, that rectangle will be split across opposite diagonals to form two triangles. By following the steps above, the split can be set to connect the other two vertices.

chunks.title: Mesh tool
chunks.heading: Mesh tool > Mesh tool > UI > Options
chunks.text:
Right click a vertex in the Viewport and choose from the following options:

* **Control with Null(s)** - Create and connect a Null to the selected vertices.
* **Set Keyframe** - Set **Offset Position** keyframes for the selected vertices.
* **Delete Vertex** - Delete the selected vertices.

chunks.heading: Pivot tool > Pivot tool > Intro
chunks.text:
Move a Shape's pivot point in the Viewport.

A pivot is the position that a Shape will rotate around or scale from. The Pivot tool can be used to manipulate the pivot without changing the visual position of a Shape or vice versa.

chunks.title: Pivot tool
chunks.heading: Pivot tool > Pivot tool > UI
chunks.text:
To position a pivot without visually moving a Shape either;

* Click + Drag the pivot.
* Click one of the 9 grid points to set the pivot to that point's position.

To position a Shape without visually moving its pivot either;

* `Option/Alt` + Click + Drag the pivot.
* `Option/Alt` + Click one of the 9 grid points to move the pivot to that position.

The shortcuts 1-9 can be used to snap to the grid points where 1 is the bottom left and 9 is the top right.

If [Viewport Snapping](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#snapping) is enabled, holding `Cmd/Ctrl` will disable it.

chunks.title: Text tool
chunks.heading: Text tool > Text tool > UI
chunks.text:
* Click in the Viewport to create a Text Shape with a **Text Box** that is automatically set to fit the text.
* Click + drag in the Viewport to create an area to enter text within. Text will wrap within the **Text Box**.

Depending on which method above is used to create a Text Shape will determine whether the **Text Box Size** is set automatically or user defined. This can be changed in the Attribute Editor by checking/unchecking the Auto checkboxes on the **Text Box Size** attribute.

* **Resize** the Text Box using the handles on the corners and edges. This requires **Auto** to be unchecked on the **Text Box Size** attribute.
* **Move** the Text using the **Transform** widget (top left).
* Increase/decrease the **Font Size** using the **Resize Text** widget (bottom right).

chunks.title: Tracking tool
chunks.heading: Tracking tool > Tracking tool > Intro
chunks.text:
Track flat surfaces (planes) in video footage and overlay graphics/animation with a [Corner Pin](/docs/nodes/shapes/corner-pin/) Shape.

This is useful for tasks like screen replacement.

Tracking is fully automated and footage can be tracked forwards or backwards meaning it can be started from any frame.

info

Planes which include tracking markers and where obstructions are minimal and brief will provide the best results. [Presets](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/tool-settings/#tracking) like ‘Edge Snap’ and ‘Robust’ may help track low quality footage when the default ‘Balanced’ mode doesn’t return a good track.

chunks.title: Tracking tool
chunks.heading: Tracking tool > Tracking tool > UI
chunks.text: See [Tool Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/tool-settings/#tracking).

chunks.title: Tracking tool
chunks.heading: Tracking tool > Tracking tool > UI > Workflow
chunks.text:
1. Import some footage to the Assets Window.
2. Drag the video/image sequence asset from the Assets Window into the Viewport.
3. Go `Tool > Tracking` to enable the tool.
4. Select the [Footage Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/footage-shape/) in the Scene Window.
5. Place 4 tracking markers onto each corner of the device/billboard to track. Click and then drag to place – once all markers are placed they can be repositioned.
6. Click '**Track**' in the [Tool Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/tool-settings/#tracking) window.
7. Create a Rectangle and add a [Checkerboard Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/checkerboard-shader/) to it.
8. With the Rectangle selected, click '**Apply**' in the [Tool Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/tool-settings/#tracking) window and pick the relevant tracking data (it will be named based on the Footage Shape).

This will create and connect a [Corner Pin](/docs/nodes/shapes/corner-pin/) Shape to the Rectangle and assign the tracking data to each of the Corner Pin's Nulls.

chunks.title: View menu
chunks.heading: View menu > View menu
chunks.text:
**Show Rulers** - Show/hide [Rulers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/rulers/) in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

**Show Guides** - Show/hide [Guides](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/rulers/#guides) in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

**Ruler Options** - Determine how the Ruler's values are displayed:

* **Origin in Centre** - Values are 0,0 in the centre of the Composition.
* **Origin In Bottom Left** - Values are 0,0 in the bottom left corner of the Composition.
* **Use Pixels** - Display values as pixels.
* **Use Percentage** - Display values as a percentage of the Composition's width/height.

**Show 2D Grid** - Show/hide the 2D Grid in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#grid).

**Show Pixel Grid** - Show/hide the Pixel Grid in in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#grid). The Pixel Grid will only appear at certain zoom levels depending on the size of the current Composition.

**Show Composition Boundary** - Show/hide the Composition Boundary. When enabled, a white border will be drawn around the Composition Boundary.

chunks.title: View menu
chunks.heading: View menu > View menu
chunks.text:
**Show Layer Names on Hover** - Show/hide Layer names for Pre-Selection Highlighting.

**Show Viewport Tool Help** - Show/hide the Viewport help overlay. It's also possible to use the checkbox in the [Viewport Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#viewport-settings) window.

**Show Layer Tools** - Show/hide the Layer Tools. Certain Layers will display purple UI elements which can be used to adjust their settings directly in the Viewport. A supported Layer must be selected for these tools to appear. Note that Layer Tools are not available when a Shape is the parent of another Shape. It's also possible to use the checkbox in the [Viewport Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#viewport-settings) window.

---

**Viewport Quality** - Set which features are rendered by the Viewport. This can be used to increase playback speed where required. Note - this setting does not affect final rendering which should be set in the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/#render-queue-item) via the **Render Quality** setting. Note that this setting will revert to **High** between sessions or when opening new Scenes.

chunks.title: View menu
chunks.heading: View menu > View menu
chunks.text:
* **Highest** (macOS only) - Use multisample anti-aliasing (MSAA).
* **High** - Full quality using standard anti-aliasing.
* **Low** - Removes **Anti-aliasing** and any **Image Filtering** (see [Image Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/image-shader/)).
* **Lowest** - As per **Low** but also removes any **Filters** and **Shaders**.

---

**Draw Outside Composition Boundary** - Enable/ disable the display of Shapes beyond the edges of the Composition.

**Draw Debug Information** - Display useful information in the Viewport for the selected Shapes.

---

**Snapping** - Enable/ disable [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) snapping.

---

**Show Snapshot** - Choose which saved Snapshot to show in the Viewport. Use `Option/Alt` + `SnapShotNumber` as a keyboard shortcut.

**Save Snapshot** - Save a Snapshot of the Viewport's current state to a slot.

**Remove Snapshot** - Remove a Snapshot from a slot. Saving a Snapshot to a slot will also overwrite any existing one.

**Clear All Snapshots** - Remove the Snapshots from all slots.

---

chunks.title: About Window
chunks.heading: About Window > About Window
chunks.text:
The About window can be used to check the version of Cavalry, the email account you are signed in with and the licence type associated with that account. It also includes any open-source software notices.

To access the window go to:

* **macOS** - **Cavalry > About**.
* **Windows** - **Help > About**.

Sign out

To sign in with a different email, go **Help > Sign Out...** to sign out which will then open the Sign In window.

chunks.title: Accounts Window
chunks.heading: Accounts Window > Accounts Window
chunks.text:
Legacy

This page only applies to Cavalry 2.6.1 and earlier.

The Accounts window can be used to discover and [manage](/docs/tech-info/licensing/licence-types/#manage-a-subscription) a Cavalry account and any connected accounts.

chunks.title: Accounts Window
chunks.heading: Accounts Window > Accounts Window > Profile
chunks.text:
Clicking the profile icon will link to the Cavalry [Account](https://account.scenegroup.co/) that's currently signed in.

Hovering the icon will reveal the email account that's currently signed in and its licence class and status.

chunks.title: Accounts Window
chunks.heading: Accounts Window > Accounts Window > Connected Accounts
chunks.text:
It's possible to connect other platforms (e.g. [Canva](https://www.canva.com)) to your Cavalry [Account](https://account.scenegroup.co/). When a connection is active, this icon's state will update from grey to green.

Clicking on the icon will display a menu dependent on the state of the connection:

Disconnected:

* **Link [platform] Account...** - open the Cavalry [Account](https://account.scenegroup.co/) and follow the steps to connect to a platform.

Connected:

* **Go to [platform]...** - navigate to the platform's website.

Sign out

To sign in with a different email, go **Help > Sign Out...** to sign out which will then open the [Sign In](/docs/getting-started/sign-in/) window.

chunks.title: Add Layers window
chunks.heading: Add Layers window > Add Layers window > Intro
chunks.text: The **Add Layers** window is the place to find and add the Layers available in Cavalry.

chunks.title: Add Layers window
chunks.heading: Add Layers window > Add Layers window > Adding Layers
chunks.text:
To add Layers to the Scene you can either:

1. Double click on a Layer.
2. Drag and drop a Layer from the **Add Layers** Window into the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).
3. Use the `⬆︎`/`⬇︎` keys to select a Layer and hit `Return` to add the selected Layer.

The search bar at the top can be used to filter the results or use the tabs to filter results based on the type of Layer.

info

Use `Cmd/Ctrl` + `⬅︎`/`⮕` to navigate the tabs.

Layers can also be added via the `+` button at the top of the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).

info

Use `Cmd/Ctrl` + `.` (period) as a shortcut to invoke the **Add Layers** popover window.

chunks.title: Align Window
chunks.heading: Align Window > Align Window > UI
chunks.text: This window is context aware depending on whether the [Select](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) or [Edit Shape](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/edit-shape-tool/) tool is enabled.

chunks.title: Align Window
chunks.heading: Align Window > Align Window > UI > Select tool
chunks.text:
To align or distribute Shapes to a selection of other Shapes, simply select more than one Shape and choose from the [options](#options) below.

Holding the `Option/Alt` key while clicking the [options](#options) below will align or distribute Shapes to the Composition.

chunks.title: Align Window
chunks.heading: Align Window > Align Window > UI > Edit Shape tool
chunks.text:
To align Points to a selection of other Points simply select more than one Point and choose from the [options](#options) below.

Holding the `Option/Alt` key while clicking the [options](#options) below will align Points to the Composition.

Holding the `Shift` key while clicking the [options](#options) below will also align a Point's **handles**.

info

If only one Shape is selected then the Alignment [options](#options) will default to being based on Composition.

chunks.title: Align Window
chunks.heading: Align Window > Align Window > UI > Options > Alignment
chunks.text:
* **Left Align** - Horizontally align the left edges of all selected Shapes/Points.
* **Centre Align** - Horizontally align the centre of all selected Shapes/Points.
* **Right Align** - Horizontally align the right edges of all selected Shapes/Points.
* **Top Align** - Vertically align the top edges of all selected Shapes/Points.
* **Middle Align** - Vertically align the centre of all selected Shapes/Points.
* **Bottom Align** - Vertically align the bottom edges of all selected Shapes/Points.

chunks.title: Align Window
chunks.heading: Align Window > Align Window > UI > Options > Distribution
chunks.text:
* **Horizontal Distribution** - Distribute all selected Shapes horizontally.
* **Vertical Distribution** - Distribute all selected Shapes vertically.
* **Even Distribution** - Distribute all selected Shapes evenly (horizontally and vertically).

caution

The **distribution** options are only supported for affecting **Shapes** with the **Select** tool.

info

* Shapes are distributed between the first and last selected Shapes.
* When distributing Shapes based on selection, a minimum of three shapes are required. If only two Shapes are selected then **Horizontal** or **Vertical Distribution** will be applied based on the [Composition](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/) (as if `Option/Alt` was held).

chunks.title: Animation Utilities
chunks.heading: Animation Utilities > Animation Utilities > UI
chunks.text:
**Bake Animation** - This command will take any selected animation curves and attempt to simplify them based on the accuracy setting chosen (Low, Medium or High). A higher setting will result in a more accurate shape but will create more keyframes.

**Snap Selected to Current Frame** - Snap all selected keys to the current frame.

**Reverse Animation** - Reverse the animation curves of selected attributes/keyframes. Select attributes or keyframes in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) and hit the button.

**Reset Transform Attributes** - Reset the Position, Rotation, Scale and Pivot attributes on a Shape or Shapes. Select a Shape(s) and hit the button.

**Crop Animation to Selected Keys** - Delete any non selected keys. Select several keys and hit the button. This command will only affect attributes which include selected keys.

**Delete Animation for Element** - Delete all animation for selected Elements.

**Nudge Value** - Increase/ decrease the value of selected keys. Set a +/- value and hit `Go!`

**Nudge Frame** - Increase/ decrease the frame of selected keys. Set a +/- value and hit Go!

chunks.title: Assets Window
chunks.heading: Assets Window
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Assets Window* Assets Window

On this page

chunks.title: Assets Window
chunks.heading: Assets Window > Assets Window > Intro
chunks.text:
The **Assets Window** is the place to add and organise external assets and Compositions.

To import an asset either:

chunks.title: Assets Window
chunks.heading: Assets Window > Assets Window > Intro
chunks.text:
* File > Import Asset...
* Double click in the Assets Window.
* Right click in an empty part of the Window and select from the following options:
  + **Import Assets...** - Import any of the supported file types from the file system.
  + **Import Reference...** - Import another `.cv` file as a [Reference](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/referencing/).
  + **Import Scene...** - Import a Cavalry Scene (`.cv` or `.cvc`). Importing a `.cv` will import the entire Scene including any assets and add them to a Group. Importing a `.cvc` file add the file's contents to the current Composition.
  + **Import Image Smart Folder...** - Import an [Image Smart Folder](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/image-smart-folder/).
  + **Import Audio Smart Folder...** - Import an [Audio Smart Folder](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/audio-smart-folder/).
  + **Import** [Google Sheet](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/google-sheets-asset/)... - Import a [Google Sheet](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/google-sheets-asset/) Asset.
  + **Import Image Smart Folder...** - Open the Finder/Explorer import dialogue an

chunks.title: Assets Window
chunks.heading: Assets Window > Assets Window > Intro
chunks.text:
d select a folder containing image assets. See [Image Smart Folder](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/image-smart-folder/)
  + **Import Audio Smart Folder...** - Open the Finder/Explorer import dialogue and select a folder containing audio assets. See [Audio Smart Folder](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/audio-smart-folder/)
* Drag supported assets from your file system into the window.

chunks.title: Assets Window
chunks.heading: Assets Window > Assets Window > Intro
chunks.text: Dragging supported assets from the file system into the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) will also add those assets to the Assets Window. When importing images or videos this way, a [Footage Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/footage-shape/) will also be created and connected to the asset.

chunks.title: Assets Window
chunks.heading: Assets Window > Assets Window > Intro > Supported file types:
chunks.text:
* **Audio**
  + .aac
  + .aif
  + .aiff
  + .caf
  + .mp3
  + .wav

Audio Export

Audio **export** is a [Professional](/docs/tech-info/licensing/licence-types/#professional) feature.

Video including audio

Where a videos contains audio, the audio track is imported to the Assets Window as a child of the video. This means that the video and/or audio track can be used in isolation if required. When a video with audio is added to a Composition, a hierarchy is created consisting of a [Footage Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/footage-shape/) as the parent to an [Image Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/image-shader/) and a [Sound Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sound/) meaning the audio can be offset from the video if required.

chunks.title: Assets Window
chunks.heading: Assets Window > Assets Window > Intro > Supported file types:
chunks.text:
* **Font**
  + .otc
  + .otf
  + .ttf
* **Image/Image Sequence**
  + .bmp
  + .exr (single channel only)
  + .ico
  + .jpg
  + .png
  + .psd (flattened only)
  + .webp
* **Movie**
  + .apng (Animated pngs will often have a `.png` file extension. Change this to `.apng` for it to be recognised as a movie.)
  + .gif
  + .mov
  + .mp4
  + .webm
* **Scene**
  + .cv - import a `.cv` file as a [Reference](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/referencing/).
* **Spreadsheet**
  + .csv
  + Google Sheets - see [Google Sheets Asset](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/google-sheets-asset/).
  + .xslx
* **SVG**
  + .svg
* **Text**
  + .txt
  + .json

The following codecs are supported for video formats:

* VP8, VP9, AV1.
* H.263, H.264, H.265 (HVEC).
* MPEG-4.
* ProRes (422, 422 HQ, 422 LT, 422 Proxy, 4444, 4444 XQ), Motion JPEG, Uncompressed 422.

Maximum Resolution

The maximum resolution supported for image assets is 15360 × 8640px.

chunks.title: Assets Window
chunks.heading: Assets Window > Assets Window > UI > Header
chunks.text:
**Search Bar** - Use the search bar to filter the items displayed.

**Sort Order** - Determine how the items are sorted:

* **None** - Items can be manually organised within a hierarchy using drag and drop. This order is saved and restored when switching from **None** to **Name**/**Type** and back to **None**.
* **Name** - Items are ordered alphabetically in ascending order (A-Z, 0-9) based on their Name.
* **Type** - Items are grouped based on their Asset Type. Note that this is by 'Type' (Audio, Audio Smart Folder, Composition, Font, Group, Image, Image Sequence, Image Smart Folder, Movie, Spreadsheet, SVG, Text) and not by 'file extension'.

info

When **Sort Order** is set to either **Name** or **Type**, any manually reordering (drag and drop) is prevented but it is still possible to group items by selecting them and using the `Cmd/Ctrl` + `G` hotkey.

chunks.title: Assets Window
chunks.heading: Assets Window > Assets Window > UI > Main Window
chunks.text:
Items appear in a hierarchy and include an icon to signify their 'Asset Type', a Name and custom Tags (dependent on Asset Type). Items can also be assigned a colour from the current [Label Palette](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/#palettes) for organisational purposes.

To **rename** an item:

1. Select an item.
2. Hit `Return`.
3. Type the new name.
4. Hit `Return` again or deselect the item to commit the change.

Previews

Hover a row to load a preview of an asset or Composition. Supported asset types are **image**, **movie** (first frame shown), **CSV/Google Sheets**, **Text/JSON** and **SVG**.

chunks.title: Assets Window
chunks.heading: Assets Window > Assets Window > UI > Footer
chunks.text:
- See [Project Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/project-settings/).

- Add a folder to the list. This can be used to group Assets/Compositions/Groups for organisational purposes. With an item or items selected, use the `Cmd/Ctrl` + `G` hotkey to create a new folder containing the selected items.

- Add a new [Composition](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/) to the Scene. Right click to create a new Composition using a [Preset](/docs/user-interface/general/presets/). Dragging an **image asset** onto this button will create a new parent Composition with its **Resolution** set to the resolution of the image. Dragging a **Composition** or **video asset** onto this button will create a parent Composition that inherits its **Resolution**, **Frame Rate** and **Frame Range** from the Composition/Video.

- With an item or items selected, clicking this button will remove those items from the Scene.

[Color Management→](/docs/user-interface/general/color-management/)

chunks.title: Audio Smart Folder
chunks.heading: Audio Smart Folder
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Assets Window* Audio Smart Folder

On this page

chunks.title: Audio Smart Folder
chunks.heading: Audio Smart Folder > Audio Smart Folder > Intro
chunks.text:
An **Audio Smart Folder** can be used to import a folder containing audio assets which can then be referenced via external data or connections.

See the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/#supported-file-types) for a list of supported audio formats.

Audio Export

Audio **export** is a `Professional` feature.

To import an **Audio Smart Folder**:

1. Right click in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) and choose **Import Audio Smart Folder...**
2. Navigate to a directory on the file system containing audio files and hit **OK**.

chunks.title: Audio Smart Folder
chunks.heading: Audio Smart Folder > Audio Smart Folder > Intro
chunks.text:
Once a folder is imported it can be used in combination with an [Asset from Smart Folder Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/asset-from-smart-folder/). Dragging the **Audio Smart Folder** from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) into the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) or [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) will create and connect an [Asset from Smart Folder Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/asset-from-smart-folder/) and [Footage Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/footage-shape/) - update the **Asset from Smart Folder**'s **Path** to the location of the audio track relative to the Audio Smart Folder to reference it. For example, `path/to/track.wav`.

Example

chunks.title: Audio Smart Folder
chunks.heading: Audio Smart Folder > Audio Smart Folder > Intro
chunks.text:
1. Import an **Audio Smart Folder** containing the files `beep.wav`, `bloop.wav` and `whoosh.wav`.
2. Drag that **Audio Smart Folder** from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) into the Attribute Editor or Viewport. This will create an [Asset from Smart Folder](/docs/nodes/utilities/asset-from-smart-folder/) Utility and [Sound](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sound/) Behaviour.
3. Create a [String Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-array/).
4. Add two more indices using the Add button and enter `beep.wav`, `bloop.wav` and `whoosh.wav` into each.
5. Connect the **String Array** to the [Asset from Smart Folder](/docs/nodes/utilities/asset-from-smart-folder/)'s **Path** attribute.
6. Uncheck **Auto Index** on the **Asset Array** and enter `1` into the **Index**.

During playback, **bloop.wav** will be audible.

Try swapping the **String Array** for a [Spreadsheet](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/) and connecting the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/)'s **Dynamic Index** to its **Index**.

Smart Folder Depth

chunks.title: Audio Smart Folder
chunks.heading: Audio Smart Folder > Audio Smart Folder > Intro
chunks.text:
Smart Folders are limited to a **maximum depth of 5 directories** for performance reasons. In the example below, the track in the **Level5** directory will be accessible whereas the track in the **Level6** directory will not.

```
📁 Root

┠ 📁 Level1

┠ track.wav

┠ 📁 Level2

┠ track.wav

┠ 📁 Level3

┠ track.wav

┠ 📁 Level4

┠ track.wav

┠ 📁 Level5

┠ track.wav

┠ 📁 Level6

┠ track.wav
```

chunks.title: Google Sheets Asset
chunks.heading: Google Sheets Asset
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Assets Window* Google Sheets Asset

On this page

chunks.title: Google Sheets Asset
chunks.heading: Google Sheets Asset > Google Sheets Asset > Intro
chunks.text: A [Google Sheet](https://www.google.com/sheets/about/) Asset can be used as an input to the [Spreadsheet](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/) Utility. Importing data from a Google Sheet means data can be edited in a browser by anyone, anywhere and updated instantly in Cavalry.

chunks.title: Google Sheets Asset
chunks.heading: Google Sheets Asset > Google Sheets Asset > Intro > Google Sheet URL
chunks.text:
To copy the URL for a Google Sheet either:

* Copy it to the clipboard directly from the address bar/omnibox of a browser tab.
* Copy it to the clipboard using the **Copy Link** button in the **Share** options. Note that, if there are multiple sheets/tabs within the Spreadsheet, this method will only copy the URL of the primary sheet. By default, this sheet's URL will end in `gid=0` but if that Sheet has been deleted, the most recently created sheet will be used. If in doubt, copy the URL from the address bar/omnibox of the browser tab instead.

chunks.title: Google Sheets Asset
chunks.heading: Google Sheets Asset > Google Sheets Asset > Intro > Reference a Sheet
chunks.text:
To reference a specific sheet/tab, copy the `url` from the address bar/omnibox of your browser with that sheet/tab open/active.

Permissions

The **Link Sharing** options available via the **Share** button must be set to **Anyone with the link**. The **Role** can be set to any of the available options.

It's not yet possible to access Sheets with restricted permissions.

chunks.title: Google Sheets Asset
chunks.heading: Google Sheets Asset > Google Sheets Asset > Intro > Importing
chunks.text:
To import a Sheet:

1. Either:
   * Right click in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) and choose **Import Google Sheet...**
   * Use the `File > Import Google Sheet...` menu item.
2. Enter the `url` of the sheet into the dialogue window.
3. Hit `OK`.

A **Google Sheet Asset** will appear in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).

chunks.title: Google Sheets Asset
chunks.heading: Google Sheets Asset > Google Sheets Asset > Intro > Connect the Data
chunks.text:
Dragging this Asset from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) into the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) or [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) will create a [Spreadsheet](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/) Utility and connect the Asset to its **File** attribute.

Alternatively, manually create a [Spreadsheet](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/) Utility and then drag the **Google Sheet Asset** from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) into its **File** attribute.

chunks.title: Google Sheets Asset
chunks.heading: Google Sheets Asset > Google Sheets Asset > Intro > Options
chunks.text:
* **Spreadsheet Settings** - Define how Cavalry will interpret the data (the same settings are available for a **CSV Asset**):
  + **Delimiter** - Set the symbol used to separate each cell within the data. Note - this must be set to `,` (comma) for Google Sheets Assets. It's possible for `.csv` data to contain a different delimiter.
  + **Quote** - Set the symbol used to determine strings within the data.
  + **Decimal Separator** - Set the symbol used to separate the integer part from the fractional part of a number. (e.g. `.` in `12.75`)
  + **Factorize** - This must be checked when using the **Factorize** attribute on the [Spreadsheet](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/). Note - factorizing data may result in a performance hit.
* **Rename** - Rename the Google Sheet Asset.
* **Reload** - Reload the Google Sheet data. This is required whenever the Google Sheet is changed.
* **Replace Google Sheet** - Replace the link from the current Google Sheet to a different one.
* **Open Google Sheet in Browser** - Open the linked Google Sheet in a web browser.
* **Delete** - Remove the Google Sheet Asset from the Scene.

Mixed data types

chunks.title: Google Sheets Asset
chunks.heading: Google Sheets Asset > Google Sheets Asset > Intro > Options
chunks.text:
Where columns contain cells with a mix of data types (strings/values/colours etc), the format may need to be specified within the Sheet in order for the contents of the cells to be 'correctly' interpreted. For example, the first cell below is a **number** so the column will be read as such but the second cell is not a valid number and so will not be read by Cavalry.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Column|  |  | | --- | --- | | 28|  | | --- | | 11/345 | | |

In this example, these cells need to be set to 'Plain Text' by using the `Format > Number > Plain Text` menu item in Google Sheets. This means they will be interpreted as strings when read by the [Spreadsheet Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/).
