Note that this will mean that the number `28` in the first cell is no longer a read as a number/value.

chunks.title: Image Sequences
chunks.heading: Image Sequences
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Assets Window* Image Sequences

On this page

chunks.title: Image Sequences
chunks.heading: Image Sequences > Image Sequences > Intro
chunks.text: Import sequentially named image files. An image sequence is a selection of image files where their file names end with sequential numbers.

chunks.title: Image Sequences
chunks.heading: Image Sequences > Image Sequences > Use
chunks.text:
To import an image sequence:

* Double click in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).
* Navigate to an image sequence on the file system.
* Double click one of the images or select one and hit 'Open'.

To add the image sequence to a Composition:

* Drag the imported **Asset** from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) into the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).

This will create and connect a [Footage Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/footage-shape/).

Valid image sequences can take the form of `<Anything><Numbers>.<Extension>`. The non exhaustive list of examples below are all valid:

* `filename_001.png`, `filename_002.png`, `filename_003.png` ...
* `filename.1.png`, `filename.2.png`, `filename.3.png` ...
* `filename-001.png`, `filename-002.png`, `filename-003.png` ...
* `filename01.png`, `filename02.png`, `filename03.png` ...
* `filename (1).png`, `filename (2).png`, `filename (3).png` ...

info

By default Cavalry will detect if an image sequence exists and import it automatically. You can prevent this by selecting the '**Any Still**' filter at the bottom of the file browser.

chunks.title: Image Sequences
chunks.heading: Image Sequences > Image Sequences > Use
chunks.text:
info

Image Sequences can be faster to load so can be used in place of video assets to optimise scenes.

chunks.title: Image Smart Folder
chunks.heading: Image Smart Folder
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Assets Window* Image Smart Folder

On this page

chunks.title: Image Smart Folder
chunks.heading: Image Smart Folder > Image Smart Folder > Intro
chunks.text:
Image Smart Folders can be used to import a folder containing image, video or image sequence assets which can then be referenced via external data or connections.

To import an **Image Smart Folder**:

1. Right click in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) and choose **Import Image Smart Folder...**
2. Navigate to a directory on the file system and hit **OK**.

Once a folder is imported it can be used in combination with an [Asset from Smart Folder Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/asset-from-smart-folder/). Dragging the **Image Smart Folder** from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) into the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) or [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) will create and connect an [Asset from Smart Folder Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/asset-from-smart-folder/) and [Footage Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/footage-shape/) - update the **Asset from Smart Folder**'s **Path** to the location of the image relative to the Image Smart Folder to reference it. For example, `path/to/image.jpg`.

Image Sequences

chunks.title: Image Smart Folder
chunks.heading: Image Smart Folder > Image Smart Folder > Intro
chunks.text:
When importing a folder containing image sequences, each sequence must be in its own separate folder.

Note that any file ending in a number may be read as an image sequence so, if individual files with similar names are required, ensure they are named uniquely – for example, `image_one`, `image_two` rather then `image_1`, `image_2` etc. or place them in their own folders.

To ignore image sequences, click the cog icon on a Image Smart Folder's asset row and uncheck 'Detect Sequences'.

Example

1. Import a **Smart Folder** containing the files `apple.png`, `orange.png` and `banana.png`.
2. Drag that **Smart Folder** from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) into the Attribute Editor or Viewport.
3. Create a [String Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-array/).
4. Add two more indices using the Add button and enter `apple.png`, `orange.png` and `banana.png` into each.
5. Connect stringArray.id→assetfromSmartFolder.path.
6. Uncheck **Auto Index** on the **Asset Array** and enter `1` into the **Index**.

The image should change from an apple to an orange.

chunks.title: Image Smart Folder
chunks.heading: Image Smart Folder > Image Smart Folder > Intro
chunks.text:
Try swapping the **String Array** for a [Spreadsheet](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/) and connecting the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/)'s **Dynamic Index** to its **Index**.

Smart Folder Depth

Smart Folders are limited to a **maximum depth of 5 directories** for performance reasons. In the example below, the image in the **Level5** directory will be accessible whereas the image in the **Level6** directory will not.

```
📁 Root

┠ 📁 Level1

┠ image.jpg

┠ 📁 Level2

┠ image.jpg

┠ 📁 Level3

┠ image.jpg

┠ 📁 Level4

┠ image.jpg

┠ 📁 Level5

┠ image.jpg

┠ 📁 Level6

┠ image.jpg
```

chunks.title: Project Settings
chunks.heading: Project Settings
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Assets Window* Project Settings

On this page

chunks.title: Project Settings
chunks.heading: Project Settings > Project Settings > Intro
chunks.text:
Project Settings create a relationship between Scenes, Assets and Renders (and more) by using file paths **relative** to a Project.

When a Project is set, a **Project Description** is created in a set location on the file system. A **Project Description** is simply a `.json` file specifying default file paths to other directories. The result of this is that when, for example, double clicking in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) to import an Asset, Finder (macOS) or Explorer (Windows) will open in the directory specified by the Project.

Setting a Project is also beneficial when multiple people are working on the same Scenes or sharing the same Assets. It means a pipeline can be set up to keep a team organised – Renders go here, Scenes go here, Assets can be found here etc. With a Project set, all file paths to images, audio, fonts etc become **relative** so all links to any imported assets are maintained when sharing a project with a client/colleague/freelancer outside of the studio.

info

chunks.title: Project Settings
chunks.heading: Project Settings > Project Settings > Intro
chunks.text: When a Project is set, click the right facing arrow icon in the footer or go `File > Show Project Folder` to reveal the directory containing the Project Description in Finder/Explorer.

chunks.title: Project Settings
chunks.heading: Project Settings > Project Settings > UI > Create a new Project
chunks.text:
To create a new Project:

1. Either:
   1. Go **File > Project Settings**.
   2. Click the folder icon in the bottom left of the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).
2. Click the `Create...` button at the bottom right of the **Project Settings** window.
3. Select a directory on the file system as the root folder for the Project.
4. Give the Project a name (by default the name of the folder chosen in step 3 will be used).

Alternatively choose `Create...` from the drop down menu in the bottom left of the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) and then follow steps 3 and 4 above.

chunks.title: Project Settings
chunks.heading: Project Settings > Project Settings > UI > Customise a Project
chunks.text:
The default locations for each directory is pre-populated within the **Project Settings** window. These can be edited to create custom paths if required.

caution

Changing the names of existing directories in the **Project Settings** window will also change the names of directories on your file system. For example, if the path to Assets was `@project/Assets` and is changed to `@project/Images`, the **Assets** directory on the file system will be renamed to **Images**.

**Name** - The name for the project. This is the name that's used within the drop down menu in the bottom left of the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).

caution

Changing the project **Name** will not change the name of the actual directory on the file system.

**Scenes** - The default location to save Scenes to or open Scenes from.

**Renders** - The default location to save renders to.

**Assets** - The default location to import Assets from.

**Autosave** - The default location to store autosave files.

chunks.title: Project Settings
chunks.heading: Project Settings > Project Settings > UI > Customise a Project
chunks.text:
**Palettes** - `.pal` files saved here will appear as Library Palettes in the [Color Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/). See - [Palettes](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/palettes/).

By default, there will now be directories called **Assets** (+ Palettes), **Renders**, **Scenes** and **Autosave** created within the 'Project' directory along with a file called `projectDescription.json`.

When running **File > Open...**, Finder/Explorer will open into the **Scenes** directory within the Project directory. This is also true for **File > Save**. When double clicking in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/), Finder/Explorer will open into the **Assets** directory. The **Path** in the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/) will be pre-populated with '@project/Renders' meaning files will be written into that directory at render time.

chunks.title: Project Settings
chunks.heading: Project Settings > Project Settings > UI > Edit an existing Project
chunks.text: To edit a Project open the **Project Settings** window again and edit the paths. Alternatively, see [custom settings](#custom-settings) below.

chunks.title: Project Settings
chunks.heading: Project Settings > Project Settings > UI > Switch Projects
chunks.text:
Recently used Projects will appear in the drop down menu in the bottom left of the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/). Selecting a Project will set that Project.

Existing Projects can also be set by choosing `Load...` from the drop down menu in the bottom left of the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) and then navigating to a directory that contains a `projectDescription.json` file.

Opening a Scene within an existing Project will also switch to that Project. See [path-to-project](#path-to-project).

chunks.title: Project Settings
chunks.heading: Project Settings > Project Settings > UI > Clear a Project
chunks.text:
To remove any Project Settings either:

* Choose choosing `Clear Settings` from the drop down menu in the bottom left of the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) or;
* Go **File > Project Settings** and then click the x on the right of the **Project Path** row.

With no Project set, any paths to assets, renders etc become **absolute** paths.

chunks.title: Project Settings
chunks.heading: Project Settings > Project Settings > path-to-project
chunks.text:
When a Project is set, a file called `path-to-project` is created alongside any saved Scene files. This is a simple file which points to the `projectDescription.json` file from the location of the `.cv` file.

Here is an example of a `path-to-project` file within a default Project:

```
📁 Project

┠ 📁 Assets

┠ 📁 Autosave

┠ projectDescription.json

┠ 📁 Renders

┠ 📁 Scenes

┠ yourSceneFile.cv

┠ path-to-project
```

The presence of a `path-to-project` file means that when opening the `yourSceneFile.cv` file, Cavalry will automatically switch to its parent Project.

When opened in a Text Editor, a `path-to-project` may read as simply `..` which just means go up one level to where the `projectDescription.json` file is located. This file can be edited as required for any custom pipelines. For example, go up two levels and then into a directory called **MyFolder** would be `../../MyFolder`.

If a Project is set, the `path-to-project` file will automatically contain the correct path relative to the Project when a new Scene is saved.

Cavalry Player

chunks.title: Project Settings
chunks.heading: Project Settings > Project Settings > path-to-project
chunks.text: A `path-to-project` file is required for scenes which include assets (images, svg, audio etc) when using [Cavalry Player](/docs/applications/cavalry-player/). It's also useful when rendering via the [Cavalry CLI](/docs/applications/cavalry-cli/).

chunks.title: Project Settings
chunks.heading: Project Settings > Project Settings > Custom settings

chunks.title: Project Settings
chunks.heading: Project Settings > Project Settings > Color Management
chunks.text:
**Enable Color Management** - When checked, Scenes, including most image/video assets and renders will be color managed. By setting a working color space for the Scene a common color space is used for compositing and other color operations making it easier to control the appearance of colors.

All image/video **assets** and **renders** will be color managed with the exception of GIF, SVG and Lottie which all convert to sRGB regardless of the working space. Any renders are automatically assigned the Scene's working color space.

**Working Color Space** - Select a color space.

**Compositing Bit Depth** - Determine the amount of color information stored per pixel. A higher bit depth results in more colors and smoother gradients:

* **8-bit** - 256 colors per channel.
* **16-bit** - 65,536 colors per channel.

[Color Management→](/docs/user-interface/general/color-management/)

chunks.title: Referencing
chunks.heading: Referencing
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Assets Window* Referencing

On this page

chunks.title: Referencing
chunks.heading: Referencing > Referencing > Intro
chunks.text:
Import other Cavalry scene files (.cv) as 'Assets' and then use them as a 'Pre-Comp'. This enables multiple artists to collaborate on a project by breaking it down into smaller Scenes which can then be combined within a main Scene.

A **Reference** is simply a Cavalry Scene file (.cv) that has been imported to the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) much like an image or video asset. A Reference can then be imported into several other Scene files and so any changes made to the original Reference are then reflected within those parent files.

An example showing 'giraffe.cv' and 'acacia.cv' imported into 'savannah.cv' as References.

chunks.title: Referencing
chunks.heading: Referencing > Referencing > UI
chunks.text: * **Artboard** - When checked, the Reference Composition's [Composition Boundary](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#show-composition-boundary) is ignored meaning that, for example, a Shape within the Reference Composition will remain visible when it animates outside of its Composition Boundary. The **Composition Background** is also ignored.

chunks.title: Referencing
chunks.heading: Referencing > Referencing > UI > Workflow > Import
chunks.text:
Double click in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) and then select a `.cv` file to import another Cavalry Scene as a Reference. This will import the Scene file as an asset and reveal any Compositions contained within it. Note that **Referenceable** must be checked in the [Composition Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/) for a Composition to appear as a child of a Reference.

Import from /Scenes

With a [Project](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/project-settings/) set, importing assets will default to the directory set for **Assets**. As .cv files used as References may have been saved to the directory set for **Scenes**, holding `Shift` when importing assets will default to that directory instead.

chunks.title: Referencing
chunks.heading: Referencing > Referencing > UI > Workflow > Overrides
chunks.text: Any attributes which have been set as a [Pre-Comp Override](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/pre-comp-overrides/) will appear under the **Overrides** tab of a Reference Composition which has been imported into a Composition within another Scene. These can then be accessed via the Pre-Comp's **Overrides** tab and used to add variation to each Pre-Comp.

chunks.title: Referencing
chunks.heading: Referencing > Referencing > UI > Workflow > Open an imported Reference
chunks.text:
Right click a Reference's parent in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) and choose `Open Reference File...` to open the `.cv` file for that Reference.

Example

Create a 'reference' Scene:

1. Create a Shape.
2. Right click on **Fill > Color** and choose **Add Pre-Comp Override**.
3. In the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/), right click the Composition, choose **Rename** and rename it to 'Reference'.
4. File > Save (`reference.cv`)

Create a 'main' Scene:

5. File > New Scene.
6. File > Import Assets...
7. Select the `reference.cv` file saved on step 5 and hit **Open**.
8. Drag the 'Reference' Composition into the Scene Window.
9. Double click the 'Reference' Composition in the Scene Window to load it into the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).
10. Under the **Shape** tab, check **Artboard**.
11. Select the Reference Composition in the Scene Window and hit `Cmd/Ctrl` + `D` to duplicate it.
12. Move it in the Viewport.
13. Double click either Pre-Composition and open the **Overrides** tab.
14. Change the **Fill Color**.
15. File > Save (`main.cv`).

chunks.title: Referencing
chunks.heading: Referencing > Referencing > UI > Workflow > Open an imported Reference
chunks.text:
Edit the 'reference' Scene:

16. Right click the reference Asset's parent and choose `Open Reference File...`.
17. Select the Shape's **Stroke** tab and enable **Stroke**.
18. File > Save.

Reload the 'main' Scene:

19. File > Open Recent > select the `main.cv` file saved on step 14.

Both Pre-Compositions are updated to include the change made to the Shape's Stroke within the Reference.

chunks.title: Referencing
chunks.heading: Referencing > Referencing > UI > Project Settings
chunks.text:
While not essential, it's recommended to use [Project Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/project-settings/) when working with references to ensure file paths are relative to other assets.

Drawables

[Nulls](/docs/nodes/utilities/null/) and [Falloffs](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/) will not appear or render when included within Reference files. Shapes set as [Guide Layers](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) (see Advanced tab) can be used as a replacement where 'helpers' that are visible but do not render are required for positioning/registration purposes.

chunks.title: Attribute Editor
chunks.heading: Attribute Editor
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Attribute Editor* Main Window

On this page

chunks.title: Attribute Editor
chunks.heading: Attribute Editor > Attribute Editor > Intro
chunks.text:
The **Attribute Editor** is one of the central windows enabling the loading of UIs for each Layer in the Scene in order to manipulate attributes, set keyframes and make connections.

Each Layer's Attribute Editor UI contains a unique collection of Attributes which are contained within **Control Rows**.

[Control Row Types→](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-types/)
[Control Row Interaction→](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-interaction/)

Setting Keyframes

Attributes only appear in the Scene Window if they are animated properties meaning a keyframe must be set in the Attribute Editor for that attribute to appear. See [Control Rows - Interaction](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-interaction/) for how to set a keyframe.

Multiple UIs can be loaded at the same time providing a global view and access to multi actions.

The Attribute Editor UI

chunks.title: Attribute Editor
chunks.heading: Attribute Editor > Attribute Editor > Window UI > Search Bar
chunks.text:
Filter the Layer UIs for their attributes. For example:

1. Select 4 Shapes.
2. Click the [Show Selected](#show-selected) button.
3. Enter "position" into the search bar.
4. Scrub `position.x`.

Each Shape's position.x will be set to the same value.

chunks.title: Attribute Editor
chunks.heading: Attribute Editor > Attribute Editor > Window UI > UI Count
chunks.text: An indication to show how many of the maximum number of UIs are currently loaded. When the maximum is reached, the next UI loaded will remove the UI at the bottom of the stack. The maximum can be set via the **Max Attribute Editor UIs** [preference](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/).

chunks.title: Attribute Editor
chunks.heading: Attribute Editor > Attribute Editor > Window UI > Live Mode
chunks.text: When Live Mode is enabled, selecting a Layer in the Scene Window will clear the Attribute Editor and load the selected Layer's UI.

chunks.title: Attribute Editor
chunks.heading: Attribute Editor > Attribute Editor > Window UI > Show Selected
chunks.text: Click this button to clear the Attribute Editor and load the selected Layer's UIs.

chunks.title: Attribute Editor
chunks.heading: Attribute Editor > Attribute Editor > Layer UI > Dependency Graph
chunks.text: When a Layer has input/output connections this button will appear. Clicking it loads a non-editable popover version of the [Dependency Graph](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/dependency-graph/) for preview purposes.

chunks.title: Attribute Editor
chunks.heading: Attribute Editor > Attribute Editor > Layer UI > Pin
chunks.text: Layers can be made persistent by **pinning** them to the Attribute Editor. Set the pin icon  in the title bar to its green state  to prevent the UI from being removed (e.g. in **Live Mode** or when `Option/Alt` + double clicking an layer in the Scene Window).

chunks.title: Attribute Editor
chunks.heading: Attribute Editor > Attribute Editor > Layer UI > Close
chunks.text: To remove a Layer's UI from the Attribute Editor click the `x` icon in the top left of the title bar.

chunks.title: Attribute Editor
chunks.heading: Attribute Editor > Attribute Editor > Working with Layers
chunks.text:
A Layer's UI will appear in the Attribute Editor on creation. There are also several ways to load Layer UIs into the Attribute Editor.

1. Drag a Layer into the Attribute Editor from the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).
2. Double click on an Layer in the Scene Window.
3. Turn on **Live Mode** in the Attribute Editor. With Live Mode on, selecting a Layer in the Scene Window will clear the Attribute Editor and load the selected Layer's UI.

info

Hold `Option/Alt` while double clicking a Layer in the Scene Window to clear out the Attribute Editor, making the new UI the only one in the window.

To learn about how to interact with the attributes see [Control Rows](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-interaction/).

chunks.title: Attribute Editor
chunks.heading: Attribute Editor > Attribute Editor > Advanced
chunks.text:
On right clicking on a Layer's header bar in the Attribute Editor some or all of the options below with be available depending on the type of Layer.

**Copy Layer Id** - Copy the Layer's Id to the clipboard. This can be useful when writing scripts with the [JavaScript APIs](/docs/tech-info/scripting/scripting-getting-started/).

**Reset all Attributes** - Reset all attributes except the [Gradient](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/) and [Graph](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/graph-attribute/) widgets to the default values. This will **not** remove any connections or keyframes.

**Delete all Animation** - Delete all keyframes on the Layer.

**Advanced**

* **Wireframe** - When checked, Shapes will be displayed in the Viewport as a wireframe.

**Context**

chunks.title: Attribute Editor
chunks.heading: Attribute Editor > Attribute Editor > Advanced
chunks.text:
* **Filter Time Offset** - Remove all **Time Offset Contexts** from this calculation.
* **Filter Index** - Remove all **Index Contexts** from this calculation. This differs from **Use Incoming Index** as this will disable the use of the Context (in this case the Index) anywhere in the upstream compute chain for this Layer.
* **Filter Position** - Remove all **Position Contexts** from this calculation.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Attribute Editor* Control Rows* Control Rows - Interaction

On this page

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Intro
chunks.text:
Every Layer consists of several attributes with values that can be keyframed or connected to or from other values. An attribute consists of two elements in the UI. A **Control Row** and a **Control**. The **Control Row** is the entire attribute row and can contain several **Controls** (`[x, y]`, `[r, g, b]` etc.).

When the cursor is placed over a **Control Row**, several UI elements will appear/highlight.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Setting Control values
chunks.text:
To set a **Control**:

1. Hover over the **Control**.
2. Click.
3. Enter a value.

**Controls** can also be 'scrubbed' to set them.

1. Hover over the **Control.**
2. Click **and** hold.
3. Move the cursor left or right.

Note that scrubbing values may be constrained when the cursor reaches the edge of a display. To prevent this, enable 'Infinite Scrubbing' in the [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/) window.

Set Double2/Double3 Controls

For Control Rows with multiple fields (e.g. Position X and Y), hold `Option/Alt` when scrubbing or committing values to affect all fields at the same time.

Set Multiple Layers

To set values for multiple Layers with matching Attributes at the same time:

1. Load a Layer into the Attribute Editor.
2. Select all the other Layers to update in the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/).
3. Update the Attribute(s) in the Attribute Editor.

Tab to next Control

Use the `⇥` (Tab key) to move the focus to the next Control or `Shift` + `⇥` to move the focus to the previous Control. Note that macOS users may need to set a preference for this to work. To do this:

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Setting Control values
chunks.text:
1. Open 'System Settings...'.
2. Navigate to 'Keyboard'.
3. Enable 'Keyboard navigation'.

This setting can be toggled on/off using the shortcut `control` + `F7` or `fn` + `control` + `F7` depending on the **Function Keys** preference.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Setting Control values > Constrain Proportions
chunks.text:
Some **int2** Controls also include a feature to constrain the proportions of the two values.

Toggling constrain proportions on/off.

When the Constrain Proportions button is enabled (green), the original width to height ratio of the two values is maintained when either dimension is changed. For example, if a Rectangle has a **Width** of `100` and a **Height** of `200`, increasing the **Width** to `200` will increase the **Height** proportionally to `400` (maintaining the 1:2 ratio).

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Setting Control values > Inline Expressions
chunks.text: It's possible to write simple mathematical expressions within a Control. For example, entering 12∗312\*312∗3 will result in a value of `36`.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Setting Keyframes
chunks.text:
To set a keyframe:

1. Hover over the **Control**.
2. A small diamond outline icon will appear in the **Control**.
3. Move the cursor above this icon and click.
4. The icon will switch to a green fill. This indicates a keyframe has been set.

Set Keyframes for Double2/Double3 Controls

For Control Rows with multiple Controls hold `Option/Alt` when clicking to create keyframes on all Controls.

The keyframe icon has 3 states:

1. **No keyframe** - Indicates there is no animation on the Control.
2. **Keyframe Set** - Indicates there is animation set on the Control.
3. **Keyframe Set** (at frame) - Indicates there is animation set on the Control at the current frame in the Timeline.

Cavalry has **Auto Key** set to on by default. This means that once a keyframe is set, any changes to the value in the Control will either set new keyframes or, in the instance where the playhead is on the same frame as an existing keyframe, update one.

Keyframes can also be set by using the Control Row's contextual menu.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Setting Keyframes
chunks.text:
1. Hover over the Control Row.
2. Right click to invoke the contextual menu.
3. Select 'Set Keyframe' to create keyframes on all channels. To create a key on a single channel choose the relevant channel to the right hand side of the window.

This window can also be used to **Delete Keyframes** in exactly the same way.

To remove all keyframes on a attribute/ channel use the **Delete Animation** option.

info

If the timeline is on the same frame as a key frame use `Cmd/Ctrl` + click to delete that keyframe.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Contextual menu
chunks.text: Right clicking on a Control Row will bring up a menu with various options depending on the type of row and whether it contains connections or not:

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Contextual menu
chunks.text:
* **Set Keyframe** - Set a keyframe for the Attribute at the current frame. Where an Attribute row contains more than one Control (e.g. int2 or double2), select the relevant Control or click on the row to create keyframes for all Controls.
* **Delete Keyframe** - Delete the keyframe(s) at the current frame. Where an Attribute row contains more than one Control (e.g. int2 or double2), select the relevant Control or click on the row to delete the keyframes for all Controls.
* **Delete Animation** - Delete all keyframes. Where an Attribute row contains more than one Control (e.g. int2 or double2), select the relevant Control or click on the row to delete all the keyframes for all Controls.
* **Disconnect Input** - Remove the input connection. Where an Attribute row contains more than one Control (e.g. int2 or double2), select the relevant Control or click on the row to delete the connections for all Controls.
* **Duplicate and Replace** - Duplicate the input connection's Layer and replace the connection with the new Layer.
* **Reset Attribute to Default** - Where an Attribute's value has been changed, return it to the default value.
* **Rename...** - Customise the name of an Attribute

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Contextual menu
chunks.text:
.
* **Edit Limits...** - Customise the range of values that can be input. See [Edit Limits...](#edit-limits).
* **Delete Selected Attributes** - Delete the selected indices of Array Layers ([Value Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/value-array/), [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/) etc).
* **Reorder** - Reorder the indices of Array Layers ([Value Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/value-array/), [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/) etc).
* **Add Expression** - See [Attribute Expressions](#attribute-expressions).
* **Add to Control Centre** - Add the selected Attribute to the [Control Centre](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/control-centre/).
* **Add Pre-Comp Override** - Add a [Pre-Comp Override](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/pre-comp-overrides/) to the selected Attribute.
* **Control with Null** - Create a [Null](/docs/nodes/utilities/null/) and connect its Position to the selected Attribute.
* **Add Behaviour** - Select a [Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/) to create and connect its Id to the selected Attribute.
* **Add Array** - Select an **Array** to create and connect its Id to the selected Attribute.
* **Add Math/Script** - Select a **Math** or **JavaSc

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Contextual menu
chunks.text:
ript Layer** to create and connect its Id to the selected Attribute.
* **Add Utility** - Select a [Utility](/docs/nodes/utilities/) to create and connect its Id to the selected Attribute.
* **Set Selected Attributes** - Set all selected Attributes with the values from the last selected Attribute. Use `Cmd/Ctrl` to select multiple Attributes.
* **Set Selected Layers** - Set any selected Layers that include this Attribute to its value. For example, select 3 Shapes in the Scene Tree and then right click on Position for one of them.
* **Copy Value** - Copy the selected Attribute's values to the clipboard.
* **Copy Layer Id** - Copy the Layer's Id to the clipboard for use with [scripting](/docs/tech-info/scripting/scripting-getting-started/).
* **Copy Scripting Path** - Copy the Attribute's path to the clipboard for use with [scripting](/docs/tech-info/scripting/scripting-getting-started/). Note that these paths are case sensitive.
* **Copy Generator Type** - Copy the Generator's type to the clipboard for use with [scripting](/docs/tech-info/scripting/scripting-getting-started/).
* **Paste Values** - Paste the values copied to the clipboard to the selected Attribute. Note that data type

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Contextual menu
chunks.text:
s must match.
* **Reveal Generator** - Reveal a Generator (e.g. Primitive Type, Distribution, Noise Type etc) to the Scene Tree so that they can be connected to other Layers. Note that once a Generator has been revealed it cannot be hidden from the Scene Tree again.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Contextual menu > Attribute Expressions
chunks.text:
**Expressions** can be added to Attributes with input connections to perform mathematical operations on the values. Unlike the [inline expressions](#inline-expressions) that controls have, these expressions are remembered and run each time the attribute value changes. Expressions are also saved with the Scene.

info

Attribute Expressions can only be added to attributes with an input connection. Use [inline expressions](#inline-expressions) to perform simple, one off calculations within a control.

Order of operations

When the output value of one attribute is connected to the input of another attribute, that incoming value is converted to the data type of the input attribute **before** an Attribute Expression is calculated.

For example, an output value of `2.34` will be converted to `2` if connected to an **int** (like a Duplicator's Count) or `1` if connected to a **bool** (e.g. checkbox) **before** the expression is calculated.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Contextual menu > Attribute Expressions > Set an Attribute Expression
chunks.text:
To set an Attribute Expression:

1. Create a Rectangle
2. Connect position.x→rotation.z
3. Right click on **Rotation**.
4. Choose **Add Expression...**.
5. Enter ∗2\* 2∗2 into the Z input (the bottom row).
6. Hit **Enter**.
7. Scrub **Position X**.

The value from **Position X** is passed to **Rotation** and **doubled** by the expression. For example, a **Position X** value of `120` will result in a **Rotation** value of 120∗2=240120 \* 2 = 240120∗2=240

Examples of valid expressions are:

* `*2` - Multiply by 2
* `/3` - Divide by 3
* `%100` - Modulus 100
* `^2` - To the power of 2
* `+10` - Plus 10
* `sqrt(9)` - Square root of 9

It's also possible to use the incoming value as part of an attribute expression. Use the string `value` to reference the input value. Examples of valid expressions are:

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Contextual menu > Attribute Expressions > Set an Attribute Expression
chunks.text:
* `-(value)` - Reverse an input value from a negative to positive value (or vice versa).
* `sqrt(value)` - Calculate the square root of the input value. If the input value is 9 the result will be 3.
* `clamp(-45, value, 45)` - Prevent the output value from going below -45 or above 45 even if the input value exceeds it.
* `round(value/10)*10` - Round the input value to the nearest 10. `round(value)` defaults to the nearest integer.
* `if(value < 0, 0, value)` - If the input value is less than 0, return 0 else return the input value.

See [ExprTk](http://www.partow.net/programming/exprtk/) for more available options.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Contextual menu > Attribute Expressions > Edit an Attribute Expression
chunks.text:
Once an expression exists, it can be edited or removed with the `π` button on the Attribute's Control Row.

* To **disable** an expression - click the `π` button to open the Expression Window and then uncheck the relevant attribute.
* To **clear/remove** an expression - click the `π` button to open the Expression Window and then delete the expression or click the `x`.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Contextual menu > Edit Limits...
chunks.text:
Attributes can be set to accept a custom range of values. This is primarily useful for attributes that are included as part of [Components](/docs/nodes/shapes/component-shape/) or [Pre-Comp Overrides](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/pre-comp-overrides/).

Right click an Attribute and choose `Edit Limits...` to define the following properties:

* **Hard Minimum** - a value which a field cannot be less than.
* **Hard Maximum** - a value which a field cannot be greater than.
* **Soft Minimum** - a minimum value which a field will stop at when scrubbed but that can be manually overridden by entering a value.
* **Soft Maximum** - a maximum value which a field will stop at when scrubbed but that can be manually overridden by entering a value.
* **Step** - the increment at which a value increases/decreases when scrubbing a value or using the `⬆︎` `⬇︎` keys

Note that Attributes with a Hard Minimum or Maximum defined by Cavalry cannot be overridden. For example, a Shape's Opacity is set by Cavalry to `0..100` so this cannot be set to values like `-20..120` which fall outside that default range.

Soft Limits

chunks.title: Control Rows - Interaction
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Interaction > Control Rows - Interaction > Contextual menu > Edit Limits...
chunks.text:
Soft limits should be treated as guides. If a value is manually set outside a Soft limit then that limit is removed until the value is set back to one within its limits.

For numeric attributes with a single value, setting a Hard Minimum and Maximum will result in the UI updating to a **Slider** the next time the UI is loaded into the Attribute Editor.

All limits are saved with the file and are 'per attribute' meaning editing the radius on an ellipse will not affect any other ellipse shapes, just the one you're editing

Editing a [Double2](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-types/#types) attribute (e.g Pivot) will edit both the X and Y attributes at once. It's not currently possible to set e.g. `pivot.x` and `pivot.y` individually.

Existing values

If an existing value is outside the limits defined, the value will be updated to one within those limits once they are committed. Be aware this may change your Composition.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Types
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Types
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Attribute Editor* Control Rows* Control Rows - Types

On this page

chunks.title: Control Rows - Types
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Types > Control Rows - Types > Intro
chunks.text: There are various types of Control Row that can appear in a Layer's Attribute Editor UI.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Types
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Types > Control Rows - Types > Types > Values
chunks.text:
* **int** - An integer is a number without a decimal point like `4`. Example - **Count** on the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).
* **double** - A number with decimal digits like `4.153`. Example - **Rotation** on a Shape.
* **int2** - A set of two integers like `1920, 1080`. Example - **Resolution** in Composition Settings.
* **double2** - A set of two doubles like `103.453, 487.543`. Example - **Shape Position** on the [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).
* **double3** - A set of three doubles like `103.453, 487.54, 2.5`. Example - **Position** for a 2.5D Shape.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Types
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Types > Control Rows - Types > Types > Color
chunks.text:
An attribute containing `R`, `G`, `B`, `A` and hex values. Note - the hex value cannot be animated.

Clicking on the color swatch will pop up a color picker which includes an eyedropper.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Types
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Types > Control Rows - Types > Types > Color > Color Names
chunks.text:
It's possible to enter the names of the **current** [Library Palette](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/#palettes) and **any** [Project Palettes](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/#palettes) into a hex field and for those labels to resolve as the corresponding hex value.

For example, if the default 'Cavalry' palette is loaded, typing `gre` will invoke an auto-complete list including the 'Green' swatch. On selecting 'Green', either via click or the arrow keys and hitting `Return`, the corresponding hex value of `#4ffd7a` will be entered into the field.

Hit `Escape` at any time to cancel the input.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Types
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Types > Control Rows - Types > Types > Slider
chunks.text: Sliders are used if an attribute has hard minimum and maximum values set. e.g. **Opacity** can have a value between 0 and 100 and cannot be set outside of that range.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Types
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Types > Control Rows - Types > Types > String
chunks.text:
A string can contain alphanumeric characters and symbols.

A string row also includes a `+` icon which is a shortcut to connect a [String Generator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/).

chunks.title: Control Rows - Types
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Types > Control Rows - Types > Types > Input List
chunks.text:
Input Lists are rows that can contain multiple connections. Input connections can be made by dragging a Layer on to the row, making a [connection](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) or by clicking the `+` icon to the right of the Control to add and connect a new Layer. This will bring up a list of compatible Layers that can be connected.

A number is shown to indicate the number of connections and clicking the connection icon will pop up a list of connections. This list can be reordered via dragging an item in the list and connections can be removed using the `x` icon to the right hand side.

To remove all the inputs, right click anywhere on the Input List's row and select **Disconnect All Inputs**.

Remove multiple Inputs

Hold `Cmd/Ctrl` when removing connections to prevent the popover window from closing. This is useful when disconnecting several Layers.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Types
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Types > Control Rows - Types > Types > Generator
chunks.text:
A Generator is a special type of drop down. These differ from a drop down in that they actually represent a list of Layers which become connected to the parent Layer when chosen.

It is possible to reuse the options within a Generator on other nodes. To do this, right click on the Generator and choose the `Reveal Generator` option. This will promote the Generator to the Scene Window and can then be connected to other Generators. For example, two **Duplicators** could share the same **Distribution**. Note - once a Generator has been 'revealed' it cannot be hidden from the Scene Window.

chunks.title: Control Rows - Types
chunks.heading: Control Rows - Types > Control Rows - Types > Types > Checkbox
chunks.text: A checkbox (aka a **bool**) is an attribute with two states. It outputs `1` when checked and `0` when unchecked.

chunks.title: Gradient
chunks.heading: Gradient
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Attribute Editor* Widgets* Gradient

On this page

chunks.title: Gradient
chunks.heading: Gradient > Gradient > Intro
chunks.text: The Gradient widget appears on several Layers including the [Gradient Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/gradient-shader/), [Gradient Map Filter](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/gradient-map-filter/), [Index to Color](/docs/nodes/utilities/index-to-color/) and [Color Blend](/docs/nodes/behaviours/color-blend/).

chunks.title: Gradient
chunks.heading: Gradient > Gradient > UI > Gradient Mode
chunks.text:
Most Layers that include a gradient widget will also include a **Gradient Mode** attribute:

**Gradient Mode** - Select an interpolation for the gradient:

chunks.title: Gradient
chunks.heading: Gradient > Gradient > UI > Gradient Mode
chunks.text:
* **RGB Interpolation** - Interpolate between colors along a straight line across the color wheel.
* **Oklab Interpolation** - Interpolate between colors along a straight line across the color wheel using [Oklab](https://bottosson.github.io/posts/oklab/) interpolation.
* **HSV Interpolation (Short Path)** - Interpolate between colors around the color wheel via the shortest path using hue (H), saturation (S) and value (V).
* **HSV Interpolation (Long Path)** - Interpolate between colors around the color wheel via the longest path using hue (H), saturation (S) and value (V).
* **LCH Interpolation (Short Path)** - Interpolate between colors around the color wheel via the shortest path. LCH interpolation blends colours by interpolating lightness (L), chroma (C), and hue (H) in a perceptually uniform colour space.
* **LCH Interpolation (Long Path)** - Interpolate between colors around the color wheel via the longest path. LCH interpolation blends colours by interpolating lightness (L), chroma (C), and hue (H) in a perceptually uniform colour space.

An illustration of how the mode affects the output of a gradient with two Color Stops.

chunks.title: Gradient
chunks.heading: Gradient > Gradient > UI > Gradient
chunks.text:
To create a new Color Stop, position the cursor along the gradient and click.

To adjust a Color Stop's properties, select a Color Stop and then adjust the attributes below the gradient:

* **Position** - Set the position of the selected Color Stop along the gradient (0-1).
* **Jitter** - Add noise to the interpolation curve based on its intensity. Jitter will be added between the selected Stop and the next one to its right. Note - this attribute is only available on the [Gradient Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/gradient-shader/) and [Gradient Map Filter](/docs/nodes/effects/filters/gradient-map-filter/)
* **Color** - Set the color of the selected Color Stop. It's also possible to `double click` a Color Stop to pop up a color window and adjust its color there.

`Option/Alt` + click + drag a Color Stop to duplicate it.

Hold `Cmd/Ctrl` to select multiple Color Stops.

Swatches from the Color Window can be dragged and dropped onto any part of the gradient's row. The **Color** for any selected Color Stops will be updated.

info

A Color Stop's **Position** and **Color** attributes can be animated or connected to.

chunks.title: Gradient
chunks.heading: Gradient > Gradient > UI > Gradient > Options
chunks.text:
* **Copy Gradient** - Copy the Color Stops to the clipboard.
* **Paste Gradient** - Paste any Color Stops copied to the clipboard to a gradient attribute.
* **Adjust Colors (HSV)** - Perform an HSV color adjustment across all Color Stops in the gradient.
* **Distribute Stops** - Distribute all Color Stops evenly across the width of the gradient.
* **Subdivide Gradient** - Add new Color Stops half way between any existing Color Stops.
* **Reverse Stop Positions** - Flip the gradient's Color Stops. Note that this does not affect the **Jitter** or **Interpolation** settings.
* **Shuffle Stop Positions** - Randomly swap the positions of the Color Stops.
* **Shift Stops Left** - Shuffle each Color Stop to the position of the next Color Stop to its left. The furthest left Color Stop will move round to the Color Stop on the furthest right side of the gradient.
* **Shift Stops Right** - Shuffle each Color Stop to the position of the next Color Stop to its right. The furthest right Color Stop will move round to the Color Stop on the furthest left side of the gradient.
* **Select All** - Select all Color Stops.
* **Invert Selection** - Deselect the selected Color Stops and select the unselec

chunks.title: Gradient
chunks.heading: Gradient > Gradient > UI > Gradient > Options
chunks.text:
ted Color Stops.
* **Select Same Color** - Select all Color Stops that have the same color as the selected Color Stop.
* **Set Interpolation** - Set the interpolation for how the selected Color Stop's color will blend to the next Color Stop's color:
  + **Linear** - Apply a linear (straight) curve.
  + **Stepped** - Apply a stepped curve.
  + **Smooth** - Apply a smooth curve.
  + **Crush** - Apply curve which is shallow at either end and steep in the middle.
  + **Smooth Blend** - Apply a smooth curve.
  + **Contrast** - Apply a curve which is steep at either end and shallow in the middle.
* **Save Gradient to Palette** - Create a new Library Palette in the [Color Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/) where each Color Stop is used to create a swatch.

chunks.title: Graph Attribute
chunks.heading: Graph Attribute
chunks.text: * * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Attribute Editor* Widgets* Graph Attribute

chunks.title: Graph Attribute
chunks.heading: Graph Attribute > Graph Attribute
chunks.text:
The Graph Attribute is found on several Layers including [Stagger](/docs/nodes/behaviours/stagger/), [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/) and [Number Range](/docs/nodes/behaviours/number-range/). It can be used to shape the effect of the Layer.

For example, a curve similar to the one below on a [Falloff](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/) would result in the 'Strength' of the Behaviour it is connected to transitioning smoothly from 'on' to 'off' (and back again) as it passed over a Shape.

Adjusting the graph is very similar to working with animation curves in the [Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/).

* Click + drag` on a point to move it.
* `Option/Alt` + click on a point to toggle the interpolation from linear to bezier.
* Click + drag to move a handle.
* Double click anywhere in the window to add a new point.
* Select > `Delete` to remove a point.

There are several **preset** curves along the right hand side. Click one to set the curve to the shapes represented by the icons.

The Graph can be **flipped** horizontally and/or vertically using the buttons at the bottom right of the window.

chunks.title: Graph Attribute
chunks.heading: Graph Attribute > Graph Attribute
chunks.text:
The Graph can be copied and/or pasted by using the buttons at the bottom right of the window. This is also possible by right clicking the Graph attribute.

Values for the points on the Graph can be input manually by selecting a point and using the `P` (position) and `V` (value) input boxes along the bottom.

Turn on **Grid Snapping** using the button to the right of the inputs.

To animate or make connections to points and handles select a point or handle and then either keyframe or drag a connection to/from the `P` (position) or `V` (value) inputs.

info

In order to make connections you'll need to make the window persistent. To do this simply click the little 'expand' icon on the top left or grab the title bar and 'tear' the panel off.

chunks.title: Audio Monitor
chunks.heading: Audio Monitor > Audio Monitor > Intro
chunks.text:
The Audio Monitor can be used to sample decibel levels for audio playback.

The meter is helpful making sure any audio in the Composition has clear and balanced audio levels. Audio that is too loud can lead to audible distortion and clipping.

chunks.title: Audio Monitor
chunks.heading: Audio Monitor > Audio Monitor > UI
chunks.text:
The meter has a decibel scale from -50 to 0 dB and will display audio levels during playback of the audible [Sound](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sound/) Behaviours.

Audio levels start green and become yellow or red if the audio approaches or begins to clip above 0 dB.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > Intro
chunks.text:
Create and manage **Library**, **Project**, **Label** and **Scene** Palettes.

Color window

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI
chunks.text:
To set a color either:

* Move the white rings in the color wheel UI.
* Use the **Eye Dropper** icon to pick any color within the app.

The resulting color chip can then be dragged and dropped onto Attributes in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/), Shapes in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) or into the palette windows below.

Colors can also be set by manually entering Hex, RGB or HSV values:

* **Hex** - Enter a hexadecimal color code (e.g. `#4ffd7a`).
* **RGB** - Enter an RGB (Reg, Green, Blue) color (e.g. `79,253,122`).
* **HSV** - Enter an HSV (Hue, Saturation and Value) color (e.g. `134, 68, 99`).

Auto-complete Hex

Where hex codes contain repeated sequences of characters or numbers, they will be auto-completed. For example, entering `AB` and then hitting `Return` will result in `#ABABAB`.

* Swatches* Generator

Use the sub-tabs along the top to load the different types of [palettes](#palettes).

Use the icons on the right hand side to switch the view between [Grid](#grid-view) and [List](#list-view) layouts.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > Add a color swatch
chunks.text:
To add a swatch either:

* Drag the color swatch from the Color Widget above into a palette.
* Select a Shape or Shapes and then choose the **Add Colors from Selection** option.

Hold `Option/Alt` while dragging a swatch from the Color Widget into a Palette to allow adding duplicate colors.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > Duplicate a swatch
chunks.text: To duplicate an existing swatch hold `Option/Alt` and drag a swatch in the [Grid view](#grid-view) to duplicate one.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > Apply a swatch
chunks.text:
To set an attribute's Color either:

* Drag a swatch's color chip directly onto a **Shape** in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) to set its **Fill Color**.
* In [Grid view](#grid-view) and with a Shape or Shapes selected:
  + Click a swatch to set a selected Shape's Fill color (requires **Fill** to be checked).
  + `Option/Alt` + click a swatch to enable a selected Shape's Fill and set its color.
  + `Shift` + click a swatch to enable a selected Shape's Stroke and set its color.
* Use the buttons on a swatch's row in the [List view](#list-view). Note that if Fill or Stroke is not already enabled that these buttons will enable those attributes.
* Drag a swatch's color chip onto a **Color** attribute in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).
* With a Layer's **Color** attribute selected in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/), click a swatch's color chip.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > Rename a swatch
chunks.text:
To rename a swatch, when in the [List view](#list-view) either:

* Double click a row.
* Select a row and hit `Return`.
* Right click a row and choose **Rename**.
* Click the row's ellipsis  icon and choose **Rename**.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > Reorder a swatch
chunks.text: When in [List view](#list-view), drag and drop a swatch's row to reorder the swatch.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > Delete a palette
chunks.text: To delete a palette use the **Delete Palette** [options](#options-menu) menu item or choose **Reveal in Finder/Explorer** from the [options](#options-menu) and delete the [.pal](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/palettes/) file from the file system.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > Delete a palette > Options menu
chunks.text:
* **New Palette...** - Create a new empty palette.
* **Import...** - Import an existing palette. Cavalry supports importing [.pal](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/palettes/), `.ase` (Adobe® Swatch Exchange) and `.theme` filetypes.
* **Save As...** - Save a version of the palette.
* **Rename Palette...** - Rename the palette.
* **Reveal in Finder/Explorer...** - Reveal the palette's location on the file system.
* **Set Gradient from Palette** - Set the color stops for a [Gradient attribute](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/widgets/gradient/) selected in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/). The [Multi-Point Gradient Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/multi-point-gradient-shader/) can also be set in this way by selecting the Layer itself – the stops created will be randomly positioned based on the Composition's resolution.
* **Create Array from Palette** - create a [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/) pre-populated with the colors in the palette.
* **Clear Palette** - Remove all swatches from the palette.
* **Delete Palette** - Remove the palette. Note this deletes the palette from th

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > Grid View
chunks.text:
The grid view displays the swatches as individual color chips in a grid layout.

Right click a swatch to reveal the following options:

* **Clear Palette** - Remove all Swatches from the palette.
* **Copy Hex Color Value** - Copy the Swatch's hex color value to the clipboard.
* **Paste Color** - Paste a hex color or a color copied from a Color Attribute.
* **Delete** - Remove the Swatch from the palette.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > List View
chunks.text: The list view exposes the swatch names and allows for reordering and renaming of swatches within the palette.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > List View > Options
chunks.text:
Use the ellipsis  icon to reveal the following additional options:

* **Rename** - Rename a swatch.
* **Set W3C Name** - Rename the swatch to use the W3C name.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > Palettes
chunks.text:
* Library* Project* Scene* Labels

Library palettes are collections of swatches that can be used to assign colors to Shapes and other Layers.

Load any saved palettes by selecting one from the dropdown menu at the top.

Project palettes are identical to Library palettes except they are saved relative to a [Project](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/project-settings/). By default, this directory is `@project/Assets/Palettes/`. Any palettes saved within the current Project's directory will appear here.

Color swatches in the Scene Palette can be used to create shared connections between Layers. They are also saved with the scene.

A Scene Palette swatch can be used to connect several Layers that share the same color. Any change to the swatch will also update any connected Layers meaning the color need only be changed from one location.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > Palettes > Connect a Scene swatch
chunks.text:
**Grid View**

* When in [Grid view](#grid-view), rollover a swatch and use the connection anchor which appears to create a [connection](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) to any Layer that has a **Color** attribute.
* When in [List view](#list-view), use the connection anchor to the left of the swatch's color chip to create a [connection](/docs/getting-started/key-concepts/connections/) to any Layer that has a **Color** attribute.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > Palettes > Connect a Scene swatch > Options
chunks.text:
Use the ellipsis  icon to reveal the following additional options:

Create a Scene Palette swatch by dragging a **Library Palette** swatch into the Scene Palette window.

* **Add Colors from Selection** - Create swatches from the Fill Color of the selected Shapes.
* **Add Colors from Selection and Connect** - Create swatches from the Fill Color of the selected Shapes and connect the Scene swatch to each of the selected Shapes.
* **Load from Library** - Add the swatches from a Library Palette to the Scene Palette.

Label palettes can be used to colourise **Layers**, **Keyframes** and **Time Markers** for organisational purposes. The current palette can be 'hot-swapped' meaning a new color theme can be applied to a Scene at any time.

If a different palette is in use when opening a saved Scene, the palette saved with the Scene will be loaded. Where a Scene is opened with a palette that doesn't exist locally, the **Default** palette is used.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > Palettes > Set a Layer's label color
chunks.text:
A Layer's label color can be set by either:

* In [List view](#list-view), click the label icon on the row
  Clicking a swatch in the Label Palette will set the label colours for any selected Layers and/or Keyframes.

Right click a swatch's color chip/row or, in the [List view](#list-view), use the ellipsis  icon on the swatch's row to reveal the following additional options:

* **Select Layers with Color** - Select all Layers that use the selected label color in the active Composition.

Use the ellipsis  icon next to the palette drop down to reveal the following additional options:

* **Reset Layers to Default Colors** - Reset all Layer labels to match the default colors. Defaults can be customised by editing the `types` key within a [.pal](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/palettes/#format) file.

The **Default** palette can be restored by right clicking in an empty part of the **Default** palette and choosing 'Restore Default Palette'.

The indicators at the bottom of the UI report how many Layers or Keyframes are currently selected and will be updated when clicking a swatch.

Generate a palette based on the current key color.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > Palettes > Set a Layer's label color
chunks.text:
**Color** - Select the Color Model to generate the palette in:

* **RGB** - Generate colors using the RGB Color Model.
* **LAB** - Generate colors using the LCh Color Model (also known as HCL).

**Type** - Select the type of palette to generate:

* **Monochromatic** - Generate different shades of the key color.
* **Analogous** - Generate colors that are next to each other on the color wheel.
* **Complementary** - Generate colors positioned on opposite sides of the color wheel from the key color.
* **Split Complementary** - Generate the key color and two colors adjacent to the key color’s complement.
* **Triadic** - Generate three colors evenly spaced around the color wheel.
* **Square** - Generate four colors evenly spaced around the color wheel.
* **Rectangular (Tetradic)** - Generate 2 colors equidistant from the key color on the color wheel and then their complements.
* **Circular** - Generate colors evenly spaced around the color wheel.
* **Golden Ratio** - Creates a color palette using the Golden Ratio. This palette type avoids repeating colours and adjacent colours are always different.

chunks.title: Color Window
chunks.heading: Color Window > Color Window > UI > Palettes > Set a Layer's label color
chunks.text:
**Make Harmonic** - When checked, any generated colors which are visually very similar are shifted slightly to make them more distinct.

**Number of Colors** - Specify the number of colors the palette contains. Number of Colors can be set to a value between 2 and 8 except for Split Complementary (6), Triadic (6) and Golden Ratio (20).

**Preview** - A preview of the palette.

**Generate** - Click to select an option:

* Save the palette so it can be used in the **Library Palette**.
* **Set Gradient from Palette** - With the Gradient attribute of a [Gradient Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/gradient-shader/) selected, set color stops using the palette.
* **Create Color Array from Palette** - Create a [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/) using the palette.

info

**Library**, **Project** and **Label** Palettes can also be created manually. See the [Palettes](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/palettes/) page for information on the format and location of palettes.

chunks.title: Palettes
chunks.heading: Palettes > Palettes > Intro
chunks.text:
Palettes are stored as human readable `.json` files that can be created either in-app via the [Color Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/) or manually in a text editor.

Palettes can be used in the **Swatches** tab of the [Color Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/).

chunks.title: Palettes
chunks.heading: Palettes > Palettes > Format

chunks.title: Palettes
chunks.heading: Palettes > Palettes > Format > Keys
chunks.text:
* `colors` (required) - An array of colors.
  + `color` (required) - Set a hex value for the color swatch.
  + `swatchName` (required) - Set a name for the color swatch. This is not currently used in the **Library Palettes** UI so can be left blank if preferred (e.g. `"swatchName": ""`) but is recommended for **Label Palettes**.
  + `uid` - The Id for the color swatch. This is used by the **Label Palettes** to reassign colors to Layer/Keyframes/Time Markers when switching palettes.
  + `types` - An array of [superTypes](/docs/tech-info/scripting/api-module/#getsupertypes) that can be used to assign default **Label Colors** to Layers from the **Label Palettes**.
* `designer` - The author's name.
* `fileType` - Specify the file extension.
* `name` (recommended) - Give the palette a name. This will appear in the **Library Palettes** and **Label Palettes** drop down menus .
* `version` - Set a version for compatibility in the future.
* `website` - Add a URL for the **designer**.

chunks.title: Palettes
chunks.heading: Palettes > Palettes > Storing Palettes > Library Palettes
chunks.text:
The default **Library Palettes** are stored as `.pal` files in:

**macOS** - `~/Library/Application Support/Cavalry/Palettes`

**Windows** - `C:\Users\USERNAME\AppData\Roaming\Cavalry\Palettes`

Further libraries of palettes can also be created simply by creating a new directory inside the Palettes directory above. For example, adding a directory called `Scene Group` inside the `Palettes` directory would create a new **Library** called `Scene Group` that can be accessed and loaded via the **Options menu** in the [Color Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/).

caution

Only directories one level below the Palettes directory are supported and a directory must contain at least one palette to appear in the Color Window options.

**Library Palettes** can also be saved as part of a **Project** when using [Project Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/project-settings/). By default, this directory is `@project/Assets/Palettes/`.

chunks.title: Palettes
chunks.heading: Palettes > Palettes > Storing Palettes > Label Palettes
chunks.text:
The default **Label Palettes** are stored as `.pal` files in:

**macOS** - `~/Library/Application Support/Cavalry/LabelPalettes`

**Windows** - `C:\Users\USERNAME\AppData\Roaming\Cavalry\LabelPalettes`

chunks.title: Control Centre
chunks.heading: Control Centre > Control Centre > Intro
chunks.text: The **Control Centre** is a place to promote the most important attributes in your scene for quick and easy access. This can be particularly useful for rigging or sharing scenes with colleagues or clients.

chunks.title: Control Centre
chunks.heading: Control Centre > Control Centre > UI
chunks.text:
To add an attribute to the **Control Centre**, right click on an attribute in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) and select **Add to Control Centre**.

To remove an attribute from the **Control Centre**, right click on an attribute in the Control Centre or the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) and select **Remove from Control Centre**.

If you add attributes from different Compositions to the Control Centre, those attributes will appear in a tab for each Composition.

UI Affordance

When adding attributes to the **Control Centre**, a small blue dot will be added to the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/)'s row.

chunks.title: Dependency Graph
chunks.heading: Dependency Graph > Dependency Graph > Intro
chunks.text: The **Dependency Graph** is a window providing an interactive schematic view or map of the connections within a Composition.

chunks.title: Dependency Graph
chunks.heading: Dependency Graph > Dependency Graph > Anatomy of a Layer
chunks.text:
When viewed in the Dependency Graph a Layer is represented as a block containing a list of attributes. The input and output connection for each attribute is represented by a 'port' with the input on the left and the output on the right.

Nodes are colour coded based on type (int, string, double etc).

chunks.title: Dependency Graph
chunks.heading: Dependency Graph > Dependency Graph > Anatomy of a Layer > Header row
chunks.text:
The header row contains the Layer's icon and inherits its color from the Layer's Label Color.

Clicking the output port will create a connection from the `Id` (output) connection.

When dropping a connection onto the input port on this row a menu will appear with a list of available Attributes that can be connected to.

chunks.title: Dependency Graph
chunks.heading: Dependency Graph > Dependency Graph > UI > Header
chunks.text:
**Grid Snapping** - When enabled, Layers will snap to the grid when being repositioned.

**Show Grid** - Show/hide the background grid.

**Mini-Map** - Show/hide a Mini-Map of the window which can be used to navigate the graph.

**Wire Style** - Set the style of the connecting wires between Layer ports:

* **Bézier** - Draw bézier curves between ports.
* **Straight** - Draw straight lines between ports.
* **Orthogonal** - Draw elbow joints between ports.

**Search** - Search for Layers within the graph. If a Layer is found, the view will update to frame it.

**Bookmarks** - Save the current view of the graph. Options:

* **Save Bookmark...** - Save the current view position as a bookmark. Once a bookmark is saved, it will appear in the list and can be used to reset the view to the bookmark.
* **Manage Bookmarks...** - Open a popover with a list of saved bookmarks which can be renamed or deleted.

**Clear Selected** - Click to clear all selected Layers from the Layout.

**Clear all** - Click to clear all Layers from the layout.

chunks.title: Dependency Graph
chunks.heading: Dependency Graph > Dependency Graph > UI > Creating Layers
chunks.text:
To create a Layer in the Dependency Graph:

* Position the cursor.
* Hit the `Tab` key.
* Scroll or search for a Layer in the popover window.
* Double click a Layer to create it.

The Layer will appear close to the position of the cursor.

chunks.title: Dependency Graph
chunks.heading: Dependency Graph > Dependency Graph > UI > Loading Layers
chunks.text:
Simply drag and drop a Layer from the Scene Tree to the Dependency Graph to map its connections. The Layer dragged is considered the 'root' Layer and any upstream Layers will also be added.

When adding a Layer to the Dependency Graph it, along with related Layers, is positioned and organised within a grid layout.

Double click a Layer or single click with **Live Mode** enabled to load its UI into the Attribute Editor.

To delete a Layer, select it and hit the `Delete` key. Note that this actually deletes the Layer from the Scene. Use the **Clear Selected** button at the top right of the UI to remove a Layer from the Layout.

chunks.title: Dependency Graph
chunks.heading: Dependency Graph > Dependency Graph > UI > Connections > Create a connection
chunks.text:
To create a connection in the Dependency Graph either:

* Click an output port from one Layer and then click on the input port of another.
* Click and drag on the output port from one Layer and then release the mouse on the input port of another.

If a Layer's Attribute is not already exposed then **right clicking** the **output** `Id` port will open a list of available Attributes.

Note that when clicking the `Id` row of the **input**, a list of Attributes for that Layer will appear – select an Attribute from the list to make a connection to.

chunks.title: Dependency Graph
chunks.heading: Dependency Graph > Dependency Graph > UI > Connections > Overwrite an existing connection
chunks.text: If a connection already exists on an attribute, attempting to make a different connection to the same attribute will replace the existing connection.

chunks.title: Dependency Graph
chunks.heading: Dependency Graph > Dependency Graph > UI > Connections > Delete a connection

chunks.title: Dependency Graph
chunks.heading: Dependency Graph > Dependency Graph > UI > Connections > Attribute Expressions
chunks.text: Right click a connection to add an [Attribute Expression](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-interaction/#attribute-expressions) or edit an existing one. A `π` symbol will appear along the connection if an Attribute Expression exists.

chunks.title: Dependency Graph
chunks.heading: Dependency Graph > Dependency Graph > UI > Layout
chunks.text:
Click and drag a Layer to reposition it within the layout.

Scroll to zoom in/out of the view.

Hit `F` to fit the current graph to the Window.

The layout is saved with the Scene.

chunks.title: Dependency Graph
chunks.heading: Dependency Graph > Dependency Graph > UI > Backdrop > Create a Backdrop
chunks.text:
To create a Backdrop:

1. Select a Layer(s).
2. Right click and choose `Create Backdrop from Selection`.

chunks.title: Dependency Graph
chunks.heading: Dependency Graph > Dependency Graph > UI > Backdrop > Edit a Backdrop
chunks.text:
* **Rename** - To rename a Backdrop and add an optional description either:
  + Double click inside the Backdrop.
  + Right click a Backdrop and choose `Edit Backdrop...`
* **Resize** - Drag the edges or corners of a Backdrop to resize it.
* **Color** - Right click a Backdrop and choose `Set Color` to select a color from the [Label Palette](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/#palettes).

chunks.title: Dependency Graph
chunks.heading: Dependency Graph > Dependency Graph > UI > Backdrop > Delete a Backdrop
chunks.text:
To delete a Backdrop:

* Right click a Backdrop and choose `Delete Backdrop`.

Unsupported features

The following connections are not currently represented in the Dependency Graph:

* Connections to **Self** - e.g. position.x→position.y.
* Connections from the **Composition Settings** - e.g. composition.time→noiseBehaviour.time.
* Connections from the **Render Manager** - e.g. renderManager.dynamicIndex→colorArray.index
* Connections from the **Scene Palette**.

chunks.title: Command Search
chunks.heading: Command Search > Command Search > Intro
chunks.text: Quickly search and execute Cavalry commands including creating Shapes, opening Windows, running menu items and opening Scripts.

chunks.title: Command Search
chunks.heading: Command Search > Command Search > UI
chunks.text:
Type `/` (slash) anywhere in the application to bring up the window. Simply search for a command and hit `Return` to execute it.

The last three commands run will appear above the search bar for quick access.

chunks.title: Command Search
chunks.heading: Command Search > Command Search > UI > Quick Actions
chunks.text:
Certain actions can be performed by choosing a '**Quick Action**' from the list. When choosing a **Quick Action**, the **Command Search** window will slide to a list of options related to the chosen action for the current selection.

Type `Option/Alt` + `/` (slash) anywhere in the application to bring up the window filtered for Quick Actions.

chunks.title: Command Search
chunks.heading: Command Search > Command Search > UI > Quick Actions > Keyframe…
chunks.text:
Show all the **keyframe-able** attributes for the selected Layers. Choosing a row will create a keyframe at the current frame for the attribute associated to that row.

It's also possible to add a keyframe to e.g. `position.x`:

* Select a Shape.
* Type `Option/Alt` + `/`.
* Start typing 'Position'.
* Use the `⬆︎`/`⬇︎` arrow keys to select the **Position** row.
* Type `Option/Alt` + `X`

Use XYZ when setting RGB keyframes. For example, with the `material.materialColor` row selected, type `Option/Alt` + `X` to set a keyframe for `material.materialColor.r`.

Where an Attribute includes 4 channels (e.g. Red, Green, Blue, Alpha), use `W` to set the forth channel.

chunks.title: Command Search
chunks.heading: Command Search > Command Search > UI > Quick Actions > Presets…
chunks.text: Show all the [Presets](/docs/user-interface/general/presets/) available for the selected Layers. Choosing a row will apply the associated Preset.

chunks.title: Workspaces
chunks.heading: Workspaces > Workspaces > Intro
chunks.text:
