Cavalry's default Workspace consists of various Windows but it's possible to set up and save custom Window layouts for context specific tasks. This can be useful when switching focus between drawing/ rigging/ animating/ etc. in order to only display the UI elements required for each specific task.

Cavalry's default Workspace

chunks.title: Workspaces
chunks.heading: Workspaces > Workspaces > Saving a Workspace
chunks.text:
To save a Workspace:

1. Arrange the various Windows in a layout of your preference.
2. Window > Save Workspace...
3. Give the Workspace a name and save.

The Workspace just saved will now appear under **Window > Workspaces > `<yourSavedWorkspace>`**

Organise Workspaces

**Workspaces** can be organised by saving them into folders/ directories. Each folder will appear as a 'category' when loading a Workspace. For example, `/Workspaces/Animation/Character.json` will appear as **Workspaces > Animation > Character** in the menu.

chunks.title: Workspaces
chunks.heading: Workspaces > Workspaces > Loading a Workspace
chunks.text:
To load a Workspace:

1. Window > Workspaces > Choose a saved Workspace.

The Windows will rearrange based on the Workspace selected.

chunks.title: Workspaces
chunks.heading: Workspaces > Workspaces > Updating a Workspace
chunks.text: Workspaces do not autosave – think of them more as a 'preset'. If you need to update an existing Workspace simply follow the steps to save a workspace and overwrite the existing workspace with the same name.

chunks.title: Workspaces
chunks.heading: Workspaces > Workspaces > General
chunks.text:
Workspaces are saved in:

* **macOS** - `~/Library/Preferences/Cavalry/Workspaces/`
* **Windows** - `C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Local\Cavalry\Workspaces\`

On exiting Cavalry, the current layout will be saved and used the next time Cavalry is launched. This is the **Active Workspace** and is saved in:

* **macOS** - `~/Library/Preferences/Cavalry/workspace.json`
* **Windows** - `C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Local\Cavalry\workspace.json`

info

**AppData** and **~/Library** are hidden folders. To find them:

* **Windows** - Check '**Hidden Items**' in the **View options** for **Explorer**.
* **macOS** - In **Finder**, **Library** will appear if you hold `Option/Alt` when opening the **Go** menu.

macOS Ventura

Due to a known bug in **macOS Ventura** that affects dragging windows, the preview normally shown when repositioning a window has been temporarily disabled. This is a purely a visual issue so does not affect functionality. We have made Apple aware of the issue and hope to have it resolved soon.

chunks.title: Glyph Browser
chunks.heading: Glyph Browser > Glyph Browser > Intro
chunks.text: The Glyph Browser provides a way to access all the glyphs within a font including those that cannot be entered via a keyboard.

chunks.title: Glyph Browser
chunks.heading: Glyph Browser > Glyph Browser > UI
chunks.text:
Select the **font** and its **weight** from options at the bottom of the window.

Use the **Size** slider to decrease/increase the preview of each glyph

Double click a glyph to copy it to the clipboard which can then be pasted into a String.

chunks.title: JavaScript Console
chunks.heading: JavaScript Console > JavaScript Console > Introduction
chunks.text:
The **JavaScript Console** can be used to debug **JavaScript** scripts. More information on how to write scripts can be found in the [Scripting](/docs/tech-info/scripting/scripting-getting-started/) section.

It is also available as an embedded panel within the [JavaScript Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/javascript-editor/). This panel will be hidden if the **JavaScript Console** is already docked as part of a [Workspace](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/general/workspaces/).

chunks.title: JavaScript Console
chunks.heading: JavaScript Console > JavaScript Console > UI
chunks.text:
**Clear logs** (button) - Use this button to clear the Console of all previous logs.

**Console** - All logs will be printed here and colour coded based on their status:

* Green = Success
* Yellow = Warning
* Red = Error

note

The JavaScript Console is editable meaning notes can be added and its contents can be copied to the clipboard.

chunks.title: JavaScript Editor
chunks.heading: JavaScript Editor > JavaScript Editor > Introduction
chunks.text:
The **JavaScript Editor** can be used to write **JavaScript** scripts which can be run in Cavalry to create, connect and affect Layers. More information on how to write scripts can be found in the [Scripting](/docs/tech-info/scripting/scripting-getting-started/) section.

caution

Scripts are saved across sessions (they will still be there when you close and reopen Cavalry) but it's important to note that the **JavaScript Editor** is not a way to edit files on the file system. A file can be imported from the file system but any edits to that script will not be saved to the original file.

Stallion

Visual Studio Code users should also check out [Stallion](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=Scenery.cavalry-bridge) – an extension to send scripts to Cavalry which ships with Cavalry's [Typescript](https://github.com/scenery-io/cavalry-types) definitions.

chunks.title: JavaScript Editor
chunks.heading: JavaScript Editor > JavaScript Editor > UI > Buttons
chunks.text:
**Run Script** - Run the script in the active tab. To run just the selected text, hold `Option/Alt` while clicking this button.

**Clear Script** - Clear the active tab.

**Load...** - Import a script from the file system. On import, a dialogue asking whether to load the script into a new tab or replace the active one will appear.

**Save As...** - Save the active tab to the file system.

**Save Encrypted...** - Save the active tab to the file system in an encrypted format.

chunks.title: JavaScript Editor
chunks.heading: JavaScript Editor > JavaScript Editor > UI > Tabs
chunks.text:
* Use the `+` button to add a new Tab.
* To rename a Tab, right click on one and choose **Rename...**.
* To close/remove a Tab, right click on one and choose **Delete** or click the `x` button.

chunks.title: JavaScript Editor
chunks.heading: JavaScript Editor > JavaScript Editor > UI > Find
chunks.text:
info

Hit `Cmd/Ctrl` + `F` to place the cursor/caret in the search field.

**Search field** - Enter a string to locate within the script.

**Previous** - Highlight the previous match to the search string.

**Next** - Highlight the next match to the search string.

**Replace** - When checked, a new row will appear with options to replace the search string with a new string.

**Replace field** - Enter a string to replace the search string(s) with.

**Replace** - Replace the current search string with the replace string.

**Replace All** - Replace all instances of the search string with the replace string.

chunks.title: JavaScript Editor
chunks.heading: JavaScript Editor > JavaScript Editor > UI > Editor
chunks.text:
Enter JavaScript code here. When writing, new lines will be auto-indented.

Commenting Code

To comment-out lines of code, select any part of a line or lines and then use the `Cmd/Ctrl` + `/` shortcut. Comments (`//`) will be added to each line which disables that code. Use the same hotkey to uncomment any code that is already commented-out.

chunks.title: JavaScript Editor
chunks.heading: JavaScript Editor > JavaScript Editor > UI > Editor > Autocomplete
chunks.text:
When typing e.g. `api.`, `cavalry.` or `ui.` an autocomplete window will appear. Use the `⬆︎`/`⬇︎` keys to select an option and then hit `Return` to select the required member function from the list of results. Alternatively, use the cursor and double click a result.

When typing `{`, `[` or `"`, the matching/closing pair will be automatically created. If deleting the first of two such matching pairs, both will be deleted.

chunks.title: JavaScript Editor
chunks.heading: JavaScript Editor > JavaScript Editor > UI > Editor > Format
chunks.text:
To tidy a script's indentation either:

* Use `Shift` + `Option/Alt` + `F` or;
* Right click > **Format All**.

Where part of the script is selected, only that part will be formatted and the context menu item will be updated to **Format Selection**.

chunks.title: JavaScript Editor
chunks.heading: JavaScript Editor > JavaScript Editor > UI > Console Panel
chunks.text: When hitting **Run Script...**, any logs are printing here and colour coded based on their status. Note that this panel will be hidden if the [JavaScript Console](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/javascript-console/) is already docked as part of a [Workspace](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/general/workspaces/).

chunks.title: JavaScript Editor
chunks.heading: JavaScript Editor > JavaScript Editor > UI > Snippet Panel > Create a Snippet
chunks.text: To create a snippet, select a section of code from the editor and drag it into the **Snippet Panel**.

chunks.title: JavaScript Editor
chunks.heading: JavaScript Editor > JavaScript Editor > UI > Snippet Panel > Insert a Snippet
chunks.text: To insert a snippet into a script, place the cursor on a line within the script and then drag and drop a snippet from the snippet panel into the script panel.

chunks.title: JavaScript Editor
chunks.heading: JavaScript Editor > JavaScript Editor > UI > Snippet Panel > Import a Snippet
chunks.text:
To import a snippet either:

* Click the  button and choose `Import...` to import a valid .json snippet file from the file system.
* Drag and drop a valid .json snippet file from the file system into the **Snippet Panel**.

chunks.title: JavaScript Editor
chunks.heading: JavaScript Editor > JavaScript Editor > UI > Snippet Panel > Rename a Snippet
chunks.text:
To rename a snippet either:

* Double click a snippet's row.
* Select a snippet and hit `Return`.
* Click the  button on the snippet's row and choose `Rename`.
* Right click a snippet's row and choose `Rename`.

chunks.title: JavaScript Editor
chunks.heading: JavaScript Editor > JavaScript Editor > UI > Snippet Panel > Delete a Snippet
chunks.text:
To delete a snippet either:

* Select the snippet row and hit the `Delete` button.
* Click the  button on the snippet's row and choose `Delete`.
* Right click a snippet's row and choose `Delete`.

chunks.title: JavaScript Editor
chunks.heading: JavaScript Editor > JavaScript Editor > UI > Snippet Panel > Export a Snippet
chunks.text:
To export a snippet either:

* Click the  button on the snippet's row and choose `Export...`.
* Right click a snippet's row and choose `Export...`.

tip

It's possible to drag and drop text directly into the **Snippet Panel** from apps that support dragging blocks of selected text like [TextEdit](https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/textedit/welcome/mac) or [Sublime Text](https://www.sublimetext.com/).

chunks.title: JavaScript Editor
chunks.heading: JavaScript Editor > JavaScript Editor > UI > Snippet Panel > Run a Snippet
chunks.text:
If a Snippet contains executable code it can be run by either:

* Click the  button on the snippet's row and choose `Run Snippet`.
* Right click a snippet's row and choose `Run Snippet`.

info

Snippets are saved as a JSON dictionary.

```
{

"resourceType": "cavalry.snippets",

"semVer": "1.0",

"snippets": [

{

"contents": "api.primitive(\"rectangle\");",

"name": "Example Snippet"

}

]

}
```

The `snippets.json` file containing snippets listed in the **Snippets Panel** can be found in:

* **macOS** - `~/Library/Application Support/Cavalry/`
* **Windows** - `C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Roaming\Cavalry\`

chunks.title: Mesh Explorer
chunks.heading: Mesh Explorer > Mesh Explorer > Intro
chunks.text:
The **Mesh Explorer** can be used to examine a [Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/)'s internal mesh structure and hierarchy.

Select a single Shape to load its information into the **Mesh Explorer**. For performance reasons, it's not possible to load more than one Shape at a time or explore a Shape with more than 200 sub-meshes.

chunks.title: Mesh Explorer
chunks.heading: Mesh Explorer > Mesh Explorer > UI
chunks.text:
**Lock** - Prevent the window from updating unless **Refresh** is clicked.

**Refresh** - Once a Shape is loaded into the window, its information is not 'live'. Use this button to update the current selection after any changes to a Shape have been made.

The small numbers on the left indicate the 'level' each mesh is at. This is useful to know when working with the [Sub-Mesh](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/) Behaviour or other Layers that can access the child-meshes.

A preview for each mesh is displayed. Where a 'parent' is found, a folder icon is displayed. For example, a Text Shape is constructed of several levels including Line, Word and Character.

Tags provide additional information like, Ids, Point Counts and whether a Material is included.

Point Counts

Note that point counts may not precisely match what is seen in the Viewport. As an example, the Mesh Explorer will report a **Point Count** of **4** for a closed triangle visually made of 3 corner points. This is because a closed triangle actually includes co-positional points at both the start and end of its path behind the scenes.

```
1. 0,10

2. 10,10

3. -10,10

4. 0,10
```

chunks.title: Message Bar
chunks.heading: Message Bar > Message Bar > Intro
chunks.text: This window sits at the bottom of the Scene Window (by default) and contains helpful messages including confirmations, warnings and tips. You can also view a list of recent messages via the **Log Window** using the speech mark button on the left hand side of the window.

chunks.title: Preferences
chunks.heading: Preferences > Preferences > Intro
chunks.text:
Set custom preferences for working in Cavalry.

info

This window appears under the [Edit](/docs/user-interface/menus/edit-menu/) menu on Windows and the **Cavalry** menu on macOS.

chunks.title: Preferences
chunks.heading: Preferences > Preferences > Preferences
chunks.text: **Show Experimental Features** - When checked, features under the 'experimental' tag will be available.

chunks.title: Preferences
chunks.heading: Preferences > Preferences > Preferences > Save
chunks.text:
**JSON format** - Set the format files will be saved in:

* **Pretty** - Indents are set to 4 spaces. This is the most 'human readable' format but produces the largest file sizes.
* **Compact** - Indents are set to 1 space and the file is further 'compacted'. This is 'human readable' but produces smaller file sizes than **Pretty**.
* **One Line** - The entire file is saved to a single line. This is not easily 'human readable' but produces the smallest file sizes.

Pretty Print

Files saved as **Compact** or **One Line** can still be converted to the **Pretty** format using ***pretty-print*** features in VSCode/Sublime/etc. or via a website like [JSONLint.com](https://jsonlint.com).

**Autosave**:

* **Off** - Do not autosave.
* **Reminders** - Show reminders in the notifications bar.
* **Autosave** - Save the file based on the **Autosave Interval**. An autosave file will only be created if any changes have been made since the last save.

**Autosave Interval** - Set a time in minutes to autosave.

**Autosave Folders** - Separate autosave files into daily directories:

chunks.title: Preferences
chunks.heading: Preferences > Preferences > Preferences > Save
chunks.text:
* **Off** - Do not save into directories.
* **Weekday-Day-Month-Year** - e.g. Thu-26-03-2023
* **Weekday-Month-Day-Year** - e.g. Thu-03-26-2023
* **Year-Month-Day-Weekday** - e.g. 2023-03-26-Thu

**Autosave Limit** - Set the maximum number of autosave files that will be created. When the maximum is reached, the oldest autosave file is deleted whenever a new one is created. If **Autosave Folders** are being used, this limit applies for each day.

info

If you have a project set then any auto saves will be saved in the directory set in the [Project Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/project-settings/). If no project is set, then files will be saved into an autosave directory in the same location as your scene file.

chunks.heading: Preferences > Preferences > Preferences > UI
chunks.text:
**UI Font Size** - Set the font size for the User Interface.

* **Default** - Set the default font size.
* **Large** -Set the large font size.

**Infinite Scrubbing** - When checked, scrubbing the values in [Controls](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-interaction/) is not constrained by the bounds of a display. The cursor will also be hidden when scrubbing values.

info

When using a tablet/pen this preference is ignored. If the cursor did wrap, it would become inconsistent with where the pen is positioned on screen for tablets with displays.

**Show Tips button in Message Bar** - Show/hide the `Tips and Tricks` button in the Message Bar.

**Show Feedback button in Message Bar** - Show/hide the `Feedback` button in the Message Bar.

**Max Attribute Editor UIs** - Set a limit for the number of UIs that can be loaded into the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/). When this limit is reached, the addition of any new UIs will remove the last (bottom) UI. Note - this limit is exclusive of any pinned UIs.

chunks.title: Preferences
chunks.heading: Preferences > Preferences > Preferences > UI
chunks.text:
**Large Previews in the Attribute Editor** - Set the height of previews for the Layers that include them (Noise, Random, Sequence etc).

**Arrow Keys Control Hierarchy** - When checked, using the arrow keys will navigate the hierarchy in the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/). When unchecked, the arrow keys will nudge selected layers in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) and holding `Option/Alt` will then navigate the hierarchy.

**Locking Layers Prevents Selection in the Scene Window** - When checked, locking a Layer in the Scene Window will prevent selection of that Layer. Note that this will also prevent **Live Mode** from working when single clicking a locked Layer.

**Preview Compositions in the Assets Window** - When checked, previews will be shown when hovering Compositions in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).

**Viewport Canvas Color** - Set a color for the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/)'s canvas (the area outside the Composition).

chunks.text:
**Pressing Return in an Attribute Field** - Determine what happens when pressing the `Return` key within a field:

* **Selects All** - Commit the input and select the contents of the field allowing for continued editing.
* **Clears Focus** - Commit the input and remove focus from the field so shortcuts/hotkeys can be used.

chunks.title: Preferences

chunks.text:
**Add new Layers to selected Tags** - If a [Tag](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/tags/) or several Tags are selected, any new Layers created will be added to it/them on creation.

**Remember Graph Editor Curve Framing** - When checked the [Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/) will remember the framing/zoom level of an animation curve from the last time you were working with it.

**Maintain Proportional Easing** - When checked, moving a keyframe in the [Time Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/) or [Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/) will also scale any bézier handles in order to maintain easing.

**Use Absolute Bézier Positions** - When checked, the `Value` and `Frame` values for the positions of bézier handles when double clicking a keyframe in the Graph Editor are displayed as absolute positions. When unchecked, the values are displayed as relative to the keyframe.

chunks.text:
**Nudge Step** - Set the number of frames a **Keyframe** or **Clip** will be moved by when holding `Shift` and using the `Animation > Nudge Backwards/Forwards` hotkeys ( `-`/`=` ).

**Default Velocity Presets** - Use the drop down to set the [Default Velocity Presets](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/motion-paths/#setting-default-velocity-presets) for use with [Motion Paths](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/motion-paths/).

chunks.text:
**Show Viewport Timecode** - Show/hide a timecode in the Viewport.

* **Never** - Never show the timecode in the Viewport.
* **During Playback** - Only show the timecode in the Viewport during playback.
* **Always** - Always show the timecode in the Viewport.

**Render Notifications** - Send OS notifications on completion of renders.

* **None** - Do not send a notification.
* **End of Render Queue Item** - Send a notification when each Render Queue Item completes.
* **End of Render Queue** - Send a notification when the entire Render Queue completes.

chunks.title: Preferences
chunks.heading: Preferences > Preferences > Preferences > Color Management
chunks.text:
**Enable Color Management** - When checked, Scenes, including most image/video assets and renders will be color managed. By setting a working color space for the Scene a common color space is used for compositing and other color operations making it easier to control the appearance of colors.

All image/video **assets** and **renders** will be color managed with the exception of GIF, SVG and Lottie which all convert to sRGB regardless of the working space. Any renders are automatically assigned the Scene's working color space.

Bit Depth

Some small colour discrepancies (up to ~1% out) are expected as Cavalry is not yet 16bit.

**Working Color Space** - Select a color space.

Display Color Space

The Viewport's color space and certain parts of the UI can be set via the [Viewport Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#viewport-settings).

**Compositing Bit Depth** - Determine the amount of color information stored per pixel. A higher bit depth results in more colors and smoother gradients:

* **8-bit** - 256 colors per channel.
* **16-bit** - 65,536 colors per channel.

[Color Management→](/docs/user-interface/general/color-management/)

chunks.heading: Preferences > Preferences > Preferences > Export
chunks.text: **Lottie Author** - The text you enter here will be added to the `.json` file for any Lottie exports.

chunks.title: Preferences
chunks.heading: Preferences > Preferences > Preferences > Bake Animation
chunks.text:
The Bake Animation command samples an animation curve and redraws it based on the chosen settings. It can also be used to convert procedural animation via Behaviours or Magic Easing to keyframed animation. These settings can be used to reduce or increase the number of keyframes created when using the command.

**Collinear Tolerance** - When sampling the animation curve, the Bake Animation command determines whether keyframes will fall withing this angle of the animation curve and not create them if they do. For example, setting a value of 1 will remove all keyframes that fall within a range of +/- 1° away from the animation curve. A higher value will create less keyframes and so a cleaner but less accurate result.

**Bake Accuracy** - A higher setting will result in a more accurate shape but will create more keyframes.

chunks.title: Preferences
chunks.heading: Preferences > Preferences > Preferences > Performance
chunks.text:

info

The settings above can be manually edited via [Preferences](/docs/tech-info/user-preferences/).

chunks.title: Render Manager
chunks.heading: Render Manager > Render Manager > Intro
chunks.text:
The **Render Manager** is the place to output scenes to files. The window consists of two sections – the **Header** and the **Render Queue**. The **Header** at the top contains a few simple controls for submitting renders and the **Render Queue** at the bottom is where you can drag in [Compositions](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/) to create **Render Queue Items**.

tip

* Adding [Compositions](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/) to the **Render Queue** creates **Render Queue Items**. This can be done by either using the `+ Current Composition` button at the top of the window or by dragging a Composition from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) into the **Render Queue**.
* **Render Queue Items** are saved with the Scene.
* Any unchecked **Render Queue Items** will not render.

chunks.text:
¹ The ProRes 4444 and ProRes 4444 XQ codecs support alpha.

Rendering with Alpha

In order to render with Alpha, don't forget to set the Composition's **Background Alpha** to **0** via the [Composition Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/).

Rendering to MP4

Rendering to H.264/MP4 is restricted to a maximum of **9,437,184** pixels. Any aspect ratio can be rendered but if the width∗heightwidth \* heightwidth∗height of a Composition exceeds this value then it will be scaled down proportionally to the maximum supported resolution when rendering.More Information

The summary above is a slight simplification. Rendering to H.264/MP4 is restricted to a resolution which contains a maximum of **36,864** macro-blocks.

A macro-block is 16 x 16px so the number of macro-blocks a Composition includes can be calculated as (width/16)∗(height/16)(width / 16) \* (height / 16)(width/16)∗(height/16).

For example, the maximum 16:9 resolution that can be rendered is **4096 x 2304px** because (4096/16)∗(2304/16)=36864(4096 / 16) \* (2304 / 16) = 36864(4096/16)∗(2304/16)=36864.

A temporary copy of the scene file is saved so that it's possible to continue working in Cavalry while the render processes. Assets (except video) are saved to RAM so any changes to these will not affect the final render. Video assets should not be moved or updated during a background render.

Once a Background Render has been launched, the render's status will appear in the [Message Bar](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/message-bar/) every 5 seconds plus a final message to confirm when the render has completed.

**Cog** - Click the cog icon to open a popover window with options to re-time the Composition at render time:

* **New Composition Length** - Enter a timecode (MINUTE:SECOND:FRAME) to set the duration of the render. For example, a 25fps Composition with a duration of 100 frames (4secs) can be retimed to 6secs by entering `00:06:00`.

Re-timing

chunks.title: Render Manager
chunks.heading: Render Manager > Render Manager > UI > Render Queue Item > Header
chunks.text:
* While it's possible to reduce the length of a Composition, it's best practice to use this feature to extend the duration. This reduces the chance of important frames (e.g. the moment a bouncing ball touches the ground) being removed.
* When extending Compositions, it's important to understand that while animation curves can be stretched at render time, stepped animation that occurs on frame integers (e.g. an image sequence/video) will result in duplicated frames.
* Where animation occurs over 1 frame, ensure the animation curve's interpolation is set to **Stepped** to prevent the result being stretched during retiming.

Link to Canva

Legacy Accounts (Cavalry 2.6.1 and earlier) - In order to upload to [Canva](https://www.canva.com), a link must be created with your Cavalry account by going to the [Account](https://account.scenegroup.co/) page and navigating to the **Linked Accounts** section. Click `Manage Links` to start the process.

**Upload Preset** - Pick a preset to send uploads to. Use the [Upload Preset Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/upload-preset-manager/) to create and edit upload locations.

Cancelling a Render

Cancelling a render will also cancel any uploads in the queue but any 'in progress' uploads will continue.

---

**Metadata**

**Enable Metadata** - When checked, metadata files will be exported along with the render(s).

**Format** - Select the formatting used for the metadata:

* **JSON** - Export the metadata as a JSON dictionary.
* **Simple Traits JSON** - Export the metadata formatted for use as a traits file. An 'image' key with the file name is included automatically.
* **NFT Traits JSON** - Export ERC-1155 compliant metadata for use with sites such as [NFT.Storage](https://nft.storage/).

Add - Add a new key-value pair.

chunks.title: Render Manager
chunks.heading: Render Manager > Render Manager > UI > Render Queue Item > Header
chunks.text:
* **Key** - An identifying name for the value. Use a dot (`.`) to group keys into their own dictionaries inside the JSON. For example, `attributes.colour` will put the key `colour` inside a dictionary called `attributes`.
* **Value** - Connect a Layer's attribute to be used as the value. Typically, the attribute will be set up as part of a [Dynamic Render](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/dynamic-rendering/) in order for it to update for each render.

Id connections

It's not currently possible to connect the **Id** (or output) connection of a layer directly into the **Value** of a key-value pair. To work around this, it's possible to go via another layer. For example, create a [Random](/docs/nodes/behaviours/random/) and a [Value](/docs/nodes/behaviours/value/) Behaviour then connect `Random.Id` to `Value.Value` and then connect `Value.Value` to the metadata's **Value**.

info

Metadata files are automatically created per rendered video, still or image sequence.

chunks.title: Render Manager
chunks.heading: Render Manager > Render Manager > UI > Render Queue Item > Header

chunks.title: Dynamic Rendering
chunks.heading: Dynamic Rendering
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Render Manager* Dynamic Rendering

On this page

chunks.title: Dynamic Rendering
chunks.heading: Dynamic Rendering > Dynamic Rendering > Intro
chunks.text:
**Dynamic Rendering** can be used to generate different values at render time and so create many variations of the same single Composition.

* Create variations on some abstract procedural artwork/animations.
* Automate otherwise time consuming and error prone workflows.
* Set up versioning for endboards.
* A/B testing.
* Output personalised advertising.
* And more...

Options for **Dynamic Rendering** can be found in the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/).

chunks.title: Dynamic Rendering
chunks.heading: Dynamic Rendering > Dynamic Rendering > Setting up a Dynamic Render
chunks.text:
**Dynamic Rendering** consists of two main components:

* **Dynamic Index** - An attribute found in the header of the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/) that simply outputs a value that increases by one each time a render completes.
* **Render Range** - An attribute found under the **Dynamic** tab of a **Render Queue Item** (RQI). The values set here determine how many times Cavalry will render the RQI (Note - **Dynamic Render** must be checked).

If **Render Range** is set to `0,2`, Cavalry will render the **Render Queue Item** 3 times. On the first render, the **Dynamic Index** will output a value of `0`, on the second render – a value of `1` and on the third – a value of `2`. This simple concept can be put to work to create variation for each output.

In the simple example below, the Polygon's sides are being driven by a [Value Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/value-array/) which is already connected to the **Dynamic Index**. By dragging a connection from the **Dynamic Index** to the **Array Index** of a [Color Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/color-array/) both the **Fill Colour** and the **Sides** of the **Polygon** will change at render time.

chunks.title: Dynamic Rendering
chunks.heading: Dynamic Rendering > Dynamic Rendering > Setting up a Dynamic Render
chunks.text:
The **Dynamic Index Offset** can be used to preview the results.

* A value of `0` outputs the first index (green) on the **Color Array**.
* A value of `1` outputs the second (yellow).
* A value of `2` outputs the third (pink).

To output all three variations the **Render Range** under the **Dynamic** tab is set to **0,2**. During rendering, Cavalry iterates through Dynamic Index's 0, 1 and 2 and outputs a separate file for each one.

The same technique is used in the following example but via a [Spreadsheet](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/) node containing team names and hex values to drive a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) and the coloured background Shapes. The logos are set up with two **SVG Assets** added to an [Asset Array](/docs/nodes/utilities/asset-array/) and then connected to an [SVG Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/svg-shape/).

Imagine what a time saver this could be for all 32 NFL teams when your client wants to change the height to 40px! You only need to make that change once and then hit `Render`. Cavalry will do the heavy lifting for you.

chunks.title: Dynamic Rendering
chunks.heading: Dynamic Rendering > Dynamic Rendering > Filenames
chunks.text:
By default, when using **Dynamic Rendering**, files will be written to separate directories that correspond to the Dynamic Index (0, 1, 2...). This is to prevent files from overwriting each other. Alternatively, a `<Dynamic>` [Render Token](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/render-tokens/) can be added to the **File Name** in the **Render Manager**. This token will add the number of the **Dynamic Index** to the **File Name** and means that files are written directly to the specified **Path**.

You can override this behaviour by unchecking **Ensure Unique File Names** under the Dynamic tab of the Render Manager. With this attribute unchecked, it's up to you to ensure files will not overwrite one another.

chunks.title: Dynamic Rendering
chunks.heading: Dynamic Rendering > Dynamic Rendering > Filenames
chunks.text:
Unique, dynamic filenames can be created by connecting a [String](/docs/nodes/utilities/string/) to the **File Name** attribute. For example, by connecting [Spreadsheet](/docs/nodes/utilities/spreadsheet/) data to the **String**, the contents of each row of a spreadsheet can then be used to generate the filename for each output at render time. As long as the data in each row is unique, each file name will be unique. This functionality can be extended further via a [Formatted String](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/formatted-string-generator/) **String Generator** which can daisy chain strings together.

[Render Tokens](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/render-tokens/) (e.g. `<Composition>`) can also be used within a **String**. Note that a Render Token will only appear styled with a teal color (to indicate it's valid) when viewed in the Render Queue Item.

chunks.title: Lottie Export
chunks.heading: Lottie Export
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Render Manager* Lottie Export

On this page

chunks.title: Lottie Export
chunks.heading: Lottie Export > Lottie Export > Intro
chunks.text:
Lottie is an open source animation file format originally created by the team at [Airbnb](https://airbnb.io/lottie/#/). Because Lottie is vector based files can be very lightweight, scalable and rendered natively on mobile and the web.

Cavalry offers native support for Lottie export via the [File menu](/docs/user-interface/menus/file-menu/) or the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/). Further options can also be found on the [Advanced tab](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).

chunks.title: Lottie Export
chunks.heading: Lottie Export > Lottie Export > UI
chunks.text:
Exporting to Lottie is very straight forward. Simply use the `File > Export Lottie...` menu item. It's also possible to export to Lottie via the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/) so can be used alongside other native features like [Dynamic Rendering](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/dynamic-rendering/).

Further options to refine how Shapes are exported to Lottie can be found in the [Advanced tab](/docs/nodes/shapes/common-attributes/) of a Shape's [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) UI.

When exporting files, Cavalry allows you to add information on the author in the exported file. This can be added via the **Lottie Author** option in the [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/) window.

chunks.title: Lottie Export
chunks.heading: Lottie Export > Lottie Export > Previewing
chunks.text: Various platforms including [LottieFiles](https://lottiefiles.com/) can be used to preview animations. Simply navigate to <https://lottiefiles.com/preview> and drag the exported `.json` Lottie file into the browser window. From here you can also share links your animations.

chunks.title: Lottie Export
chunks.heading: Lottie Export > Lottie Export > Troubleshooting > Optimising
chunks.text:
While the Lottie format is expanding, it is not as full featured as Cavalry so there are some limitations as to what can be exported. However, where feature parity is lacking, Cavalry will attempt to intelligently bake the shape animation so a wide range of possibilities are available.

Generally speaking, Lottie files are very small but the less baking required, the smaller the exported file will be. If file size is very important to you then the list below comprises the features that will not require any baking whatsoever (assuming there are no Deformers connected to the Shape) and will therefore result in the smallest files:

* **Position**
* **Rotation**
* **Fill > Alpha**
* **Stroke > Alpha**
* **Stroke > Width**
* **Stroke > Trim Start**
* **Stroke > Trim End**
* **Stroke > Trim Travel**
* **Path Animation**
* **Star > Point Count**
* **Star > Radius**
* **Star > Inner Radius**

The following features are all supported but are known to create relatively large files when exporting to Lottie:

chunks.title: Lottie Export
chunks.heading: Lottie Export > Lottie Export > Troubleshooting > Optimising
chunks.text:
* **Deformers**.
* [Magic Easing](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/) on paths.
* Animating any Primitive attribute (except for [Star](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/star/))
  . e.g. **Tooth Depth** on [Cogwheel](/docs/nodes/shapes/basic-shape/cogwheel/).
* [Rig Control](/docs/nodes/utilities/rig-control/) and [Animation Control](/docs/nodes/utilities/animation-control/) (when used with Path Animation).
* [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).

Optimisation Tips

* If the exported file size is large but the Scene doesn't have any animation in it you may want to change **Lottie Baking** setting from **Automatic** to **Still** in the **Advanced** tab of the Shape's [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) UI.
* If your Lottie export is missing some animation you were expecting to see, try one of the **Animated** or **Nuclear** Lottie Baking options in the **Advanced** tab of the Shape's [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) UI.

chunks.title: Lottie Export
chunks.heading: Lottie Export > Lottie Export > Troubleshooting > Working with Images
chunks.text:
It's possible to export image assets to Lottie. [LottieFiles](https://lottiefiles.com/) support previewing a zipped file containing the `.json` and an `images` folder containing any image assets.

1. Import an image.
2. Drag the image into the Viewport to create a [Footage Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/footage-shape/) and an [Image Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/image-shader/) and connect the image.
3. Export to Lottie. This will output a `.json` file and an `images` folder containing the image.
4. Zip both the `.json` file and `images` folder.
5. Uploaded the .zip to [LottieFiles](https://lottiefiles.com/).

caution

Support does not yet extend to **Image Sequences** and it's not possible to directly embed an image into the `.json` file — only to reference the image asset in the `images` directory.

Render tokens can be added to the **File Name** or **Path** attributes in the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/) and used to automate the file names of renders.

To add a **Render Token**, simply right click in the **File Name** or **Path** input and select one from the drop down menu. If an invalid token is accidentally entered it will be highlighted red and will not be used.

Environment Variables can also be used as **Render Tokens**. Use the syntax `<Env:VARIABLENAME>`. For example:

* **macOS** - adding `<Env:HOME>` to the **Path** would result in files being written to `Macintosh HD/Users/<YourUser>`.
* **Windows** - adding `<Env:USERPROFILE>` to the **Path** would result in files being written to `C:\Users\<YourUser>`.

To find out which environment variables are in use:

* **macOS** - type `printenv` into **Terminal**.
* **Windows** - type `set` into **Command Prompt**.

The [Formatted String Generator](/docs/nodes/utilities/string-generator/formatted-string-generator/) can be used to concatenate Tokens with other attribute values/strings as a way to generate dynamic file names.

chunks.title: Scene Window
chunks.heading: Scene Window
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Scene Window* Scene Window

On this page

chunks.title: Scene Window
chunks.heading: Scene Window > Scene Window > Intro
chunks.text:
The **Scene Window** is the heart of Cavalry. It consists of several other areas:

The areas of the Scene Window

* The [Timeline](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/timeline/) for navigating time.
* The [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/) for arranging Layers and hierarchy.
* The [Time Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/) for retiming Layers and animation.
* The [Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/) for adjusting animation curves.

The Scene Window

chunks.title: Scene Window
chunks.heading: Scene Window > Scene Window > Manage Compositions
chunks.text: Several [Compositions](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/) can be open at the same time. They are represented by **tabs** at the top of the Scene Window.

chunks.title: Scene Window
chunks.heading: Scene Window > Scene Window > Manage Compositions > Open Compositions
chunks.text:
To open a Composition, either:

* Double click one in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/).
* Click the `Open` button where a Composition is nested within another Composition. See [Pre-Comps](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/#pre-comp).

chunks.title: Scene Window
chunks.heading: Scene Window > Scene Window > Manage Compositions > Close Compositions
chunks.text:
To close a Composition either:

* Choose `Composition > Close Composition` from the menu to close the active Composition.
* Click the `x` that appears on a Composition's tab.
* Right click on a Composition's tab and choose from the following options:
  + **Close** - Close the selected Composition.
  + **Close Others** - Close all Compositions except the selected Composition.
  + **Close Tabs to the Left** - Close all Compositions that appear to the left the selected Composition.
  + **Close Tabs to the Right** - Close all Compositions that appear to the right the selected Composition.

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Scene Window* Graph Editor

On this page

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Intro
chunks.text:
The Graph Editor can be used to edit Keyframes and their resulting animation curves. An animation curve is the line drawn between Keyframes to represent the speed in which the Keyframe values change — also known as 'interpolation'. This can be adjusted by manipulating the handles of a Keyframe to create more natural movement using easing.

Previewing procedural animation curves is also supported. For example, if a [Noise Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/noise/) is connected to `position.x` of a Shape, the resulting animation curve can be shown in the Graph Editor.

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Adjusting Animation Curves
chunks.text:
To load Keyframes and their animation curves into the Graph Editor either:

* Select a Layer or Layers in the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) - this will load all animated Attributes.
* Select an Attribute or Attributes in the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) - this will load all selected animated Attributes.
* Select a Keyframe or Keyframes in the [Time Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/) - this will load all the Attributes associated with the selected Keyframe(s) when switching to the **Graph Editor**.

Once animated Attributes are loaded into the Graph Editor, select the Keyframes to adjust them.

* Move Keyframes **up/down** to increase/decrease their value.
* Move Keyframes **left/right** to move them backward/forward in time.

info

To reveal bézier handles, select a Keyframe(s) or an animation curve.

The animation curve can be adjusted by manipulating a Keyframe's bézier handles. Keyframe's have 3 basic interpolations (or states):

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Adjusting Animation Curves
chunks.text:
* **Linear** - The resulting animation curve is a straight line representing a uniform rate of change between two Keyframes.
* **Bézier** - The resulting animation curve is a curved line representing a smooth rate of change between two Keyframes. Bézier keyframes can be used to ease in and out of values.
* **Step** - The resulting animation curve is an L shape representing no change of values between Keyframes. Also know as 'hold' keyframes, values jump abruptly as the playhead reaches each Keyframe.

To change the interpolation of Keyframes either:

* Select a Keyframe or Keyframes > right click > **Key Interpolation** and then choose an option.
* Select an animation curve or curves > right click > **Curve Interpolation** and then choose an option (this will convert all keyframes on the animation curve(s)).

**Bézier** Keyframes display handles in the Graph Editor. Moving the handles will manipulate the animation curve. See the [shortcuts](#shortcuts) below for how to interact with handles.

Double click to Edit

Double clicking a keyframe will pop up a window with options to set a keyframes properties inline.

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Adjusting Animation Curves
chunks.text:
* **Value** - Set the attribute's value for the keyframe.
* **Interpolation** - Set the [interpolation](#interpolation) for the keyframe.
* **Magic Easing** - Select an option for [Magic Easing](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/#magic-easing).
* **Bézier Handle Positions** - Set the positions for the keyframes bézier handles. These can be absolute or relative via the **Use Absolute Bezier Positions** [preference](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/).
* **Angle Locking** - When a keyframe's **Interpolation** is set to **Bézier**, when checked, changing the angle of one handle will be mirrored by the other handle.
* **Weight Locking** - When a keyframe's **Interpolation** is set to **Bézier**, when checked, adjusting the length of one handle will proportionally affect the length of the other.

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Adjusting Animation Curves > Shortcuts
chunks.text:
Add Keyframe to Curve

Double click a curve to add a keyframe along the animation curve.

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Adjusting Animation Curves > Looping
chunks.text:
To set looping on an animation curve select a curve or curves and right click to bring up the contextual menu. Choose from:

* **Loop After** - Looping will occur after the last keyframe:
  + **None** - Don't loop.
  + **Looping** - Start the loop at the value of the **first** keyframe.
  + **Looping with Offset** - Start the loop at the value of the **last** keyframe.
  + **Oscillate** - Ping pong between the first and last keyframes.
* **Loop Before** - Looping will occur before the first keyframe:
  + **None** - Don't loop.
  + **Looping** - Start the loop at the value of the **first** keyframe
  + **Looping with Offset** - Start the loop at the value of the **last** keyframe.
  + **Oscillate** - Ping pong between the first and last keyframes.

The buttons in the Toolbar at the bottom of the window can also be used.

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Adjusting Animation Curves > Procedural Animation Curves
chunks.text:
Where a Shape's animation is being driven by another Layer, its inherited animation curve can also be previewed in the Graph Editor. For example, if a [Noise Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/noise/) is connected to a Shape's **Position**, selecting that Shape in the **Graph Editor** will preview its animation curve.

This is also true of [Animation Offsets](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/#animation-offsets).

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Tools > Keyframe Layers
chunks.text: See [Keyframe Layers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/keyframe-layers/).

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Tools > Keyframe Values
chunks.text:
**Frame** - With a Keyframe(s) selected, set the frame number for that Keyframe(s).

**Value** - With a Keyframe(s) selected, set the value for that Keyframe(s).

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Tools > Transform tool
chunks.text:
The Transform tool can be used to move and scale selections of keyframes. With the tool active, a green area will appear around any selected keyframes. `Click + drag`:

* The **middle** of the green area to move the selection.
* An **edge** of the green area to horizontally or vertically scale the keyframes.
* A **corner** of the green area to scale the keyframes both horizontally and vertically.

Hold `Option/Alt` when scaling from an edge to scale the keyframes from the centre of the green area.

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Tools > Grid Snapping
chunks.text: When checked, keyframes will snap to the defined increments. Use the checkbox to enable and set the size of the grid.

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Tools > Ghosting
chunks.text: When enabled, a faint line will be drawn whenever adjustments are made to keyframes or handles showing where the animation curve was.

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Tools > Draw Channel Names
chunks.text: When enabled, attribute names will be displayed on the left side of the Graph Editor.

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Tools > Pacing Markers
chunks.text:
Add guides to indicate seconds or audio beats. Toggle the button to enable/disable them or use the arrow to open a disclosure window containing the following options:

**Mode** - Select a mode:

* **Seconds** - Add Pace Markers on each second.
* **Beats per Minute** - Add Pace Markers based on a **BPM**.

**Divisions** - When **Mode** is set to **Seconds**, determine how many sub-steps to add between seconds.

**Beats per Minute** - When **Mode** is set to **Beats pre Minute**, set the **BPM** for the audio track. Grey guides represent **Beats** with the blue guides marking the **Bars**.

**Offset** - When **Mode** is set to **Beats per Minute**, move the markers forward or backward in time.

**Beats per Bar** - When **Mode** is set to **Beats per Minute**, set the number of beats in each bar.

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Tools > Interpolation
chunks.text:
Set the interpolation of the animation curve bewteen keyframes:

* **Linear** - A straight line between neighbouring keyframes.
* **Bézier** - Draw bézier curves between keyframes where handles can be used to manually manipulate the shape of each curve.
* **Stepped** - The animation curve will hold the value of a keyframe and jump to the value of the next.

chunks.title: Graph Editor
chunks.heading: Graph Editor > Graph Editor > Tools > Align
chunks.text: Align selected keyframes from different attributes. When aligning left/right all selected keys will be aligned to the key furthest left/right. When centre aligning keys they will be aligned to the average position of all selected keys.

chunks.title: Keyframe Layers
chunks.heading: Keyframe Layers
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Scene Window* Keyframe Layers

On this page

chunks.title: Keyframe Layers
chunks.heading: Keyframe Layers > Keyframe Layers > Intro
chunks.text: Keyframe Layers make it possible to blend between keyframes/animation curves. This is very useful when needing to switch between animation states like running and walking. Keyframe Layers can transition between these states without the need to copy/paste blocks of animation.

chunks.title: Keyframe Layers
chunks.heading: Keyframe Layers > Keyframe Layers > UI
chunks.text:
**Active** - Enable/disable the layer.

**Strength** - Determine the strength of the layer.

**Mode** - Set a mode for how the layer's values blend with the layers below it:

* **Normal** - Keyframes on the layer are additive.
* **Overwrite** - Keyframes on the layer will overwrite other layers.

Double click a layer's header row to set it as the current layer. The controls will reflect the current layer's values and any changes will be applied to it.

An additional read-only control will appear in the [Scene Tree](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/) when keyframes are added to any non-Default **Keyframe Layers**. This will display the combined value of all Keyframe Layers.

Use the trash icon to remove a Keyframe Layer.

tip

To load the **Strength** animation curve into the [Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/), open the **Keyframe Layer Editor** and select the layer to adjust.

Increasing the Keyframe Layer's Strength increases the arm swing.

Example

chunks.title: Keyframe Layers
chunks.heading: Keyframe Layers > Keyframe Layers > UI
chunks.text:
1. Open **keyframeLayers.cv** (example file below👇) and load the Start Composition.
2. At the bottom of the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/), click the **Keyframe Layer Editor** button
3. Click the `+` button in the bottom right of the window to create a new **Keyframe Layer**.
4. Double click the new Keyframe Layer to switch to it.
5. Set keys on **armUpper.rotation** of:
   * fr0 = -50
   * fr20 = 50
   * fr40 = -50
6. Set keys on **armLower.rotation** of:
   * fr6 = 0
   * fr26 = 40
   * fr46 = 0
7. Switch to the [Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/) to adjust the animation curves.
8. Move the timeline to frame 100.
9. Back in the **Keyframe Layer Editor** set the **Strength** to **0** and set a key.
10. Move the timeline to frame 150.
11. Set **Strength** to a value of **100**.
12. Press Play.

The arm's swing height should increase over frames 100 to 150.

[Example Files↓ Download](/docs/files/keyframeLayers.cv)

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Scene Window* Scene Tree* Scene Tree

On this page

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Intro
chunks.text: The Scene Tree sits to the left of the [Time Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/)/[Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/) within the Scene Window and consists of a dual hierarchy of both parent/child Layers and animated attributes. Layers can be parented underneath one another for animation purposes and/or to organise a Composition.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Lock Layers
chunks.text:
On the far left hand side of the **Scene Tree** there are several columns containing switches. The column to the far left contains the **lock** switch for each Layer. Clicking in this area for each row will show a lock icon which disables selection in the Viewport for 'drawable' Layers like Shapes, Falloffs and Nulls. This can be useful where it's important that Shapes do not get accidentally moved when selecting/moving other Shapes. Locking a Layer also prevents renaming a Layer of any type.

See the **Locking Layers Prevents Selection in the Scene Window** [preference](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/) to customise how locking a Layer affects selection in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Hide/Disable Layers
chunks.text:
The second column contains a switch with either an **eye** or a **checkmark** icon. For a 'drawable' Layers like Shapes, Falloffs and Nulls this will display an eye icon and clicking a row will toggle between hiding or drawing the Layer in the Viewport. For any non-drawable Layers, a checkmark icon is shown. Toggling this will enable/disable the Behaviour/Utility/Effect (i.e. stop it calculating).

A Shape which is a child of another Shape inherits its parent Shape's visibility so, where a parent's visibility is off, this will be indicated in the UI by dimming the child's eye icon (where it is set to visible).

The children's visibility icons are dimmed because the parent's is set to hidden.

info

Hidden Shapes are not rendered but, where they are connected to other Layers (e.g. as an Input Shape to a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) or [Outline](/docs/nodes/shapes/outline/)), they will be calculated.

Keyframe Shape Visibility

Every Shape also has its **Hidden** attribute available under the **Advanced** tab in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/). This can also be keyframed or connected to hide/show Shapes over time.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > 2.5D
chunks.text: When a [Camera](/docs/nodes/utilities/camera/) is included in the Composition, Shapes with this toggle enabled will be placed in a 2.5D environment.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Audio Playback
chunks.text:
The [Sound Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sound/) Layer includes a toggle to enable/disable audio playback. This also affects whether audio is exported or not.

Keyframe audio playback

Audio playback can be keyframed by using the **Play Audio** attribute under a [Sound Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sound/)'s **Advanced** tab in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Set label colours
chunks.text:
Use the coloured squares to give each Layer a **label** colour. Clicking a square will open a list of predefined colours which can be used to visually categorise Layers for organisational purposes.

Layer colours are also inherited by the Time Editor and Graph Editor.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Tags
chunks.text: Click the label icon to quickly assign [Tags](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/tags/). If tags do not already exist in the Scene, they will be created.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Hierarchy
chunks.text:
A hierarchy is a collection of related Layers arranged in a tree. Parent Layers show their children underneath them with their names and icons slightly indented to the right. Hierarchies can be many layers deep. For example, a child can be the parent to a grandchild, and so on.

A simple hierarchy of Layers.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Hierarchy > Create a hierarchy
chunks.text:
To make **Layer1** a child of **Layer2**, click and drag on **Layer1** and move it so it's over **Layer2**. A box will appear around **Layer2** to indicate that it will become the parent to **Layer1**. On releasing the mouse, **Layer1** will be positioned underneath **Layer2** and indented to the right indicating it is now a child of **Layer2**.

Creating a hierarchy of Layers.

When dragging one Shape onto another Shape, holding `Shift` will reset the child's transform meaning it will 'snap' to its parent's position, rotation and scale.

Alternatively, click **Layer1** to select it then `Cmd/Ctrl` + click **Layer2** to add it to the selection – pressing `Cmd/Ctrl` + `P` will then make **Layer2** the parent of **Layer1**. In the event that more than two Layers are selected, the **last** Layer selected will become the parent to the others.

An arrow disclosure icon will appear to the left of a parent Layer's icon. This be used to expand or collapse the hierarchy which is useful for simplifying your Scene Tree display. Note that collapsing the hierarchy doesn't hide the Layers, it's purely an organisational tool.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Hierarchy > Create a hierarchy
chunks.text:
For 'drawable' Layers like Shapes, Falloffs and Nulls a child Layer also inherits the transformations of its parent Layer. For example, when the parent is moved the child will move with it.

tip

Where a Layer within a collapsed hierarchy is selected in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/), the disclosure icon of its parent will be tinted green and a green vertical line will appear to the right of the row so it can be more easily located within the Scene Tree.

Use the **Edit > Show in Scene Window** command (`Cmd/Ctrl` + `L`) to scroll the Scene Tree to the Layer and expand any hierarchy it may be contained within.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Hierarchy > Remove a Layer from a hierarchy
chunks.text: To unparent a Layer, drag it out of its parent hierarchy into a blank space in the Scene Tree, or between two Layers at a different level, and release the mouse.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Hierarchy > Reorder a hierarchy
chunks.text:
Layers can be moved up/down or in/out of hierarchies. Simply click + drag a Layer (or Layers) up or down in the list of Layers. A white line will appear in between other Layers to indicate where the Layer(s) will be positioned in the list. On releasing the mouse the Layer(s) will be repositioned within the list. Pay attention to the horizontal position of the white line. The line will indent depending on whether the gap between Layers represents the last child Layer within an expanded hierarchy or the position below the collapsed hierarchy.

Reordering a Layer below Layer 4 but not as a child of Layer 3.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Show/hide animated attributes
chunks.text:
Layers with animated attributes show a small dot to the right of the hierarchy arrow icon. Clicking this dot will hide all the animated attributes for the Layer. This can be useful for focussing on organisation and scene hierarchy.

Showing/hiding animated attributes.

tip

A quick way to show and hide the animation of several Layers at once is to first select them, then use the shortcut `Cmd/Ctrl` + `Shift` + `H` to toggle the **Show/Hide Animation** state. This option can also be found in the [Edit](/docs/user-interface/menus/edit-menu/) menu.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Name Layers
chunks.text:
To rename a Layer in Cavalry simply select the row in the Scene Tree and press the `Return` key. This will make the name editable. Once done, either press `Return` again or click out of the box to commit the name change. Pressing `Escape` will stop the editing process without committing the new name.

Multiple Layers can be renamed at the same time. Click a Layer to select it then `Shift` + click another Layer to add it, and any Layers between it, to the selection. Hitting `Return` will switch the last Layer selected to edit mode – anything typed will be applied to all the other selected layers along with a suffix (Name 1, Name 2, Name 3...).

Auto-renaming multiple Layers.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Search
chunks.text:
There is a search bar at the top of the Scene Window above the main hierarchy of Layers. To search simply click in this box and start typing. Layers will then be filtered by name.

Search can also be populated by dragging a Layer into the search field.

Searching Child Layers

Note that a minimum of 3 characters is required when searching for Layers that are hidden because they are children of other Layers. This is to narrow the search and reduce the chance of hierarchies being unexpectedly forced open.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Group Layers
chunks.text: To group a Layer or selection of Layers, simply select a Layer(s) and then press `Cmd/Ctrl` + `G`. The selected Layer(s) will then be parented under a new [Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/group/).

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Select Layers
chunks.text: Layers can be selected by clicking anywhere on their row. Use `Cmd/Ctrl` + click to add or remove Layers from an existing selection. Holding `Shift` when selecting a second Layer will select everything between the two.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Double clicking Layers
chunks.text:
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Action Result|  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Double click a Layer Load the Layer's UI into the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).| `Option/Alt` + double click a Layer Clear the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) before loading the Layer's UI.| `Option/Alt` + `Cmd/Ctrl` + double click a [Composition](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/) Layer Open the Composition. This is the equivalent of clicking the `Open` button on the Composition Layer's row. | | | | | | | |

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > Anatomy of the Scene Tree > Animation Offsets
chunks.text:
Connections can be made to layer additional animation on top of any existing keyframe animation. For example, a [Noise Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/noise/) can be added to some linear animation to give the movement a more natural feel. When picking up a connection from a Layer, an additional input will appear on the row of any Layer with keyframe animation. Drop the connection on this input to create the **Animation Offset**.

When previewing a Layer with a connected **Animation Offset** in the [Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/), the original animation curve will appear ghosted.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > UI > Header
chunks.text:
**Search** - Filter the contents of the Scene Window based on search results.

**Add Layers** - Access a pop up version of the [Add Layers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/add-layers-window/) window to add Layers to a Composition. Use the `Cmd/Ctrl` + `.` shortcut.

**Motion Blur** - Enable Motion Blur for the Composition.

**Presets** - Save and/or apply a [Preset](/docs/user-interface/general/presets/) for the Composition.

**Composition Settings** - Open the [Composition Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/) window.

**Frame/Timecode display** - Set the current frame for the playhead by either entering a value or scrubbing the control. Toggle between a frame or timecode display by clicking the `F` or `T` prefix or `Option/Alt` clicking the input.

chunks.title: Scene Tree
chunks.heading: Scene Tree > Scene Tree > UI > Footer
chunks.text:
**Tags** - Open/close the [Tags](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/tags/) drawer.

**Animation Layer Filter** - Filter the Scene Tree to only show selected layers and their animated attributes. The following hotkeys can be used:

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hotkey Result|  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `U` Any selected layers are filtered and, if any animated attributes are hidden, they are revealed. If there is no selection the entire scene is filtered.|  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `Option/Alt` + `U` Any selected layers are filtered including any children with any animated attributes and, if any animated attributes are hidden, they are revealed.|  |  | | --- | --- | | `Shift` + `Option/Alt` + `U` Any selected layers are filtered including any children and, if any animated attributes are hidden, they are revealed. | | | | | | | |

**Time Editor/Graph Editor switch** - Use this to switch between the Time Editor and Graph Editor.

chunks.title: Composition Settings
chunks.heading: Composition Settings
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Scene Window* Scene Tree* Composition Settings

On this page

chunks.title: Composition Settings
chunks.heading: Composition Settings > Composition Settings > Intro
chunks.text: The Composition Settings window can be used to set the resolution, frame range and other properties of a Composition. It can be opened via the `Composition > Composition Settings...` menu item (`Cmd/Ctrl` + `K`) or via the  button at the top of the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/).

chunks.title: Composition Settings
chunks.heading: Composition Settings > Composition Settings > UI
chunks.text:
**Resolution** - Set the width and height of your composition in pixels. Use the drop down above to select some common presets.

**Frame Range** - Set the frame numbers for the start and end of the Composition.

**Playback Range** - Set the start and end frame numbers used during playback. This value can also be set using the bookends (bars with green ends) at the top of the [Time Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/).

**Time** - Shows the current frame. It does not accept inputs but can be connected to other attributes although [Frame](/docs/nodes/behaviours/frame/) is often a better solution here.

**Frame Rate** - Set the frames per second the composition will playback at.

**Background** - Set the Composition's background color using hex or rgb values (note - only rgb values can be animated).

tip

Set the background color by dragging a swatch from the [Color Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/) into an empty part of the Viewport.

info

chunks.title: Composition Settings
chunks.heading: Composition Settings > Composition Settings > UI
chunks.text:
Compositions created via the contextual menu (right click) within the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) are set to have a **Background Alpha** of 0.

**Playback Step** - Play every nth frame.

**Motion Blur** - Enable/disable [Motion Blur](/docs/nodes/general/motion-blur/).

**Shutter Angle** - Set the angle of the shutter. The default of 180° will result in a 'filmic look'. That is, 50% of your frame rate.

**Motion Blur Centre** - Affects whether the blur is backward or forward of the current frame. The default of 0 will centre it on the frame (the motion blur will be even in both directions of travel).

**Blur Align** - Adjust the position the motion blur samples are taken from relative to the **Motion Blur Centre**. This can be useful for controlling the level of motion blur at the beginning/end of an animation. For example, setting the **Blur Align** to `-100` will result in no motion blur if the Shape is static on the previous frame.

**Motion Blur Samples** - Determine how many times the motion blur is sampled. A higher number will result in a smoother blur but also comes with a performance penalty.

chunks.title: Composition Settings
chunks.heading: Composition Settings > Composition Settings > UI
chunks.text:
**Linear Gamma** - Enable a linear color space.

**Keyfrane Layer** - The current active [Keyframe Layer](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/keyframe-layers/).

**Referenceable** - When checked, the Composition will appear in the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) when the Scene is imported as a [Reference](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/referencing/).

info

These settings can also be accessed by dragging a Composition from the [Assets Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/assets-window/) into the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Clips
chunks.text:
As the cursor hovers over the end of a clip it will highlight. Click + drag either end of a Shape's clip to adjust the frames that appear in the Viewport. A [Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/) will be visible when the playhead is over part of the clip. For [Behaviours](/docs/nodes/behaviours/), the clip represents when it will be enabled.

The clip has no effect for [Utilities](/docs/nodes/utilities/), [Filters](/docs/nodes/effects/) or [Shaders](/docs/nodes/effects/). These Layers will appear as a chevron clip. [Utilities](/docs/nodes/utilities/) that draw in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) like [Falloffs](/docs/nodes/utilities/falloff/) and [Nulls](/docs/nodes/utilities/null/) and the [Sound Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sound/) are the exception to this rule. They behave in the same way Shapes do.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Clips > Setting start/end points
chunks.text:
It's possible to adjust the start/end points of multiple Layers at the same time by holding down `Option/Alt` as you hover over an end point. The ends of any Layers that share a common in/out point will highlight and will all move when click + dragging. This is also true where one Layer's **in point** is on the same frame as another's **out point**.

Click and drag the bar between the in and out points to move the entire Clip.

Editing Clips.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Clips > Setting start/end points > Hotkeys
chunks.text:
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shortcut Description|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `[` Move the selected Clip's in points to the current frame.|  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `]` Move the selected Clip's out points to the current frame.|  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `Option/Alt` + `[` Trim the selected Clip's in points to the current frame.|  |  | | --- | --- | | `Option/Alt` + `]` Trim the selected Clip's out points to the current frame. | | | | | | | | | |

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Clips > Split/Merge Clips
chunks.text:
Further options for supported Clips can be accessed by right clicking on a Layer and choosing **Clips > ...** :

* **Split Clip** - Split a Clip at the current frame. This splits the clip into two meaning a Layer can be turned on/off in the Viewport several times.
* **Merge Clip** - Where Clips have been split, combine the Clips back into a single Clip.
* **Add Clip to Start** - If the start of a Clip is set after frame 0, add a section that starts at frame 0 and ends at the start of the existing clip.
* **Add Clip to End** - If the end of a Clip is set before the last frame, add a section that starts at the at the end of the existing clip and ends at the last frame of the Composition.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Clips > Show Names
chunks.text:
Right click anywhere in the Time Editor and select an option under the **Show Names** item to display the name of an Layer on its Clip.

* **None** - Do not show the layer names.
* **Left** - Show the layer names aligned to the left hand edge of Clips.
* **Right** - Show the layer names aligned to the right hand edge of Clips.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Keyframes > Creating Keyframes
chunks.text:
Once you have set a [Keyframe](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/control-rows/control-rows-interaction/#setting-keyframes) via the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/) you are able to set further Keyframes in the **Time Editor**. To do so, either:

* Move the playhead and scrub the Attribute's value.
* Move the playhead and click the Keyframe icon in the Attribute control.
* Select a Keyframe or Keybar and then right click > Add Keyframe.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Keyframes > Editing Keyframes
chunks.text:
To edit a Keyframe you can either:

* Move the playhead to the same frame as an existing Keyframe and scrub or edit the attribute's value.
* Double click a Keyframe and scrub or edit the attribute's value via the pop up control. Holding `Option/Alt` when double clicking will also move the playhead to that Keyframe.

Editing a Keyframe's value inline.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Keyframes > Moving Keyframes
chunks.text:
To move a Keyframe simply click and drag.

To move a selection of Keyframes either `Cmd/Ctrl` + click or marquee select multiple Keyframes and drag to move. You can also select and move Keyframes from multiple attributes and/or Layers.

Select and move Keyframes.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Keyframes > Deleting Keyframes
chunks.text:
To remove a Keyframe or Keyframes either:

* Select a Keyframe or Keyframes and hit the `Delete` key.
* Select a Keyframe or Keyframes and **right click > Delete Keyframe(s)**.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Keyframes > Copying Keyframes
chunks.text:
To copy a Keyframe, select one and choose **Edit > Copy Keyframe** (`Cmd/Ctrl` + `C`) then move the playhead and chose **Edit > Paste** (`Cmd/Ctrl` + `V`). You can do the same with multiple Keyframes on the same attribute.

You can also copy keyframe data from one Layer to another. If the keyframe data you are copying is from an attribute that already exists on the Layer you are pasting to, then those keys will be added to that attribute. If the attribute does not exist, it will be added along with the keyframe data.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Keyframes > Duplicating Keyframes
