chunks.text: To duplicate Keyframes, select them and then `Option/Alt` + click + drag one of the selection. Copies of the Keyframes will be created on mouse release. This action can be performed across multiple attributes.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Keyframes > Coloring Keyframes
chunks.text: To change the color of a Keyframe select a Keyframe or Keyframes and **right click > Set Color > choose your color**. This can be useful for highlighting key moments in your animation.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Keyframes > Copying easing
chunks.text:
Copying the easing of Keyframes to other Keyframes can be achieved via the right click menu.

* Select a Keyframe or Keyframes on the same attribute.
* Right click and choose > **Copy Easing**.
* Select some different Keyframes.
* Paste (`Cmd/Ctrl` + `V`)

Where a selection does not match – for example, copying 3 Keyframes and pasting them onto 2 Keyframes – Cavalry will copy Keyframe1 to Keyframe1, Keyframe2 to Keyframe2 and ignore Keyframe3.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Keybars
chunks.text:
Keybars are lines that connect Keyframe pairs and can be used to move entire animation curves without the need to select a range of Keyframes.

A Keybar appears as a **solid line** when between two Keyframes of different values. If a Keybar connects two keys of the same value it will appear as **dashed line**. This is designed to help identify areas where Layers remain static or unchanged.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Keybars > Moving Keybars
chunks.text:
To move an entire Keybar simply click and drag one.

Moving whole and/or part Keybars.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Selection
chunks.text:
When marquee selecting in the **Time Editor** the following selection logic applies.

* If a Keyframe exists within a selection, only select **Keyframes**.
* If no Keyframes exist within a selection, select the **Keybars**.

Hold `Option/Alt` when using marquee selection to filter out any Keyframes or Keybars to ensure only Clips are selected.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Tools > Keyframe Layers
chunks.text: **Keyframe Layer** - See [Keyframe Layers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/keyframe-layers/).

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Tools > Align
chunks.text:
Align selected keys to each other. This works in the same way [aligning shapes](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/align-window/) does. Imagine a rectangle bordering each 'group' of selected keys on each attribute and then aligning those rectangles to each other.

* **Left** - Align keys to the key nearest to the beginning (left) of your timeline.
* **Centre** - Centrally align keys.
* **Right** - Align keys to the key nearest to the end (right) of your timeline.

Aligning key selection to the left.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Tools > Transform tool
chunks.text: The Transform tool can be used to move and scale selections of keys. With the tool active, a green area will appear around any selected Keyframes. Click + drag the middle of the green area to move the selection or click + drag either end of the green area to scale the Keyframes.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Tools > Snapping Settings
chunks.text:
Snap Keyframes and Clip ends to other Keyframes, Clips and Time Markers.

**Options:**

* **Enable Snapping** - Enable/disable snapping.
* **Snapping Threshold** - Set the distance (in screen pixels) within which snapping will happen.
* **Keyframes** - Enable/ disable snapping to Keyframes.
* **Clips** - Enable/ disable snapping to the ends of Clips.
* **Time Markers** - Enable/ disable snapping to Time Markers.

Move the playhead to Keyframes

Position the playhead at the next Keyframe by using the `Option/Alt` + `Cmd/Ctrl` + `⬅︎`/`⮕` arrow hotkeys. Keyframes can also be filtered by selecting Layers, Attributes or selections of Keyframes. For example, if the **position.x** Attribute is selected, Keyframes on other attributes will be ignored.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Tools > Pacing Markers
chunks.text:
Add guides to the **Time Editor** to indicate seconds or audio beats. Toggle the button to enable/disable them or use the arrow to open a disclosure window containing the following options:

**Mode** - Select a mode:

* **Seconds** - Add Pace Markers on each second.
* **Beats per Minute** - Add Pace Markers based on a **BPM**.

**Divisions** - When **Mode** is set to **Seconds**, determine how many sub-steps to add between seconds.

**Beats per Minute** - When **Mode** is set to **Beats per Minute**, set the **BPM** for the audio track. Grey guides represent **Beats** with the blue guides marking the **Bars**.

**Offset** - When **Mode** is set to **Beats per Minute**, move the markers forward or backward in time.

**Beats per Bar** - When **Mode** is set to **Beats per Minute**, set the number of beats in each bar.

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Tools > Zoom
chunks.text: Drag the slider to zoom in/out of the window or click the magnifying glass icons at either end of the slider. Alternatively, use the following keyboard shortcuts:

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Tools > Zoom

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Tools > Zoom

chunks.title: Time Editor
chunks.heading: Time Editor > Time Editor > Magic Easing
chunks.text:
Apply mathematical interpolation between Keyframes.

1. Select one or more Keyframes.
2. Right click > Magic Easing.
3. Choose an option.

It's possible to add custom expressions for Magic Easing by choosing **Edit Custom Expression...** from the options. Some examples:

```
1 - pow(1 - x, 5)
```

```
x * x * x * x * x
```

```
-(cos(PI * x) - 1) / 2
```

```
var c1 := 1.70158;

var c2 := c1 * 1.525;

x < 0.5

? (pow(2 * x, 2) * ((c2 + 1) * 2 * x - c2)) / 2

: (pow(2 * x - 2, 2) * ((c2 + 1) * (x * 2 - 2) + c2) + 2) / 2;
```

tip

You can bake the animation to Keyframes using the **Bake Keyframe Animation** command in the [Animation](/docs/user-interface/menus/animation-menu/) menu.

info

**Note** - Cavalry follows the forthcoming Web Animation standard for easing which may be less familiar to **After Effects** users. This is not an official page but see [here](https://easings.net/) for some nice examples. The W3C Candidate Recommendations can be seen [here](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-easing-1/).

chunks.title: Time Markers
chunks.heading: Time Markers
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Scene Window* Time Markers

On this page

chunks.title: Time Markers
chunks.heading: Time Markers > Time Markers > Intro
chunks.text: Time Markers can be used to reference significant moments along the Timeline. They can also be connected to Keyframes and Clip Ends meaning it's possible to link them together.

chunks.title: Time Markers
chunks.heading: Time Markers > Time Markers > UI
chunks.text:
To **add** a **Time Marker** either:

* Right click in the timeline and choose **Add Time Marker** or;
* Position the playhead and use the hotkeys `Cmd/Ctrl` + `*` or `Shift` + `Cmd/Ctrl` + `8`.

To **select** a **Time Marker** click one or hold `Option/Alt` to marquee select several Time Markers.

To **move** a **Time Marker** click and drag one.

To move multiple **Time Markers**, marquee select several **Time Markers** and then click and drag one of the selected Time Markers.

Double click a Time Marker to open its settings:

chunks.title: Time Markers
chunks.heading: Time Markers > Time Markers > UI
chunks.text:
* **Label** - Enter a description of the Time Marker. If a label is entered, it will appear depending on the **Timeline Draw** or **Pre-Composition Draw** settings (below).
* **Color** - Select a color from the current [Label Palette](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/color-window/) for the Time Marker.
* **Locked** - When checked, moving the Time Marker is prevented.
* **Use Relative Placement** - When checked, a Time Marker is positioned relative to the duration of the Composition.
* **Absolute Time** - Set a frame number for the Time Marker.
* **Relative Time** - Set a value between 0 and 1 where 0 = the start of the Composition and 1 = the end of the Composition.
* **Display Color Region** - When checked, a region of the Time/Graph Editor is highlighted.
* **Color Region** - Set the number of frames before and after Time Marker to show the color region.
* **Timeline Draw** - Choose how a Time Marker's label will appear in the Timeline:
  + **Show Label on Rollover** - Only show a label when hovering the cursor over a Time Marker.
  + **Always show Label** - Show the label at all times.
* **Pre-Composition Draw** - Choose how a Time Marker's label will appear when its paren

chunks.title: Time Markers
chunks.heading: Time Markers > Time Markers > UI
chunks.text:
t Composition is used within another Composition:
  + **Show Label on Rollover** - Only show a label when hovering the cursor over a Time Marker.
  + **Always show Label** - Show the label at all times.

chunks.title: Time Markers
chunks.heading: Time Markers > Time Markers > UI
chunks.text:
A Time Marker's Color Region in a Composition.

The same Time Marker's Color Region within a Pre-Composition.

chunks.title: Time Markers
chunks.heading: Time Markers > Time Markers > UI > Connections
chunks.text:
Connect a **Time Marker** to a **Keyframe** or the ends of a **Clip** by either:

* Hovering over a **Time Marker** and using the **Connection Anchor**.
* Double clicking a **Time Marker** to open its settings and use the **Connection Anchor** at the top.

Once connected, moving a Time Marker will also move the Keyframe or Clip end.

Connect to multiple keyframes at the same time by selecting several keyframes and dragging a connection from a Time Marker to one of the selected keyframes.

To remove a connection - select a **Clip** (Layer) or **Keyframe** and then `right click > Time Markers > Disconnect [option]`

Delete a Time Marker by selecting one (or more) and hitting the delete key. Right click anywhere in the Timeline and select 'Delete All Markers' to clear the Timeline.

chunks.title: Time Markers
chunks.heading: Time Markers > Time Markers > Shortcuts
chunks.text:
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hotkey Command|  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `&#60` Move the playhead to the previous Time Marker.|  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `&#62` Move the playhead to the next Time Marker.|  |  | | --- | --- | | `1`, `2`, `3`...`9` Move the playhead to the first, second, third... Time Marker. | | | | | | | |

info

**Absolute** Time Markers will always snap to exact frames. **Relative** Time Markers will not.

chunks.title: Timeline
chunks.heading: Timeline > Timeline > Intro
chunks.text: The **Timeline** is the area above the [Time Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-editor/) or [Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/) which includes the playhead and also houses [Time Markers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-markers/).

chunks.title: Timeline
chunks.heading: Timeline > Timeline > Setting the current frame
chunks.text:
* Click + drag the teal playhead to scrub through the Timeline.
* Click anywhere in the Timeline to move the playhead to that frame.

chunks.title: Timeline
chunks.heading: Timeline > Timeline > Playback Range
chunks.text: Click + drag the teal bookends to set the beginning and end frames for the **Playback Range**. Click and drag the bar between the start and end points to move the entire **Playback Range**.

chunks.title: Timeline
chunks.heading: Timeline > Timeline > Time Markers
chunks.text: [Time Markers](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-markers/) can be used to reference significant moments along the timeline and to group Keyframes and Clip ends. Right click in the Timeline to add one.

chunks.title: Timeline
chunks.heading: Timeline > Timeline > Shortcuts
chunks.text:
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hotkey Command|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `B` Set the Playback Range's beginning.|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `N` Set the Playback Range's end.|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `Cmd/Ctrl` + `⬅︎`/`⮕` Nudge 1 frame increments backwards/forwards in time.|  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `Shift` + `Cmd/Ctrl` + `⬅︎`/`⮕` Nudge 5 frame increments backwards/forwards in time.|  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `Shift` + drag the playhead Snap to every 10th frame (0, 10, 20 etc) or to a [Time Marker](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/time-markers/)| `Option/Alt` + `Cmd/Ctrl` + `⬅︎`/`⮕` Position the playhead at the next keyframe. Selecting Layers, Attributes or keyframes will filter the results. | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

tip

`Hold q + drag` to scrub the **Timeline** from any window.

chunks.title: Timeline
chunks.heading: Timeline > Timeline > Shortcuts
chunks.text:
`Option/Alt` + `Cmd/Ctrl` + drag can be used to drag the playhead with the cursor in the Time Editor.

tip

Enable **Update the UI during playback** in the [Viewport Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#viewport-settings) to see the playhead animate during playback.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Intro
chunks.text: The Shelf is located at the top of the default Workspace and contains shortcut buttons for setting up quick actions that can be used to speed up common workflows.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Demo Scenes
chunks.text: Select a Scene to add to the current Composition as an example to inspire or learn from. Not all examples are set up to animate but holding `Cmd/Ctrl` when selecting a menu item will automatically start playback. These can also be accessed via the [Create](/docs/user-interface/menus/create-menu/) menu.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Try Pro / Pro Features
chunks.text: This will launch a window containing simple examples that use the **Professional** features for evaluation. This button will appear as 'Try Pro' for Starter licences and 'Pro Features' for Professional licences. Note that **Starter** users will be switched into 'Restricted Mode' which prevents saving and rendering – deleting the Pro Layer(s) will restore saving and rendering.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Duplicator
chunks.text: Create a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/) and add any selected Shapes to its **Input Shapes** attribute.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Extrude
chunks.text: Create an [Extrude](/docs/nodes/shapes/extrude/) Shape and add any selected Shapes to its **Input Shapes** attribute.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Forge Dynamics
chunks.text: Create an [Forge Dynamics](/docs/nodes/shapes/forge-dynamics/forge-dynamics-shape/) Shape and add any selected Shapes to its **Bodies** attribute.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Particles
chunks.text: Create an [Particle Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/particle-shape/) Shape and [Particle Emitter](/docs/nodes/utilities/particle-emitter/).

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Auto-Animate
chunks.text: Add an [Auto-Animate](/docs/nodes/behaviours/auto-animate/) Behaviour to the Composition and connect it to the **Deformers** attribute of any selected Shapes.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Align
chunks.text: Add an [Align Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/align/) to the Composition and connect it to the **Deformers** attribute of any selected Shapes.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Animation Control
chunks.text: Add an [Animation Control](/docs/nodes/utilities/animation-control/) to the Composition.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Rubber Hose
chunks.text: Create a default [Rubber Hose Limb](/docs/nodes/behaviours/rubber-hose-limb/). If a Shape is selected the Rubber Hose will be connected to its **Deformers** attribute.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Cel Animation
chunks.text: Create a [Cel Animation Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/cel-animation-shape/) and enable the [Pencil tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pencil-tool/) (unless the [Pen tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/pen-tool/) is already active).

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Text along a Path
chunks.text: With a [Text Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) and a Shape selected, clicking the **Text along a Path** button will connect the **Path** to the Text Shape's **Text Path** attribute placing the Text along the Path. It will also connect the Text Shape's **Path Travel** to the Composition's **Time** meaning that it will move along the Path in playback. Remove this connection to customise the animation.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Scheduling Group - Schedule
chunks.text: Add the selected Shapes to a [Scheduling Group](/docs/nodes/utilities/scheduling-group/) and check the **Sequence** attribute.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Scheduling Group - Stagger
chunks.text: Add the selected Shapes to a [Scheduling Group](/docs/nodes/utilities/scheduling-group/), add a [Stagger](/docs/nodes/behaviours/stagger/) Behaviour and connect it to the Scheduling Group's **Child Offset**.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Layout Group - Horizontal
chunks.text: Add the selected Shapes to a [Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layout-group/) with its **Direction** attribute set to **Horizontal**.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Layout Group - Vertical
chunks.text: Add the selected Shapes to a [Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layout-group/) with its **Direction** attribute set to **Vertical**.

chunks.title: Shelf
chunks.heading: Shelf > Shelf > Buttons > Layout Group - Grid
chunks.text: Add the selected Shapes to a [Grid Layout Row](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-row/) embedded within a [Grid Layout Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/grid-layout-group/).

chunks.title: Shortcut Manager
chunks.heading: Shortcut Manager > Shortcut Manager > UI
chunks.text:
Enter the cursor into the input field and type the shortcut to use for the associated command. If a shortcut is already in use, the input field will flash red and the associated command will be listed in the [Message Bar](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/message-bar/).

Shortcuts are organised into tabs.

Each tab can be filtered by using the search bar at the top of the window.

Scripts

Shortcuts can also be assigned to third-party [scripts](/docs/tech-info/scripting/scripting-getting-started/).

warning

Multiple shortcuts for a single command are not supported.

chunks.title: Tag Window
chunks.heading: Tag Window > Tag Window
chunks.text:
Experimental Feature

This is an experimental feature. To enable, check **Enable Experimental Features** in [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/). Experimental features are only available as part of a **Professional** licence.

chunks.title: Tag Window
chunks.heading: Tag Window > Tag Window > Intro
chunks.text: Tags can be assigned to layers to provide a way to quickly make selections or filter the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) and/ or [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/). Tags can also be nested for extra control and clarity.

chunks.title: Tag Window
chunks.heading: Tag Window > Tag Window > UI
chunks.text:
**Mode** - The result of selecting a tag.

* **Select** - Select all layers assigned with the selected tag(s).
* **Filter Scene Window** - Show only layers assigned with the selected tag(s) in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).
* **Filter Viewport** - Show only layers assigned with the selected tag(s) in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).
* **Filter Both** - Show only layers with the assigned tag(s) in both the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) and the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/).

**Clear Tag Selection (button)** - Deselect all selected tags.

**Add Tag (button)** - Add a new tag.

chunks.title: Tag Window
chunks.heading: Tag Window > Tag Window > Window
chunks.text:
The tag window contains 3 types of tags:

* **Quicklist** - The quicklist can be thought of as a temporary tag. Its state is not saved with a scene.
* **System Tags** - Auto-assigned tags based on **Label Color** and **Type**.
* **User Tags** - Custom Tags created by a user.

chunks.title: Tag Window
chunks.heading: Tag Window > Tag Window > Managing Tags > Adding/ Removing Tags
chunks.text:
Add tags by either:

* Clicking the `+` button at the top of the **Tag Window** then type the name of your tag and hit **Return/Enter**.
* Click `Cmd/Ctrl` + `Shift` + `T` in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) to bring up the **Add Tag** window. Type the name of a tag and hit `Return`. If you check **Assign Tag to Selection** any selected layers will also be assigned with the new tag.

info

A quick way to **Assign Tag to Selection** is to hold `Option/Alt` as you hit **Return/Enter**. This will assign that tag to any selected Layers regardless of whether the checkbox is enabled or not.

Remove tags by either:

* Selecting a tag and hitting the **Delete** key.
* Right click on a tag and choose **Delete Tag** from the contextual menu.

Deleting a tag will also un-assign it from any Layers.

chunks.title: Tag Window
chunks.heading: Tag Window > Tag Window > Managing Tags > Assigning/ Un-assigning Tags
chunks.text:
Assign tags by either:

* Dragging and dropping a Layer(s) from the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) onto a tag.
* Check the **Assign Tag to Selection** option as a Tag is added.
* Click the `tag/label` icon in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) then type the name of a tag and hit **Return/Enter**.

Un-assign tags by either:

* Right click on an Layer in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/) and select **Remove Tag** from the contextual menu.
* Right click on a tag in the **Tag Window** and then select **Clear Tag**. Note - this will remove a tag from **all** Layers.

chunks.title: Tag Window
chunks.heading: Tag Window > Tag Window > Managing Tags > Activating Tags
chunks.text:
Simply select a tag in the Tag Window to activate it. You can use `Cmd/Ctrl` or `Shift` to select and/or deselect multiple tags.

info

Holding `Option/Alt` as you drag Layers on to tags to assign them will also activate that tag on mouse up.

chunks.title: Tag Window
chunks.heading: Tag Window > Tag Window > Managing Tags > Quicklist
chunks.text:
The Quicklist can be thought of as a temporary tag. It can be used as a way to quickly solo a selection of Layers. Its contents are only saved during a session and not saved with your scene.

The Quicklist can be converted into a tag by right clicking anywhere in the **Tag Window** and choosing the **Convert Quicklist to Tag** option in the contextual menu.

chunks.title: Tag Window
chunks.heading: Tag Window > Tag Window > Managing Tags > Nested Tags
chunks.text:
Relationships between Tags can be crated by nesting them on creation. To do this type a `/` (Forward Slash) between tags. e.g. `Character/Body` will create two tags called **Character** and **Body** with **Body** as a child of **Character**. Selecting **Character** will select all Layers with both the **Character and Body** tags assigned to them whereas selecting **Body** will only select the Layers with **Body** assigned to them.

tip

When setting up a **Character** a hierarchy as follows may be created:

* Character
  + Head
    - Hair
    - Ears
    - Eyes
    - Nose
    - Mouth
  + Body
    - Arms
      * Hands
    - Legs
      * Feet

Selecting **Head** would then show the entire head including the hair, ears, eyes, nose and mouth. Be as granular as needed.

If a tag already exists then a child can be added to it by typing `<yourExistingTag>/<yourNewTag>`

chunks.title: Tool Settings
chunks.heading: Tool Settings > Tool Settings > Intro
chunks.text:
The tool settings window contains context specific options depending on the current tool in use. It is positioned at the top left of the default Workspace.

Viewport Tool Help

Helpful hints for shortcuts/hotkey for each tool can be overlaid in the Viewport by enabling **Viewport Tool Help** in the [Viewport Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#viewport-settings).

Layer Tools

Note that many Layers have bespoke **Layer Tools**. When selected, certain Layers will display purple UI elements which can be used to adjust their settings directly in the Viewport. In order for these tools to appear, **Layer Tools** must be enabled in the [Viewport Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#viewport-settings).

Note that Layer Tools are not available when a Shape is the parent of another Shape.

chunks.title: Tool Settings
chunks.heading: Tool Settings > Tool Settings > Tools > Select
chunks.text:
**Snap Angle** - Set an angle for Shapes to snap to when being rotated with the `Shift` key held.

**Manipulator** - When checked, a '3d-like' manipulator is drawn in the Viewport when selecting Shapes and certain other features like Lattice points.

* **Transform** - Click and drag the centre of the manipulator to freeform move the selection or use the red and green arrows to axis snap.
* **Rotation** - Click and drag the circle around the manipulator to rotate the selection.
* **Scale** - Click and drag the red and green squares to scale the selection along the X or Y axis. Hold `Shift` to affect both axis at the same time.
* **World/Local Transform** - Click the black diamond on the top left of the manipulator to toggle between world and local space.

**Transform mode** - with multiple selections determine whether the Transform tool should act on the selection as a group or as individual Shapes:

* **Group** - Rotate/Scale all selected Shapes together.
* **Individual** - Rotate/Scale all selected Shapes from each layers individual pivot point.

Corner Radius

Hold `Option/Alt` to adjust individual corner radii for a Rectangle.

chunks.title: Tool Settings
chunks.heading: Tool Settings > Tool Settings > Tools > Edit Shape
chunks.text:
**Snap Angle** - Set an angle for Shapes to snap to when being rotated with the `Shift` key held.

**Tooltips** - When checked, information will be displayed in the Viewport when hovering the cursor over a Shape's points.

**Transform Tool** - When checked, selected points can be rotated or scaled as a group.

info

When the Transform tool is enabled, any bézier handles are hidden and it is not possible to convert points from corner to bézier, to split a path or to use the 'bézier moulding' feature.

**Close Distance** - Set the distance within which a selected point will merge with another point when dropped near it. Note - this value is independent of the Viewport scale. This distance is indicated in the Viewport when the cursor is positioned within this distance of the first point.

**Curve Ghosting** - When checked a 'ghost' of the path will appear when editing points as a reference.

chunks.title: Tool Settings
chunks.heading: Tool Settings > Tool Settings > Tools > Pen
chunks.text:
**Snap Angle** - Set an angle for Shapes to snap to when being rotated with the `Shift` key held.

**Stroke Width** - Set the width of the Stroke.

**Cap Style** - Set the appearance of caps (each end of the stroke) for open paths.

* **Flat** - A flat end that terminates at the end point.
* **Round** - A hemispherical end with the end point at its centre.
* **Projecting** - A flat end that projects half the Width beyond the end point.

**Close Distance** - If the last point of a Shape is drawn within this value of the start point, a closed path will be created. Note - this value is independent of the Viewport scale. This distance is indicated in the Viewport when the cursor is positioned within this distance of the first point.

chunks.title: Tool Settings
chunks.heading: Tool Settings > Tool Settings > Tools > Pencil
chunks.text:
**Stroke Width** - Set the width of the Stroke.

**Cap Style** - Set the appearance of caps (each end of the stroke) for open paths.

* **Flat** - A flat end that terminates at the end point.
* **Round** - A hemispherical end with the end point at its centre.
* **Projecting** - A flat end that projects half the Width beyond the end point.

**Accuracy** - Determine how closely your resulting shape resembles your cursor movements. A higher setting will result in a more accurate shape but will create more points.

**Stabiliser** - When checked, the path will be 'stabilised' as it is drawn. This can be useful for drawing smoother curves with less points.

**Stability Radius** - Determine the level of stability. A higher value will create longer, smoother curves.

chunks.title: Tool Settings
chunks.heading: Tool Settings > Tool Settings > Tools > Pencil
chunks.text: **Close Distance** - If the last point of a Shape is drawn within this value of the start point, a closed path will be created. When closing a path, anything within the Close Distance is resampled so a smooth join can be created. This means that the start of the path will also be updated. Note - this value is independent of the Viewport scale. This distance is indicated in the Viewport when the cursor is positioned within this distance of the first point.

chunks.title: Tool Settings
chunks.heading: Tool Settings > Tool Settings > Tools > Line
chunks.text:
**Stroke Width** - Set the width of the Stroke.

**Cap Style** - Set the appearance of caps (each end of the stroke) for open paths.

* **Flat** - A flat end that terminates at the end point.
* **Round** - A hemispherical end with the end point at its centre.
* **Projecting** - A flat end that projects half the Width beyond the end point.

chunks.title: Tool Settings
chunks.heading: Tool Settings > Tool Settings > Tools > Mesh
chunks.text:
**Soft Selection** - When checked, mesh vertices can be selected within a range of the cursor. The strength of the selection falls off away from the centre.

**Soft Selection Size** - Set the **Soft Selection**'s radius.

chunks.title: Tool Settings
chunks.heading: Tool Settings > Tool Settings > Tools > Tracking
chunks.text:
* **Edge Snap** - Intelligently 'snap' to the borders of the screen rather than tracking points inside it.
  + Strengths:
    - A very fast track, especially for long takes.
    - If the screen has clearly defined, high-contrast edges against its background.
    - When the content on the screen is uniform, blurry, animated in some way, or lacks trackable features.
    - When an object (like a hand or prop) briefly moves in front of the screen. This tracker is better at 're-finding' the screen after it's been blocked.
  + Weaknesses:
    - Requires well-defined screen borders. It may fail if the edges are blurry, low-contrast, or blend in with the background.
* **Balanced** - Provides a good combination of speed and accuracy for most common tracking situations. It works by tracking a dense cloud of feature points inside the screen.
  + Strengths:
    - Good for the majority of your tracking tasks.
    - When the screen has plenty of texture or unique visual details e.g tracking markers.
    - When the camera motion is smooth to moderately fast.
  + Weaknesses:
    - May lose track if a large portion of the screen is blocked (e.g. by a hand or another object).
    - Can struggle with

chunks.title: Tool Settings
chunks.heading: Tool Settings > Tool Settings > Tools > Tracking
chunks.text:
screens that have very little texture, motion blur, or large reflections.
* **Robust** - This tracker is designed to handle interruptions. It works by remembering a 'keyframe' of the screen's features and trying to find them again in the current frame. This makes it slower but more resilient.
  + Strengths:
    - When an object (like a hand or prop) briefly moves in front of the screen. This tracker is better at 're-finding' the screen after it's been blocked.
    - When the track is drifting due to fast motion or motion blur.
  + Weaknesses:
    - Slower than the **Balanced** preset.
    - It may still fail if the obstruction is too large or lasts for too long.

chunks.title: Tool Settings
chunks.heading: Tool Settings > Tool Settings > Tools > Tracking
chunks.text:
**Supervised** - When checked, tracking will stop if the quality degrades too much enabling markers to be manually repositioned before continuing the track. This is only available with the **Balanced** and **Robust** Presets.

**Show Grid** - When checked, a preview of the tracked plane is drawn in the Viewport.

**Track Backwards** - With tracking markers placed, click this to analyse the footage and create the tracking data by moving backwards in time.

**Track Forwards** - With tracking markers placed, click this to analyse the footage and create the tracking data by moving forwards in time.

**Create a Keyframe** - Refine tracking data by setting keyframes for markers to override any auto-tracking data. This is useful for correcting any individual frames that may deviate too far or to manage tracks where gaps between sections are required. Keyframes are represented by a green frame just below the [Timeline](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/timeline/).

chunks.title: Tool Settings
chunks.heading: Tool Settings > Tool Settings > Tools > Tracking
chunks.text:
**Apply** - Select a Shape and choose the relevant data to create and connect a [Corner Pin](/docs/nodes/shapes/corner-pin/) Shape to the selected Shape and assign the tracking data to each of the Corner Pin's Nulls.

**Clear** - Remove any tracking data.

chunks.title: Tool Settings
chunks.heading: Tool Settings > Tool Settings > Tools > Primitives
chunks.text:
The following settings will appear for the following tools:

* [Rectangle](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/rectangle-tool/)
* [Ellipse](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/ellipse-tool/)
* [Polygon](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/polygon-tool/)
* [Star](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/star-tool/)
* [Arc](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/arc-tool/)
* [Super Ellipse](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/super-ellipse-tool/)
* [Cogwheel](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/cogwheel-tool/)
* [Arrow](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/arrow-tool/)
* [Capsule](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/capsule-tool/)

**Create Editable Primitives** - When checked, creating any primitive Shapes will create an [Editable Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/editable-shape/).

Toolbar

When **Create Editable Primitives** is checked, a small `E` is added to the icons for each of the primitive tools within the Toolbar.

**Tool Help** - When checked, helpful hints will be overlaid in the bottom left corner of the Viewport.

**Draw in 2.5D** - When checked, **2.5D** will be enabled for the Layer on creation meaning Shapes can be drawn in 2.5D when a Camera is active.

chunks.title: Toolbar
chunks.heading: Toolbar > Toolbar
chunks.text:
A vertical window that sits to the left of the Viewport in the default Workspace containing the Viewport [Tools](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/).

The icons for the primitive tools (Rectangle, Ellipse etc) will inherit a slightly different appearance depending on other settings.

chunks.title: Toolbar
chunks.heading: Toolbar > Toolbar > Create Editable Primitives
chunks.text:
When **Create Editable Primitives** is enabled, a small `E` is added to the icons for each of the primitive tools within the Toolbar.

This setting is accessible from either the [Shape menu](/docs/user-interface/menus/shape-menu/) or from any of the Primitive tool's [settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/tool-settings/).

chunks.title: Toolbar
chunks.heading: Toolbar > Toolbar > Quick Mask
chunks.text: By double clicking on the Pen, Pencil or any Primitive Tool its Toolbar icon will tint yellow to indicate the tool is in 'Quick Mask' mode. Drawing in this mode will create a new Shape which will be used as a **Clipping Mask** to any selected Shape.

chunks.title: Upload Preset Manager
chunks.heading: Upload Preset Manager > Upload Preset Manager > Intro
chunks.text: Create and edit presets which can then be selected in the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/)'s **Advanced** tab in order to upload images/videos as part of the render process.

chunks.title: Upload Preset Manager
chunks.heading: Upload Preset Manager > Upload Preset Manager > UI
chunks.text:
**Preset** - Select an existing preset to edit. Click the `+` icon to create a new preset or click the trash icon to delete the currently selected preset.

**Preset Name** - Give the preset a name. This is the name that will appear in the Render Manager's **Upload Preset** dropdown attribute.

**URL** - Enter the base URL.

**Path** - Enter the URL's endpoint.

**Automatic MIME Types** - Automatically detect and set the content type.

**Authentication Type** - Select an authentication method:

* **Basic** - Manually add authentication **Header**(s).
* **Bearer** - Authentication requires a Bearer Token or API key. With this option selected, add the **Token** below.
* **None** - No authentication **Header**(s) required.

**Token** - Enter a password/token/key.

**Headers** - Enter any required header information as key-value pairs. Use the `+` button to add additional headers.

tip

After adding a preset, the [Render Manager](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/render-manager/) must be closed and reopened for the new **Upload Preset** to appear.

info

The [web3.storage](https://web3.storage/) is pre-configured and only allows editing of the **Token**.

caution

chunks.title: Upload Preset Manager
chunks.heading: Upload Preset Manager > Upload Preset Manager > UI
chunks.text: It's not currently possible to delete **Headers** from the list but any empty headers will be ignored so are harmless.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Intro
chunks.text:
The Viewport is where Shapes within a Composition are rendered and made visible so they can be visually composed.

Use the [tools](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/) to select, transform, edit and draw Shapes and to edit supported Filters and Shaders.

When hovering over Shapes in the Viewport with the [Select](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) tool, the Shape's name will appear and, depending on the Shape's complexity, its paths or bounding box will highlight to indicate what will be selected on click. The level of detail for this 'pre-selection highlighting' is automated:

* **Full** - All paths/contours will highlight for Shapes with low complexity.
* **Medium** - Bounding boxes are drawn for individual child-meshes where Shapes are of moderate complexity. [Text Shapes](/docs/nodes/shapes/text-shape/) get special handling where bounding boxes are drawn for each word as the character count increases.
* **Low** - A single bounding box is drawn for complex Shapes.

Show Layer Names

Showing Layer names when hovering with the [Select](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) tool is optional and can be set via `View > Show Layer Names on Hover`.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Intro
chunks.text:
When Shapes are selected, a bounding box is drawn and a label with the Layer's name appears at the top right. See [Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/group/#interacting-with-groups-in-the-viewport) for selecting Groups and their children.

info

The Viewport's canvas (the area outside the Composition) color can be set via **Viewport Canvas Color** in the [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/) window.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Multiple Viewports
chunks.text:
To open additional Viewports use the `Window > Add Viewport` menu item.

When there is more than one Composition in the Scene, a drop down menu will appear in the footer of any secondary Viewports which can be used to choose and preview a particular Composition. The drop down also includes an option for the 'active' Composition – this is the current tab open in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).

Secondary Viewports will not show the [playback](#playback) controls when there is more than one Composition in the Scene.

Playback is only supported for the 'active' Composition but dragging the time thumb or stepping through frames with hotkeys or the [playback](#playback) controls can be used to preview a non-active Composition's animation. A non-active Composition's current frame will also update when playback stops.

When multiple Viewports are in use, any Viewport set to the 'active' composition will show a purple border around the window.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Zoom
chunks.text:
Set the viewport scaling. Either use the dropdown to set a value or type in a value.

Shortcuts

* With nothing selected, hit `F` to set the Viewport scaling to best fit.
* With a Shape(s) selected, hit `F` to set the Viewport scaling to best fit the selection.
* Use `Cmd/Ctrl` + `+`/`-` to double/half the Viewport zoom incrementally.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Camera
chunks.text: When multiple Cameras exist in a Scene, use the drop down to select the Camera view for each Viewport.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Playback
chunks.text:
* **Go to the first frame** - Move the playhead to the first frame of the playback range.
* **Go to the previous frame** - Nudge the playhead back one frame.
* **Playback** - Start playback. Click again to stop playback.
* **Go to the next frame** - Nudge the playhead forward one frame.
* **Go to the last frame** - Move the playhead to the last frame of the playback range.

**Playback Mode** - Determine what happens when the playhead reaches the **Playback End** during playback:

* **Loop Playback** - When the playhead reaches the **Playback End** frame, go to the **Playback Start** frame and continue playback.
* **Playback Once** - When the playhead reaches the **Playback End** frame, stop playback.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Tag Filtering
chunks.text: This icon will turn green to indicate that the [Quicklist tag](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/tags/) is active and affecting what is being displayed in the Viewport.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Color Management
chunks.text:
Enable/disable [Color Management](/docs/user-interface/general/color-management/).

**Options:**

* See [Color Management](/docs/user-interface/general/color-management/).

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Audio Playback
chunks.text:
Globally enable/disable audio playback.

**Options:**

* **Play Audio** - Enable/disable audio playback.
* **Audio Device** - Select the audio device to play audio back through.
* **Playback Volume** - Increase/decrease the volume of the audio in playback. Note that this does not affect the volume of the exported audio.

Audio Device Names

Audio devices that include unicode characters in their name may prevent audio playback to that device. These characters will not render correctly in the list – replace or remove them by renaming the device via the OS.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Snapping
chunks.text:
Snap Shapes to grids, other shapes, the composition etc.

**Options:**

* **Enable Snapping** - Enable/disable snapping.
* **Snapping Threshold** - Set the distance from a grid (in screen pixels) within which snapping will happen.
* **Grid** - Enable/disable [Grid](#grid) snapping.
* **Ruler Guide** - Enable/disable snapping to [Guides](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/rulers/#guides).
* **Composition** - Enable/disable snapping to the centre of the composition.
* **Bounding Box** - Enable/disable snapping to bounding boxes.
* **Point** - Enable/disable snapping to the points of Shapes.
* **Pixel** - Enable/disable snapping to the **Pixel Grid**. The Pixel Grid can be enabled/disabled via the [Grid](#grid) settings and the [View](/docs/user-interface/menus/view-menu/) menu.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Grid
chunks.text:
Display grid lines in the Viewport. Note that clicking the icon will only enable/disable the 2D grid.

Grid preferences

The **2D Grid** is saved 'per-Composition' whereas the **3D** and **Pixel Grid** are saved as a preference meaning if the 2D Grid is enabled that does not mean it will remain enabled the next time a new Composition is created or loaded (unless the 2D Grid has been saved as enabled in that Composition).

* 2D* 3D* Pixel

**Show 2D Grid** - Show/hide the 2D grid.

**Copy/Paste Grid** - Use these buttons to copy/paste a grid from one Composition to another.

**Grid Type** - Determine the type of 2D grid:

* **Regular** - A grid with subdivisions and an origin.
* **Swiss** - A simple grid with options for gutters.

**Origin** - When the **Grid Type** is set to **Regular**, determine where the grid's origin is placed.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Grid
chunks.text:
* **Centre** - Position the grid's origin at the centre of the Composition.
* **Top Left** - Position the grid's origin at the top left of the Composition minus the **Margin**.
* **Bottom Left** - Position the grid's origin at the bottom left of the Composition minus the **Margin**.
* **Top Right** - Position the grid's origin at the top right of the Composition minus the **Margin**.
* **Bottom Left** - Position the grid's origin at the bottom right of the Composition minus the **Margin**.

**Rotation** - Rotate the grid. Note that when the **Grid Type** is set to **Regular**, the **Origin** must also be set to **Centre**.

**Margins** - Set the distances from the Composition boundary to start or clip the grid.

**Size Mode** - When the **Grid Type** is set to **Regular**, choose how the size of a cell is determined:

* **Size Of Cell** - Set the dimensions of the major grid cells in pixels.
* **Number of Divisions** - Major cells are created by dividing the Composition's width/height minus any Margins by these values.

**Cell Size** - Set the size of the gaps between the major 2D grid lines in pixels.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Grid
chunks.text:
**Subdivision Count** - When the **Grid Type** is set to **Regular**, determine how many minor cells are created within each major cell.

**Gutter** - When the **Grid Type** is set to **Swiss**, set the size of space between cells in pixels.

**Major Line Color** - Set a color/alpha for the 2D grid's major cells.

**Minor Line Color** - Set a color/alpha for the 2D grid's minor (subdivided) cells.

**Show 3D Grid** - Show/hide the 3D grid.

**Grid Color** - Set a color/alpha for the 3D grid.

**Grid Size** - Set the total size of the 3D grid in pixels.

**Grid Step** - Set the size of the gaps between the 3D grid lines in pixels.

**Show Pixel Grid** - Show/hide the Pixel Grid. The Pixel Grid will only appear at certain [Zoom](#zoom) levels depending on the resolution of the current Composition.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Update the UI during Playback
chunks.text:
When checked, the user interface will update during playback. This includes elements like the **playhead** in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/), the **Equalizer** on the [Sound Behaviour](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sound/) and attributes in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/attribute-editor/). Note that this may occasionally have a detrimental affect on performance.

info

Note that [Playback Caching](#playback-caching) must be disabled for [Update the UI during Playback](#update-the-ui-during-playback) to be enabled.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Playback Caching
chunks.text:
Enable/disable playback caching. Note that if [Show Drawables](#viewport-settings) is set to **Except during Playback**, drawables (Falloffs, Nulls etc) will be hidden once the playback is cached. Set this to **Always** to keep them visible.

caution

Playback Caching is for the entire Composition so any change to the Composition (except time changes) will clear the entire cache.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Show Composition Boundary
chunks.text:
When checked, a border will be drawn around the Composition Boundary.

Options:

* **Boundary Color** - Set the color for the Composition Boundary.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Motion Paths
chunks.text:
When checked, paths that represent the direction and speed of selected animated Shapes will be drawn in the Viewport. See [Motion Paths](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/motion-paths/).

Options:

* **Show Frames** - When checked, dots are drawn to represent a Shape's position on each frame.
* **Show Seconds** - When checked, bars are drawn along the path to represent a second. Each bar represents the first frame of a second.
* **Show Keyframes** - When checked, larger dots are drawn to represent the Shape's position keyframes.
* **Show Path** - When checked, lines are drawn between the points representing each frame.
* **Show Direction** - When checked, chevron arrows are drawn to indicate direction.
* **Path Duration** - Set the visible length of a Motion Path in seconds. Note that this value is the overall duration of the path so a value of 6 will result in 3 seconds displayed before and after the current frame.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Onion Skinning
chunks.text:
Draw onion skinning layers in the Viewport.

Options:

* **Onion Skinning** - Enable/disable onion skinning.
* **Pre Color** - Set the color for the shapes before the current frame.
* **Pre Frames** - Set how many frames to draw before the current frame.
* **Post Color** - Set the color for the shapes after the current frame.
* **Post Frames** - Set how many frames to draw after the current frame.
* **Outline Only** - Do not fill each shape.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Clipping Mask Overview
chunks.text:
Draw clipping masks in the Viewport.

**Options:**

* **Show Clipping Masks** - When checked, masks connected to selected Shapes will be drawn as an outline in the Viewport.
* **Fill** - When checked, a green overlay will appear in the Viewport whenever a shape with a mask connected is selected.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Transparency Style
chunks.text:
Set the transparency style of the viewport.

**Options:**

* **Use Checkerboard** - when checked, a checkerboard will display where there is transparency. Note - all [Compositions](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/scene-tree/composition-settings/) have a Composition Background. If the Alpha is set to 255 checking this setting will have no effect (there is no transparency).

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Viewport Settings
chunks.text:
* **Viewport Quality** - Set which features are rendered by the Viewport. This can be used to increase playback speed where required. Note - this setting does not affect final rendering.
  + **High** - Full quality using standard anti-aliasing.
  + **Balanced** (macOS only) - Use multisample anti-aliasing (MSAA). This setting balances performance with quality.
  + **Low** - Removes **Anti-aliasing** and any **Image Filtering** (see [Image Shader](/docs/nodes/effects/shaders/image-shader/)).
  + **Lowest** - As per **Low** but also removes any **Filters** and **Shaders**.
* **Color Space** - When color management is enabled in [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/), by default, RGB pixel values are converted to the color space of your computer monitor from the working color space. Alternative spaces can be enabled to preview how a Composition will appear on other devices.
* **Layer Tools** - When checked, certain Layers will display purple UI elements which can be used to adjust their settings directly in the Viewport. A supported Layer must be selected for these tools to appear. Note that Layer Tools are not available when a Shape is the parent of anothe

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Viewport Settings
chunks.text:
r Shape.
* **Draw Debug Information** - Draw (non-renderable) diagnostics information in the Viewport. This can be useful to visualise the point Ids in a Duplicator.
* **Show FPS in Playback** - Display the frames per second the Viewport is running at during playback at the bottom of the Viewport.
* **Viewport Tool Help** - When checked, helpful hints for each [tool](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/toolbar/) will be overlaid in the bottom left corner of the Viewport.
* **Show Drawables** - Control the display of drawables (Falloffs/Nulls/Camera Guides)
  + **Always** - Always show drawables.
  + **Except during Playback** - Show drawables except during playback.
  + **Never** - Never show drawables.
* **Shape Depth Debug** - Can be used to diagnose the depth of certain Shapes within [Sub Meshes](/docs/nodes/behaviours/sub-mesh/). Useful for things like SVG artwork.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Settings > Viewport Settings
chunks.text:
caution

**Debug Information** currently only supports **pointId** and does not display in playback.

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Contextual menu
chunks.text: Right clicking a Shape or an empty space in the Viewport will bring up a menu with various options:

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Contextual menu
chunks.text:
* **Select** - Select the Shape under the cursor. Where multiple Shapes overlap, choose the required Shape from the menu items.
* **Select Hierarchy** - Where a Shape is the child of another Layer, use the menu items to select the Layers above it in the hierarchy.
* **Get Info** - Reveal information about the Shape under the cursor. Clicking a menu item will copy its value to the clipboard.
* **Zoom to Fit** - Zoom the Viewport so that the Composition fits within it.
* **Zoom** - Set a zoom level for the Viewport.
* **Save Snapshot** - Save a Snapshot of the Viewport's current state to a slot.
* **Remove Snapshot** - Remove a Snapshot from a slot.
* **Clear All Snapshots** - Remove the Snapshots from all slots.
* **Copy Layer Id** - Copy the Layer's Id to the clipboard for use with [scripting](/docs/tech-info/scripting/scripting-getting-started/)
* **Copy as SVG** - Copy the selected Shapes to the clipboard as [SVG](/docs/nodes/general/vector-artwork-support/) data.
* **Copy as JavaScript** - Copy the selected Shapes' information to the clipboard as JavaScript code. See [Cavalry Module](/docs/tech-info/scripting/cavalry-module/#path-class).
* **Make Editable** - Convert a Primitive

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Contextual menu
chunks.text:
to an [Editable Shape](/docs/nodes/shapes/editable-shape/).
* **Add Background to Selected** - Create a background for the selected Shapes by creating a **Rectangle** and a [Bounding Box](/docs/nodes/utilities/bounding-box/) Utility.
* **Layout** - Add the selected Shapes to a [Layout](/docs/nodes/shapes/layouts/layouts-intro/).
* **Bring to Front** - Move the selected Shapes to the top of their parent's hierarchy.
* **Bring Forward** - Move the selected Shapes up one layer within their parent's hierarchy.
* **Send Backward** - Move the selected Shapes down one layer within their parent's hierarchy.
* **Send to Back** - Move the selected Shapes to the bottom of their parent's hierarchy.
* **Add to Duplicator** - Add the selected Shapes to a [Duplicator](/docs/nodes/shapes/duplicator/).
* **Group Selected** - Add the selected Shapes to a [Group](/docs/nodes/shapes/group/)
* **Lock Selected** - Lock the selected Shapes to prevent accidental selection. Note that the locking behaviour will depend on the [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/).
* **Show in Attribute Editor** - Load or reveal the selected Shapes in the [Attribute Editor](/docs/user-interface/m

chunks.title: Viewport
chunks.heading: Viewport > Viewport > Contextual menu
chunks.text:
enus/window-menu/attribute-editor/).
* **Show in Scene Window** - Load or reveal the selected Shapes in the [Scene Window](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/).

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Intro
chunks.text:
Draw and edit paths that represent the direction and speed of selected animated Shapes.

Motion Paths can be enabled/disabled in the [Viewport Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#viewport-settings) and will appear for up to 10 selected Shapes.

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Appearance
chunks.text:
The information density for a Motion Path can be determined in the [Viewport Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#motion-paths) with options to display frames, seconds, keyframes and the path and its direction. The path's length can also be set to represent a period of time.

Up to 10 selected Shapes can be displayed at once.

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Interaction
chunks.text: It's possible to interact with a Motion Path directly in the Viewport. This is very similar to how interactions work in the [Graph Editor](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/scene-window/graph-editor/) and with the [Edit Shape](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/edit-shape-tool/) tool.

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Interaction > Keyframes > Move a Keyframe
chunks.text:
A keyframe is indicated by a diamond shape.

To move a keyframe in the Viewport, with the [Select](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) tool active:

* Click + Drag a keyframe to a new position.

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Interaction > Keyframes > Add a Keyframe
chunks.text:
To add a new keyframe to a Motion Path, with the [Select](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) tool active:

* Select a Shape in the Viewport, hold the `S` key and click on a frame along a motion path.

While `S` is held, a preview of where the new keyframe will be created is displayed. A new keyframe will be created on a whole frame as long as a keyframe does not already exist on that frame.

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Interaction > Keyframes > Delete a Keyframe
chunks.text:
To delete a keyframe from a Motion Path, with the [Select](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) tool active:

* Select a keyframe and hit the `Delete` key.

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Interaction > Interpolation
chunks.text:
A keyframe's handles determine the acceleration/deceleration of a Shape either side of their parent keyframe. A handle appears for a bézier keyframe as a small circle on the end of a line. Note that a linear keyframe has no visible handles.

To convert a handle, with the [Select](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) tool active:

* `Option/Alt` + Click a keyframe to toggle between bézier/linear interpolation.
* `Option/Alt` + Click + Drag a keyframe to toggle between bézier/linear interpolation **and** edit the handle(s).

Bézier handles can be joint or broken. A joint handle will also move its opposing handle whereas a broken handle will not.

To set a handle's joint/broken state:

* `Option/Alt` + Click + Drag a handle to toggle it between a joint and broken state.
* `Option/Alt` + Click + Drag a handle to toggle it between a joint and broken state **and** move it.

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Interaction > Velocity Editing
chunks.text:
Velocity editing is a way to increase/decrease a Shape’s velocity while maintaining the shape of its Motion Path.

To edit a Shape's velocity, with the [Select](/docs/user-interface/menus/tool-menu/select-tool/) tool active:

* Hold `Shift` + `Cmd/Ctrl` and drag a handle. If the handle is joined, both handles will be affected.
* Hold `Shift` + `Cmd/Ctrl` + `Option/Alt` and drag a handle. If the handle is joined, only the selected handle will be affected.

Ensure that **Frames** are enabled in the **Motion Path** [Viewport Settings](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#motion-paths) to visualise the change in velocity.

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Interaction > Velocity Presets
chunks.text: Easing presets can be applied to keyframes via the Viewport. Click on part of the Motion Path between two visible keyframes to pop up a menu:

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Interaction > Velocity Presets > Built-in Velocity Presets
chunks.text: By default, a list of built-in Presets are displayed in a list. Clicking one will apply that Velocity Preset to each of the keyframes either side of that section of the Motion Path. Like Velocity Editing, the easing is applied while maintaining the original shape of its Motion Path.

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Interaction > Velocity Presets > Custom Velocity Presets
chunks.text: To save a custom Velocity Preset, chose `Create Custom Preset...` from the list and then enter the required values into the window:

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Interaction > Velocity Presets > Custom Velocity Presets
chunks.text:
* **Preset Name** - Enter a name for the Velocity Preset.
* **Speed In** - Set a value of between `0` and `2` to determine a Shape's speed from the first keyframe where a value of `0` is a very slow start and `2` is a very fast start. `0` can be thought of as the equivalent of a horizontal handle in the Graph Editor.
* **Influence In** - Set a length of between `0` and `1` for the first keyframe's handle where `0` is zero length and `1` is the maximum length.
* **Speed Out** - Set a value of between `0` and `2` to determine a Shape's speed into the last keyframe where a value of `0` is a very slow finish and `2` is a very fast finish. `0` can be thought of as the equivalent of a horizontal handle in the Graph Editor.
* **Influence Out** - Set a length of between `0` and `1` for the last keyframe's handle where `0` is zero length and `1` is the maximum length.
* **Allow New Keyframe** - Cavalry attempts to maintain the Motion Path's shape when applying Velocity Presets. When the **Speed** and **Influence** values are both below a value of `0.1`, it may be necessary to add an additional keyframe between the existing ones to maintain the Motion Path's shape. Unchecking this will preve

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Interaction > Velocity Presets > Custom Velocity Presets
chunks.text: Once a **Custom Preset** is saved, it will appear under a `Custom Presets` menu item when clicking the Motion Path.

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Interaction > Velocity Presets > Manage Custom Velocity Presets
chunks.text: Once one or more Custom Velocity Presets have been saved, they can be edited and/or exported. To edit a custom Velocity Preset, chose `Manage Custom Presets...` from the list to pop open a window with the following options:

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Interaction > Velocity Presets > Manage Custom Velocity Presets > List
chunks.text:
Use the `...` button to the right of each row to:

* **Rename** - Rename the Velocity Preset. Double clicking a row can also be used to rename.
* **Edit...** - Edit the Velocity Preset. The options in the window are identical to [above](#custom-velocity-presets). Click `Save` to commit any changes.
* **Export...** - Save the Velocity Preset to the filesystem.
* **Delete** - Remove the Velocity Preset.

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Interaction > Velocity Presets > Manage Custom Velocity Presets > Buttons
chunks.text:
* **Import** - Import a Velocity Preset.
* **Export All...** - Export all of the Custom Velocity Presets in the list to a `.json` file. See [Setting Default Velocity Presets](#setting-default-velocity-presets).

chunks.title: Motion Paths
chunks.heading: Motion Paths > Motion Paths > Interaction > Setting Default Velocity Presets
chunks.text:
By saving the [Export All...](#buttons) `.json` file to...

* macOS - `~/Library/Preferences/Cavalry/VelocityPresets/`
* Windows - `C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Local\Cavalry\VelocityPresets\`

...the Velocity Presets contained within it can be used populate the menu via the **Default Velocity Presets** preference in the [Preferences](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/preferences/) window.

Once this has been set, when clicking on part of the Motion Path between two visible keyframes, the menu will populate the top of the list with the Velocity Presets contained within the file and demote the 'Built-in' presets to a sub-menu.

This can be useful when working on a project with a pre-defined motion language to ensure consistency across a team of animators.

chunks.title: Playback Controls
chunks.heading: Playback Controls
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Viewport* Playback Controls

On this page

chunks.title: Playback Controls
chunks.heading: Playback Controls > Playback Controls > UI
chunks.text:
**Go to the first frame** - Move the playhead to the first frame of the **Playback Range**.

**Go to the previous frame** - Nudge the playhead back one frame.

**Playback** - Start playback. Click again to stop playback.

**Go to the next frame** - Nudge the playhead forward one frame.

**Go to the last frame** - Move the playhead to the last frame of the **Playback Range**.

**Playback Mode** - Determine what happens when the playhead reaches the **Playback End** during playback:

* **Loop Playback** - When the playhead reaches the **Playback End** frame, go to the **Playback Start** frame and continue playback.
* **Playback Once** - When the playhead reaches the **Playback End** frame, stop playback.

chunks.title: Rulers and Guides
chunks.heading: Rulers and Guides
chunks.text:
* * User Interface* Menus* Window menu* Viewport* Rulers and Guides

On this page

chunks.title: Rulers and Guides
chunks.heading: Rulers and Guides > Rulers and Guides > Rulers
chunks.text: **Rulers** appear at the top and left hand side of the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) and can be used to measure the pixel or percentage values of a [Composition](/docs/nodes/shapes/composition/) as well as displaying the position of the cursor.

chunks.title: Rulers and Guides
chunks.heading: Rulers and Guides > Rulers and Guides > Rulers > Show/Hide Rulers
chunks.text: To show/hide the Rulers, choose **View > Show Rulers** or use the use the shortcut `Cmd/Ctrl` + `R`.

chunks.title: Rulers and Guides
chunks.heading: Rulers and Guides > Rulers and Guides > Rulers > Ruler Options
chunks.text:
Determine how the values of Rulers are displayed by using the **View > Ruler Options** menu:

* **Origin in Centre** - Values are 0,0 in the centre of the Composition.
* **Origin In Bottom Left** - Values are 0,0 in the bottom left corner of the Composition.
* **Use Pixels** - Display values as pixels.
* **Use Percentage** - Display values as a percentage of the Composition's width/height.

chunks.title: Rulers and Guides
chunks.heading: Rulers and Guides > Rulers and Guides > Guides
chunks.text: **Guides** are horizontal and vertical non-rendering lines that can be placed in the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/) and used to position [Shapes](/docs/nodes/shapes/).

chunks.title: Rulers and Guides
chunks.heading: Rulers and Guides > Rulers and Guides > Guides > Create a Guide
chunks.text: To create a **Guide**, hover the cursor over a [Ruler](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/rulers/) and `click + drag` into the [Viewport](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/). When dragging, a thin red line will appear along with a number indicating its X or Y position. Release the mouse to place the Guide.

chunks.title: Rulers and Guides
chunks.heading: Rulers and Guides > Rulers and Guides > Guides > Move a Guide
chunks.text:
To move a Guide, either:

* Hover the cursor over a Guide, `click + drag` and then release to reposition the Guide or;
* Hover the cursor over a Guide, `double click` and then enter a new value in the popover input.

Nearest Pixel

When creating or repositioning Guides they are always snapped to the nearest pixel. While it's possible to manually enter decimal values, they will be rounded to the nearest integer when the Rulers are in **Use Pixels** mode or repositioned to the nearest pixel when in **Use Percentage** mode. Note that the nearest pixel is unlikely to result in an integer value when in **Use Percentage** mode.

chunks.title: Rulers and Guides
chunks.heading: Rulers and Guides > Rulers and Guides > Guides > Remove a Guide
chunks.text: To remove a Guide, `click + drag` one back over a [Ruler](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/rulers/) and then release the mouse.

chunks.title: Rulers and Guides
chunks.heading: Rulers and Guides > Rulers and Guides > Guides > Show/Hide Guides
chunks.text:
Use the **View > Show Guides** menu option or `Cmd/Ctrl` + `;` to show/hide Guides.

Snapping

**Guides** can be snapped to by enabling **Ruler Guide** Snapping in the [Viewport Snapping](/docs/user-interface/menus/window-menu/viewport/#snapping) options.

chunks.title: Welcome
chunks.heading: Welcome > Welcome
chunks.text:
Cavalry is a powerful **2D Animation** software for **macOS** and **Windows** making waves in the worlds of animation, motion design, creative coding, film, generative art, data visualisation, experiential and advertising.
